12888.s: This order amends the Manual for Courts-Martial. It changes rules on military judges, pretrial confinement, evidence, guilty pleas, findings, and trial records. It also changes rules for classified information and security clearances in military cases.

12889.s: This order sets up a United States section of the NAFTA Secretariat in the Department of Commerce and puts rules in place to carry out parts of NAFTA. It directs federal agencies to follow special notice rules for proposed technical regulations and sanitary or phytosanitary measures, and it changes how some federal procurement rules apply to eligible products and suppliers from Canada and Mexico. It also sets procedures for the federal government’s use of patented technology without a license and says the order does not create a right that can be enforced in court.

12886.s: This order adjusts the monthly basic pay and basic allowances for subsistence and quarters for members of the uniformed services. The new rates are effective on January 1, 1994. It also supersedes Section 4 and Schedule 8 of Executive Order No. 12826.

12887.s: This order amends a section of Executive Order 12878. It changes one membership reference from 30 members to 32 members and another from Ten members to Twelve members.

12885.s: This order changes a previous executive order on the National Industrial Security Program. It extends the deadline for issuing the National Industrial Security Program Operating Manual to no later than June 30, 1994, and applies to the Secretary of Defense and the Director of Central Intelligence when making related changes.

12883.s: This order gives the President’s Pay Agent authority to exercise the President’s powers under section 5304(h). That authority is for extending locality-based comparability payments to certain categories of positions that are not otherwise covered.

12884.s: This order delegates certain presidential duties under the Freedom Support Act and related foreign aid laws to the Secretary of State, a Coordinator, the United States International Development Cooperation Agency, the Secretary of Agriculture, and other agency heads. It covers functions tied to reporting, determinations, directives, and administration of specific programs and activities. It also says some of these officials may redelegate the functions if allowed by law.

12882.s: This order creates the President's Committee of Advisors on Science and Technology, called PCAST. It says PCAST will advise the President on science and technology matters and help the National Science and Technology Council secure private sector involvement in its work. The committee may have up to 16 members, serve without pay, and use Office of Science and Technology Policy funds and services.

12881.s: This order establishes the National Science and Technology Council. It puts the President in charge of the Council and includes several cabinet officials and other top advisers as members. The Council is directed to coordinate science and technology policy across the federal government, work on research and development budget recommendations, and help ensure science and technology are considered in federal policies and programs.

12880.s: This order gives the Office of National Drug Control Policy the lead role in setting the Nation’s drug control policies, priorities, and objectives. It directs coordination of international counternarcotics policy, drug interdiction, drug data sharing, and reviews of drug abuse treatment and prevention efforts. It also requires budget recommendations and reports from federal departments and agencies involved in the National Drug Control Program.

12879.s: This order sets the line of succession for who will act as Secretary of the Navy if that office becomes vacant or if the Secretary is temporarily absent or disabled. It names the Under Secretary first, then the Assistant Secretaries and General Counsel by length of service, then the Chief of Naval Operations, and then the Commandant of the Marine Corps. The acting role is temporary and does not change the person’s permanent appointment.

12878.s:
This order creates a Bipartisan Commission on Entitlement Reform. The Commission has 30 members appointed by the President, including Senators, Members of the House, and people from the public or private sector with experience in the areas the Commission will review.

The Commission must recommend long-term budget savings measures involving revisions to statutory entitlement and other mandatory programs, and alternative tax reform proposals. It must report its recommendations to the National Economic Council and congressional leaders, and it ends 30 days after it submits its report.

12877.s: This order changes an earlier order about United States relations with the Freely Associated States. It makes the Secretary of State responsible for those relations and for support to the Interagency Group. It also says executive departments and agencies shall cooperate, while the Secretary of Defense keeps authority over security and defense matters in or relating to the Freely Associated States.

12876.s: This order creates a Presidential advisory board and a White House initiative at the Department of Education for historically Black colleges and universities. It directs federal departments and agencies to work with these schools through grants, contracts, cooperative agreements, technical assistance, and annual plans to increase their participation in federal programs. It also calls for private sector help, advice on financial security, and a program to improve recruitment of their students and graduates for federal jobs.

12875.s: This order directs federal agencies to reduce unfunded mandates on State, local, and tribal governments when they are not required by statute, unless federal funds are provided or the agency explains the need for the rule after consulting with those governments. It also requires agencies to create a process for meaningful input from State, local, and tribal officials on major regulatory proposals. Agencies must review and streamline waiver requests and, when possible, decide complete waiver applications within 120 days. Independent agencies are requested to comply.

12874.s: The order creates a three-member emergency board to investigate a dispute between the Long Island Rail Road and certain employees represented by the United Transportation Union. The board must report its findings to the President within 30 days. While the board is active and for 120 days after it is created, the carrier and the employees cannot change the conditions that led to the dispute unless both sides agree.

12873.s: This order tells executive agencies to add waste prevention and recycling into daily operations and to favor environmentally preferable and recycled products when buying goods and services. It creates a Federal Environmental Executive and agency Environmental Executives to help carry out the order and report on progress. Agencies must also set up affirmative procurement programs, review their standards and specifications, and use more electronic purchasing to reduce paper waste.

12871.s: This order creates a National Partnership Council to advise the President on labor-management relations in the executive branch. It brings together federal officials and union leaders to support labor-management partnerships, share information, and suggest needed statutory changes. Agency heads are directed to form or adapt labor-management committees or councils, involve employees and their union representatives as full partners, provide training, negotiate on certain subjects, and evaluate progress.

12869.s: This order continues several federal advisory committees and reestablishes the President’s Council of Advisors on Science and Technology. It says the listed committees will keep operating until September 30, 1995, and that the head of each named department or agency will carry out the President’s duties under the Federal Advisory Committee Act for those committees, except for annual reporting to Congress. It also revokes several executive orders for committees that have ended or finished their work.

12870.s: This order creates the Trade Promotion Coordinating Committee, made up of representatives from many federal departments and agencies, with the Secretary of Commerce as chairperson. The committee is meant to coordinate federal export promotion and export financing and to develop a governmentwide strategic plan for trade promotion. It must also give information to the business community, reduce duplicate federal efforts, and recommend resource levels. The chairperson must submit a report on the plan, its implementation, and any revisions to Congress.

12868.s: This order declares a national emergency over the proliferation of nuclear, biological, and chemical weapons and the means to deliver them. It directs the Secretary of Commerce, with the Secretary of State, to keep regulating the activities of United States persons to prevent their participation in activities that could contribute to weapons proliferation. It also says the order does not affect existing rules, licenses, or other administrative actions under the Export Administration Act or the earlier orders named in it.

12867.s: This order revokes Executive Order 12730 and rescinds the declaration of economic emergency tied to export control rules. It says the revocation does not change past violations that happened while the order was in effect. It also keeps certain export control rules, licenses, and other administrative actions in force until they are amended or revoked by the proper authority.

12866.s: This order sets rules for how federal agencies should plan, review, and write regulations. It says agencies should consider costs and benefits, use the best available information, avoid duplicate or conflicting rules, and make regulations simple and easy to understand. It also gives the Office of Management and Budget a review role and requires agencies to prepare regulatory agendas and plans.

12864.s: This order creates the United States Advisory Council on the National Information Infrastructure in the Commerce Department. The council may have up to 25 members, appointed by the Secretary of Commerce, and it advises the Secretary on developing a national information infrastructure and a national strategy for it. It may address topics like public and private roles, regulation, electronic commerce, health care, government services, national security, universal access, privacy, security, and copyright. The Commerce Department provides support, and the council is set to exist for two years unless its charter is extended.

12862.s:
This order tells executive branch agencies that serve the public to set customer service standards and try to match the best private-sector service. Agencies must identify their customers, survey them, post service standards, measure results, and provide ways to handle complaints.

Each agency must report on its customer surveys and publish a customer service plan that customers can understand. Independent agencies are requested to follow the order, and it does not create a right or benefit that can be enforced against the government.

12863.s: This order establishes the President’s Foreign Intelligence Advisory Board in the White House and a smaller Intelligence Oversight Board within it. The boards review intelligence activities, including how agencies collect and use intelligence and whether any activities may be unlawful or contrary to executive orders or presidential directives. Federal intelligence agencies and other departments must give them the information they need, to the extent allowed by law. The order also revokes two earlier executive orders.

12860.s: This order adds three more members to the Committee on Foreign Investment in the United States. The new members are the Director of the Office of Science and Technology Policy, the Assistant to the President for National Security Affairs, and the Assistant to the President for Economic Policy. It takes effect immediately.

12861.s: The order directs each executive department and agency to eliminate at least half of its civilian internal management regulations that are not required by law within 3 years. It says these cuts should focus on areas that improve productivity, streamline operations, and improve customer service. It applies to all executive branch departments and agencies, and independent regulatory commissions and agencies are asked to comply. The Director of the Office of Management and Budget is to issue instructions, including needed exemptions for essential services and compliance with law.

12859.s: This order creates the Domestic Policy Council and makes the President its chairman. It includes several Cabinet officials and other top White House and agency officials, and the President or the Assistant to the President for Domestic Policy may call its meetings. The council is meant to coordinate domestic policy advice, keep domestic policy decisions and programs consistent with the President’s goals, and monitor the President’s domestic policy agenda. All executive departments and agencies must coordinate domestic policy through the council and cooperate with it as needed.

12858.s: This order creates a separate Treasury account called the Deficit Reduction Fund. It directs that money from the net deficit reduction in the Omnibus Budget Reconciliation Act of 1993 be put into the fund and used only to redeem certain maturing Treasury debt held by foreign governments. It also bars those amounts from being used for new spending or for measures that increase the deficit, and it requires yearly reporting on the fund in the President’s Budget.

12857.s: This order sets up a system to track direct spending costs and compare them with set targets. If spending goes over the target, it requires a special budget message with recommendations, which can include cuts, revenue increases, or no changes. It also directs the budget process to adjust the targets for changes in beneficiaries, revenue laws, emergency-designated costs, and congressional action. The order applies to direct spending targets for fiscal years 1994 through 1997.

12856.s: Federal agencies that own or operate covered facilities must follow pollution prevention and right-to-know rules for toxic chemicals and extremely hazardous substances. They must reduce toxic chemicals in their waste streams, recycle waste where possible, report releases and transfers publicly, and improve emergency planning and accident notification. Agencies also must make plans to reduce unnecessary buying and use of extremely hazardous substances or toxic chemicals and to review their standards and procurement practices.

12855.s: This order changes Executive Order 12852. It says the Department of the Interior must provide administrative services for the Council on a reimbursable basis. It also changes Section 4 to replace the Office of Administration in the Executive Office of the President with the Department of the Interior.

12854.s: This order tells federal agencies to take the steps needed to carry out the Cuban Democracy Act. It assigns the Secretary of State, Treasury, and Commerce to handle specific parts of the law, including certain transactions with Cuba and exports to Cuba of goods and technology. It also says the order does not affect functions already given by law to the Federal Communications Commission.

12851.s: This order delegates several sanctions, reporting, and certification duties on chemical and biological weapons proliferation, missile proliferation, and arms control to Cabinet officials. It covers decisions about certain imports, exports, government contracts, waivers, and reports to Congress. It also assigns Middle East arms control functions, China and weapons proliferation reporting, and Arrow anti-missile program certifications to the Secretary of State.

12850.s: This order sets conditions for deciding whether China’s most-favored-nation trade status should be extended for the 12-month period beginning July 3, 1994. It directs the Secretary of State to recommend extension only if China is complying with the prison labor agreement and if extension would substantially promote freedom of emigration. It also calls for a review of China’s progress on human rights, treatment of prisoners, Tibet’s religious and cultural heritage, and access for international radio and television broadcasts, and it directs U.S. officials to pursue actions on fair trade and nonproliferation commitments.

12849.s: This order puts into effect a government procurement agreement with the European Community. It directs listed agencies to give no price difference between U.S. goods and goods from European Community member states for covered purchases. It applies to certain solicitations above the listed threshold amounts and sets rules for how origin is determined.

12848.s: This order directs federal agencies, through the Interagency Council on the Homeless, to develop one coordinated Federal plan to break the cycle of existing homelessness and prevent future homelessness. The plan must recommend administrative and legislative steps, and may seek to streamline and consolidate programs that assist homeless individuals and families. It also must look at ways to link housing, support, and education services, and to coordinate work with local providers, school districts, and advocates.

12847.s: This order amends an earlier executive order to cover permits for a wider range of facilities at the borders of the United States. It gives the Secretary of State authority to receive applications for permits for pipelines, conveyor belts, water or sewage facilities, transportation facilities, bridges where congressional authorization is not required, and similar facilities. Permits already issued, and permits issued under this order, stay in effect unless they are changed or revoked by the proper authority.

12845.s: This order directs federal agencies to buy microcomputers, including personal computers, monitors, and printers, that meet EPA Energy Star energy-efficiency requirements within 180 days. It also requires these computers to have a low-power standby feature, with some case-by-case exemptions allowed. Agencies must tell users about the feature in computer training and report exempted purchases each year.

12844.s:
This order directs federal agencies to make plans to buy more alternative fueled vehicles and to exceed the purchase requirements in the Energy Policy Act of 1992. The federal government must acquire alternative fueled vehicles in numbers that are 50 percent above the 1993 through 1995 requirements, subject to available funds and life cycle costs.

It also sets up a task force to advise on the order, requires annual reports, and allows the Secretary of Energy and the General Services Administration to help with buying and using these vehicles. The order affects federal agencies, with separate exceptions for national security, protective, and law enforcement activities.

12842.s: The order designates the International Development Law Institute as a public international organization. It gives the organization the privileges, exemptions, and immunities under the International Organizations Immunities Act. It also says this designation does not limit any privileges, exemptions, or immunities the organization may already have or later get through international agreements or congressional action.

12843.s: This order directs federal agencies to cut back on buying and using substances that deplete the ozone layer. It tells agencies to use safe alternatives when possible, review their current and future use of these substances, and change contracts and procurement rules to fit ozone protection policies. It also requires agencies to report on their progress and have certain practices in place within 6 months where feasible.

12841.s: This order changes positions in levels IV and V of the Executive Schedule. It adds the Commissioner on Aging at the Department of Health and Human Services to one section, removes that position and the Transition Manager of the United States Enrichment Corporation from another section, and renumbers two subsections.

12840.s: This order extends the period for peaceful nuclear cooperation with the European Atomic Energy Community through March 10, 1994. It says that ending this cooperation would harm U.S. non-proliferation goals and could affect the common defense and security of the United States. It also says Executive Order 12791 is superseded.

12839.s: This order directs executive branch departments and agencies with over 100 employees to cut at least 4% of their civilian personnel positions over the next 3 fiscal years. The cuts are to be made through attrition or early out programs, and at least 10% of the reductions must come from senior executive and higher-grade positions. Independent regulatory commissions and agencies are requested to comply.

12838.s: This order tells executive departments and agencies to end at least one-third of the advisory committees they sponsor that are covered by federal law and not required by statute. It also requires them to send reports about whether other committees should continue or end. New advisory committees covered by that law can only be created or sponsored if they are required by statute or meet strict approval rules.

12836.s: This order revokes two earlier executive orders on federal contracting. One had prohibited the use of project agreements on federal construction contracts, and the other had required federal contractors to post a notice that workers are not required to join unions. It also directs executive agency heads to revoke any orders, rules, or regulations that carried out those two revoked orders, as far as the law allows.

12837.s: This order requires executive departments and agencies to list administrative expenses separately when they submit budget requests to the Office of Management and Budget. It directs agencies to seek reductions in those administrative expenses from the fiscal year 1993 baseline for fiscal years 1994 through 1997. The Director of the Office of Management and Budget is to define administrative expenses, review agency requests, and can lower a request if an agency does not comply. Independent regulatory commissions and agencies are requested to follow the order.

12835.s: This order creates the National Economic Council and sets up its membership, led by the President. The Council is meant to coordinate economic policy advice, keep economic policy and programs in line with the President’s goals, and watch over the President’s economic policy agenda. All executive departments and agencies must coordinate economic policy through the Council and help it with information, advice, and support as allowed by law.

12834.s: This order requires certain executive branch appointees and trade negotiators to sign ethics pledges when they take office or before they join a trade negotiation. The pledges restrict them from lobbying their former agency for five years and from representing, aiding, or advising foreign governments, foreign political parties, or foreign business entities in certain matters after they leave government service. It also lets the President grant waivers, sets agency rules for compliance, and allows enforcement through agency or court action.

12833.s: This order adds the Transition Manager for the United States Enrichment Corporation to level V of the Executive Schedule. It affects that federal position by placing it in that pay level.

12832.s: This order updates the rules for the National Research Council of the National Academy of Sciences. It says the Council should help stimulate research, encourage cooperation in research, gather and share scientific and technical information, and help address military, industrial, environmental, health, and economic problems. It also encourages federal scientists and other technical professionals to take part in the Council’s work when allowed, and says the Academy may be paid for its actual expenses under set funding rules.

12831.s: This order prohibits certain transactions in the United States or by U.S. persons that involve transshipment of commodities or products through the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia (Serbia and Montenegro). It also prohibits transactions involving vessels with a majority or controlling interest held by a person or entity in, or operating from, that country, no matter what flag the vessel flies. The Secretary of the Treasury is authorized to take further actions, including rules and regulations, and federal agencies are directed to help carry out the order.

12830.s: This order creates a Military Outstanding Volunteer Service Medal, along with ribbons and other items that go with it. It is for members of the Armed Forces, including Reserve components, who do outstanding volunteer service to the civilian community in a sustained, direct, and consequential way. The Secretary of Defense must set the rules for the award and wear of the medal, and it may be awarded posthumously.

12828.s: This order gives the Office of Personnel Management authority to shorten advance notice for reductions in force and to allow performance-based cash awards for some employees who would not otherwise qualify. It also gives the Director of the Office of Management and Budget authority to designate certain agency positions as critical positions. These changes affect federal personnel management.

12827.s: This order changes a prior executive order to extend the reporting period of the National Commission on America's Urban Families. It replaces the old reporting deadline of December 31, 1992, with January 20, 1993.

12829.s: This order creates a National Industrial Security Program to protect Federal classified information that is released to contractors, licensees, and grantees. It applies to executive branch departments and agencies and sets rules for safeguarding classified information during contracting, licensing, and grant activities. The order also sets up oversight, a policy committee, and a manual for how the program will work, and it directs agencies to follow its requirements and fix violations.

12826.s: This order changes pay rates and allowances for several federal pay systems, including the General Schedule, the Foreign Service Schedule, and Veterans Health Administration schedules. It also changes pay for senior executive service members, executive branch salaries, the vice president, Congress, and judges and justices. Members of the uniformed services get new monthly pay and allowances, and some federal employees in listed geographic areas get interim geographic pay adjustments. The new schedules take effect on or after January 1, 1993.

12825.s: This order closed executive departments and agencies of the federal government for the last half of the workday on Christmas Eve, December 24, 1992, and excused employees from duty. Agency heads could keep certain offices open and require some employees to work for reasons of national security, defense, or other essential public reasons. It applies only to the federal government and not to state or local governments.

12824.s: This order establishes the Transportation Distinguished Service Medal, along with ribbons and other items that go with it. The Secretary of Transportation may award it to a Coast Guard member who has given exceptionally meritorious service in a duty of great responsibility while assigned in the Department of Transportation or in other activities under that Secretary’s responsibility. It also sets rules for the medal’s design, precedence, one award per person, and posthumous awards.

12823.s: This order amends Executive Order 12757 on the Enterprise for the Americas Initiative. It changes several references to federal laws and updates the names and duties of the board and related sections. It also says the order is only for internal management of the Federal Government and does not create a right or benefit that can be enforced against the United States.

12821.s: This order directs certain federal departments, agencies, and laboratories to help improve mathematics and science education. It says they should help train elementary and secondary school teachers, allow brief excused absence for federal employees who help with these programs, and develop implementation plans. It also gives elementary and secondary schools priority for education-related federal equipment and sets up a committee to coordinate the transfers.

12822.s: This order changes a prior executive order to allow regulations for paying allowances to employees assigned to Johnston Island. The allowances are for helping employees keep their spouses or dependents, or both, at a place other than Johnston Island. The order takes effect as of January 1, 1992.

12820.s: The order tells each executive department and agency to encourage employees to take part voluntarily in community service. It says community service may include efforts related to drug abuse, crime, homelessness, illiteracy, AIDS, teenage pregnancy, hunger, low-income housing, education, health care, and the environment. Each department and agency must name a senior official and an office to support this work, and submit an annual report on its actions.

12819.s: This order establishes a youth award for community service. It recognizes voluntary community service by individuals ages 5 to 22. The Director of the White House Office of National Service is to set the award criteria, and the award is to be selected and presented through the offices named in the order.

12818.s: This order directs federal agencies to promote open bidding on federal and federally funded construction projects. It bars agencies and contractors from requiring bidders, contractors, or subcontractors to join or follow agreements with labor organizations, or from making workers pay dues or fees over their objection, except for voluntary lawful agreements. It also tells agencies to review grant and cooperative agreement rules, and it allows exemptions for special circumstances involving public health, safety, or national security.

12817.s: This order directs the Treasury Secretary to carry out United Nations Security Council Resolution 778 and to take steps tied to blocked funds and other assets linked to the Government of Iraq. If the Treasury Secretary determines that certain funds or assets are proceeds from Iraqi petroleum or petroleum products sold on or after August 6, 1990, U.S. financial institutions must transfer them to the Federal Reserve Bank of New York. The Federal Reserve Bank of New York is authorized to receive, hold, invest, or transfer those funds and assets as directed by the Treasury Secretary.

12816.s: This order creates the President's Council on Management Improvement, an interagency group made up of officials from many federal departments and agencies. The council is to discuss problems, recommend improvements in federal management and operations, and advise the Chairman on these matters. It also sets out the Chairman's duties and says Executive Order No. 12479 is revoked.

12815.s: This order extends the President's Commission on Management of the Agency for International Development programs. It changes the commission's end date from September 30, 1992 to December 31, 1992.

12813.s: This order creates a five-member advisory commission made up of private sector members appointed by the President. The commission advises the Administrator of AID on reviewing and carrying out recommendations from an earlier report on AID programs, and it reports progress to the Deputy Secretary of State. AID is to provide funding and administrative support, and the commission is set to end no later than September 30, 1992.

12814.s: This order adds members of the Chemical Safety and Hazard Investigation Board to Level IV of the Executive Schedule. It changes the pay level for those board members under the federal schedule.

12812.s: This order directs executive departments and agencies to review materials about American prisoners of war and missing in action lost in Southeast Asia for declassification. It also directs them to make declassified materials public, except for records that would invade personal privacy or harm executive branch deliberations.

12810.s: This order blocks property and interests in property of the Government of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia (Serbia and Montenegro) that are in the United States or under the control of United States persons. It also bans many transactions involving trade, transport, financial transfers, sporting events, and scientific, cultural, and technical exchanges with Serbia and Montenegro. Some activities tied to the United Nations Protection Force, the Conference on Yugoslavia, or the European Community Monitor Mission are excepted.

12811.s: This order waives the application of sections 402(a) and 402(b) of the Trade Act of 1974 with respect to Tajikistan and Turkmenistan. It affects those two countries by removing those requirements from the act for them.

12809.s: This order waives the application of sections 402(a) and 402(b) of the Trade Act of 1974 for Albania, Azerbaijan, Georgia, Kazakhstan, Moldova, Ukraine, and Uzbekistan. It affects those countries by removing those Trade Act requirements for them.

12808.s: This order declares a national emergency over the actions and policies of the governments of Serbia and Montenegro. It blocks property and interests in property of those governments, and of the former Yugoslav governments, that are in the United States or under control of United States persons. It also prohibits United States persons from making transactions that evade or try to evade these restrictions.

12806.s: The order directs the Secretary of Health and Human Services to establish a human fetal tissue bank. The tissue in the bank must come only from ectopic pregnancies and spontaneous abortions. The Secretary must set up procedures to make tissue available for approved research projects and keep a registry of physicians and hospitals interested in using the tissue for specific medical objectives.

12805.s: This order creates two councils made up of inspectors general and other federal officials. The councils are meant to review weak spots in federal programs, help prevent fraud, waste, and abuse, and develop coordinated plans and policies. It also sets duties for the council chairperson, provides administrative support, and revokes a previous executive order on the same topic.

12804.s: This order directs the use of Armed Forces units and Federal law enforcement officers to suppress the violence described in the proclamation and restore law and order in and about Los Angeles and other districts of California. It authorizes the Secretary of Defense to use needed Armed Forces, including calling National Guard units or members into active military service for an indefinite period. It also authorizes the Attorney General to coordinate Federal agencies helping with the suppression of violence and the administration of justice.

12803.s: This order directs federal agencies to review and adjust rules on federally financed infrastructure assets owned by state and local governments to encourage privatization when allowed by law. It defines privatization as the transfer or sale or long-term lease of an infrastructure asset to a private party, and it covers assets such as roads, bridges, airports, water systems, schools, prisons, and hospitals. It also says state and local governments may get approval to privatize only if the proceeds are used for new infrastructure, debt or tax reduction, and the asset keeps being used for its originally authorized purposes.

12802.s: This order waives the application of sections 402(a) and 402(b) of the Trade Act of 1974 for the Republic of Byelarus, the Republic of Kyrgyzstan, and the Russian Federation. It affects those three countries under the Trade Act.

12801.s: This order prohibits giving permission for an aircraft to take off from, land in, or overfly the United States if the flight is going to Libya or has taken off from Libya. It also directs the Secretary of the Treasury, with the Secretary of Transportation, to issue rules and take other steps to carry it out. Federal agencies affected by the order must help implement it and may suspend or end existing licenses or other authorizations.

12799.s: This order gives the Secretary of Defense the President’s authority to remove the name of a commissioned officer of the Naval Reserve or Marine Corps Reserve from a promotion list for promotions below rear admiral (lower half) or brigadier general. It also lets that authority be passed to the Deputy Secretary of Defense, assistant secretaries of defense, or the Secretary of the Navy, with further subdelegation to certain subordinates. The order does not change the President’s authority to remove a name from a selection board report.

12800.s: This order requires most federal contractors to post a notice telling employees about their rights related to union membership, union dues, and fees. It says employees cannot be required to join a union to keep their jobs, and that nonmembers may object to some uses of their payments and may be entitled to a refund in some cases. The Secretary of Labor is responsible for enforcing the order, investigating complaints, and taking action against contractors that do not comply.

12798.s: This order waives the application of sections 402(a) and 402(b) of the Trade Act of 1974 with respect to Armenia. It affects Armenia under the Trade Act.

12797.s: This order sets up a review process for proposed increases in basic pay for certain employees of the Department of Veterans Affairs and some other agencies. It gives the Director of the Office of Personnel Management the power to approve or disapprove those pay increases and to explain any disapproval to Congress. The order says the increases must be in the best interest of the Federal Government and may be used to match pay in the private sector, fill staffing needs, or recruit people with specialized skills.

12796.s: This order creates a five-member emergency board to investigate disputes between the National Railroad Passenger Corporation and certain employee labor organizations. The board must report to the President by May 3, 1992. While the board is active and for 30 days after its final report, the railroads and employees may not change the conditions that led to the disputes unless they agree to do so.

12795.s: This order creates a five-member board to investigate a dispute between the Consolidated Rail Corporation and its employees represented by the Brotherhood of Maintenance of Way Employes. The board is to report to the President, and the railroads and employees must keep the current conditions in place unless both sides agree to a change.

12794.s: This order creates a three-member emergency board to investigate disputes between certain railroads and employees represented by the International Association of Machinists and Aerospace Workers. The board is to report to the President, and the railroads and employees may not change the conditions tied to the disputes except by agreement during the board period and for 30 days after the final report.

12792.s: This order creates the National Commission on America's Urban Families, with up to eight members appointed by the President. The commission is to examine the condition of urban families, review government policies and programs, study ways to improve services and private efforts, and make recommendations to strengthen families living in urban areas. It must report to the President and then ends 30 days later.

12793.s: This order continues the Presidential Service Certificate and the Presidential Service Badge. The certificate may be awarded to certain members of the Army, Navy, Marine Corps, Air Force, and Coast Guard who served in White House-related assignments or other direct support positions in the Executive Office of the President for at least one year after January 21, 1989. The badge may be awarded to members of the Armed Forces who receive the certificate, and both may be granted after death. Only one certificate may be awarded to a person.

12791.s: This order extends the time period for peaceful nuclear cooperation with the European Atomic Energy Community until March 10, 1993. It says this is being done after a finding that ending that cooperation would be seriously harmful to U.S. non-proliferation goals and would threaten U.S. defense and security.

12790.s: This order amends a prior order on the Southwest Asia Service Medal. It changes one reference from "Armed Forces" to "Uniformed Services." It also directs several department heads to set uniform rules for awarding and wearing the medal for the military departments, the Coast Guard when it is not operating in the Navy, the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration, and the Public Health Service.

12789.s: This executive order delegates certain reporting functions under the Immigration Reform and Control Act of 1986. It gives the Attorney General and the Secretary of Labor different duties that were vested in the President under sections 401 through 404 of the law. The order says these functions must be carried out under OMB Circular A-19 and takes effect immediately.

12788.s: This order directs the Secretary of Defense to create a Defense Economic Adjustment Program. The program is meant to help communities affected by major Defense base closures, realignments, Defense contract changes, and civilian encroachment on military installations. It also sets up an Economic Adjustment Committee and tells executive agencies to help coordinate federal support for affected states, regions, municipalities, and communities.

12787.s: This order sets the line of succession for who will act as Secretary of Defense if the office is vacant because of death, permanent disability, or resignation. It also says these officials may act during a temporary absence or disability, but only on an interim basis and without changing their own appointments. The order also revokes Executive Order 12514.

12786.s: This order sets new pay and salary rates for several federal pay systems, including the General Schedule, Foreign Service, Veterans Health Administration, Senior Executive Service, executive salaries, justices and judges, and members of the uniformed services. It also sets interim geographic adjustments for covered employees and United States Park Police in listed areas. Some agencies are directed to issue regulations on how those adjustments apply.

12784.s: This order delegates to the Secretary of Energy the President’s functions under two sections of the U.S. Code about the naval petroleum and oil shale reserves. It also requires the Secretary of Energy to prepare and send the President a full report on the agreements and programs carried out under this order. The delegated authority expires on October 2, 1994.

12785.s: This order extends the President's Education Policy Advisory Committee. It changes the end date in an earlier executive order from December 31, 1991, to December 31, 1992.

12783.s: This order changes the end date for the President's Council on Rural America. It amends the earlier order so the council will terminate on January 16, 1993.

12782.s: This order changes the rules for awards that recognize outstanding voluntary contributions by individuals and organizations. It says the President will decide the award names, design, presentation, categories, and who may receive them, with help from the White House Office of National Service and the ACTION agency.

12781.s: This order delegates certain presidential functions to the Secretary of the Treasury, the Attorney General, and the Secretary of Defense. It lets the Secretary of Defense set a uniform military ration for the Army, Navy, and Air Force and sets rules for its components, value, and review. It also changes the name of the "Nezperce National Forest" to the "Nez Perce National Forest."

12780.s: This order directs federal agencies to start or expand programs to reduce waste and recycle reusable materials in their operations and facilities. It also requires agencies to use waste reduction and recycling opportunities as much as practicable and to use certain solid-waste fuel capabilities when they have them. The order sets up recycling coordinators and a council to guide agency programs, track reports, and review federal procurement of products made with recovered materials.

12779.s: This order blocks property and property interests of the Government of Haiti and related entities that are in the United States or under the control of United States persons. It also prohibits direct or indirect payments or transfers to the de facto regime in Haiti, with certain transfers to be placed in an account at the Federal Reserve Bank of New York. The order bars imports of most goods of Haitian origin and services performed in Haiti, and it bars exports from the United States to Haiti of most goods, technology, and services, with some listed exceptions. It applies to United States persons and to property and transactions tied to the Government of Haiti and the de facto regime in Haiti.

12778.s: This order directs federal agencies and their lawyers to handle civil cases against the United States more quickly and efficiently. It tells them to try settlement first, limit unnecessary discovery, use reliable expert testimony, and seek sanctions for abusive practices when appropriate. It also tells agencies to review proposed laws and regulations to reduce ambiguity, limit needless litigation, and make legal standards clearer for affected conduct.

12776.s: This order allows the National Defense Service Medal to be awarded to members of the Reserve Components of the Armed Forces of the United States. It applies to people who were in good standing during a period the Secretary of Defense designated as the Persian Gulf crisis for this order. It also allows the medal to be awarded after death to a reserve member who meets the requirements.

12777.s: This order assigns federal agencies responsibility for carrying out parts of the laws on oil pollution and hazardous substance spills. It sets up and directs the National Contingency Plan, National Response Team, and Regional Response Teams for planning and response, and it divides duties between the Environmental Protection Agency, the Coast Guard, the Department of the Interior, the Department of Transportation, and other agencies. It also covers removal of discharges, response plans, liability limits, and financial responsibility rules for vessels, onshore facilities, offshore facilities, and deepwater ports.

12774.s: This order continues ten federal advisory committees until September 30, 1993. It also says the department or agency head for each committee will carry out the President’s duties under the Federal Advisory Committee Act, except for annual reporting to Congress. The order revokes three earlier executive orders or sections that created committees whose work was completed or that were terminated, and it supersedes Executive Order 12692.

12773.s: This order changes Executive Order 10480 to move certain responsibilities under the Defense Production Act from the General Services Administration to the Secretary of Defense and the Department of Defense. It replaces references to the Administrator of General Services and the General Services Administration with the Secretary of Defense and the Department of Defense.

12771.s: This order revokes two earlier orders that blocked Kuwaiti government property and prohibited some transactions with Kuwait. It says the change is because Iraq's occupation forces were expelled, Kuwait was restored to its citizens, and its lawful government was reinstated. The revocation does not end the national emergency tied to the Government of Iraq.

12772.s: This order waives the application of sections 402(a) and 402(b) of the Trade Act of 1974 with respect to Romania. It affects Romania and changes how those parts of the law apply to it.

12770.s: This order directs federal executive departments and agencies to use the metric system in their procurements, grants, and other business-related activities when it is economically feasible. It also asks agencies to improve public understanding of metric units, make metric transition plans, and name a senior official to help carry out the transition. The Secretary of Commerce is assigned to coordinate these efforts and report progress to the President.

12769.s: This order says the Government of South Africa has taken the steps needed under section 311(a) of the Comprehensive Anti-Apartheid Act, so title III and sections 501(c) and 504(b) have ended. It directs affected executive departments and agencies to take the steps needed to carry out the end of those sanctions. It also keeps most of Executive Order 12571 in effect and revokes two earlier executive orders.

12768.s: This order extends the President's Council of Advisors on Science and Technology. It changes the council's end date from June 30, 1991, to June 30, 1993.

12767.s: This order amends the Manual for Courts-Martial rules for military trials. It changes rules on witnesses, pretrial agreements, speedy trial limits, appeals, post-trial rights, and the handling of polygraph evidence. It also requires notice to accused servicemembers about their post-trial and appellate rights.

12765.s: This order gives the Secretary of Defense authority to make certain defense-related decisions without further action by the President. It lets the Secretary assign command among commissioned officers of the same grade, direct where certain combatant and escort vessels are built, and approve exceptions for some vessel construction or repair rules when national security requires it. The Secretary may also pass this authority on to others, if allowed by law.

12766.s: This order designates the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development as a public international organization with privileges, exemptions, and immunities under the International Organizations Immunities Act. It also amends earlier executive orders to add that bank and to replace the European Space Research Organization with the European Space Agency. The order says the change for the European Space Agency does not limit any privileges, exemptions, or immunities it may already have or later acquire.

12763.s: This order gives the Secretary of Transportation the President’s duties under the Federal Advisory Committee Act for the Advisory Commission on Conferences in Ocean Shipping. It does not include the duty to receive the Commission’s report.

12764.s: This order establishes a Federal Salary Council as an advisory committee on locality-based comparability payments for General Schedule employees. The Council has nine members appointed by the President, with one member serving as chairman and another as vice chairman. It meets with the President’s Pay Agent to give views and recommendations on pay localities, survey coverage, pay comparisons, and comparability payments.

12762.s: This order changes the rules in Executive Order 11157 for the basic allowance for quarters. It replaces references to "seven consecutive days" and "7-day" with "thirty consecutive days" and "30-day."

12761.s: This order establishes a White House awards program for environmental and conservation achievements. It is for U.S. residents and organizations, groups, or entities doing business in the United States, and it covers achievements in the United States or its territories. The program will recognize work in environmental management, partnerships, innovation, and education and communication, and it will be run by the Council on Environmental Quality.

12760.s: This order abolishes the President's Commission on Executive Exchange. It also revokes Executive Order No. 12493 and directs the Director of the Office of Personnel Management to end the Commission's functions by September 30, 1991.

12758.s: This order adds the Director of the National Institutes of Health to Level IV of the Executive Schedule. It changes the pay level for that federal position.

12759.s: This order tells federal agencies to make their buildings, facilities, and vehicles more energy efficient. It directs agencies to cut energy use in federal buildings, improve energy efficiency in other facilities, reduce petroleum use where possible, and buy energy-efficient goods and products. It also requires agencies to make plans for fuel-efficient vehicles, use alternative fuel vehicles when practicable, and report their progress each year.

12756.s: This order keeps the President's Drug Advisory Council in place until November 13, 1993. It also changes the council's membership limit from 30 to 35. This affects the council created by Executive Order 12696.

12757.s: This order delegates several functions under the Agricultural Trade Development and Assistance Act to the Secretary of the Treasury and the Secretary of State. It expands the membership of the National Advisory Council for these matters and sets rules for the Environment for the Americas Board. It also says no new agreement or credit agreement may be made with a country that is in default on certain obligations unless the country meets its obligations or the President authorizes it.

12755.s: This order keeps the Export Administration Review Board in place and lists its members. It says the Board will include the Secretary of Commerce, the Secretary of State, the Secretary of Defense, the Secretary of Energy, and the Director of the United States Arms Control and Disarmament Agency, with some others as non-voting members. It also adds concern about the nonproliferation of armaments to the matters the Board considers when reviewing export controls.

12754.s: This order establishes the Southwest Asia Service Medal. It may be awarded to members of the Armed Forces who took part in military operations in Southwest Asia, nearby waters, or air space on or after August 2, 1990, until a date set by the Secretary of Defense. It may also be awarded after death. The military departments and the Secretary of Transportation for the Coast Guard are directed to set uniform rules for awarding and wearing the medal.

12753.s: This order extends the period for peaceful nuclear cooperation with the European Atomic Energy Community until March 10, 1992. It says Congress was notified of the determination, and it supersedes Executive Order 12706 on the effective date.

12752.s: This order sets up programs to sell agricultural commodities to developing countries and to donate agricultural commodities to foreign countries and to least developed countries. It assigns those programs and related duties to the Secretary of Agriculture, the Agency for International Development, the Secretary of State, and other officials. It also creates a Food Assistance Policy Council to coordinate policy and makes several presidential functions under the two acts go to specific officials. The order revokes two earlier executive orders.

12751.s: This order says that if the Department of Veterans Affairs is asked by the Department of Defense to help provide care and services to members of the U.S. Armed Forces on active duty in Operation Desert Storm, the Secretary of Veterans Affairs may make contracts with private facilities. Those contracts would be for hospital care and medical services for veterans, to the fullest extent allowed by the cited law.

12750.s: This order designates certain areas in and around the Arabian Peninsula, including airspace above them, as the "Persian Gulf Desert Shield area" for purposes of section 7508 of the Internal Revenue Code. The areas include the Persian Gulf, the Red Sea, the Gulf of Oman, part of the Arabian Sea, the Gulf of Aden, and the land area of Iraq, Kuwait, Saudi Arabia, Oman, Bahrain, Qatar, and the United Arab Emirates. Individuals who performed Desert Shield services in those areas, and their spouses, are entitled to the benefits of that tax section.

12749.s: This order adds two Department of Justice positions to Level IV of the Executive Schedule. The positions are the Director of the Office for Victims of Crime and the Director of the Bureau of Justice Assistance.

12747.s: This order creates the National Nutrition Monitoring Advisory Council. The Council gives scientific and technical advice on the nutrition monitoring program and comprehensive plan, and it advises the Secretaries of Agriculture and Health and Human Services. It includes 9 voting members, with appointments made by the President and Congress, and it also includes nonvoting joint chairpersons of the Interagency Board. Members serve without compensation, and the Council is set to end 10 years after the final comprehensive plan is prepared.

12748.s: This order sets rules for federal pay adjustments and gives agencies roles in carrying them out. It also lets the Office of Personnel Management handle certain pay actions, cash awards, bonuses, retention allowances, staffing differentials, and advance payments to new appointees. The order revokes two earlier orders and ends the Executive Assignment System.

12746.s: This order waives the application of subsections (a) and (b) of section 402 of the Trade Act of 1974 with respect to Mongolia. It applies to Mongolia after the required report to Congress is made.

12745.s: This order waives the application of subsections (a) and (b) of section 402 of the Trade Act of 1974 with respect to Bulgaria. It affects Bulgaria and changes how those trade rules apply to it.

12744.s: This order designates certain areas in and around the Arabian Peninsula as a combat zone for purposes of section 112 of the Internal Revenue Code. It covers the Persian Gulf, the Red Sea, the Gulf of Oman, part of the Arabian Sea, the Gulf of Aden, and the land areas of Iraq, Kuwait, Saudi Arabia, Oman, Bahrain, Qatar, and the United Arab Emirates. It also says the combatant activities in the zone began on January 17, 1991.

12743.s: This order lets the Department of Defense and the Department of Transportation order Ready Reserve units and some individual reservists to active duty, other than for training, for up to 24 consecutive months. It also lets the President suspend certain rules about officer strength, officer distribution, promotion, involuntary retirement, and separation in the Army, Navy, Air Force, and Marine Corps. The Secretary of Defense is allowed to use these authorities and pass them down to certain civilian subordinates.

12742.s: This order says the United States must be able to quickly mobilize resources for national security. It lets the government place orders and require priority performance for articles, products, and materials needed for national security. It delegates that authority to the Secretaries of Agriculture, Energy, Transportation, and Commerce for food, energy, civil transportation, and other articles and materials, but only after certain national security determinations are made. It also requires agencies to update their rules and gives the order no private right to be enforced in court.

12741.s: This order extends the President's Education Policy Advisory Committee by changing its end date. It affects the committee by replacing December 31, 1990, with December 31, 1991.

12739.s: This order closed all Federal executive departments and agencies for the last half of the workday on Christmas Eve, December 24, 1990, and excused employees from duty. Agency heads could keep some offices open and require some employees to work for national security, defense, or other essential public reasons. It applies only to Federal departments and agencies, not State or local governments.

12740.s: This order waives the application of subsections (a) and (b) of section 402 of the Trade Act of 1974 with respect to the Soviet Union. It says the President made the report to Congress required by the Act before issuing the waiver.

12737.s: This order creates the President's Commission on Environmental Quality as an advisory committee. The Commission has up to 25 members, including the Chairman of the Council on Environmental Quality, and the other members come from the private sector with experience in environmental and natural resources matters. The Commission advises the President on environmental quality, and executive agencies must provide information it needs when allowed by law.

12738.s: This order changes how certain foreign assistance and arms export control functions are delegated under earlier executive orders. It assigns some duties to the Secretary of State, the Secretary of Defense, and the Administrator of the Agency for International Development, and says some of those duties must be carried out in consultation with other officials. It also updates references to several sections of foreign aid, development, and narcotics control laws.

12735.s: This order declares a national emergency over the spread of chemical and biological weapons. It directs the United States to work with other countries to control these weapons and to seek a global convention to prohibit the production and stockpiling of chemical weapons. It also directs controls on exports, sanctions on foreign persons and foreign countries linked to these weapons, and restrictions on certain imports and air carrier rights.

12736.s: This order sets new pay rates and salaries for several federal pay systems, including the General Schedule, the Foreign Service Schedule, certain Veterans Affairs schedules, the Senior Executive Service, the Executive Schedule, the Vice President and Congress, and federal judges. It also sets pay and allowances for members of the uniformed services. Some employees in covered pay systems who work in listed geographic areas are entitled to an interim geographic adjustment, and agencies must issue regulations for how those adjustments apply.

12734.s: This order invokes emergency construction authority and makes it available to the Secretary of Defense. The Secretary of Defense may also make it available to the Secretaries of the military departments. It is meant to provide additional authority to respond to the national emergency tied to Iraq’s invasion of Kuwait.

12733.s: This order authorizes extending the period of active duty for units of the Selected Reserve and for Selected Reserve members not assigned to a unit. It gives the Secretary of Defense, and the Secretary of Transportation for the Coast Guard when it is not part of the Navy, authority to make those extensions. The order says it is for internal management of the executive branch and does not create any legal right or benefit.

12732.s: This order designates the International Fund for Agricultural Development as a public international organization under the International Organizations Immunities Act. It gives the organization the privileges, exemptions, and immunities allowed by that law, without reducing any it already has under other agreements or Acts of Congress.

12731.s: This order sets ethical rules for executive branch employees. It says they must avoid conflicts of interest, not use public office for private gain, protect government property, report waste or fraud, and follow laws and regulations on equal opportunity. It also limits outside earned income for certain presidential appointees, gives the Office of Government Ethics power to issue standards and disclosure rules, and revokes two earlier executive orders.

12730.s: This order keeps export control rules in place after the Export Administration Act of 1979 expired. It continues rules and actions on U.S. exports, including regulations issued by the Secretary of Commerce, until they are changed or revoked. It also keeps rules related to section 38(e) of the Arms Export Control Act in effect until changed or revoked.

12729.s: This order creates a President’s Advisory Commission and a White House Initiative in the Department of Education for educational excellence for Hispanic Americans. The commission advises the Secretary of Education on the progress of Hispanic Americans toward national education goals and on ways to improve education. It also focuses on parental involvement, early childhood education, removing barriers to success in education and work, and helping students reach their potential. Federal departments and agencies are directed to help advance educational opportunities for Hispanic Americans and to share data and report progress.

12728.s: This order gives the Secretary of Defense, and the Secretary of Transportation for the Coast Guard when it is not part of the Navy, the President's power to suspend laws about the promotion, retirement, or separation of members of the armed forces. They may use this power for members determined to be essential to the national security of the United States. The order also allows this authority to be passed on to certain subordinates.

12726.s: This order waives the application of sections 402(a) and 402(b) of the Trade Act of 1974 with respect to the German Democratic Republic. It applies to the German Democratic Republic and follows a report made to Congress under the Act.

12727.s: This order authorizes the Secretary of Defense, and the Secretary of Transportation for the Coast Guard in some cases, to order units and individual members of the Selected Reserve to active duty. It says this is needed to augment the active armed forces for operational missions in and around the Arabian Peninsula. It also says the order is meant to improve internal management of the executive branch.

12725.s: This order blocks property and interests in property of the Government of Kuwait that are in the United States or under the control of United States persons. It also prohibits many transactions involving Kuwait, including imports from Kuwait, exports to Kuwait, travel and transportation related to Kuwait, and contracts or transfers of funds for projects in Kuwait. Some exceptions are allowed for certain humanitarian donations and for official government, United Nations, or journalistic travel.

12724.s: This order blocks property and interests in property of the Government of Iraq that are in the United States or under the control of United States persons. It also prohibits imports of goods or services of Iraqi origin, exports to Iraq, certain dealings involving Iraqi property, travel-related transactions with Iraq, transportation transactions, contracts that support projects in Iraq, and transfers of funds or other resources to the Government of Iraq or people in Iraq. The order allows limited exceptions for some humanitarian donations, official government or United Nations travel, and certain journalistic travel.

12723.s: The order blocks all property and interests in property of the Government of Kuwait, its agencies, controlled entities, and the Central Bank of Kuwait that are in the United States or under the control of United States persons. It also covers property that later comes into the United States or comes into the possession or control of United States persons, including their overseas branches. The Secretary of the Treasury is authorized to use powers under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act to carry out the order.

12721.s: This order lets certain U.S. citizens who are family members of federal civilian employees, nonappropriated fund employees, or uniformed service members be appointed noncompetitively to some competitive civil service jobs in the executive branch after overseas service. It applies to jobs within the United States, including Guam, Puerto Rico, and the Virgin Islands. The Office of Personnel Management must issue rules to carry it out, and agencies may waive a written test in some cases.

12720.s: This order creates the President's Council on Rural America, an advisory council of up to 20 members appointed by the President. The council advises the President and the Economic Policy Council on how the federal government can improve rural economic development policy. It also reviews that policy and may receive information and support from executive agencies and the Farmers Home Administration.

12718.s: This order establishes the President’s Advisory Commission on the Public Service. The commission has 13 members from private life and is meant to give advice on ways to improve public service in American life. It is directed to consider the federal civil service, student interest in public service careers, and the image of public service, and it must report each year to the President and the Director of the Office of Personnel Management.

12719.s: This order creates a commission to study how to simplify the Presidential appointment process. The commission will look at reducing the number and complexity of forms filled out by presidential nominees and at making the executive branch and Senate forms work better together. It will also look for ways to simplify the SF-278 Executive Disclosure Report and its instructions. The commission must report to the President within 90 days after its first meeting, and it will end after that report is submitted.

12717.s: This order revokes Executive Order No. 12691, which had created the President's Advisory Committee on the Points of Light Initiative Foundation. It affects that committee because it says the committee has completed its tasks.

12716.s: This order gives the National Commission on Superconductivity more time to finish its report. It changes the date the commission must end to August 7, 1990.

12715.s: This order says cooperation and assistance for scouting activities overseas is necessary for the morale, welfare, and recreation of members of the armed forces. It directs the Secretary of Defense, or a designee, to issue rules for that cooperation and support.

12714.s: This order creates a three-member emergency board to investigate disputes between certain railroads and their employees represented by certain labor organizations. The board must report to the President on the disputes. While the board is working and for 30 days after it reports, the railroads and employees may not change the conditions that led to the disputes unless both sides agree.

12713.s: This order gives the Secretary of Commerce the authority to submit the annual report required by section 502 of the Automotive Products Trade Act of 1965 to Congress. It affects the Secretary of Commerce and the reporting process to Congress.

12712.s: This order amends a previous order to add the Secretary of Energy to the National Space Council. It also renumbers the later sections of that order.

12711.s: This order directs federal agencies to defer the enforced departure of certain nationals of the People’s Republic of China and their dependents who were in the United States on or after June 5, 1989, through January 1, 1994. It also waives the valid passport requirement for that period and tells the agencies to provide documents to help with travel and return to the United States. The order gives these people certain immigration protections, including work authorization, help keeping lawful status, and notice before deportation proceedings. It also directs enhanced consideration for people from any country who fear persecution tied to forced abortion or coerced sterilization.

12710.s: This order revokes a previous executive order and ends the national emergency with respect to Panama. It says the emergency had been tied to the policies and actions of Manuel Antonio Noriega and to the need to deal with that threat. It also says some pending actions and past rights or duties are not affected, and it keeps certain limits on transactions involving property in which the Government of Panama has an interest.

12709.s: This order raises the membership of the President's Council on Physical Fitness and Sports from 18 members to 20 members. It changes a prior executive order by replacing the word "eighteen" with "twenty."

12707.s: This order ends the national emergency with respect to Nicaragua. It revokes Executive Order 12513 and says the earlier emergency is no longer needed. It also says pending cases, past acts, and any rights or duties already earned are not affected.

12708.s: This order changes the Manual for Courts-Martial, which governs military justice cases. It updates rules on who is covered by certain military justice provisions, when defenses and objections must be raised, and how records, recommendations, and review actions are handled. It also changes some rules on military evidence, offenses, and nonjudicial punishment for servicemembers.

12706.s: This order extends the time period for peaceful nuclear cooperation with the European Atomic Energy Community until March 10, 1991. It says that stopping this cooperation would be seriously harmful to U.S. non-proliferation goals and could jeopardize the common defense and security of the United States. It also says Executive Order 12670 is replaced on the effective date of this order.

12703.s: This order assigns duties under the Support for East European Democracy Act to several federal officials. It gives the SEED Program Coordinator duties for reports to Congress, gives the USAID Administrator duties for Enterprise Funds for Poland and Hungary, and gives the Commerce and Treasury Secretaries duties on a SEED Information Center System and debt reduction for certain East European countries.

12704.s: This order changes several earlier executive orders. It renames the Interagency Committee on Handicapped Employees as the Interagency Committee on Employment of People with Disabilities and updates one committee membership title. It also changes how the President's Committee on the Arts and the Humanities may pay its administrative costs, and it revokes the section that continued the Advisory Committee on Small and Minority Business Ownership.

12701.s: This order changes Executive Order 12334 by deleting one sentence in section 1 and replacing it with new wording. The new sentence says that one member shall be designated by the President as Chairman.

12702.s: This order waives the application of subsections (a) and (b) of section 402 of the Trade Act of 1974 with respect to Czechoslovakia. It says the required report to Congress was made before the waiver was issued.

12700.s: This order creates the President's Council of Advisors on Science and Technology. The council advises the President on science and technology matters and reviews developments in those fields. It has up to 15 members, including the Director of the Office of Science and Technology Policy and 14 private sector members appointed by the President. Executive agencies must provide information to help the council do its work, and the council is set to end on June 30, 1991 unless extended.

12699.s: This order directs federal agencies to use seismic design and construction standards for new Federal buildings and for new buildings leased for Federal use. It also covers some federally assisted and federally regulated new construction, including grants, loans, loan insurance, and building safety rules. The order aims to reduce earthquake risks to building occupants and others affected by building failures.

12697.s: This order gives the National Commission on Superconductivity more time to finish its report. It changes one deadline to March 31, 1990, and says the commission must disband no later than May 31, 1990.

12698.s: This order sets new rates of basic pay and salaries for several federal pay systems, including the General Schedule, Foreign Service, Veterans Health Services and Research Administration, Senior Executive Service, executive branch offices, Congress, judges, and justices. It also sets pay and allowances for members of the uniformed services. The new rates take effect on the dates listed in the order, and it supersedes Executive Order 12663.

12696.s: This order sets up the President's Drug Advisory Council in the federal government. The council is made up of no more than 30 private citizens appointed by the President, and one member is chosen as chairman. It advises the President and the Director of National Drug Control Policy on how to explain and carry out national drug control policy, including outreach to the public and the private sector.

12694.s: This order changes an earlier executive order about the President's Council on Physical Fitness and Sports. It lets the President choose one or more members to serve as Chairmen and one or more members to serve as Vice Chairmen. The change applies to members of that council and takes effect immediately.

12695.s: This order gives the Administrator of the Agency for International Development authority to carry out certain debt relief powers under section 572 of the Foreign Operations, Export Financing, and Related Programs Appropriations Act, 1989. The administrator must act within IDCA and with the concurrence of the Development Coordination Committee. It changes how presidential authority under that section is carried out and takes effect immediately.

12693.s: This order excludes the Defense Mapping Agency Reston Center and all elements under the operational control of the Joint Special Operations Command from the Federal Labor-Management Relations Program. It says these organizations have a primary function in intelligence, counterintelligence, investigative, or national security work. It also amends a prior executive order to reflect this change.

12692.s: This order keeps several federal advisory committees in place until September 30, 1991. It also says the head of the named department or agency will carry out most duties under the Federal Advisory Committee Act for those committees, except for reporting to Congress. The order revokes several other executive orders that had created committees whose work was finished or ended, and it supersedes Executive Order 12610.

12691.s: This order creates the President's Advisory Committee on the Points of Light Initiative Foundation. The committee may have up to five members, who are appointed by the President, and it will advise the President on the foundation's legal structure and the legislation needed to establish it. It also directs executive offices to give the committee information and support, and the committee's term ends on June 30, 1991 unless extended sooner.

12689.s: This order says that when a person or group is debarred, suspended, or otherwise excluded from a procurement or nonprocurement activity, that exclusion can apply across the federal government. No agency may let that party take part in any procurement or nonprocurement activity, unless an exception is allowed under the rules. The Office of Management and Budget may help federal agencies resolve differences in the rules, and agencies must publish proposed and final regulations on that schedule.

12690.s: This order directs the Armed Forces to help suppress violence and restore law and order in and around the Virgin Islands. It authorizes the Secretary of Defense to use needed forces and to call National Guard units or members into active duty for an indefinite period. The Secretary of Defense must coordinate law enforcement policies with the Attorney General and decide when federal forces and federalized National Guard units are withdrawn.
