The parties must submit final offers for settlement within 30 days after the board is created, and the board must then report the most reasonable offer to the President within 30 days after that. From the time the board is requested until 60 days after its report, the parties may not change the conditions tied to the dispute unless they agree to do so.

12491.s: This order establishes a three-member board to investigate a dispute between the Long Island Rail Road and the Brotherhood of Locomotive Engineers. The parties must submit final settlement offers to the board within 30 days after it is created. The board must then send the President a report choosing the most reasonable offer, and the parties may not change the conditions tied to the dispute except by agreement during the stated period.

12490.s: This order establishes the National Commission on Space. The commission is to study existing and proposed United States space activities and help form an agenda for civilian space programs. It is also to identify long-range goals, opportunities, and policy options, then submit its plan and any proposed legislation to the President and Congress within 12 months. NASA is to provide administrative support, and the commission ends 60 days after it submits its report.

12488.s: This order amends a previous executive order to define one category of hazardous duty for incentive pay. It covers certain military members whose primary duties involve servicing, handling, testing, loading, transporting, or maintaining toxic fuels or propellants used in aircraft and missile systems. The pay is based on the risk of accidental or inadvertent exposure, not on actual measured exposure.

12489.s: This order keeps several federal advisory committees in place past their earlier end dates. Most of the listed committees are continued until September 30, 1985, and the International Private Enterprise Task Force is continued until December 31, 1984. It also says the heads of the listed departments or agencies will carry out the President’s functions under the Federal Advisory Committee Act for these committees, except for the annual report to Congress.

12486.s: This order creates a three-member emergency board to investigate a dispute between Port Authority Trans-Hudson Corporation and the Brotherhood of Railroad Signalmen. The board must report its findings to the President within 30 days after it is created. From the day the board is created and for 120 days after, neither side may change the conditions that led to the dispute unless both agree.

12487.s: This order changes certain rates of pay by replacing Schedule 8 in a prior executive order with a new Schedule 8. The new pay rates take effect on the first day of the first applicable pay period beginning on or after January 1, 1984.

12485.s: This order changes one date in the Central Intelligence Agency Retirement Act. It updates the retirement system to match certain amendments to the Civil Service Retirement and Disability System.

12484.s: This order amends the Manual for Courts-Martial, United States, 1984. It makes many wording, punctuation, and formatting changes in the rules for courts-martial, military evidence rules, and the punitive articles and sample specifications. It also directs the Secretary of Defense to send a copy of the order to Congress.

12483.s: This order removes articles in TSUS item 706.39 from the list of goods eligible for benefits under the Generalized System of Preferences. It also deletes that item from the related preference lists and removes the listing for Hong Kong, the Republic of Korea, and Taiwan in general headnote 3(c)(iii). The changes apply to covered articles imported on or after January 1, 1976, and entered or withdrawn from warehouse for consumption on or after June 25, 1984.

12482.s: This order extends the life of the President's Advisory Committee on Women's Business Ownership. It changes the committee's job from fostering something to studying methods of obtaining it. The committee is set to end on December 31, 1984, unless it is extended sooner.

12481.s: This order creates a three-member board to investigate a dispute between The Long Island Rail Road and the union that represents some of its employees. The board must report its findings to the President within 30 days after it is created. From the day the board is created, the carrier and the employees may not change the conditions that led to the dispute for 120 days unless both sides agree.

12480.s: This order creates a three-member emergency board to investigate a dispute between The Long Island Rail Road and the Brotherhood of Locomotive Engineers. The board must report its findings to the President within 30 days. From the day the board is created and for 120 days after, the carrier and the employees may not change the conditions that caused the dispute unless both sides agree.

12479.s: This order creates the President’s Council on Management Improvement as an interagency committee. The council is made up of federal officials from many departments and agencies, and it is meant to improve management and administrative systems across the federal government. It also works on long-range plans, agency reforms, interagency problems, and coordination with the Office of Management and Budget, the General Services Administration, and the Office of Personnel Management.

12477.s: This order changes certain rates of pay by replacing the schedules in a previous executive order with new schedules. The new pay rates take effect on the first applicable pay period beginning on or after January 1, 1984. It affects the rates of pay covered by those schedules.

12478.s: This order transfers to the Secretary of State the authority to decide when reimbursable extraordinary protective activities are needed for foreign diplomatic missions and to approve the terms and conditions for them. It also gives the Secretary of State the power to make reimbursements to state and local governments for services, personnel, equipment, and facilities, and transfers certain unused money from the Treasury for that purpose. The authority is to be used with State Department protective security programs for foreign missions.

12476.s: This order changes the name of the Advisory Group on United States-Japan Relations to the United State-Japan Advisory Commission. It says the commission may conduct studies, hearings, and meetings, gather and share information, and issue reports and other publications. It also says the commission will end on October 31, 1984, unless it is extended sooner.

12475.s: This order directs the Secretary of the Treasury to issue regulations for the entry or withdrawal of textiles and textile products under the United States Textile Import Program. The regulations may clarify country-of-origin rules, set rules for goods changed in a customs bonded warehouse, and require importers to provide more information or documents. It also creates a Textile and Apparel Task Force in Customs to coordinate enforcement, and tells the Treasury Department and CITA to share information on textile import issues.

12474.s: This order changes the annex to a previous order to reflect changes in the names or status of agencies covered by the Agreement on Government Procurement. It deletes the Community Services Administration, changes "National Tool Center" to "Tools Commodity Center," and adds the Peace Corps to the list.

12473.s: This order prescribes a new Manual for Courts-Martial, United States, 1984, for military court-martial and nonjudicial punishment proceedings. It takes effect on August 1, 1984, and applies to court-martial processes started on or after that date, with rules for some earlier cases staying under the old rules. It also rescinds the 1969 Manual for Courts-Martial effective August 1, 1984, and directs the Secretary of Defense to revise the manual each year and recommend changes to the President.

12472.s: This order creates the National Communications System to help plan and coordinate national security and emergency preparedness telecommunications for the federal government. It gives the Secretary of Defense the role of Executive Agent and assigns roles to the National Security Council, the Office of Science and Technology Policy, and the Office of Management and Budget. It also sets up a committee and a coordinating center to help with planning, priorities, standards, and restoring communications during crises or emergencies.

12471.s: This order changes the Generalized System of Preferences rules for certain goods from beneficiary developing countries. It updates the tariff schedule, revises lists of articles that can get GSP benefits, and makes technical changes to the list of beneficiary developing countries. It also sets staged duty reductions for some new tariff items and says when the changes take effect.

12469.s: This order gives the United States Trade Representative the reporting duties of the East-West Foreign Trade Board. It is meant to make reporting to Congress more efficient.

12470.s: This order keeps export control rules in force after the Export Administration Act of 1979 expired. It covers rules and actions about exports of U.S. goods, technology, and technical data, as well as certain boycott-related matters. It also keeps rules under the Arms Export Control Act section 38(e) in effect until changed or ended.

12467.s: This order designates the International Boundary and Water Commission, United States and Mexico, as a public international organization under the International Organizations Immunities Act. That means the Commission is entitled to the privileges, exemptions, and immunities given by that law. The designation does not apply to the United States Section of the Commission for matters under its exclusive control, supervision, or jurisdiction.

12466.s: This order changes a prior executive order about federal employee relocation expenses. It gives the President’s authority to set rules for reimbursing federal, state, and city income taxes tied to travel, transportation, and relocation expenses for employees moved at government expense. It also covers guidance for how agencies carry out their duties under a federal law on relocation expenses.

12465.s: This order makes the Department of Transportation the lead federal agency for encouraging and coordinating commercial expendable launch vehicle activities by private U.S. companies. It tells the department to help with licensing, keep other agencies working together, and serve as the main contact for launch-related applications and documents. It also directs other federal agencies to help by reviewing their rules and setting timetables for handling licenses and approvals.

12464.s: This order amends the rules for awarding the Purple Heart. It adds coverage for people wounded or killed after March 28, 1973, in an international terrorist attack against the United States or a friendly foreign nation, if the attack is recognized for this purpose by the proper secretary. It also adds coverage for people wounded or killed after March 28, 1973, during military operations outside the United States while serving as part of a peacekeeping force.

12468.s: This order creates the Presidential Advisory Council on the Peace Corps. The council is made up of up to 15 people appointed by the President, and the President chooses the chairman and vice chairman. It advises the President and the Director of the Peace Corps on actions needed to promote the Peace Corps Act and must submit an annual report on its review and recommendations. The council members do not receive pay for their work, and the council is set to end two years after the order unless extended sooner.

12462.s: This order creates the President's Advisory Committee on Mediation and Conciliation. The committee advises the President and the Director of the Federal Mediation and Conciliation Service on ways to improve arbitration and other dispute resolution methods under collective bargaining agreements. It also reviews certain Service regulations that affect arbitration and mediation procedures and reports its findings and recommendations. Members serve without pay, and the committee is set to end on December 31, 1984 unless extended sooner.

12463.s: This order extends the period for peaceful nuclear cooperation with the European Atomic Energy Community until March 10, 1985. It says ending that cooperation would be seriously harmful to U.S. non-proliferation goals and could jeopardize the common defense and security of the United States.

12461.s: This order designates the District of Columbia Police and Firefighters' Retirement and Disability System as a covered retirement system for certain Federal employees covered under the Act. It also names the Secretary of the Treasury as the agency head for that system, and says the Secretary should be guided by information and recommendations from the Mayor of the District of Columbia.

12460.s: This order amends the Manual for Courts-Martial to set new rules for capital cases under the Uniform Code of Military Justice. It says death may be adjudged only if the listed legal requirements are met, including notice to the defense, proof of aggravating circumstances, and consideration of evidence in extenuation and mitigation. It also adds rules for voting, instructions, and announcement in capital cases, and it says the amendments apply immediately to trials of capital offenses committed on or after that date.

12459.s: This order changes the Generalized System of Preferences rules for certain imported articles. It amends the tariff schedules, removes some listed items, and adds others for imports from designated beneficiary countries. It also changes which articles qualify for benefits from countries such as Taiwan, the Republic of Korea, and Hong Kong.

12458.s: This order delegates certain foreign assistance functions to the Secretary of State. It amends a prior executive order to add functions under specified foreign assistance laws and to change several exceptions, including functions related to El Salvador and Haiti.

12456.s: This order adjusts basic pay and salaries for several federal pay systems, including the General Schedule, Foreign Service, Veterans Administration medical and surgery schedules, and the Senior Executive Service. It also adjusts pay and allowances for members of the uniformed services, and pay for the Vice President, executive branch officials, members of Congress, and judges. The new pay rates take effect with the first applicable pay period beginning on or after January 1, 1984.

12457.s: This order changes the rules for the President's Commission on Industrial Competitiveness. It allows the President to appoint or designate members and extends the commission's term until December 31, 1984 unless it is extended sooner.

12455.s: This order extends the life of the President's Private Sector Survey on Cost Control in the Federal Government. It changes the date for when the committee will end to January 31, 1984, unless it is extended sooner.

12453.s: This order delegates certain presidential functions to the Secretary of State. Those functions are tied to periodic reports to Congress needed before United States funds can be paid in satisfaction of guarantees or assurances on loans and credits to the Polish People's Republic. Before making those determinations and reports, the Secretary of State must consult with the Secretary of the Treasury and, when needed, the Secretary of Agriculture and other interested agencies.

12454.s: This order keeps the President's National Security Telecommunications Advisory Committee in place until September 30, 1985. The committee was first established by Executive Order No. 12382.

12452.s: This order updates the list of communicable diseases covered by federal rules for apprehending, detaining, or conditionally releasing people to prevent the spread of disease. The listed diseases include cholera, diphtheria, infectious tuberculosis, plague, suspected smallpox, yellow fever, and suspected viral hemorrhagic fevers. It also revokes three earlier executive orders.

12451.s: This order revokes a prior order that had continued export control regulations under IEEPA and rescinds the declaration of economic emergency. It says the export control rules, regulations, orders, licenses, and other administrative actions that were already in effect will stay in force until changed or revoked by proper authority. It also keeps in effect certain actions relating to section 38(e) of the Arms Export Control Act.

12450.s: This order changes the membership list in an earlier executive order on the Interagency Committee on Handicapped Employees. It adds the Secretary of Health and Human Services as a new member and changes the title of the Secretary of Education to Co-Chairman.

12449.s: This order changes the National Bipartisan Commission on Central America so it must report to the President by February 1, 1984. It affects the commission and the President.

12448.s: This order gives the heads of executive departments and agencies the power to void or rescind contracts or other benefits obtained through bribery, graft, or conflict of interest after a final conviction under chapter 11 of title 18. It also allows those agencies to write rules to carry out that authority. The rules must include written notice, a chance to submit information, and, if requested, a hearing. They must also provide a final written decision on restitution or other remedy.

12447.s: This order extends the life of the President's Private Sector Survey on Cost Control in the Federal Government. It changes the committee's termination date to December 31, 1983, unless it is extended sooner.

12446.s: This order changes the Foreign Service Retirement and Disability System to make it more like the Civil Service Retirement and Disability System. It changes interest rates on contributions, refunds, and redeposits, changes how some annuities are rounded, and changes when some annuities begin. It also changes credit for military service, sets a rule for some annuities based on Social Security benefits, and limits cost-of-living increases for annuities. These changes affect Foreign Service participants, annuitants, and survivors.

12445.s: The order gives the Secretary of the Treasury authority to approve and certify containers and vehicles for international transport of goods under customs seal. The Secretary must follow the procedures and technical conditions in the listed conventions and may set fees for the services provided. The Secretary may also use the services of non-profit firms or associations, and older Transportation Department regulations stay in effect until Treasury replaces them.

12444.s: This order keeps export control rules in place after the Export Administration Act of 1979 expired. It continues rules and actions on exports of United States commercial goods, technology, and technical data, unless the Secretary of Commerce changes or revokes them. It also keeps in force rules for section 38(e) of the Arms Export Control Act and related orders and licenses. The order stays in effect until it is terminated, and it says it is intended to end if a new bill reauthorizing those powers becomes law.

12443.s: This order changes rules for the Central Intelligence Agency Retirement and Disability System. It updates when disability annuities stop, how annuities start and are rounded, and when contributions can be returned after separation. It also changes how military service, civilian service, and certain deposits are counted, and it lets the Director of Central Intelligence request information from other federal agencies to help run the system.

12442.s: This order changes the deadline for the Commission’s final report to the President and the Secretary of the Interior to November 30, 1984. It also says the Commission will end 30 days after it sends that final report, unless it is extended sooner.

12441.s: This order changes parts of the Generalized System of Preferences and makes technical corrections to the Tariff Schedules of the United States. It deletes one article description, changes the lists of articles that can get GSP benefits, and updates which countries are linked to certain items. The changes affect imported articles and the countries listed in the trade schedule.

12440.s: This order changes the President’s Commission on Industrial Competitiveness so it can have no more than thirty members. Those members are to be appointed or designated by the President.

12439.s: This order creates the President's Task Force on Food Assistance to study federal and other programs that provide food assistance to needy people. The task force is to make recommendations to the President and the Secretary of Agriculture on how those programs may be improved. Its members serve without pay, and the Department of Agriculture is to provide support as allowed by law.

12437.s: This order revokes Executive Order No. 12217. It relates to the conversion of certain Federal powerplants to alternative fuel sources under the Powerplant and Industrial Fuel Use Act of 1978.

12438.s: This order sets a review process for proposed increases in basic pay for certain employees of the Veterans' Administration. It gives the Director of the Office of Personnel Management the power to review and disapprove those increases and to send Congress a written reason for any disapproval. The Administrator of Veterans' Affairs must give the Director any information requested for this review.

12436.s: This order sets up payment of certain benefits to the surviving spouses and children of some people who died in or as a result of military service. It names the Administrator of Veterans' Affairs to run the program. The Secretary of Health and Human Services must give information and technical help, and the Secretary of Defense must transfer money to the Veterans' Administration account to pay the benefits and related expenses.

12435.s: This order establishes the President's Commission on Organized Crime as an advisory committee on organized crime. The Commission may have no more than twenty members, and the President designates its chairman. It is directed to study organized crime, review federal laws, advise the President and the Attorney General, and make recommendations for law enforcement and justice improvements. The Commission must submit its final report by March 1, 1986, unless it is extended, and it will terminate two years from the date of the order unless extended.

12433.s: This order creates the National Bipartisan Commission on Central America and limits it to no more than 12 members chosen or named by the President. The commission must study United States interests in Central America, the threats to those interests, and ways to address social, economic, and democratic development as well as security and stability in the region. It must advise the President, the Secretary of State, and Congress, and it must report by December 1, 1983.

12432.s: This order directs federal agencies with major procurement or grantmaking authority to create annual minority business development plans. The plans must set objectives and methods for encouraging prime contractors and grantees to use minority business enterprises. It also requires agencies to set up programs for direct assistance, procurement assistance, and management and technical assistance to minority business enterprises, and to encourage minority business participation in contracts tied to federal grants and cooperative agreements.

12431.s: This order adds the Administrator of the Office of Juvenile Justice and Delinquency Prevention in the Department of Justice to level IV of the Executive Schedule. It affects that one position by placing it in a higher pay and rank level under the schedule.

12430.s: This order revokes Executive Order 10936, which had required agencies to report identical bids. It removes that reporting requirement and says the goal is to use agency resources in a more effective way to prevent antitrust violations.

12429.s: This order extends the life of the President's Private Sector Survey on Cost Control in the Federal Government. It changes the committee's end date to October 30, 1983, unless it is extended sooner.

12428.s: This order creates the President's Commission on Industrial Competitiveness as an advisory committee. The commission is to review ways to increase the long-term competitiveness of United States industries, with special emphasis on high technology, and advise the President, the Cabinet Council on Commerce and Trade, and the Department of Commerce. It may have up to twenty-five members, and executive agencies and the Secretary of Commerce are to provide support and information as allowed by law.

12426.s:
This order creates the President's Advisory Committee on Women's Business Ownership. The committee can have up to 15 members, and they are appointed or designated by the President.

The committee reviews the status of businesses owned by women and gives advice to the President and the Small Business Administration. It also works to encourage private-sector financial, educational, and procurement support for women entrepreneurs.

12427.s: This order creates the President's Advisory Council on Private Sector Initiatives. The Council has up to 39 members from the public sector and private life, and it advises the President on private sector initiative policies, including public/private partnerships and private social service programs. The members serve without pay, though private citizens may get travel expenses, and the Council ends after two years unless extended.

12425.s: This order designates the International Criminal Police Organization, or INTERPOL, as a public international organization under the International Organizations Immunities Act. It gives INTERPOL the privileges, exemptions, and immunities covered by that law, except for certain customs duty and import tax provisions and several other sections listed in the order. It applies to INTERPOL and to the United States' participation in that organization.

12424.s: This order updates the President's Commission on Strategic Forces. The commission must review progress on recommendations about the Peacekeeper Missile, a small single-warhead intercontinental ballistic missile system, and strategic arms control, and give advice to the President and several federal agencies. It must report by request and no later than December 15, 1983, and it is set to end on January 3, 1984 unless extended.

12422.s: This order adds the Executive Secretary of the National Security Council to level IV of the Executive Schedule. It affects that position by placing it in a higher pay level within the executive branch.

12423.s: This order changes two earlier executive orders about foreign assistance and arms control. It updates one section to include a new subsection and changes another section to assign matters under sections 22(a), 29, and 30 of the Act to the Secretary of Defense.

12420.s: This order defines two added kinds of hazardous duty for incentive pay rules. One covers certain uniformed service members assigned to entomology, pest control, pest management, or preventive medicine work who do fumigation with highly toxic pesticides. The other covers members who do laboratory work with live dangerous viruses or bacteria while doing certain research assignments.

12421.s: This order creates the Presidential Commission on the Conduct of United States-Japan Relations, with up to eight members appointed or designated by the President from among U.S. citizens. The commission is to develop recommendations on United States-Japan relations, study issues and opportunities for cooperation, and submit its recommendations to the President and the Secretary of State before it ends one year after this date.

12419.s: This order directs the Secretary of the department in which the Coast Guard is operating to carry out the United States' obligations under the International Convention on Tonnage Measurement of Ships. It also allows that Secretary to authorize one or more U.S. corporations or associations to measure vessels and issue International Tonnage Certificates under the Convention.

12418.s: This order transfers certain functions about vessels’ financial responsibility for water pollution to the Secretary of the department in which the Coast Guard is operating. It also gives that Secretary authority over some rules for vessels, offshore facilities, penalties, and oil loaded from the Trans-Alaska pipeline. Federal agencies with duties under the National Contingency Plan are empowered to remove oil and hazardous substances after a discharge or when there is a substantial threat of one. Records, property, personnel, positions, and unused funds related to these functions are to be moved from the Federal Maritime Commission, and existing related actions stay in effect until changed.

12417.s: This order changes a prior executive order to delegate certain functions under the Strategic and Critical Materials Stock Piling Act to the Director of the Federal Emergency Management Agency. It is meant to provide for the performance of certain reporting functions.

12416.s: This order changes parts of an earlier executive order on intergovernmental review of Federal programs. It gives State, regional, and local governments more time to carry out new Federal regulations. It also adds a reference to Section 204 of the Demonstration Cities and Metropolitan Development Act of 1966 and changes two deadlines in the earlier order.

12414.s: This order sets up a three-member emergency board to investigate a dispute between The Long Island Rail Road and certain labor organizations representing its employees. The parties must give the board final offers for settling the dispute, and the board must then send a report to the President with its choice of the most reasonable offer. Until 60 days after the board’s report, the parties may not change the conditions that led to the dispute unless they agree to do so.

12415.s: This order extends the Presidential Commission on Drunk Driving until December 31, 1983. It is meant to continue efforts to assist the States in fighting drunk driving.

12412.s: This order creates the Peace Corps Advisory Council and lets the President appoint up to 30 members. The council advises the President and the Director of the Peace Corps on initiatives needed to promote the purposes of the Peace Corps Act, and it must send an annual report on its recommendations and activities. Members serve without pay, may receive travel expenses, and the council is set to end on December 31, 1983 unless extended.

12413.s: This order changes the Generalized System of Preferences rules for certain imported articles from beneficiary developing countries. It updates the tariff schedules, changes which articles are eligible for GSP treatment, and makes technical changes to the list of beneficiary developing countries. It also sets staged duty reductions for some new items and corrects a typographical error in a prior order.

12411.s: This order directs federal executive agencies to cut back on work space to what is needed for their missions and to keep inventories of space and furnishings. It also tells agencies to manage office space, furniture, and other items to use public money carefully, and to report vacant space for possible use by other federal agencies when allowed. The Administrator of General Services is given authority to set objectives, conduct surveys, and make rules for the planning and reporting systems.

12410.s: This order adds the Joint Special Operations Command (JSOC) to the list of agency subdivisions excluded from the Federal Labor-Management Relations Program. It affects JSOC by exempting it from that program.

12409.s: This order extends the time period for peaceful nuclear cooperation with the European Atomic Energy Community until March 10, 1984. It says that ending this cooperation would be seriously harmful to U.S. non-proliferation goals and would endanger the common defense and security of the United States. The Congress was notified of this decision.

12407.s: This order revokes Executive Order No. 12314, which had established the Federal Regional Councils. It ends that interagency and intergovernmental coordination mechanism.

12408.s: This order changes a prior executive order by adding a new section. It gives the Secretary of State the President’s functions under two sections of the Department of State Authorization Act for Fiscal Years 1982 and 1983.

12405.s: This order creates a three-member emergency board to investigate a dispute between the Consolidated Rail Corporation and the Brotherhood of Locomotive Engineers. The board must report its findings to the President within 30 days. During that time and for 30 days after the report, the carrier and the employees may not change the conditions that led to the dispute unless both sides agree.

12406.s: This order amends the rules for the President's Commission on Strategic Forces. It requires the commission to report to the President by April 15, 1983, and says the commission will end 60 days after it reports unless it is extended sooner.

12404.s: This order changes the rules for the Combined Federal Campaign, which lets voluntary health and welfare agencies ask for contributions from Federal employees and members of the uniformed services at their workplaces. It limits participation to agencies that provide direct health and welfare services to individuals or their families, and it excludes agencies that seek to influence elections or public policy through political activity, lobbying, or litigation for others. It also allows some international organizations that serve people overseas and some local voluntary agencies to take part if they meet the other criteria.

12403.s: This order designates the African Development Bank as a public international organization that can receive the privileges, exemptions, and immunities under the International Organizations Immunities Act. It also amends an earlier order to add the African Development Bank to certain sections. The order delegates some presidential functions under Public Law 97-35 to the Secretary of the Treasury.

12402.s: This order changes the deadline for the National Commission on Social Security Reform to give its report to the President. The commission must make its report by January 20, 1983.

12401.s: This order creates a Presidential Commission on Indian Reservation Economies. The commission is to advise the President on ways to strengthen the private sector on federally recognized Indian reservations, reduce tribal dependence on federal money and programs, and reduce the federal presence in Indian affairs. It is also to look at barriers to private investment on reservations and recommend changes to remove those barriers.

12397.s: This order changes the deadline for the National Commission on Social Security Reform to give its report to the President. The commission must now submit its report by January 15, 1983.

12399.s: This order continues several Federal advisory committees for set periods, including committees on the White House, science, fitness, mental retardation, exports, small and minority business ownership, occupational safety and health, labor, economic policy, productivity, the arts, and other topics. It also continues the President's National Security Telecommunications Advisory Committee for a shorter period. For those committees, the listed department or agency head does the President's duties under the Federal Advisory Committee Act, except annual reporting to Congress. The order revokes several earlier orders that created committees that had ended or finished their work, and it supersedes Executive Order 12258.

12396.s: This order gives the Secretary of Defense the President’s authority over several officer appointment, promotion, and retirement actions for the Armed Forces. It also lets the Secretary act during war or a national emergency to suspend some rules on officer strength, temporary appointments, promotion, involuntary retirement, or separation. The order allows some of this authority to be passed down to other defense and military officials, and it revokes parts of earlier executive orders.

12395.s: This order creates the International Private Enterprise Task Force as an advisory committee. Its members are appointed by the President from leaders in the private sector, and it advises the President and certain agency officials on the role private enterprise can play in foreign assistance programs and on specific private enterprises involved in those programs. The Agency for International Development provides support, and the task force is set to end on December 31, 1982 unless extended sooner.

12394.s: This order defines two kinds of hazardous duty for military incentive pay. It covers members who do frequent and regular flight deck work on aircraft carriers or other ships that launch aircraft, and members whose main duty is servicing aircraft or missiles with highly toxic fuels or propellants. It also says a member cannot get this pay in a month if they are eligible for other hazardous duty pay under the law.

12393.s: This order establishes an emergency board to investigate a dispute between the Long Island Rail Road and certain labor organizations that represent its employees. The board must report its findings to the President within 30 days. During the board’s work, the carrier and the employees may not change the conditions that led to the dispute except by agreement, and the board ends 90 days after the report is submitted.

12392.s: This order gives the Secretary of the Treasury the President’s authority under Section 129 of Public Law 97-276. That authority is for making payments to certain international financial institutions.

12391.s: This order suspends some federal labor-management rules for certain U.S. citizen Department of Defense employees working outside the United States, except in the Republic of Panama. The suspensions apply when a matter would affect the implementation of a treaty or agreement between the United States and the host nation. It also sends disputes about whether a matter is covered to the Secretary of Defense, whose decision is final after consulting the Secretary of State.

12390.s: This order gives the Secretary of State the President’s functions under Section 306 of the Supplemental Appropriations Act of 1982. Before making the required determination and written reports, the Secretary of State must consult with the Secretary of the Treasury and, as needed, the Secretary of Agriculture and other interested executive agencies. It also confirms and ratifies similar functions that were delegated under Section 205 of Public Law 97-216.

12388.s: This order updates several executive orders to replace “International Communication Agency” and “United States International Communication Agency” with “United States Information Agency.” It also says those references should be treated as referring to the United States Information Agency. The change is effective as of August 24, 1982.

12389.s: This order changes the tariff schedule used for the Generalized System of Preferences. It adds and removes certain articles from GSP eligibility and makes related changes to duty rates and item numbers. The changes affect imports from designated beneficiary developing countries and, for some items, imports linked to Taiwan and Romania.

12386.s: This order sets up a three-member emergency board to investigate a dispute between the New York Metropolitan Transportation Authority, the Connecticut Department of Transportation, and certain labor organizations. The dispute is about new collective bargaining agreements for employees of Consolidated Rail Corporation who are being transferred to the MTA and CDOT. The board must hold a public hearing, file an initial report, ask for final offers if there is no settlement, and then send the President its choice of the most reasonable offer.

12387.s: This order adjusts rates of basic pay and salaries for several federal pay systems, including the General Schedule, Foreign Service, Veterans Administration medical and surgery schedules, and the Senior Executive Service. It also adjusts pay and allowances for members of the uniformed services, including basic pay, subsistence, and quarters allowances. The order also adjusts salaries for the Vice President, congressional salaries, and judicial salaries. Most of the changes take effect on the first day of the first pay period beginning on or after October 1, 1982, and the uniformed services pay and allowance changes take effect on October 1, 1982.

12385.s: This order sets up a three-member emergency board to investigate a labor dispute between New Jersey Transit Rail Operations and certain railroad labor organizations. The dispute is about the terms and conditions of new collective bargaining agreements for employees being transferred from Consolidated Rail Corporation to New Jersey Transit Rail Operations. The board must hold a public hearing, report within 30 days, and if the dispute is still not settled, review final offers and send a final report to the President.

12384.s: This order creates a three-member emergency board to investigate a labor dispute between SEPTA, the Delaware Transportation Authority, and certain labor organizations. The dispute is about the terms and conditions of new collective bargaining agreements for employees moving from Conrail to SEPTA and DTA. The board must hold a public hearing, report within 30 days, and, if there is still no settlement, require final offers and choose the most reasonable one.

12383.s: This order amends the military courts manual to add new rules and punishments for offenses involving controlled substances. It covers wrongful use, possession, manufacture, introduction, and distribution of drugs such as amphetamine, cocaine, heroin, marijuana, and other controlled substances. It also increases the maximum punishment by 5 years when certain drug offenses are committed while on sentinel or lookout duty, on board a vessel or aircraft, in or at a missile launch facility, in a hostile fire pay zone, or during time of war.

12381.s: This order transfers certain emergency management functions from the President to the Director of the Federal Emergency Management Agency. It excludes some functions tied to declarations of emergencies and major disasters, Federal facilities, and food coupons and surplus commodities. It also changes one older order and revokes one section of it.

12382.s: This order creates the President’s National Security Telecommunications Advisory Committee. The committee can have up to 30 members with telecommunications knowledge, and the President appoints them and names a chairman and vice chairman each year. It gives advice and information to the President on national security telecommunications policy and ways to improve telecommunications-related national security. The committee also reports to the President and the Secretary of Defense and is set to end on December 31, 1982 unless extended.

12380.s: This order changes rules for submarine duty incentive pay for Navy enlisted members and officers. It gives continuous monthly pay to members in submarine service on a career basis, and it provides pay for members who perform frequent and regular operational submarine duty under orders. It also lets some Naval Reserve members get an increase in compensation for duty on a submarine during underway operations, if appropriations allow.

12379.s: This order revokes a series of executive orders that had created or continued different boards, councils, and committees. It also terminates the Veterans' Federal Coordinating Committee and the President's Council on Energy Efficiency. The affected groups include federal advisory bodies and several labor dispute boards involving railroads, airlines, and other employers and employees.

12378.s: This order increases the membership of the President's Committee on the Arts and the Humanities by one. It changes a previous order to add the Chairman of the Board of Trustees of the John F. Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts to the committee. It affects the committee's membership and the officials named in the amended section.

12377.s: This order changes the makeup of the Joint Mexican-United States Defense Commission. It adds a Marine Corps member to the United States side, joining the Army, Navy, and Air Force members. The Secretary of Defense will designate these members, choose the chairman, and may name alternate members.

12376.s: This order changes the Presidential Commission on Drunk Driving so it can have up to 28 members appointed by the President. It increases the commission’s membership by two.

12374.s: This order delegates certain presidential duties under the Foreign Assistance Act to the Secretary of State. It also requires the Director of the Office of Management and Budget to send the Secretary of State reports received from agencies. These reports are for Congress on United States contributions to international organizations.

12375.s: This order gives the Administrator of General Services the President’s role in carrying out certain fuel economy duties under the Motor Vehicle Information and Cost Savings Act. It directs the Administrator to make sure passenger automobiles bought by executive agencies meet a fleet average fuel economy standard. It also requires rules for nonpassenger automobiles, with exceptions for combat-related, law enforcement, and emergency rescue use, and says the Administrator must consult with the Secretaries of Transportation and Energy.

12373.s: This order establishes a three-member board to investigate a dispute between the United Transportation Union and certain railroads. The board must report its findings to the President within 30 days. While the board is in place, and for 30 days after it reports, the railroads and their employees may not change the conditions tied to the dispute unless they agree.

12372.s: This order tells federal agencies to give state and local elected officials a chance to review and comment on proposed federal financial assistance and direct federal development. It asks agencies to work through state review processes, share plans early, and try to address concerns when possible. It also directs the Office of Management and Budget to keep a list of state review entities, set new rules, and report on agency compliance.

12371.s: This order changes the Generalized System of Preferences rules for certain imported articles from beneficiary developing countries. It updates the Tariff Schedules of the United States by adding some item numbers, deleting others, and making staged duty reductions for new items. It also corrects a typographical error in another executive order. The changes apply to articles entered or withdrawn from warehouse for consumption on or after the next day, and to earlier entries that were not yet final.

12370.s: The order creates a three-member emergency board to investigate a dispute between the Brotherhood of Locomotive Engineers and certain railroads. The board must report its findings to the President within 30 days of being created. From the board’s creation date and for 30 days after its report, the carriers and their employees may not change the conditions that led to the dispute unless they agree to do so.

12369.s: This order creates a committee of up to 150 private citizens to study cost control in the Federal Government. The committee is to review executive agencies and advise on ways to improve management and reduce costs, including possible changes through executive action or legislation. It also directs executive agencies and the Secretary of Commerce to provide information and support, and says the committee serves without pay.

12368.s: This order assigns the Office of Policy Development to help the President carry out drug abuse policy functions under the Drug Abuse Prevention, Treatment, and Rehabilitation Act. It names the Director of the Drug Abuse Policy Office as the main official for directing those activities and for helping form, coordinate, and oversee drug abuse policy in executive agencies. It also makes that director responsible for the drug policy staff and revokes Executive Order 12133.

12366.s: This order changes the Presidential Commission on Broadcasting to Cuba so it can have one more member. The commission is to be made up of twelve members appointed by the President from among citizens of the United States.

12365.s: This order changes how foreign assistance and arms export control duties are assigned under earlier executive orders. It adds several sections of the International Security and Development Cooperation Act of 1981 to the list of foreign assistance functions and updates some related references. It also gives the Secretary of Defense certain authorities under the arms export controls order and says some Defense Department determinations need the concurrence of the Secretary of State and the Secretary of the Treasury.

12364.s: This order reconstitutes the Presidential Management Intern Program to recruit and select people for careers in federal public sector management. It applies to eligible graduate-level applicants who have an advanced degree or expect to receive one soon, and it limits new interns to no more than 200 in any fiscal year. The Office of Personnel Management must set procedures for recruitment, nomination, screening, placement, and career development, and interns may be placed in Schedule A of the excepted service. Interns do not get a right to further federal employment when the internship ends, though some may receive competitive civil service status if they meet the required conditions.

12367.s: This order creates the President's Committee on the Arts and the Humanities as an advisory committee. It is made up of certain federal officials and other members appointed by the President, and it may include members chosen by leaders of Congress and invited officials from other cultural institutions. The committee is to study ways to increase private support for the arts and humanities, report recommendations, and collect data on public and private support and local cultural resources. It ends on December 31, 1982, unless extended sooner.

12362.s: This order lets certain U.S. citizens who are family members of civilian employees or uniformed service members apply for some Executive branch jobs in the United States without competing. They must have completed 24 months of satisfactory overseas service and meet other requirements set by the Office of Personnel Management. The order also tells the Director of the Office of Personnel Management to issue rules for carrying it out.

12363.s: This order changes how the Foreign Service is run in the Department of State. It establishes the Board of the Foreign Service and sets out who may serve on it and who will handle its administration. It also lets the Department of Agriculture and the Department of Commerce use the Foreign Service personnel system for certain offices, up to the stated position limits. It revokes a prior executive order.

12360.s: This order creates the President's Task Force on Victims of Crime. The task force is made up of members from public and private life appointed by the President, and the President must choose a chairman from among them. It will review national, state, and local policies and programs affecting victims of crime and advise the President and the Attorney General on actions to improve help and protection for victims of crime.

12361.s: This order gives the Secretary of State the President’s reporting function under the Multinational Force and Observers Participation Resolution. The Secretary of State must consult with the Director of the Office of Management and Budget, the Secretary of Defense, the Director of the United States Arms Control and Disarmament Agency, the Assistant to the President for National Security Affairs, and other executive agency heads as needed.

12359.s: This order designates the Multinational Force and Observers and the International Food Policy Research Institute as public international organizations under the International Organizations Immunities Act. It says these organizations are entitled to the privileges, exemptions, and immunities that the Act provides, with some exceptions for the International Food Policy Research Institute.

12358.s: This order creates the Presidential Commission on Drunk Driving to help states fight drunk driving on the nation’s roads. The commission is directed to raise public awareness, encourage states and communities to use more organized methods, and support stronger enforcement of state and local drunk driving laws. Executive agencies and the Department of Transportation are told to provide information and support, and the commission is set to end one year after the order.

12357.s: This order gives the Director the President’s powers under section 6 of the Special International Security Assistance Act of 1979. It directs the Director to phase out the Sinai Support Mission after the Multinational Force and Observers becomes operational and to end the mission’s functions by September 30, 1982. After that date, the Secretary of State is responsible for any remaining actions needed to finish matters started by the mission.

12356.s: This order sets a uniform system for classifying, declassifying, and safeguarding national security information. It creates three classification levels: Top Secret, Secret, and Confidential, and says information may be classified only if its release could reasonably harm national security. It also limits who can classify information, requires it to be declassified or downgraded when national security allows, and says classification cannot be used to hide errors or embarrassment.

12355.s: This order changes a prior executive order so the Attorney General or his designee must report findings to the President through the Cabinet Council on Legal Policy. It replaces the older reference to the Cabinet Council on Human Resources with the new Cabinet Council on Legal Policy. It affects the Attorney General and the way those reports are sent to the President.

12354.s: This order changes the Generalized System of Preferences rules for certain imported articles. It updates tariff schedule items, changes which articles are eligible for GSP benefits, and modifies the list of beneficiary developing countries. It also provides staged reductions in duty rates for some new tariff items.

12353.s: This order sets up an annual Combined Federal Campaign to let voluntary agencies ask for contributions from Federal employees and members of the uniformed services at their places of employment or duty. It gives the Director of the Office of Personnel Management power to set eligibility rules, set the annual solicitation period, and allow only one annual solicitation except for emergency or disaster appeals. It also says contributions must be voluntary, may be kept confidential, and that local campaign groups must manage funds fairly and report their management.

12351.s: This order extends the time for peaceful nuclear cooperation with the European Atomic Energy Community until March 10, 1983. It says that ending this cooperation would be seriously prejudicial to U.S. nonproliferation objectives and would jeopardize the common defense and security of the United States.

12352.s: This order directs executive agencies that buy products and services from the private sector to cut unnecessary paperwork, simplify small purchases, improve competition, and make sure contractors, especially small businesses, are paid on time. It also tells agencies to set clear contracting authority, manage procurement staff better, and assign a Procurement Executive to oversee these systems. The order asks Defense, General Services, and NASA to keep working on a single simplified Federal Acquisition Regulation, and it directs personnel and budget officials to support procurement reform across agencies.

12350.s: This order revokes Executive Order No. 12074, which was titled "Urban and Community Impact Analyses." It ends that earlier order’s requirements for federal urban and community impact analyses.

12349.s: This order makes technical corrections to the Generalized System of Preferences and the Tariff Schedules of the United States. It removes some listed items and adds one new item for goods eligible for GSP benefits when imported from designated beneficiary developing countries. It also changes certain tariff schedule headnotes and applies the changes to covered imports and entries on the dates named in the order.

12348.s: This order sets up a Property Review Board to help manage federal real property. The board reviews policies, looks at federal property holdings, sets yearly targets for executive agencies to identify excess property, and makes recommendations to the President. Executive agencies must review their property and report unused, underused, or not optimally used property to the Administrator of General Services and the board. The Administrator must consult the board before assigning or conveying property for public benefit discount conveyances, and Executive Order 11954 is revoked.

12347.s: This order amends a previous executive order to add the Maritime Administration of the Department of Transportation to the annex. It says the Maritime Administration is still covered by the Agreement on Government Procurement after being moved from the Department of Commerce to the Department of Transportation.

12346.s: This order stops new awards for purchases or financial assistance under Section 305 of the Defense Production Act. It moves certain synthetic fuels projects and related funds from the Department of Energy to the United States Synthetic Fuels Corporation, if the Corporation’s board approves the transfer. It also revokes Executive Order 12242, but keeps that order in effect for any loan guarantee issued under it.

12345.s: This order tells the Secretary of Health and Human Services to develop and coordinate a national program for physical fitness and sports. It calls for public education, more coordination among federal, state, and local programs, and cooperation with schools, community groups, professional societies, and other organizations. It also continues the President's Council on Physical Fitness and Sports and sets out its duties, membership, and administrative rules.

12344.s: This order sets up the Naval Nuclear Propulsion Program as one integrated program in the Department of Energy and the Department of the Navy. It says the same director will lead both parts and be approved by the President. The director is given responsibility for technical work, training, safety, and program administration for naval nuclear propulsion plants and related facilities.

12342.s: This order revokes Executive Order No. 11643, as amended. It does so to permit effective predator control with environmental safeguards under Federal statutory programs.

12343.s: This order sets who will act as Secretary of State if the Secretary and Deputy Secretary are both unavailable because of absence, disability, or vacancy. It says the Secretary of State may set an order of succession among certain State Department officers, and if there is no such order, officers will serve in rank order and by the order they took the oath. It also lets the President direct a specified officer to act as Secretary of State and revokes Executive Order No. 10839.

12341.s: This order reassigns some responsibilities for providing assistance to Cuban and Haitian entrants. It gives certain functions under the Refugee Education Assistance Act of 1980 to the Secretary of Health and Human Services and the Attorney General. It also revokes Executive Order No. 12251, while actions taken under that order stay in effect until they are replaced.

12340.s: This order amends the Manual for Courts-Martial. It changes rules for military trials, including pretrial confinement, counsel for the accused, individual military counsel, and review of court-martial decisions. It also changes how some military appellate notices and deadlines are handled.

12339.s: This order increases the membership of the President's Commission on Housing by eight members. It says the commission will have no more than 30 members from private life and from state and local governments, all appointed by the President.

12338.s: This order excludes certain agencies and subdivisions from coverage under the Federal Labor-Management Relations Program. It adds several military intelligence and strategic command offices to the excluded list. It also updates the listed Department of Energy offices covered by the exclusion.

12337.s: This order defines “field duty” and “sea duty” for the rules on basic allowances for subsistence for members of the Uniformed Services. It says field duty includes service when a member is fed by a Government mess or field rations while under orders with troops operating against an enemy, or while serving with troops on maneuvers, war games, field exercises, or similar operations. It says sea duty means service on an active self-propelled vessel that is in commission or in service and has berthing and messing facilities.

12336.s: The order creates the Task Force on Legal Equity for Women. It is made up of representatives from listed executive agencies and is chaired by a member chosen by the President. The task force coordinates changes in sex-discriminatory federal regulations, policies, and practices, and the Attorney General must review federal laws and report findings on language that unfairly treats people differently based on sex.

12334.s: This order creates the President's Intelligence Oversight Board in the White House Office with three members. The board is to tell the President about intelligence activities that may violate the Constitution, laws, executive orders, or presidential directives, and it may send reports to the Attorney General. It also reviews intelligence agency guidelines and reporting practices, and heads of intelligence agencies must give it the information it needs when allowed by law.

12333.s: This order sets rules for how U.S. intelligence agencies gather, share, and use intelligence about foreign powers, organizations, persons, and their agents. It gives the National Security Council and the Director of Central Intelligence major roles in guiding intelligence work, budgets, and special activities. It also requires executive branch departments and agencies to cooperate, share relevant information, and report possible law or security violations, and it gives the CIA specific intelligence and counterintelligence duties.

12335.s:
This order creates the National Commission on Social Security Reform. The Commission will review the Social Security trust funds, identify problems that may threaten their long-term solvency, analyze possible solutions, and make recommendations to the Secretary of Health and Human Services, the President, and Congress.

It will be made up of members chosen by the President, the Senate Majority Leader, and the Speaker of the House, and the President will name the chairman.

12332.s: This order establishes the National Productivity Advisory Committee. The committee is made up of citizens appointed by the President, and one member may be a full-time federal employee. It advises the President, the Secretary of the Treasury, and other government offices on ways to improve national productivity and economic growth, including the possible impact of federal laws and regulations. Federal agencies must provide information the committee needs, and the committee is to end on December 31, 1982 unless extended.

12331.s: This order creates the President's Foreign Intelligence Advisory Board within the White House Office. The board advises the President on intelligence work and reviews the quality, quantity, and adequacy of intelligence collection, analysis, counterintelligence, and related activities. It may also review the performance of government agencies involved in intelligence and make recommendations to improve their work. Members serve at the President's pleasure and must keep classified information secret.

12330.s: This order adjusts rates of basic pay and salaries for several federal pay systems, including the General Schedule, Foreign Service Schedule, Veterans Administration medical and surgery schedules, and the Senior Executive Service. It also adjusts monthly basic pay and basic allowances for subsistence and quarters for members of the uniformed services. The order also makes adjustments for the Vice President, executive salaries, congressional salaries, and judicial salaries, and it supersedes two earlier executive orders.

12329.s: This order creates the President’s Task Force on Private Sector Initiatives. The task force is made up of people appointed by the President from private citizens, state and local officials, and members of the federal government. It advises the President, the Secretary of Commerce, and other agency heads on ways to support private sector leadership, public-private partnerships, and less dependence on government. It also serves as a center for private sector action on public problems.

12328.s: This order gives the Secretary of the Interior the President’s authority to make rules for Bureau of Indian Affairs officers, employees, or agents who buy from or sell to any Indian any service or property. It also gives the Secretary of Health and Human Services the same authority for Indian Health Service officers, employees, or agents. Until new rules are issued, the earlier rules for Federal employees contracting or trading with Indians stay in effect.

12327.s: This order exempts Fort Allen from parts of federal water pollution, clean air, noise control, and solid waste laws. It was issued to provide for the immediate relocation and temporary housing of Haitian nationals who were in the custody of the United States in Florida. The exemptions apply to the federal facility at Fort Allen in Puerto Rico for one year.

12326.s: This order changes the Central Intelligence Agency retirement and disability system. It adds rules for survivor benefit notifications, disability retirement, and how some military retired pay or Veterans Administration benefits affect an annuity. It also changes cost-of-living increases, lets the Director request certain information from other federal officials, and allows state income tax withholding from annuities if requested in writing.

12325.s: This order amends a previous order about the Presidential Task Force on the Arts and Humanities. It removes a rule limiting how many members could be full-time federal officers or employees, and it says the Task Force will end on October 31, 1981.

12323.s: This order creates the Presidential Commission on Broadcasting to Cuba. The commission is made up of 11 members appointed by the President, with one member named as chairman and a three-member executive committee. It must develop a recommended plan for radio broadcasting to Cuba and examine related issues such as content, staffing, legal structure, budgets, and possible broadcasting stations. The commission must report to the President and the Secretary of State and then end on the stated deadline.

12322.s: Before a federal agency sends a water or related land resources project report, proposal, or plan to Congress, it must first send it to the Office of Management and Budget. The Office of Management and Budget reviews it for consistency with the President's policy, planning guidelines, and other applicable laws and rules. Any later submission to Congress must include the advice received from that office.

12320.s: This order directs the Secretary of Education to lead a federal program to increase the participation of historically Black colleges and universities in federally sponsored programs. It requires executive departments and certain agencies to make annual plans, report progress, and review barriers that may limit these colleges’ participation. It also asks for comments from presidents of historically Black colleges and universities and encourages private sector efforts to strengthen these schools.

12319.s: This order ends six river basin commissions on the dates listed and revokes the executive orders that created them. It tells federal agencies to help with an orderly closeout and, if the member states choose, a transition of some commission activities to the states. It also directs that commission assets may be transferred to the member states or other state-designated entities, subject to approval.

12321.s: This executive order changes parts of two earlier executive orders about foreign assistance and arms export control. It removes one reference from Executive Order 12163 and rewrites one section of Executive Order 11958. The change affects how authority is described for the Secretary of Defense under those laws.

12317.s: This order gives the President's Commission on Hostage Compensation more time to prepare its report. It changes the deadline for the commission to submit its final report to the President to September 21, 1981.

12318.s: This order transfers certain statistical policy functions from the Secretary of Commerce to the Director of the Office of Management and Budget. It also requires the Director to redelegate some functions to the Administrator for the Office of Information and Regulatory Affairs. Records, property, personnel, and unexpended appropriations tied to these functions are transferred as well, and some prior executive orders and sections are revoked.

12316.s: This order amends the National Contingency Plan to set procedures for coordinating response actions to releases of hazardous substances into the environment. It creates a national response team made up of representatives from several federal agencies. The order also delegates many response, cleanup, liability, funding, and litigation functions to agencies including the Environmental Protection Agency, the Coast Guard, the Department of Health and Human Services, the Federal Emergency Management Agency, and others.

12315.s: This order amends the Manual for Courts-Martial rules on sentencing in military cases. It changes what evidence the prosecution and defense may present after a finding of guilty, including service data, prior convictions, aggravating evidence, and matters in extenuation or mitigation. It also sets rules for rebuttal, witness production, and how requests for witnesses in presentencing proceedings must be made.

12314.s:
The order restructures Federal Regional Councils for each of the ten standard Federal regions. Each council includes officials from several federal agencies and is led by a chairman named by the President.

The councils are meant to work with state, tribal, regional, and local offices and to inform elected officials about government policies and initiatives. They also help explain federal aid reforms, devolution of federal programs, and the reduction of federal regulations and administrative requirements.

12312.s: This order changes the rules for the Meritorious Service Medal. It allows the medal to be awarded to members of the armed forces of friendly foreign nations as well as members of the armed forces of the United States. The medal may be given for outstanding meritorious achievement or service.

12313.s: This order sets January 21, 1981, as the return date for certain U.S. citizens and resident aliens who were held after the seizure of the United States Embassy in Iran. It says this date is for purposes of sections of the Hostage Relief Act of 1980. It applies to people who were returned to the United States or otherwise accounted for and were no longer under foreign control.

12311.s: This order changes the tariff rules for the Generalized System of Preferences. It modifies which articles are eligible for GSP benefits from designated beneficiary developing countries and from all designated beneficiary countries except certain ones listed in the trade schedules. It also changes the tariff schedules and sets effective dates for the different amendments.

12310.s: This order creates the President's Commission on Housing, a presidential advisory committee with up to 22 members from private life and state and local governments. The Commission advises the President and the Secretary of Housing and Urban Development on national housing policy, federal housing programs, housing costs, and housing finance. It also reviews existing federal housing policies and programs and reports its findings and recommendations to them.

12309.s: This order changes the rules for who can serve on the President's Economic Policy Advisory Board. It deletes language that limited members to people "from private life."

12308.s: This order creates the Presidential Task Force on the Arts and Humanities, with up to 36 members appointed by the President. It directs the task force to advise the President on ways to increase private support for the arts and humanities, rely more on nongovernmental experts, and improve the management and structure of federal arts and humanities programs. The task force must report its findings and recommendations to the President and the leaders of the National Endowment for the Arts and the National Endowment for the Humanities.

12307.s: This order changes the schedule for the President's Commission on Hostage Compensation. It says the commission must submit a report to the President by August 20, 1981. It also says the commission may hold public hearings to identify issues and possible solutions related to compensation.

12306.s: This order changes Military Rule of Evidence 410 for court-martial cases. It says certain guilty pleas, withdrawn pleas, nolo contendere pleas, and related statements are not admissible against the accused, with a few listed exceptions. The change applies to court-martial proceedings taken on or after August 1, 1981, and does not invalidate investigations, trials, or other actions begun before that date.

12305.s: This order revokes several earlier executive orders that had set up federal advisory committees. It terminates the United States Circuit Judge Nominating Commission, the Committee on Selection of Federal Judicial Officers, the Judicial Nominating Commission for the District of Puerto Rico, and the United States Tax Court Nominating Commission. It also revokes parts of another executive order that had extended these committees.

12304.s: This order approves an official seal for the Panama Canal Commission. It describes the seal’s design in detail and makes the attached design part of the order. The seal is for the Commission’s official use.

12303.s: This order creates the Presidential Advisory Committee on Federalism. The committee is made up of private citizens, state and local officials, and members of the federal legislative and executive branches, all appointed by the President. It advises the President on federalism policy, and executive agencies may provide it information on federalism issues. Its members serve without pay, and the committee is set to end on December 31, 1982 unless extended sooner.

12302.s: This order changes the Generalized System of Preferences trade rules by revising tariff schedule items and the lists of articles that can receive preference treatment. It also changes duty rates for certain items, adds special treatment for least developed developing countries for two tariff items, and updates which beneficiary developing countries are covered. The changes apply to certain imports and warehouse withdrawals on or after March 31, 1981, and to articles imported on or after January 1, 1976.

12301.s: This order creates the President's Council on Integrity and Efficiency to coordinate government efforts against fraud and waste in federal programs and operations. The Council is also told to set standards for inspector general-type work and to develop plans, policies, audits, and investigations to promote economy, efficiency, and effectiveness. It applies to the agencies and officials named on the Council and to other executive agencies through the Coordinating Conference.

12299.s: This order ends the Presidential Advisory Board on Ambassadorial Appointments. It revokes parts of two earlier executive orders that created or amended that board.

12300.s: This order moves certain Department of Agriculture positions out of the competitive service and into Schedule C. It applies to State Executive Directors in the Agricultural Stabilization and Conservation Service and to State Directors or State Directors-at-Large in the Farmers Home Administration. The order says these jobs are confidential, policy-determining, policy-making, or policy-advocating positions.

12298.s: This order ends the Tahoe Federal Coordinating Council. It also revokes Executive Order No. 12247 and removes federal involvement that had been tied to the Tahoe Regional Planning Agency.

12297.s: This order delegates the President’s functions under the International Coffee Agreement Act of 1980 to the United States Trade Representative. The Trade Representative must consult with the Secretary of Agriculture and the Secretary of State when carrying out those functions. The Trade Representative may also give some or all of those functions to the head of another executive agency with that agency head’s consent.

12296.s: This order creates the President's Economic Policy Advisory Board, made up of private citizens appointed by the President. The Board advises the President on domestic and international economic policy and works with the Cabinet Council on Economic Affairs. It also reviews economic policy, may get needed information from executive agencies, and must keep that information confidential when allowed by law.

12295.s: This order extends the time for peaceful nuclear cooperation with the European Atomic Energy Community until March 10, 1982. It applies to that cooperation and follows notice to Congress.

12293.s: This order gives the Secretary of State several duties and powers over the Foreign Service under the Foreign Service Act of 1980. It sets salary classes for the Senior Foreign Service and establishes a Board of Examiners in the Department of State. It also lets the Secretary of State ask for certain pay, pension, and compensation information to help run the Foreign Service retirement and disability system.

12292.s: This order updates several older executive orders to match the Foreign Service Act of 1980. It changes legal references in rules about Foreign Service allowances, benefits, leave, and related authority. It also revokes some older executive orders and parts of others.

12294.s: This order suspends certain claims that may be brought before the Iran-United States Claims Tribunal and gives those claims no legal effect in U.S. courts while the suspension lasts. It applies to claims in courts now pending or filed after the order’s effective date, but it does not require dismissal for want of prosecution. It does not apply to claims about standby letters of credit, performance or payment bonds, or similar instruments, and it allows counterclaims or set-offs in cases brought by Iran or entities controlled by Iran.
