12290.s: This order revokes Executive Order 12264, which dealt with federal policy on exporting banned or significantly restricted substances. It says the Export Administration Act of 1979 should be carried out with the minimum regulatory burden.

12291.s: This order sets rules for federal agencies when they make or review regulations. It requires agencies to look at the benefits and costs of major rules, prepare regulatory impact analyses, and send those rules for review by the Director of the Office of Management and Budget. It also requires agencies to review existing rules, publish regulatory agendas, and delay or reconsider some major rules already issued but not yet effective.

12289.s: This order changes parts of the Foreign Service Retirement and Disability System to conform it more closely to the Civil Service Retirement and Disability System. It changes how the first annuity increase is figured for some participants and surviving spouses, and it changes how annuities are computed for participants who also receive military retired or retainer pay or Veterans' Administration pension or compensation. The changes take effect on February 15, 1981.

12288.s: This order revokes Executive Order No. 12092, as amended. It authorizes the heads of executive agencies and military departments, including the Council on Wage and Price Stability and the Office of Federal Procurement Policy, to take steps to end actions taken in response to that order. It affects federal agencies and military departments involved in the wage and price program.

12284.s: This order blocks certain property and assets in the United States that are under the control of the former Shah of Iran’s estate or close relatives who are defendants in cases brought by Iran. It requires people and federal agencies with information about that property to report it to the Secretary of the Treasury, who may share identifying information with the Government of Iran. It also directs the Attorney General to present the United States’ position in court that Iran’s claims for recovery of the property should not be barred and that Iranian decrees and judgments about those assets should be enforced under U.S. law.

12286.s: This order sets the National Oil and Hazardous Substance Pollution Contingency Plan as the main way the government coordinates responses to releases of hazardous substances, pollutants, and contaminants into the environment. It gives the Environmental Protection Agency, the Coast Guard, and other executive agencies authority to carry out response, remedy, abatement, liability, and financial responsibility duties under the law. It also assigns authority over claims against the Fund, use of the Fund, and litigation under the Act to different officials, including the Attorney General.

12280.s: This order directs certain people and institutions in the United States that hold funds or securities of Iran or its agencies to transfer them to the Federal Reserve Bank of New York. It revokes and nullifies certain licenses, court orders, attachments, and other claims tied to those Iranian assets. It also bars people from getting or using rights in those properties, and it tells the Attorney General to defend actions taken under the order.

12279.s: This order directs U.S.-jurisdiction banking institutions to transfer funds, securities, and deposits owned by the Government of Iran or its agencies, instrumentalities, or controlled entities to the Federal Reserve Bank of New York. It also revokes licenses and blocks rights or claims to those properties that came from court orders, attachments, injunctions, or similar proceedings after November 14, 1979, 8:10 a.m. EST. The Attorney General is told to intervene in related litigation, and the Secretary of the Treasury is given authority to carry out the order.

12277.s: This order directs the Federal Reserve Bank of New York to transfer gold bullion and other assets of the Government of Iran, or its agencies and controlled entities, to accounts at the Bank of England. It also revokes licenses and other rights tied to those assets and bars people subject to U.S. jurisdiction from claiming or using them. The order says compliance with it protects people from liability for actions taken in good faith under it.

12275.s: This order creates an interagency Design Liaison Council to encourage good design within the Federal Government. The council is made up of heads or designees from many federal agencies, and some other agencies are invited to take part. It is to share information and research on design issues and recommend changes to agency standards and procedures that would improve the functional and visual quality of design products and processes.

12274.s: This order changes military pay rules for Navy submarine duty, career sea duty, and basic allowance for quarters. It sets out who may receive submarine duty incentive pay and career sea pay, and it adds a premium for some members after 36 consecutive months of sea duty. It also extends basic allowances for quarters to certain members without dependents when their unit is deployed for more than 90 days.

12276.s: The order lets the Secretary of the Treasury set up escrow or related agreements with a foreign central bank and the Central Bank of Algeria. It also lets the Treasury direct the Federal Reserve Bank of New York to receive, hold, invest, or transfer money and other assets in which Iran or its agencies have an interest. These steps are tied to the release of 52 U.S. diplomats and nationals being held hostage in Iran and to claims by United States nationals against Iran.

12273.s: This order changes the Central Intelligence Agency Retirement and Disability System to match certain changes in the Civil Service Retirement and Disability System. It changes how the first cost-of-living increase is figured for annuities paid from the fund to retired participants or to the widow or widower of a deceased participant. The change applies to annuities starting after January 19, 1981.

12272.s: This order changes part of the Foreign Service Retirement and Disability System to match the Civil Service Retirement and Disability System more closely. It replaces one paragraph in the Foreign Service Act with a different provision from Title 5 of the U.S. Code. The change applies to annuities that begin after January 19, 1981.

12271.s: This order corrects two typographical errors in Executive Order No. 12258. One correction changes a citation for the President's Advisory Committee for Women, and the other changes a citation for the Federal Advisory Council on Occupational Safety and Health.

12270.s: This order creates a President's Council on Spinal Cord Injury with 12 members appointed by the President. The council advises the President, through the Secretary of Education, on prevention, diagnosis, treatment, and reversal of spinal cord injury. The Secretary of Education provides administrative support, and the council is set to end on December 31, 1981 unless extended.

12269.s: This order creates a President's Committee on Small Business Policy made up of seven members appointed by the President. The committee advises the President, through the Administrator of the Small Business Administration, on responses to recommendations from the White House Conference on Small Business. The Small Business Administration must provide the committee's administrative support, and the committee is set to end on December 31, 1982 unless extended sooner.

12268.s: This order delegates to the Secretary of State the President’s functions under certain sections of the Hostage Relief Act of 1980. The Secretary of State must consult with the heads of appropriate executive agencies when carrying out those functions.

12267.s: This order changes the Generalized System of Preferences for certain imported articles from beneficiary developing countries. It removes some items from preference lists, makes technical changes to the tariff schedules, and deletes two items from special country-specific rules for the Philippines and Thailand. Some of the changes apply only to certain imports and entries made on or after listed dates.

12266.s: The order establishes a Food Security Wheat Reserve made up of reserve stocks of wheat. The reserve cannot be more than four million metric tons. The Secretary of Agriculture must choose the specific wheat stocks that will make up the reserve.

12264.s: The order sets rules for federal agencies that regulate substances that are banned or significantly restricted, including certain foods, drugs, devices, pesticides, chemicals, and other products. It requires agencies to publish lists of those substances and to send notification information to the Department of State when such substances are exported to foreign countries. It also says export controls should be used only in limited cases for extremely hazardous substances, and the Departments of State and Commerce must work together on licensing and review procedures.

12265.s: This order changes the Consumer Affairs Council so it has more members. It says the Council will include representatives from listed federal agencies and other officers or employees the President designates. Each agency on the Council must be represented by the agency head or a senior-level official chosen by that head.

12263.s: This order delegates the President’s functions under section 5 of the Strategic and Critical Materials Transaction Authorization Act of 1979 to the United States Trade Representative. It is issued to provide for the contribution of tin to the Tin Buffer Stock under the Fifth International Tin Agreement.

12262.s: This order creates the Interagency Employee Benefit Council. The Council is made up of several federal officials and agencies, and the Secretary of Labor serves as chair. It helps coordinate proposals affecting employee benefits under ERISA, identify economic effects, improve information sharing, and recommend ways to reduce inconsistencies in ERISA programs. It also must meet each quarter and send the President a yearly report.

12261.s: This order requires federal agencies that own or lease motor vehicles to use gasohol in vehicles that can run on it, when it is available at reasonable prices and in reasonable quantities. In buying unleaded gasoline, agencies are to treat gasohol as an acceptable substitute whenever feasible and give it a preference. Agencies must identify which vehicles can use gasohol, set rules for its use, and share gasohol usage data with the Department of Energy when asked.

12260.s: This order puts the Agreement on Government Procurement into effect for eligible products bought by certain executive agencies listed in the order. It says those purchases must follow Office of Federal Procurement Policy rules, and it gives the United States Trade Representative responsibility for interpreting the agreement. Agencies must consult the Trade Representative before talks with foreign governments about government procurement, and purchases under 150,000 Special Drawing Rights are not covered.

12259.s: This order puts the Secretary of Housing and Urban Development in charge of leading federal fair housing work under the Federal Fair Housing Act. It requires executive agencies to run housing and urban development programs in a way that furthers fair housing and to cooperate with HUD. It also gives agencies steps for reporting, reviewing, and enforcing compliance, including possible sanctions for people or entities that do not comply.

12257.s: This order lets executive agencies give certain excepted appointments to qualified people who completed job training or work experience under the Comprehensive Employment and Training Act. It applies to positions up to CS-3 or the equivalent, and only if the person finished the program within the past three months. Agencies may later convert these appointments to career or career-conditional status if the person completes at least six months of continuous service and meets the other required qualifications. The Office of Personnel Management must issue guidelines for training programs, performance reviews, and removal of people who do not perform satisfactorily.

12258.s: This order continues several listed federal advisory committees until December 31, 1982. It also says the department or agency head named for each committee will perform the President’s functions under the Federal Advisory Committee Act, except for the annual report to Congress. The order revokes several older executive orders that created committees that had ended or finished their work, and it supersedes Executive Order 12110.

12256.s: This order tells the Bureau of the Census to identify certain states, counties, and local governments that had at least fifty legal immigrants from Cuba or Haiti who arrived between April 1, 1980, and September 30, 1980. It also requires executive branch agencies to use those census estimates in formulas for distributing benefits based on population or population characteristics, unless doing so would be against the law. The order applies to affected governments and to the departments and agencies that use these estimates.

12255.s: This order closed executive departments and agencies on Friday, December 26, 1980, and excused their employees from duty. Agency heads could keep certain offices open and require some employees to work for national security, defense, or other public reasons. The day was also treated as a holiday for federal pay and leave.

12253.s: This order changes the Central Intelligence Agency Retirement and Disability System to match changes in the civil service retirement system. It removes the “living with” requirement for recognized natural children and adds a dependency requirement for a child. A child is treated as dependent if the participant was living with the child or contributing to the child’s support when the participant died. The Director of Central Intelligence may issue regulations to carry this out.

12254.s: This order establishes a National Advisory Community Investment Board. The Board is to carry out the functions and activities set out in the Economic Opportunity Act of 1964, and the Director of the Community Services Administration is to provide its administrative support. The order also assigns some Federal Advisory Committee Act duties to that Director and says the Board will end on December 31, 1981 unless it is extended sooner.

12252.s: This order directs that the U.S. flag be flown at half-staff until interment in memory of the Honorable John William McCormack, a former Speaker of the House and Representative from Massachusetts. It applies to federal buildings, grounds, and naval vessels in the United States, its territories and possessions, and U.S. facilities abroad, including military facilities and naval vessels and stations.

12250.s: This order puts the Attorney General in charge of coordinating how executive agencies carry out and enforce several nondiscrimination laws in federal programs and programs that receive federal financial assistance. It gives the Attorney General authority to review agency rules, set standards for enforcement and investigations, issue guidance on compliance, and oversee recordkeeping, reporting, and training. Executive agencies must work with the Attorney General and submit their implementation plans and directives for review. The order also revokes two earlier executive orders and says it does not cover equal employment provisions.

12249.s: This order establishes a new Foreign Service Schedule. It sets salary classes for certain members of the Foreign Service. The salary rates in the schedule take effect on the first day of the first pay period that begins on or after October 1, 1980.

12251.s: This order gives the Secretary of Health and Human Services the President’s powers under the Refugee Education Assistance Act for Cuban and Haitian entrants. It makes federal funds available to reimburse state and local governments for cash and medical assistance and social services. It also directs the Secretary to provide assistance for Cuban and Haitian entrants at several named sites and any other sites he may designate, and it revokes a prior executive order.

12248.s: This order adjusts certain rates of pay and allowances for several federal pay systems. It covers the General Schedule, the Foreign Service, the Department of Medicine and Surgery in the Veterans Administration, the Senior Executive Service, members of the uniformed services, the Vice President, executive branch salaries, congressional salaries, and judicial salaries. The uniformed services pay and allowances are effective on October 1, 1980, and the other pay changes take effect on the first applicable pay period on or after October 1, 1980.

12247.s: This order sets up a Federal council to coordinate agency actions in the Lake Tahoe Region. It directs the council to set environmental quality thresholds and carrying capacities for air, water, and land in the region, with help from California, Nevada, local governments, and the public. Federal agencies must review planned actions in the region for possible adverse environmental effects, and they must limit certain actions until the thresholds are issued. The order does not apply if an action is essential for public health or safety, national security, or maintaining or restoring environmental quality in the region.

12246.s: The order gives the Secretary of State the President’s functions under a section of the Refugee Education Assistance Act of 1980. It directs the Secretary to take action to provide assistance for Cuban and Haitian entrants at the listed sites and any other sites he designates.

12245.s: This order changes the Peace Corps Advisory Council to allow two co-chairpersons. It says the President may appoint up to 30 members to the council, and the members serve at the President’s pleasure.

12244.s: This order exempts Fort Allen in Puerto Rico from some requirements of the Federal Water Pollution Control Act, the Clean Air Act, the Noise Control Act, and the Solid Waste Disposal Act. The exemption applies to sources and facilities at Fort Allen, with some parts of those laws still in place. It says the exemptions are for one year and are tied to the immediate relocation and temporary housing of Haitian and Cuban nationals held by the United States in Florida.

12243.s: This order changes the rules for a variable housing allowance for military members. It says a member is in a "high housing cost area" when the average monthly housing cost, including utilities, is more than 115 percent of that member’s basic allowance for quarters. It also allows members to be paid a variable housing allowance during fiscal year 1981 as permitted by the law it cites.

12242.s: This order directs the Secretaries of Defense and Energy to manage synthetic fuel work for national defense needs. It gives them roles in deciding how much synthetic fuel is needed, handling purchase contracts, and preparing a report to Congress. It also says new awards and financial assistance stop after the United States Synthetic Fuels Corporation is determined to be established and fully operational, and loan guarantees need Treasury approval.

12241.s: This order sets up publication of a National Contingency Plan to protect public health and safety in case of accidents at nuclear power facilities. It gives the Director of the Federal Emergency Management Agency the President’s functions under the cited law. It also says copies of the plan shall be published from time to time in the Federal Register.

12240.s: This order extends the life of the Nuclear Safety Oversight Committee if funds are available. It says support for the committee must follow a cited appropriations law starting October 1, 1980. It also says the committee will end on September 30, 1981, and changes its membership from five persons to six persons.

12239.s: This order suspends several Navy and Marine Corps promotion limits for a set period. It also makes certain disability retirement and separation rules in the Armed Forces effective during a set period. The order revokes Executive Order No. 12082.

12238.s: This order designates the International Maritime Satellite Organization as a public international organization under the International Organizations Immunities Act. It gives that organization the privileges, exemptions, and immunities allowed by that law. It applies to the organization because the United States participates in it under the Communications Satellite Act of 1962.

12237.s: This order changes the Executive Schedule to place two new Deputy Under Secretary positions in level V. The positions are in the Department of Education.

12236.s: This order changes Level IV of the Executive Schedule. It removes the position of Senior Adviser to the Secretary, Department of State, and the Special Assistant to the Special Representative for Trade Negotiations. It adds the position of Counselor to the Secretary, Department of the Treasury.

12235.s: This order gives the Secretary of Energy the President’s functions under parts of the Natural Gas Policy Act of 1978 and the Public Utility Regulatory Policies Act of 1978 for natural gas supply emergencies. The President keeps the power to declare, extend, and end a natural gas supply emergency. The Secretary must consult with the Environmental Protection Agency, the Federal Emergency Management Agency, and other executive agencies, and other agencies must help carry out the order.

12234.s: This order carries out the International Convention for the Safety of Life at Sea, 1974, for the United States. It tells the Secretary of State, the Coast Guard department, the Secretary of Commerce, and the Federal Communications Commission to carry out the parts of the convention that fall within their duties and help each other do so. It also makes the Coast Guard department or other authorized agencies responsible for issuing required certificates and says the Coast Guard department shall write the needed regulations. It supersedes one earlier executive order and revokes another, to the extent stated in the order.

12233.s: This order makes clarifying and technical changes to the Manual for Courts-Martial and the Military Rules of Evidence. It changes several rules about expert testimony, privileged claims, interrogation, wire and oral communications, and the use of government information in military justice cases. It affects members of the armed forces, their agents, military officials, and people involved in court-martial cases.

12232.s: This order directs the Secretary of Education and other executive agencies to increase the participation of historically Black colleges and universities in federally sponsored programs. It tells agencies to review their programs, find and remove unfair barriers, and set annual goals to improve participation. The Secretary of Education must also give college presidents a chance to comment and send the President an annual report.

12231.s: This order delegates certain presidential functions about the strategic petroleum reserve to the Secretary of Energy. It covers functions in the Energy Policy and Conservation Act, Title 10 of the United States Code, and the Energy Security Act.

12230.s: This order lets certain Drug Enforcement Administration criminal investigators be moved noncompetitively to career or career-conditional federal jobs. It applies to investigators with Schedule A or B appointments who have completed three years of fully satisfactory service and who meet other requirements set by the Office of Personnel Management. The Office of Personnel Management must issue regulations to carry out the order.

12229.s: This order creates the White House Coal Advisory Council, a nine-member group appointed by the President. The council advises the President and the Secretary of Labor on labor-management relations in the coal industry, mine safety, productivity, and other issues they request. The Secretary of Labor provides support for the council, and members serve without pay but may get travel expenses. The council ends one year after the order.

12228.s: This order sets rules for paying extra compensation and allowances for certain personnel serving in foreign areas. It gives the Secretary of State authority over some regulations for quarters, quarters allowances, and cost of living allowances. It also gives the Administrator of Veterans Administration authority over some allowances and benefits, and it revokes Executive Order 10853.

12227.s: This order changes the duties of the United States Sinai Support Mission. The mission is to help carry out parts of the peace treaty between Egypt and Israel by checking zones, force levels, fortifications, installations, and technical installations. It also gives the mission other tasks to support the treaty and says the mission should help the United States role encourage good-faith compliance with the agreement.

12226.s: This order amends a prior executive order to add the Director of the Peace Corps to the Development Coordination Committee. It changes who is on that committee. It affects the Peace Corps and the committee members.

12225.s: This order phases out the credit controls authorized by a prior executive order. It revokes some authorizations for the Federal Reserve Board to set uniform requirements for changes in terms in open-end consumer credit accounts, and it also revokes other authorizations under that earlier order.

12223.s: This order changes the effective date of a previous order on occupational safety and health programs for Federal employees. It gives more time to develop instructions for those programs before they take effect.

12224.s: This order delegates the President’s functions under Public Law 96-236 to the United States Trade Representative. The Trade Representative must consult with the Secretary of Agriculture and the Secretary of State when carrying out those functions. With the consent of another executive agency’s head, the Trade Representative may delegate some or all of those functions to that agency’s head.

12221.s: This order changes a prior executive order so it will expire on April 30, 1981, unless extended. It keeps existing procedures for improving government regulations in place while regulatory reform legislation is pending.

12222.s: This order changes the list of articles that can get benefits under the Generalized System of Preferences when imported from designated beneficiary developing countries. It also makes technical corrections to a prior order and changes the tariff schedule to match those updates. The changes affect certain imported articles, including items listed for Thailand and the Philippines.

12220.s: This order delegates certain functions under the Agricultural Trade Development and Assistance Act to the Secretary of Agriculture, the Director of the United States International Development Cooperation Agency, and the Secretary of State. It also sets rules for using foreign currencies received under the Act and gives some related duties to other agencies, including the Treasury and the Office of Management and Budget. The order revokes several earlier executive orders, in whole or in part.

12219.s: This order changes the end date of the Presidential Commission on World Hunger. It extends the commission’s life until August 31, 1980.

12217.s: This order directs executive agencies to follow fuel use prohibitions and pollution control standards for new and existing powerplants and major fuel-burning installations. It requires agencies to work with the Secretary of Energy, survey covered facilities, and submit annual fuel use conversion plans with cost estimates. It also says agencies must request funding for compliance and may use those funds only for that purpose unless allowed by law and approved by the Office of Management and Budget.

12215.s: This order delegates many Panama Canal functions from the President to the Secretary of Defense. It also delegates some functions to the Secretary of State and one function to the Director of the Office of Personnel Management. The order requires agencies to consult with the Secretary of Defense on pay and employment practices, and it revokes two prior provisions in earlier executive orders.

12214.s: This order delegates most functions under the Export Administration Act of 1979 to the Secretary of Commerce. It keeps certain listed functions with the President and gives some functions to the Secretary of State. Existing rules, orders, licenses, and other actions under the act stay in effect until changed by proper authority.

12216.s:
This order creates the President's Committee on the International Labor Organization. The committee includes the Secretaries of Labor, State, and Commerce, the Assistant to the President for National Security Affairs, and the presidents of the AFL-CIO and the United States Council of the International Chamber of Commerce, or their representatives.

The committee will monitor and assess the work of the ILO, make recommendations to the President or other federal officers, and try to develop a coordinated United States position on ILO issues. It also may do other related work requested by the President or the Chairman, and it will end on December 31, 1980 unless extended.

12213.s: This order changes the membership rules for the United States Holocaust Memorial Council to allow broader participation. It sets the Council at no fewer than 35 and no more than 60 members, with appointments from the President and invitations for five members each from the Senate and House. It also gives the Council more time to finish its work and requires a final report by December 15, 1980. The Council is set to end on January 15, 1981 unless it is extended sooner.

12212.s: This order makes the Department of Education Organization Act take effect on May 4, 1980. It also directs the Director of the Office of Management and Budget to carry out the transfers called for in that act, including funds, records, property, personnel, and positions. The order is to be published in the Federal Register.

12210.s: This order changes an earlier executive order on arms export controls. It gives the Secretary of Defense authority under certain sections of the Arms Export Control Act, and says the Secretary of Defense must consult with the Secretary of State when carrying out Section 27. It also adds a new delegation of authority under Section 43(c) to the Secretary of Defense.

12209.s: This order changes the rules for pricing crude oil from marginal properties for January, February, and March 1980. It sets the base production control level using 20 percent of the property’s 1978 old crude oil production and sales, with the amount adjusted by the days in the month. It also lets the Secretary of Energy adopt regulations needed to conform the crude oil pricing rules to this order.

12211.s: This order adds more limits on transactions with Iran to address the declared national emergency. It bars the import of Iranian goods or services into the United States, with an exception for materials imported for news publication or broadcast. It also limits certain transactions tied to travel to Iran for U.S. citizens and permanent residents, and directs the Secretary of the Treasury to revoke certain existing licenses for transactions with Iran Air, the National Iranian Oil Company, and the National Iranian Gas Company.

12208.s: This order delegates some refugee admission duties to the Secretary of State, the Attorney General, and the United States Coordinator for Refugee Affairs. It requires them to consult with the Senate and House Judiciary Committees and to prepare and share information for those committees. It keeps certain refugee decisions with the President, including special circumstances for refugee status, some admission determinations, and the number of refugees to be admitted.

12207.s:
This order creates a three-member board to investigate a dispute between the Port Authority Trans-Hudson Corporation and certain of its employees represented by the Brotherhood of Railway Carmen of the United States and Canada. The board must report its findings to the President within 30 days.

For 30 days after the report, neither the corporation nor its employees may change the conditions that led to the dispute unless they agree to do so.

12206.s: This order changes a previous executive order about authority over the entry of certain aliens into the United States. It removes the words "holding nonimmigrant visas" from that order.

12205.s: This order prohibits many U.S.-linked transactions with Iran and with Iranian government entities or people in Iran. It bans the sale, shipment, or transfer of most items to Iran, with exceptions for food, medicine, supplies for medical purposes, and donations of clothing to relieve human suffering. It also blocks new credits or loans, certain deposit changes, more favorable payment terms, service contracts for industrial projects in Iran, and transactions meant to evade these bans.

12203.s: This order temporarily extends a delegation of authority to the Secretary of Defense. It changes a prior order so that the delegation stays in effect until May 15, 1980. It affects the Secretary of Defense and the Panama Canal regulations covered by that earlier order.

12204.s: This order changes the Generalized System of Preferences rules for certain imported articles and updates the tariff schedules used for those goods. It adds some countries as beneficiary developing countries, removes Afghanistan and Ethiopia from that status, and makes other country list changes. It also sets different duty treatment and effective dates for some tariff items and articles.

12202.s: This order creates the Nuclear Safety Oversight Committee to advise the President and other officials on progress in improving nuclear safety. The committee also reviews work by federal and state agencies, the Nuclear Regulatory Commission, the nuclear power industry, and emergency planning groups. It must report on safety reforms, worker and public health safety, public information, and emergency preparedness.

12201.s: This order gives the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System authority to regulate and control consumer credit. It also lets the Board regulate credit from certain financial intermediaries that mainly make short-term credit, and credit to commercial banks that are not members of the Federal Reserve System when it is in the form of managed liabilities. The order also allows the Board to set recordkeeping requirements for all forms of credit.

12200.s: This order updates pay schedules attached to a prior executive order and adds footnotes showing new limits on payable rates of salary and basic pay. It also adds a schedule for judicial salaries and makes a technical correction to a statutory reference. The changes affect salary and pay schedules for covered federal positions, including Senior Executive Service positions and judicial salaries.

12199.s: This order changes one Level IV position in the Executive Schedule. It removes the job title “Deputy Adviser for Labor-Management, Council on Wage and Price Stability” and replaces it with “Executive Director, White House Conference on Aging, Department of Health, Education, and Welfare.”

12198.s: This order changes the Manual for Courts-Martial by setting out new Military Rules of Evidence. The rules cover how evidence may be used in courts-martial, including self-incrimination, searches and seizures, confessions, eyewitness identification, privileges, witnesses, hearsay, and documents. It affects military judges, the accused, witnesses, and others involved in courts-martial.

12196.s: This order sets safety and health rules for most Executive Branch agencies, except military personnel and uniquely military equipment, systems, and operations. Agency heads must provide workplaces free from recognized hazards, run safety and health programs, inspect workplaces, respond to hazard reports, and train employees. The Secretary of Labor must guide and review agency programs, and the General Services Administration must help correct unsafe conditions in facilities it controls.

12197.s: This order changes the Central Intelligence Agency Retirement and Disability System to match later changes in the civil service retirement system. It lets annuitants choose survivor annuities for a new spouse after remarriage, restores reductions in some cases, and requires annual notice of election rights. It also allows court orders in divorce, annulment, or legal separation cases to direct some payments to another person.

12195.s: This order creates the President's Commission on United States-Liberian Relations. The Commission is to review relations with Liberia, identify problem areas, and make recommendations to improve the relationship. It must send a final report to the President and the Secretary of State, and it will end after that report is sent or within six months.

12194.s: This order establishes the Radiation Policy Council to coordinate federal policy on radiation protection. The council includes heads or representatives from several federal agencies, and the Environmental Protection Agency chair oversees it. It advises on radiation protection policy, monitors how agencies carry it out, helps resolve conflicts between agencies, and serves as a forum for public participation and comment. It must send an annual report and will end four years after the order.

12192.s: This order creates the State Planning Council on Radioactive Waste Management as an advisory committee. The Council gives advice and recommendations to the President and the Secretary of Energy on nuclear waste management, including transport, storage, disposal, and siting of facilities. It includes members from state and local government, a tribal government representative, and several federal agency heads. The Council must submit a public report and then end after it sends its final report or after the stated time limit.

12191.s: This order directs executive agencies to promote ridesharing for people working at Federal facilities, including carpools, vanpools, public transportation, and other multi-occupancy travel. Agencies must set yearly ridesharing goals, name a transportation coordinator, and report their progress. The Administrator of General Services must issue rules to carry it out and may exempt some small, remote Federal facilities.

12193.s: This order extends the time period for peaceful nuclear cooperation with the European Atomic Energy Community until March 10, 1981. It says that ending this cooperation would be seriously harmful to U.S. non-proliferation goals and would jeopardize the common defense and security of the United States. It affects the United States and the European Atomic Energy Community.

12190.s: This order creates an Advisory Committee on Small and Minority Business Ownership. The committee is to help monitor and encourage private-sector subcontracts with eligible small businesses, especially small minority businesses, and to study what incentives and assistance are needed for training, development, and upgrading. It must make reports and recommendations to the President and report yearly to the President and Congress. The Small Business Administration is to provide staff support, and the committee is set to end on December 31, 1980.

12189.s: This order changes the definition of “heavy crude oil” for purposes of an exemption from price controls on the first sale of that oil. It sets different gravity limits for heavy crude oil for two time periods: August 17, 1979 through December 20, 1979, and December 21, 1979 and after. The rules apply to crude oil produced from a property only if the property met the stated weighted average gravity test in the last month before July 1979. The Secretary of Energy may adopt regulations to carry out the order.

12188.s: This order makes the United States Trade Representative the main U.S. representative for many trade talks and negotiations, including work under the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade and other trade and commodity issues. It also keeps the Trade Policy Committee, sets up a Trade Negotiating Committee, and says the Trade Representative and other agencies must consult with each other on trade policy. The order also lets the Secretary of Commerce create a Foreign Commercial Service and moves or changes several trade-related duties, rules, and references in earlier executive orders.

12187.s: This order sets a new base production control level for marginal properties under crude oil pricing rules for months after December 31, 1979. It says the level is based on 20 percent of the property’s 1978 old crude oil production and sales, using a month-by-month formula. The Secretary of Energy may adopt regulations to make the pricing rules match this order.

12186.s: This order changes the definition of “heavy oil” by raising the API figure from 16.0° to 20.0°. It amends an earlier executive order that deals with petroleum allocation.

12185.s: This order directs federal agencies that give financial assistance to use those programs to help conserve petroleum and natural gas. Each agency must review its assistance programs, publish a list for public comment, and then issue rules to support conservation. No financial assistance may be awarded unless it follows those conservation rules. The order also allows rules to reduce or suspend assistance after a hearing if the recipient does not comply, and it requires yearly reports on agency activities.

12184.s: This order establishes a special commission to study ethical problems in medicine and biomedical and behavioral research. It says the commission will follow the rules in Public Law 95-622 and may receive financial support from the Department of Health, Education and Welfare if funds are available. The Administrator of General Services will provide administrative support services. The special commission will end when appropriations are available for the commission created by Public Law 95-622, or no later than two years after this order unless extended.

12183.s: This order revokes three earlier executive orders that limited trade and other transactions involving Zimbabwe-Rhodesia. It applies to transactions after the effective date of the order. It also keeps prior actions, violations, liabilities, penalties, and forfeitures under those earlier orders in effect for transactions before that date, and directs certain federal agencies to carry out the order.

12182.s: This order creates a three-member board to investigate a dispute between the Long Island Rail Road and certain of its employees represented by the listed labor organizations. The board must report its findings to the President within 30 days. From the date of the order and for 30 days after the report, neither the railroad nor its employees may change the conditions involved in the dispute except by agreement.

12181.s: This order changes parts of the Generalized System of Preferences for certain imported articles. It removes some items from the lists of goods that can get GSP benefits and adds others. It also changes which countries are listed for certain items, including deleting the Philippine Republic and the Republic of Korea for one item and adding Mexico for another.

12180.s: This order changes the Generalized System of Preferences for certain articles from beneficiary developing countries. It updates tariff schedule rules and revises the lists of articles that can get GSP benefits, including changes to some country names. The changes apply to imports and entries for consumption on the dates stated in the order.

12179.s: This order closes executive departments and agencies on Monday, December 24, 1979, and excuses their employees from duty that day, except for offices or employees kept on duty for national security, defense, or other public reasons. It also says that day will count as a holiday for federal pay and leave purposes.

12178.s: This order changes a prior executive order to say that certain functions under chapter 7 of the Foreign Assistance Act, dealing with air base construction in Israel, may be carried out without regard to several listed laws. It affects the functions authorized for that work and the agencies or officials carrying them out.

12177.s: This order directs how Federal Government pension plan financial and actuarial statements are handled. It gives the Director of the Office of Management and Budget the President’s functions under the Act and allows that Director to assign duties to other federal officers or agencies. It also requires agency heads to make sure pension plan administrators follow the Director’s rules for filing, and it assigns the Secretary of the Treasury responsibility for developing the annual report form and content unless the Director says otherwise.

12176.s: This order extends the time for the President's Commission on the Coal Industry to finish its report. It says the final report must be sent no later than March 15, 1980, and the Commission will end on that date.

12175.s: This order makes Section 2(b)(1) of Reorganization Plan No. 3 of 1979 effective right away. That section establishes the Office of Deputy Secretary of Commerce, so it affects the Department of Commerce.

12174.s: This order directs federal agencies to reduce the paperwork burden on people outside the federal government. It says agencies should use forms only when needed, keep them short, and pay special attention to the burden on individuals and small organizations. Agencies must also review forms on a regular schedule, make annual paperwork budgets, and report on their paperwork burden control.

12172.s: This order gives the Secretary of State and the Attorney General authority over entry rules for Iranians holding nonimmigrant visas. They may set limits and exceptions on the rules and regulations for the entry of aliens into the United States. The order took effect immediately.

12173.s: This order keeps certain Panama Canal regulations in effect if they were in force on September 30, 1979, unless the President or the Panama Canal Commission changes or ends them. It does not apply where a regulation conflicts with the Panama Canal Treaty of 1977, its implementing agreements, or Public Law 96-70. It also gives the Secretary of Defense the President’s powers and responsibilities under the Panama Canal Code and Public Law 96-70, except for specific powers listed in the order, for 120 days.

12171.s: This order excludes certain federal agencies and subdivisions from the Federal Labor-Management Relations Program because they do intelligence, counterintelligence, investigative, or national security work. It also suspends those labor-management rules for some listed agencies, installations, or activities outside the 50 States and the District of Columbia. The order affects agencies in the Treasury, Defense, Justice, Energy, and Agency for International Development, among others.

12169.s: This order establishes a United States Holocaust Memorial Council to help carry out recommendations for a Holocaust memorial. The Council is to recommend ways to create a memorial museum, an educational and research foundation, and a Citizens Committee on Conscience. It also is to suggest site locations, funding methods, and ways to mark Days of Remembrance of Victims of the Holocaust.

12168.s: This order creates the President's Commission for a National Agenda for the Eighties, made up of private citizens appointed by the President. The Commission is directed to study major public policy issues of the 1980s, including the role of federal government, private institutions, social and economic trends, and barriers to policy agreement. It must seek citizen participation, consult with Congress and state and local officials, and submit a final report with recommendations to the President and Congress.

12167.s: This order waives the application of two parts of section 402 of the Trade Act of 1974 with respect to the People's Republic of China. It affects the treatment of China under that law after the required report to Congress was made.

12166.s: This order gives the Secretary of State the President’s power to decide when it is in the national interest for the Export-Import Bank to deny a credit application for nonfinancial or noncommercial reasons. It says the Secretary must consult with the Secretary of Commerce and other interested executive agencies first. The order applies to Export-Import Bank credit applications and to decisions involving international terrorism, nuclear proliferation, environmental protection, and human rights.

12165.s: This order adjusts rates of basic pay and salaries for several federal pay systems, including the General Schedule, Foreign Service, Veterans Administration medical staff, and the Senior Executive Service. It also adjusts pay and allowances for members of the uniformed services, plus pay for the Vice President, executive branch salaries, and congressional salaries. The uniformed services changes are effective October 1, 1979, and the other changes take effect at the first pay period beginning on or after that date.

12163.s: This order establishes the United States International Development Cooperation Agency and places the Agency for International Development within it. It delegates many foreign assistance functions to the Director of IDCA, the Secretary of State, the Secretary of Defense, the Secretary of the Treasury, and other agency heads, with some duties to be done in consultation with other officials. It also creates the Institute for Scientific and Technological Cooperation, the Council on International Scientific and Technological Cooperation, a Development Loan Committee, and a Development Coordination Committee.

12162.s: This order amends Executive Order 12140. It deletes the first sentence in Section 1-105 of that order.

12161.s: This order amends the anti-inflation program to set standards for company prices and pay increases. It says a company’s price increases should not be higher than its historical rate from 1976-77, with exceptions for uncontrollable cost increases. It also directs the Council on Wage and Price Stability to reconstitute Pay and Price Advisory Committees to advise on policies for private industry, employers, and labor.

12160.s: This order creates a Consumer Affairs Council made up of representatives from several federal agencies. It directs those agencies to improve how they handle consumer matters, including public participation, information materials, staff training, and complaint handling. Each agency must name a senior official to oversee its consumer activities and report its consumer program to the Council.

12159.s: The order creates a three-member emergency board to investigate disputes between the Chicago, Rock Island, Pacific Railroad & Peoria Terminal Company and certain employees represented by two railroad unions. The board must report its findings to the President within 30 days. During that time, and for 30 days after the report, the company and its employees may not change the working conditions involved unless they agree to do so.

12158.s: This order changes the rules for choosing some Presidential Scholars. It lets the Commission choose up to twenty more scholars each year, from the listed jurisdictions, based on outstanding scholarship and proven ability and accomplishment in the visual and performing arts or in creative writing.

12157.s: This order creates the President's Management Improvement Council. The Council is meant to advise the President and executive agencies on management problems, management systems, and ways to improve Federal programs. Its members come from executive agencies and the non-Federal sector, and they are appointed by the President. The Council is set to end on December 31, 1980 unless extended sooner.

12155.s: This order delegates several presidential functions about strategic and critical materials to the Director of the Federal Emergency Management Agency, the Administrator of General Services, the Secretary of the Interior, and the Secretary of Agriculture. It also requires the Secretaries of the Interior and Agriculture and the Administrator of General Services to send written reports to the FEMA Director twice a year. The order also revokes one part of a prior executive order and adds two new delegated functions to FEMA's Director.

12156.s: This order makes corrective changes to two earlier executive orders. It adds the Director of the Federal Emergency Management Agency to one order and changes energy-related references in another order to use the Secretary of Energy and the Department of Energy instead of the Federal Energy Administration.

12153.s: This order exempts first-sale prices of heavy crude oil from price controls under the Emergency Petroleum Allocation Act of 1973. It defines heavy crude oil as crude oil from a property that had a weighted average gravity of 16.0° API or less in the last month before July 1979 when oil was produced and sold there. It also directs the Secretary of Energy to hold a public inquiry on whether other types of heavy crude oil should also be exempted from price controls.

12154.s: This order places several federal jobs in level IV and level V of the Executive Schedule. It affects positions in the Departments of State, Labor, Defense, and Health, Education, and Welfare, along with some Council on Wage and Price Stability jobs and the Pension Benefit Guaranty Corporation. It says current occupants of those positions do not need to be reappointed. It also revokes Executive Order 12076, as amended.

12151.s: This order gives the President’s Commission on the Holocaust more time to finish its work. It changes the deadline for the Commission to submit its final report to the President and the Secretary of the Interior to September 28, 1979.

12152.s: This order delegates certain functions that were vested in the President to the Director of the Office of Management and Budget. Those functions are the ones listed in sections 305(b), 4111(b), and 4112(a) of Title 5 of the United States Code.

12150.s: This order changes the duties of the United States Sinai Support Mission. It requires the mission to help carry out the United States proposal for the early warning system in Sinai in connection with the agreements between Egypt and Israel, under the supervision of the Secretary of State.

12149.s: This order keeps Federal Regional Councils in each of the ten standard Federal regions. The councils are made up of representatives from listed federal agencies and are led by a chairman chosen by the President. They are meant to help federal programs follow overall government policy, share information among agencies, and work with State, tribal, regional, and local officials. The order also gives the Office of Management and Budget and the Interagency Coordinating Council roles in guidance and oversight, and it revokes Executive Order 11647.

12148.s: This order moves many emergency planning, disaster relief, and civil defense functions to the Director of the Federal Emergency Management Agency. It also transfers related records, property, personnel, and funds needed to carry out those functions. The order gives the Director responsibility to set federal emergency policies, coordinate agencies, work with state and local governments, and report to the President. It also revokes several earlier executive orders and establishes the Emergency Management Council to advise and assist the President.

12147.s: This order makes Sections 2, 3, and 4 of Reorganization Plan No. 2 of 1979 effective right away. Those sections provide for the offices of Director, Deputy Director, and Associate Directors. The order applies to the United States International Development Cooperation Agency.

12146.s: This order sets up a Federal Legal Council made up of the Attorney General and representatives from other agencies. It directs the Council to improve coordination, training, shared legal resources, and management of federal legal offices, and to make recommendations to avoid inconsistent or unnecessary litigation. It also requires the Attorney General to run a litigation notice system and encourages agencies to submit some legal disputes to the Attorney General before going to court.

12145.s: This order changes the Foreign Service Retirement and Disability System to match certain changes made to the Civil Service Retirement and Disability System. It makes changes to annuities, survivor elections, annual notices, and credit for service, including credit for World War II internment and additional creditable service. It also revokes Executive Order 11952.

12144.s: This order transfers certain enforcement functions for equal pay and age discrimination in employment from the Department of Labor to the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission. It also transfers related records, property, personnel, positions, and available funds. The order takes effect on July 1, 1979.

12143.s: This order says the United States will keep commercial, cultural, and other relations with the people on Taiwan without official representation or diplomatic relations. It gives some Taiwan Relations Act duties to the Secretary of State and some to the Director of the Office of Personnel Management, while reserving other duties to the President. It also sets rules for certain contracts and says the Coordination Council for North American Affairs is the unofficial body that can make assurances and take other actions for Taiwan under the Act.

12142.s: This order puts Reorganization Plan No. 1 of 1979 into effect on July 1, 1979 and sets up an Executive Policy Board for the Alaska natural gas transportation system. The Board includes several department and agency leaders and is told to advise the Federal Inspector and other agency officers on policy, enforcement, and construction progress. The Federal Inspector must keep the Board informed and make certain written enforcement determinations public.

12140.s: This order gives each Governor the authority to set a system for allocating motor gasoline to end users. If a state or locality has a gasoline shortage that endangers public health, safety, or welfare, the Governor may set odd-even day sales rules, set minimum purchase amounts, and limit sales by time or day. It also lets Governors make other rules to carry out the allocation system and define who counts as a Governor for this order.

12141.s: This order changes rules for the independent review of Federal water resource programs and projects. After October 1, 1979, an agency may not send the Council more than one-third of the reports, proposals, and plans set for review in a fiscal year during any calendar quarter. The Chairman of the Council, or a designee, must send the review results to the agency head within 60 days and include any specific differences from approved procedures and the steps needed to bring the plan into line.

12138.s: This order creates a national policy to support women's business enterprise. It tells federal departments and agencies to help strengthen women-owned businesses through assistance, education, training, counseling, information, and procurement, and to require recipients of federal financial assistance to avoid discrimination against women's business enterprise because of sex. It also creates an interagency committee to coordinate these efforts, review progress, and report to the President.

12139.s: This order sets rules for electronic surveillance for foreign intelligence purposes under the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act of 1978. It lets the Attorney General approve such surveillance without a court order if the required certifications are made, and also lets the Attorney General ask a court for an order. It names certain national security and defense officials who may make the required certifications, if they were appointed by the President with Senate consent.

12137.s: This order places the Peace Corps as an agency within ACTION and gives the Peace Corps Director many of the President’s functions under the Peace Corps Act. It also keeps some powers with the President, including appointing the Peace Corps Director and Deputy Director and approving certain actions. The order creates the Peace Corps Advisory Council to advise the President and the Director on initiatives to promote the Peace Corps Act.

12135.s: This order continues and renames the National Advisory Committee for Women as the President's Advisory Committee for Women. The President appoints up to 30 members, including a chair and up to two vice chairs. The committee advises the President on ways to promote full equality for American women, reviews related initiatives and programs, gathers and shares information, and works with the Interdepartmental Task Force. It must finish its work and submit a final report by December 31, 1980.

12136.s: This order continues the President’s Commission on Personnel Interchange under a new name, the President’s Commission on Executive Exchange. The commission is made up of executive agency officials and private sector people appointed by the President, and the President designates the chairman. It must develop a program that places selected executives from the government and the private sector into positions in the other sector and oversee that program. Executive agencies must cooperate with the commission, and the Office of Personnel Management must provide administrative support.

12134.s: This order transfers the main responsibility for printing and duplicating support services from the Office of Administration in the Executive Office of the President to the Department of the Navy. It also moves the related records, property, personnel, and unused appropriations to the Navy. The Office of Management and Budget Director is directed to take the actions needed to carry out these transfers.

12132.s: The order creates a three-member board to investigate a labor dispute between the National Railway Labor Conference and certain of its employees represented by the American Train Dispatchers Association. The board must report its findings to the President within 30 days. From the date of the order, and for 30 days after the report, the parties may not change the conditions involved in the dispute except by agreement.

12133.s: This order assigns the Domestic Policy Staff to help the President carry out drug policy functions transferred under earlier government reorganization plans. It says the Associate Director for Drug Policy is mainly responsible for helping with those functions, including policy on international and domestic drug abuse work by Executive agencies. It also makes that official directly responsible for the drug policy staff within the Domestic Policy Staff.

12130.s: This order creates the President's Commission on the Accident at Three Mile Island. The commission is directed to study the accident, including its causes, the role of the managing utility, and the emergency response by federal, state, and local authorities. It must also review Nuclear Regulatory Commission licensing, inspection, operation, and enforcement procedures for the facility, then send a final report with findings and recommendations to the President and certain department heads.

12129.s: This order creates a Critical Energy Facility Program to help coordinate federal decisions on permit applications for certain non-nuclear energy facilities. The Office of Management and Budget is told to recommend which facilities should be included, set deadlines for federal actions, and help with joint reviews by federal, state, and local agencies. It applies to listed federal agencies and to applicants for these facilities, and it does not change the legal duties of agencies or the chance for state, local, and public participation.

12128.s: This executive order changes employee-management rules for the Foreign Service so a representative of the Federal Labor Relations Authority can take part in labor-relations decisions affecting Foreign Service employees. It also sets up an Employee-Management Relations Commission with three senior representatives and updates related executive orders to remove one reference and define which agencies count as foreign affairs agencies.

12127.s: This order makes Reorganization Plan No. 3 of 1978 effective and provides for the orderly activation of the Federal Emergency Management Agency. It directs the Office of Management and Budget to handle the needed transfers of functions from the Department of Commerce, the Department of Housing and Urban Development, and the President. The order also covers functions tied to the Emergency Broadcast System, fire prevention and control, and federal flood insurance payments.

12126.s: This order corrects Executive Order 12107 by deleting an incorrect reference to a revoked executive order. It removes the number "11512" from Section 2-101(b), which affects the Civil Service Commission and labor-management in the Federal service.

12124.s: This order changes the Generalized System of Preferences rules for certain imported articles. It updates the tariff schedules, changes the lists of articles that can get GSP benefits, and revises the list of beneficiary developing countries and territories. It also sets effective dates for these changes and removes one item from Annex II starting March 1, 1980.

12125.s: This order changes civil service rules so some handicapped federal employees can get competitive status without taking a competitive examination. It applies to severely physically handicapped employees and mentally retarded employees who complete at least two years of satisfactory service in an excepted position. The employing agency must recommend them, and the Office of Personnel Management may set requirements.

12123.s: This order delegates some presidential powers under the Outer Continental Shelf Lands Act Amendments of 1978. It gives the Secretary of Commerce and the Secretary of the Interior authority over oil pollution claims for natural resources they manage or control. It also gives the Federal Maritime Commission and the Secretary of Transportation authority over financial responsibility and penalties for vessels and offshore facilities.

12122.s: This order changes the rules for the Office of Administration. It gives the Director authority to organize the office, contract for supplies and services, and carry out certain functions under federal law. It also lets the Director appoint employees and set their pay under the listed law, while saying the Director is not responsible for the program and management duties of other units in the Executive Office of the President.

12121.s: This executive order enlarges the membership of the Energy Coordinating Committee. It adds the Director of the Community Services Administration and the Chairman of the Council on Wage and Price Stability to that committee.

12119.s: This order amends an earlier executive order to place the Counselor on Legislative and Intergovernmental Policy at the Department of the Treasury in level IV of the Executive Schedule. It also removes the listing for the Assistant Attorney General, United States Attorneys and Trial Advocacy, Department of Justice, and replaces it with that Treasury position.

12120.s: This order directs that the flag of the United States be flown at half-staff on the day of interment for the Honorable Adolph Dubs, the U.S. Ambassador to Afghanistan, who was killed while performing his duty. It applies to federal buildings, grounds, and naval vessels in the District of Columbia, throughout the United States and its territories and possessions, and at U.S. embassies, consular offices, and other facilities abroad, including military facilities and naval vessels and stations.

12118.s: This order changes how foreign assistance and arms export control duties are handled under earlier executive orders. It gives some responsibilities to the Secretary of State and the Secretary of Defense, while keeping others with the President. It also changes rules for notifications to Congress and revokes one subsection of a prior order.

12117.s: This order tells the Treasury Secretary to carry out import restrictions on goods grown, produced, or made in Uganda. It bars corporations, institutions, groups, or individuals from importing those goods into the United States or its territories or possessions, and lets the Treasury Secretary issue rules to enforce the ban. It also says the Secretary of State must advise the President if the Government of Uganda is no longer committing a consistent pattern of gross violations of human rights, and if the President makes that finding, the import rules must be revoked.

12116.s: This order lets the United States Postal Service issue food stamps through post offices in any state, or part of a state, when the proper state agency asks for it. It applies to eligible households that receive food stamps.

12114.s: This order sets procedures for federal agencies to consider environmental effects outside the United States when they approve major federal actions. It covers actions that significantly affect the oceans, Antarctica, foreign nations, or other protected natural or ecological resources. The order also lists exemptions, including actions by the President, national security actions, intelligence activities, arms transfers, export licenses or permits, and disaster or emergency relief.

12115.s: The order directs the Secretary of State to finish negotiations with Panama for the United States to administer part of Corozal Cemetery as a permanent American cemetery for the remains of United States citizens. It also directs officials to remove or reinter remains from Mount Hope Cemetery and Corozal Cemetery, unless next of kin ask in writing for the remains to stay, be moved to the United States, or be reinterred in Corozal Cemetery. The order says the United States will pay the costs it requires, while some costs for reinterment in the United States will be paid by the next of kin who make the request.

12112.s: This order establishes an official seal for the Office of Administration in the Executive Office of the President. It describes the seal’s design and says the design attached to the order is part of it.

12113.s: This order requires the Water Resources Council to set principles and procedures for federal water resource plans and projects and to do an impartial technical review of certain reports, proposals, and plans. It also requires agencies to send those materials to the Council before approval, with information on costs, alternatives, conservation measures, legal compliance, and public involvement. Before sending related reports to Congress, agencies must first get advice from the Office of Management and Budget, and Executive Order 9384 is revoked.

12111.s: This order puts the position of Counselor on Labor Management Relations at the Department of Commerce in level IV of the Executive Schedule. It also changes an earlier executive order by removing one listed Interior Department position and adding this Commerce position instead.

12109.s: This order gives the Director of the Office of Personnel Management, working with the Director of the Office of Management and Budget, the authority to set rules for comparability allowances for certain Federal physicians. The allowances are for recruiting and retaining those physicians, and until the Office of Personnel Management is established, the Civil Service Commission will use that authority.

12110.s:
This order keeps several named federal advisory committees in place until December 31, 1980. It says the head of each listed department or agency will carry out the President’s duties under the Federal Advisory Committee Act for those committees, except for the annual report to Congress.

It also revokes several earlier executive orders that created committees that have ended or finished their work. One other executive order is superseded.

12108.s: This order makes the provisions of Reorganization Plan No. 4 of 1978 take effect on December 31, 1978. It affects the changes covered by that reorganization plan.

12107.s: This order sets up the Office of Personnel Management, the Merit Systems Protection Board, the Office of Special Counsel, and the Federal Labor Relations Authority, and makes those changes effective on January 1, 1979. It also changes federal civil service rules, including probationary periods, investigations, evaluations, enforcement, and information-sharing requirements. The order revokes some executive orders and transfers certain civil service and labor-management functions to the new offices and the Director of the Office of Personnel Management.

12106.s: This order transfers certain equal employment enforcement functions from the Civil Service Commission to the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission. It changes other executive orders to reflect that transfer and updates the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission’s role in federal equal employment policy. It also revises the membership of some councils and committees to include the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission chair.

12105.s: This order sets rules for enforcing legal obligations to provide child support or make alimony payments owed by employees of the Executive branch. It gives the United States Civil Service Commission authority to write regulations for the Executive branch, with consultation from the Attorney General, the Secretary of Defense for armed forces members, and the Mayor of the District of Columbia for District employees. It also revokes Executive Order 11881, while keeping earlier regulations and actions in effect until the Civil Service Commission changes them.

12104.s: This order amends the Generalized System of Preferences to make conforming changes to the Tariff Schedules of the United States. It changes which articles are eligible for GSP benefits when imported from a designated developing country by deleting some item numbers and adding others. The changes apply to articles entered or withdrawn from warehouse for consumption on or after March 13, 1978, if the entries or withdrawals were not yet final.

12103.s: This order creates the President's Commission on the Coal Industry. The commission must review the state of the coal industry in the United States, with attention to productivity, capital investment, labor-management relations, health and safety, new technology, and federal regulations. Its five members are appointed by the President, and it must send a final report with findings and recommendations to the President, the Secretary of Labor, and the Secretary of Energy within one year. The commission is then set to end one year after the order.

12102.s: This order changes who serves on the Trade Policy Committee and the East-West Foreign Trade Board. It removes some listed positions and replaces them with the Chairman of the Council of Economic Advisers and the Director of the Office of Management and Budget on the Trade Policy Committee, and with the Chairman of the Council of Economic Advisers on the East-West Foreign Trade Board. It also deletes the Assistant to the President for Economic Affairs from the East-West Foreign Trade Board.

12101.s: This order designates the Secretary of State to carry out certain functions that the Diplomatic Relations Act gives to the President. It is meant to implement liability insurance and other requirements relating to diplomatic personnel and diplomatic missions.

12100.s: This order changes a prior executive order on the President’s Commission on Pension Policy. It says the commission’s activities were effective on September 21, 1978, and it lets the Chairman appoint a staff and set their pay, including one position at the CS-18 level. The Chairman may also obtain services under federal law if funds are available.

12099.s: This order changes Executive Order 12076 to place the Director of Policy Review, Department of Defense, in level IV of the Executive Schedule. It affects that Department of Defense position and amends the list of Executive Schedule jobs.

12098.s: This order changes the rules for the President's Council on Physical Fitness and Sports. It says the Council will have 15 members appointed by the President, and the President will choose the Chairman from among those members.

12097.s: This order sets standards and guidelines for choosing nominees for United States district judge vacancies. It says the President shall nominate a person with the needed character, experience, ability, and commitment to equal justice under law, and it directs the Attorney General to help review and recommend qualified people. It also lists qualifications for district judges, including United States citizenship, good standing in a bar, integrity, fair-mindedness, sound health, and strong legal ability.

12095.s: This order creates a three-member board to investigate a dispute between Wien Air Alaska, Inc. and certain individuals represented by the Air Line Pilots Association. The board must report its findings to the President within 30 days, and its members cannot have a financial or other interest in any airline employee organization or carrier.

12096.s: This order sets pay rates for several officials in the Industry and Trade Administration at specific levels under the Executive Schedule and General Schedule. It applies to the Senior Deputy Assistant Secretary for Industry and Trade, the Deputy Assistant Secretary for Trade Regulation, the Deputy Director of the Bureau of Trade Regulation, and the Director of the Office of Industrial Mobilization. It also supersedes Executive Order No. 11759.

12093.s: This order creates the President's Commission on the Holocaust as an advisory committee. The Commission is to recommend how to establish and maintain a memorial to those who perished in the Holocaust, and to look at ways to fund it through contributions by the American people. It also is to recommend ways for the nation to commemorate the Days of Remembrance of Victims of the Holocaust.

12094.s: This order changes rules for special pay for enlisted members on sea duty. It says eligible enlisted members with over three cumulative years of sea duty and in pay grade E-4 or above can receive career sea pay while on sea duty. It also sets pay rules for enlisted members assigned to designated places outside the 48 contiguous States and the District of Columbia, and it says a member cannot receive both kinds of pay for the same period.

12092.s: This order tells executive agencies and military departments to include contract terms that require contractors, subcontractors, and suppliers to follow set pay and price standards. It directs the Chairman of the Council on Wage and Price Stability to monitor company pay and price practices, issue rules and guidance, and publish the names of people or companies that do not comply. It also sets standards for what counts as noninflationary price and pay behavior, with exemptions and exceptions allowed.

12091.s: This order changes the Small Business Conference Commission so it has eleven members. It tells the commission to advise on a White House Conference on Small Business to be held in early 1980. It also directs the Small Business Administration to hold open regional and local meetings before the conference to identify issues and seek candidates for delegates.
