12090.s: This order extends the life of the President's Commission on Foreign Language and International Studies for five months. It also changes the deadline for the Commission to submit its final report to the President and then end thirty days later.

12089.s: This order creates the National Productivity Council to coordinate federal efforts to improve productivity in the public and private sectors. The council includes heads of several executive agencies and is chaired by the Director of the Office of Management and Budget. It works with executive agencies to find cooperative projects, identify overlapping or duplicative programs, study productivity issues, and advise the President on policy issues, including possible legislative initiatives.

12088.s: This order requires each Executive agency to prevent, control, and reduce environmental pollution at Federal facilities and activities under its control. It says agencies must comply with applicable pollution control standards, cooperate and consult with the Environmental Protection Agency and state, interstate, and local agencies, and submit annual pollution control plans with cost estimates. It also requires agencies to request enough funding for compliance, sets a process for handling violations and conflicts, and revokes Executive Order No. 11752.

12087.s: This order adjusts rates of pay and allowances for several groups, including federal employees under certain pay systems, Foreign Service employees, Department of Medicine and Surgery employees in the Veterans Administration, members of the uniformed services, and officials paid under executive, congressional, and judicial salary schedules. It sets effective dates for the adjustments, with uniformed services pay and allowances effective October 1, 1978, and other pay changes effective at the start of the first applicable pay period on or after that date. It also supersedes Executive Order No. 12010.

12086.s: This order transfers federal contract compliance functions for equal employment opportunity to the Secretary of Labor from several agencies. It also changes Executive Order 11246 so the Department of Labor is responsible for enforcing its equal employment opportunity rules for government contractors and subcontractors. The order says contracting agencies must cooperate with the Secretary of Labor and follow the Secretary’s directions.

12085.s: This order creates a three-member board to investigate a dispute between the Norfolk and Western Railway Company and certain of its employees. The board must report its findings to the President within 30 days. During that time, and for 30 days after the report, neither the company nor its employees may change the conditions that caused the dispute unless both sides agree.

12084.s: This order creates the Judicial Nominating Commission for the District of Puerto Rico. The Commission has seven members appointed by the President, and the President chooses a chairman from among them. It works when asked to help identify qualified people for a vacancy on the United States District Court for the District of Puerto Rico, gives public notice, reviews potential nominees, and reports its results to the President. Members serve without pay, and the Commission is set to end on December 31, 1978 unless the President extends it.

12082.s: This order suspends several Navy and Marine Corps promotion limits for the period from September 15, 1978, to September 30, 1979. It also makes certain Armed Forces disability retirement and separation conditions effective for that same period. The order revokes four earlier executive orders.

12083.s: This order establishes an Energy Coordinating Committee to help coordinate federal energy policies and the management of energy resources. It is made up of senior officials from several executive agencies, and it can make recommendations on energy matters that involve more than one agency. When the committee is not meeting, its work goes to an Executive Council. The order also revokes a prior order that had created an Energy Resources Council.

12081.s: This order says the Vietnam hostilities period is to be treated as ending on October 15, 1978. That ends the time when active-duty service in the Armed Forces could qualify for certain exemptions from the usual naturalization rules, including length of residence and fees. It affects people in the Armed Forces who seek naturalization based on military service.

12080.s: This order changes the process for handling approved commemorative proclamations. It says the Director must send any approved commemorative proclamations to the President.

12079.s: This order lets heads of departments and agencies carry out certain actions under the Airport and Airway Development Act of 1970 without the President’s approval. It applies to acts and instruments needed to make a conveyance requested by the Secretary of Transportation. It also revokes Executive Order 10536, as amended.

12078.s: This order creates the Presidential Commission on World Hunger to study the causes of world hunger and malnutrition. The Commission is told to review existing public and private programs, hold hearings or inquiries, and develop recommendations to reduce hunger and malnutrition. It includes presidential appointees and members invited from the Senate and House, and it must submit interim and final reports to the President before it ends.

12077.s: This order exempts Roy T. Sessums, a member of the Mississippi River Commission, from mandatory retirement. It lets him stay in that position until October 1, 1978.

12076.s: This order places several named federal positions in levels IV and V of the Executive Schedule. It also says the order does not end anyone’s appointment or require anyone to be reappointed if they already held one of those positions. It revokes Executive Order 11861, as amended.

12074.s: This order sets up a process for federal agencies to analyze how proposed federal policies may affect cities, counties, and other communities. The Office of Management and Budget must set the criteria, standards, and procedures for these analyses and help review them. Executive agencies must prepare these impact analyses for major policy initiatives and cooperate with the required review process.

12075.s: This order creates the Interagency Coordinating Council to help coordinate federal urban and regional policy. The Council includes leaders from several federal departments and agencies, and the President designates its chairperson. It works with executive agencies to involve state, county, and local governments, the private sector, neighborhood groups, and civic associations, and to solve problems that get in the way of federal coordination.

12073.s: This order tells executive agencies to give more attention to procurement set-asides in labor surplus areas. It directs the Administrator of General Services to set procurement targets, work with state and local officials, and report progress to the President every six months. It also directs the Secretary of Labor to classify labor surplus areas and give labor market data to agencies and state and local officials.

12072.s: This order sets rules for planning, buying, using, and managing federal office space. In urban areas, federal space is supposed to support city development, take local conditions into account, and give first consideration to a central business area when possible. The Administrator of General Services must issue rules, survey space needs, and work with executive agencies and other officials to meet space needs efficiently. Executive agencies must cooperate and use space economically, and a prior executive order is revoked.

12071.s: This order creates the President's Commission on Pension Policy as an advisory commission with eleven members appointed by the President. The commission must review retirement, survivor, and disability programs in the United States, including private, Federal, State, and local programs. It must develop national policy recommendations and submit reports to the President on gaps, finances, retirement ages, benefit levels, financing, and needed reforms. The commission will end one year after its effective date.

12070.s: This order changes how cost of living allowance rates are set for certain federal employees. It suspends the rule that quarters, subsistence, commissary, or other purchasing privileges must be considered, except when those privileges are provided because of federal civilian employment. It also directs the United States Civil Service Commission to study problems with carrying out the law and send its findings and recommendations to the President.

12069.s: This order changes one position listed in level IV of the Executive Schedule. It deletes "Deputy Under Secretary, Department of Transportation" and replaces it with "Administrator, Research and Special Programs Administration, Department of Transportation."

12068.s: This order makes a transfer of certain Section 707 functions to the Attorney General effective on July 1, 1978. It says those functions must be carried out using Department of Justice procedures previously followed under Section 707, and it clarifies the Attorney General's authority to begin public sector litigation under that section.

12067.s: This order gives the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission leadership and coordination duties over federal equal employment opportunity programs. It applies to federal departments and agencies that enforce laws, orders, rules, and policies covering equal employment opportunity without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, or handicap. It also requires federal agencies to cooperate with the Commission and says the order does not reduce any other person’s or entity’s duties under federal equal employment law.

12066.s: This order tells the Secretary of State to give the Inspector General, Foreign Service the duties and powers that had belonged to the Inspector General, Foreign Assistance. It says the inspector general should focus on matters that directly affect the Secretary of State’s responsibilities and should not duplicate the work of other audit, investigation, or inspection offices. It also directs the transfer of offices, property, and records to the Office of the Inspector General, Foreign Service.

12064.s: The order creates the United States Tax Court Nominating Commission. The commission has six members appointed by the President, and at least some must be Federal officials while the private members must have special expertise in Federal taxation. When asked by the President to help fill a Tax Court vacancy, it reviews possible candidates, reports up to five names, and may be asked for more inquiries and reports. Commission members serve without pay, and no member may be nominated to a Tax Court judgeship while serving or for one year after.

12065.s: This order sets rules for classifying national security information as Top Secret, Secret, or Confidential. It limits who can classify information, what kinds of information may be classified, and how long it can stay classified. It also says classified documents must be marked, and that classification may not be used to hide lawbreaking, mistakes, embarrassment, or to block public release of information that cannot be classified.

12063.s: This order creates the United States Court of Military Appeals Nominating Commission. The commission has six members appointed by the President, including the General Counsel of the Department of Defense as chair, and the private members must come from the legal profession. When asked by the President, it looks for qualified people to fill vacancies on the court, reports up to five names, and can ask executive and state agencies for information and help. Members serve without pay, may get travel expenses, and may not be nominated to the court while serving or for one year after.

12062.s: This order creates the President's Commission on the Coal Industry to review the state of the coal industry in the United States. The Commission is to study productivity, capital investment, labor-management relations, health and safety conditions, new technology, and the effects of federal regulations. It must send a final report with findings and recommendations to the President, the Secretary of Labor, and the Secretary of Energy, and it will end 30 days after the report is submitted.

12061.s: This order creates a Small Business Conference Commission made up of five members appointed by the President. The commission is to recommend dates and issues for a White House Conference on Small Business, recommend delegate candidates, and hold open regional and local meetings before the conference. It may ask executive agencies for information, and the Small Business Administration is to provide staff support and other help. The commission will end on December 31, 1979, or 60 days after the conference ends, whichever comes first.

12059.s: This order sets up a United States Circuit Judge Nominating Commission made up of 13 panels for different circuits. The panels help the President by giving public notice of court vacancies, looking into possible nominees, and recommending the people they find best qualified. It also sets rules for who may serve on the panels, what qualities nominees should have, and how the work is paid for. The order also revokes two earlier executive orders and says the commission will end unless extended by the President.

12060.s: This order changes which federal positions are listed in levels IV and V of the Executive Schedule. It adds the Assistant Attorney General for United States Attorneys and Trial Advocacy, and it replaces one title with Deputy Under Secretary for Regional Affairs. It also removes one level V position and revokes three earlier executive orders.

12058.s: This order assigns certain nuclear non-proliferation duties to the Secretary of Energy, the Secretary of State, and the Secretary of Commerce. It also says the Secretary of Energy and Secretary of State must consult and coordinate with each other and with other concerned agencies. The order revokes a previous executive order on export licensing policy for nuclear materials and equipment, and says these functions should not be delayed while procedures are being developed.

12057.s: This order changes the membership rules for the National Advisory Committee for Women. It lets the President appoint up to forty people to serve on the committee and choose a chairperson or co-chairpersons from among them.

12056.s: This order exempts G. Joseph Minetti, a member of the Civil Aeronautics Board, from mandatory retirement. It keeps that exemption in place until August 31, 1978.

12055.s: This order authorizes an export of special nuclear material to India under a Nuclear Regulatory Commission export license application. The export must not happen for 60 days.

12053.s: This order creates the National Commission on the International Year of the Child, 1979. The commission is to plan and promote the U.S. observance of that year and work with local, state, national, and international groups, including UNICEF. It is also to study the needs and rights of children, make recommendations to the President, and submit reports before it ends on April 1, 1979.

12054.s: This order creates the President's Commission on Foreign Language and International Studies. The commission is to hold hearings, inquiries, and studies and make recommendations on foreign language and international studies, the need for foreign language and area specialists, and related academic programs and support. It also reviews existing laws and recommends changes, and it is to end after submitting its final report.

12052.s: This order changes the membership of the National Commission for the Review of Antitrust Laws and Procedures. It sets the commission at 22 members and includes officials from the Justice Department, the Federal Trade Commission, Congress, a federal judge, a state attorney general, and people from the private sector.

12051.s: The order waives the application of sections 402(a) and 402(b) of the Trade Act of 1974 with respect to the Hungarian People's Republic. It affects the Hungarian People's Republic and changes how those parts of the law apply to it.

12050.s: This order creates a National Advisory Committee for Women. The committee is to advise the President on ways to promote full equality for American women, review related initiatives and policies, gather and share information, and work with an interdepartmental task force.

12049.s: This order sets up a federal Economic Adjustment Program to help with serious economic and social impacts from major Defense realignments. It directs the Secretary of Defense to identify affected communities, coordinate plans and information sharing, and work with federal, state, and local officials on assistance. It also continues the Economic Adjustment Committee and tells executive agencies to support these efforts and give priority to community requests tied to comprehensive plans.

12048.s: This order makes the International Communication Agency effective and transfers certain functions, authority, records, property, personnel, and funds to it. It gives the Agency Director responsibility for governmentwide policy guidance on international informational, educational, and cultural activities, including exchange programs. The Director is also made the main adviser to the President, the National Security Council, and the Secretary of State on these matters.

12045.s: This order makes the transfer of all functions from the Domestic Council, the Office of Drug Abuse Policy, and the Economic Opportunity Council effective. It also abolishes those offices and redesignates the Domestic Council Staff as the Domestic Policy Staff. The Domestic Policy Staff is to perform functions the President directs and assist with the transferred drug abuse policy functions.

12046.s: This order puts several telecommunications functions under the Secretary of Commerce and makes other functions part of the President’s office, the Office of Management and Budget, and the National Security Council. It abolishes the Office of Telecommunications Policy and makes the new Assistant Secretary for Communications and Information position effective in the Department of Commerce. It also moves duties over radio frequency assignments, communications satellites, emergency communications, and related policy work to the offices named in the order.

12043.s: This order changes Civil Service rules on notices for certain jobs outside the competitive service. It requires notice of decisions allowing appointments to excepted positions, and notice of changes to be published in the Federal Register. It also requires the Civil Service Commission to list in its annual report, by agency, the positions authorized for Limited Executive Assignment and Noncareer Executive Assignment.

12044.s: This order directs executive agencies to make regulations simpler, clearer, and less burdensome. It requires agencies to review both new and existing regulations, give the public a chance to comment, and consider other options before issuing significant rules. It also sets rules for when agencies must do a regulatory analysis and says some types of regulations are not covered.

12042.s: This order creates a Board of Inquiry to look into labor disputes affecting the bituminous coal industry in the United States. The disputes involve coal mine operators, coal mine contractors, and certain employees represented by the United Mine Workers of America and its locals and affiliates. The Board is to report to the President as soon as possible.

12040.s: This order transfers certain environmental evaluation functions from the Council on Environmental Quality and the Office of Environmental Quality to the Administrator of the Environmental Protection Agency. It also directs the Director of the Office of Management and Budget to take the actions needed to carry out the transfer, including moving funds, personnel, property, records, and other items related to those functions.

12041.s: This order changes the Generalized System of Preferences rules for certain imported articles from beneficiary developing countries. It modifies the U.S. tariff schedules and updates which articles are eligible for GSP benefits under different country lists. The changes apply to articles imported on or after January 1, 1976, and entered or withdrawn from warehouse for consumption on or after March 1, 1978.

12038.s: This order updates many earlier executive orders and proclamations to reflect duties moved to the Secretary of Energy under the Department of Energy Organization Act. It replaces references to the Federal Energy Administration, Federal Power Commission, Secretary of the Interior, and Energy Research and Development Administration with the Department of Energy or Secretary of Energy in those orders. It also says some Atomic Energy Commission functions go to the Secretary of Energy, and some go to the Nuclear Regulatory Commission.

12039.s: This order moves certain science and technology policy functions from the Office of Science and Technology Policy and its Director to the Director of the National Science Foundation, and it makes related transfers effective. It also gives some of the transferred functions to the Director of the Office of Science and Technology Policy and some to the Director of the Office of Management and Budget. The order abolishes the Intergovernmental Science, Engineering, and Technology Advisory Panel and the President's Committee on Science and Technology, and it establishes the Federal Coordinating Council for Science, Engineering, and Technology.

12037.s: This order exempts G. Joseph Minetti, a member of the Civil Aeronautics Board, from mandatory retirement. It extends that exemption until May 1, 1978.

12036.s: This order sets rules for organizing and controlling United States foreign intelligence activities. It gives the National Security Council review and direction over national foreign intelligence and counterintelligence, and it sets up committees and boards to help with those jobs. It also lays out duties for the Director of Central Intelligence and adds limits on some intelligence collection and special activities. It affects intelligence agencies, officials, and oversight bodies in the executive branch.

12035.s: This order changes one position listed in Level IV of the Executive Schedule. It removes the title “Adviser to the Secretary (Counselor, Economic Policy Board), Department of the Treasury” and replaces it with “Assistant Secretary (Enforcement and Operations), Department of the Treasury.” It affects the Department of the Treasury position named in the order.

12033.s: This order removes the Southeast Asia Treaty Organization and the International Coffee Study Group from the list of international organizations that get certain privileges and immunities. It says those organizations no longer exist and revokes two earlier executive orders.

12034.s: This order makes some former ACTION community volunteers eligible for noncompetitive appointment to the Civilian Career Service. It applies to people certified as having served at least one year as full-time ACTION Community Volunteers, including Criminal Justice Volunteers, Volunteers in Justice, and VETREACH Volunteers, if they were enrolled before October 1, 1976. The order takes effect 60 days after it was signed and covers people who had finished their volunteer service by then.

12032.s: This order changes the Generalized System of Preferences for certain imported articles. It amends the tariff schedules and updates lists of articles that can receive GSP benefits from beneficiary developing countries. It also changes which articles are covered for some countries and sets different effective dates for the amendments.

12031.s: This order exempts Jerome K. Kuykendall, Chairman of the Indian Claims Commission, from mandatory retirement. It lets him stay in office until September 30, 1978 instead of retiring on December 31, 1977.

12030.s: This order terminates the Federal Property Council and revokes part of a prior executive order that reconstituted it. It also renumbers the remaining sections of that earlier order. The Director of the Office of Management and Budget is directed to review federal real property policies and reports on underutilized real property, and to make recommendations to the President.

12028.s: This order sets up the Office of Administration in the Executive Office of the President. The office is directed to give common administrative support and services to units in that office, including personnel, financial, data processing, records, office, and supply services, except for services mainly in direct support of the President. It also transfers primary responsibility for those support functions, along with related records, property, personnel, and funds, to the Office of Administration, while each unit keeps responsibility for its own program and management work.

12027.s: This order transfers certain executive development and personnel functions from the Office of Management and Budget to the United States Civil Service Commission. It gives the Civil Service Commission responsibility for executive personnel selection, development, and management, as well as some work on position classification, compensation, and labor-management relations. It also transfers related records, property, personnel, and unspent funds to the Civil Service Commission.

12029.s: This order ends the Quetico-Superior Committee. It also revokes Executive Order No. 11342, as amended, and supersedes a part of Executive Order No. 11948 that had extended the committee.

12026.s: This order says certain employees of the Atomic Energy Commission or the Energy Research and Development Administration who were moved to the Department of Energy will have their service counted as Career or Career-Conditional service for reinstatement in the competitive civil service. It does not apply to employees in attorney positions. It affects those transferred employees and their eligibility to be reinstated.

12025.s: This order changes one position listed in Level IV of the Executive Schedule. It removes the "Associate Attorney General, Department of Justice" from that slot and puts in the "Adviser to the Secretary and Deputy Secretary of Defense for NATO Affairs, Department of Defense" instead. It affects the pay and placement of that executive branch position.

12024.s: This order moves certain advisory committee functions from the Office of Management and Budget and its Director to the Administrator of General Services. It also gives the Administrator the President’s functions under the Federal Advisory Committee Act, except the annual report to Congress, which must be prepared for the President’s review and transmittal. The order also revokes Executive Order 11769.

12023.s: This order sets rules for the Central Intelligence Agency Retirement and Disability System and its fund. It says some retirement money cannot be assigned or taken through legal process, except as allowed by law, and it lets an annuitant make allotments or assignments that the Director approves. It also sets deadlines for benefit applications and says salary deductions must be deposited into the Treasury to the credit of the fund. The Director of Central Intelligence may issue regulations to carry out the order.

12022.s: This order establishes the National Commission for the Review of Antitrust Laws and Procedures. The Commission is to study antitrust laws and procedures, including ways to speed up complex antitrust cases and whether certain exemptions and immunities should be kept. It is made up of 15 members appointed by the President, and it must finish its work, report to the President and the Attorney General, and then end.

12021.s: This order changes civil service rules for certain regional director and regional administrator jobs in the Community Services Administration, ACTION, the Defense Civil Preparedness Agency, and the General Services Administration. It places some of these positions in Schedule C or designates them as Noncareer Executive Assignments, depending on grade or agency. People already serving in the competitive service or in Career Executive Assignments in those jobs on November 29, 1977, are not affected by these changes.

12020.s: This order lets the Administrator of Veterans' Affairs keep paying monthly educational assistance benefits to veterans and eligible dependents when a school closes between terms to save energy. The school must show that energy use will be abnormally high or that energy supplies will be inadequate, and the closure can last no more than 45 days. The authority can be used only once in any 12-month period for each school.

12018.s: This order amends the Manual for Courts-Martial about command authority when members of the Armed Forces are prisoners of war or otherwise detained by a hostile force. It says a commissioned officer, and in some cases a warrant officer, noncommissioned officer, or petty officer, can have authority over members of another armed force when normal command lines cannot be used. It also says such a member may be a superior who can issue orders that must be obeyed under those same circumstances.

12019.s: This order establishes the Defense Meritorious Service Medal, with ribbons and other items, for members of the Armed Forces. It can be awarded by the Secretary of Defense for outstanding non-combat meritorious achievement or service in certain Defense and joint assignments. The order also limits each person to one medal, allows a device for later awards, and allows posthumous awards to a representative of the deceased.

12017.s: This order changes part of the Code of Conduct for members of the Armed Forces. It says that if a member becomes a prisoner of war, they must give their name, rank, service number, and date of birth, avoid answering further questions as much as they can, and make no statements disloyal to their country and its allies or harmful to their cause.

12016.s: This order extends G. Joseph Minetti’s exemption from mandatory retirement. It lets him stay in his job as a member of the Civil Aeronautics Board until January 31, 1978.

12014.s: This order abolishes the Distinguished Civilian Service Awards Board and changes the rules for the President’s Award for Distinguished Federal Civilian Service. It gives the Chairman of the United States Civil Service Commission a role in reviewing nominations and advising the President, but the President still selects the recipients. It also says the Chairman sets the nomination form and procedures, with certain limits on who can be recommended.

12015.s: This order lets some students in approved career-related work-study programs be moved noncompetitively into career or career-conditional jobs in the competitive service. To qualify, they must have finished the related school program, meet course requirements, be recommended by the agency where they worked, and meet other rules set by the Civil Service Commission. The Civil Service Commission must also write regulations for these student employment programs and evaluate each student's work. The order revokes Executive Order 11813.

12013.s: This order transfers certain statistical policy functions from the Director of the Office of Management and Budget to the Secretary of Commerce. It also moves related records, property, personnel, and unspent appropriations to the Secretary of Commerce. The order creates the Statistical Policy Coordination Committee, chaired by the Secretary of Commerce, to advise and assist the President on federal statistical services.

12012.s: This order changes the rules for White House Fellowships. It removes the word “young,” says applicants must be early in their chosen careers and show exceptional promise, deletes one rule, and adds “age” to the list of traits that cannot be used in the selection process.

12011.s: This order exempts G. Joseph Minetti, a member of the Civil Aeronautics Board, from mandatory retirement. It keeps him in that exempt status until October 31, 1977.

12010.s: This order adjusts basic pay and salaries for certain federal pay systems, including the General Schedule, the Foreign Service, and the Department of Medicine and Surgery in the Veterans Administration. It also adjusts monthly basic pay and basic allowances for subsistence and quarters for members of the uniformed services. The changes take effect on October 1, 1977, or on the first applicable pay period after that date for other pay adjustments.

12009.s: This order sets October 1, 1977, as the effective date of the Department of Energy Organization Act. It also directs the Director of the Office of Management and Budget, working with the Secretary of Energy and the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission as needed, to carry out the transfer of functions required by the Act. That includes transfers of funds, personnel, positions, assets, liabilities, contracts, property, records, and other related items.

12008.s: This order establishes the Presidential Management Intern Program to bring people with special training in planning and managing public programs and policies into Federal service. It lets eligible graduate-level applicants with an advanced degree apply, and the Civil Service Commission must set up the recruitment, screening, and selection process. Candidates selected for the program are appointed as interns for up to two years, and only those who complete the internship satisfactorily and meet other requirements may be granted competitive civil service status.

12007.s: This order terminates several presidential advisory committees, including the Citizens' Advisory Council on the Status of Women, the Citizens' Advisory Committee on Environmental Quality, the Advisory Council for Minority Enterprise, the Consumer Advisory Council, and the President's Advisory Board on International Investment. It also revokes or changes parts of earlier executive orders that referred to these committees. It affects the work of the committees and the agencies that were directed to support them.

12006.s: This order exempts G. Joseph Minetti, a member of the Civil Aeronautics Board, from mandatory retirement. It delays his retirement until September 30, 1977.

12005.s: This order changes the Tariff Schedules of the United States for the Generalized System of Preferences by redefining one product category. It replaces the old description with a new one for articles made with certain amounts of cotton, wool, man-made fibers, or textile materials with wool. The change applies to articles imported on or after January 1, 1976, and entered or withdrawn from warehouse for consumption on or after March 1, 1977.

12003.s: This order changes rules for federal vehicles and federal buildings to support energy conservation. It tells the General Services Administrator to set rules that raise fleet fuel economy for passenger cars bought by executive agencies, with exceptions for combat, law enforcement, emergency rescue, and some special-purpose vehicles. It also directs agencies to make ten-year plans to cut energy use in federally owned buildings and to report on progress each year.

12004.s: This order changes the process for advising the President on federal pay systems. It names the Secretary of Labor, the Director of the Office of Management and Budget, and the Chairman of the United States Civil Service Commission as the President's Pay Agent. It also gives the Advisory Committee on Federal Pay a role in giving opinions on unresolved issues, attending meetings, and helping direct the discussion. The President's Pay Agent must include a full discussion of each issue the committee has given an opinion on in its annual report to the President.

12002.s: This order delegates most powers under the Export Administration Act of 1969 to the Secretary of Commerce, with some powers kept by the President. It also gives the Secretary of State authority over efforts to secure the removal or reduction of foreign assistance to international terrorists. The order keeps the Export Administration Review Board in place to review certain export license matters and revokes several earlier executive orders.

12001.s: This order transfers certain bicentennial functions to the Secretary of the Interior. The Secretary must use existing National Park Service programs to continue commemoration of events relating to the American Revolution through December 31, 1983, and must administer existing contracts and grants of the American Revolution Bicentennial Administration. It also transfers related powers, personnel, records, property, appropriations, funds, and revenues to the Secretary, and revokes Executive Order 11840.

12000.s: This order exempts Arthur S. Flemming from mandatory retirement until June 30, 1978. It applies to Flemming, who was serving as Commissioner on Aging and Chairman of the Commission on Civil Rights.

11999.s: This order amends a prior executive order to add two positions to level V of the Executive Schedule. The new positions are in the Department of the Interior and the Department of Labor.

11997.s: This order tells the Secretary of the Treasury to set up agreements for withholding District of Columbia, state, city, and county income or employment taxes from pay. It applies to Federal employees and members of the Armed Forces. The agreements must set how withholding starts, how the amount is figured, and how the taxes are filed and paid. Agencies may not be required to collect delinquent tax debts.

11996.s: This order directs that the flag of the United States be flown at half-staff until interment in memory of the Honorable Tom C. Clark, a former Associate Justice of the Supreme Court. It applies to Federal Government buildings, grounds, and naval vessels in the United States and its territories, and to U.S. embassies, legations, consular offices, and other facilities abroad, including military facilities and naval vessels and stations.

11998.s: This order creates the President's Commission on Military Compensation, with no more than nine members appointed by the President. The Commission is to study military compensation, retirement, and related issues, hold public hearings, and make recommendations on how the system can best serve the national interest. It must report to the President through the Secretary of Defense by March 15, 1978, and it ends thirty days after submitting its report.

11995.s: This order adds the Executive Director of the Federal Personnel Management Systems Study at the United States Civil Service Commission to level V of the Executive Schedule. It affects that federal position and how it is classified in the executive branch pay schedule.

11994.s: This order changes parts of a previous executive order to match organizational changes in the direction and control of intelligence activities. It replaces several references to the "Committee on Foreign Intelligence" and "CFI" with "PRC". It also replaces "Operations Group" with "SCC" in one section.

11993.s: This order changes the rules for the United States Circuit Judge Nominating Commission. It gives the Panel for the District of Columbia Circuit the added job of recommending nominees for the United States District Court for the District of Columbia, using the same standards and procedures used for circuit judge nominees.

11991.s: This order changes the rules for how the Council on Environmental Quality issues regulations to federal agencies under environmental law. The regulations are meant to make environmental impact statements more useful, reduce paperwork, and require them to be concise, clear, and supported by evidence. Federal agencies must follow those regulations unless doing so would conflict with statutory requirements.

11992.s: This order creates the Committee on Selection of Federal Judicial Officers. When asked by the President, the Committee looks for people who may be qualified to serve as Federal judicial officers, other than United States Circuit Judges or District Judges, and reviews their qualifications. It sends the President and the Attorney General a report with no more than five names and may be asked to do more inquiries. Committee members serve without compensation, and the Committee ends on December 31, 1978 unless extended sooner.

11990.s: This order directs federal agencies to minimize the destruction, loss, or degradation of wetlands when carrying out federal land, construction, and related programs. It says agencies should avoid new construction in wetlands unless there is no practicable alternative and harm is minimized. It also limits how federally owned wetlands are leased or disposed of to non-Federal parties, and it does not apply to certain private-party permits on non-Federal property or to some emergency work.

11988.s: This order directs federal agencies to reduce flood loss and the harm floods can cause to human safety, health, and welfare. It requires agencies to check whether proposed actions are in floodplains, consider other locations when possible, and limit harm when they must work in a floodplain. It also applies to federal real property, financial transactions tied to floodplains, and certain public notices and reviews. Agencies covered by the order must update their rules and procedures to follow it.

11986.s: This order changes which Department of Defense positions are listed in levels IV and V of the Executive Schedule. It removes two positions from level IV and adds two positions to level V.

11987.s: This order directs executive agencies to restrict the introduction of exotic species into natural ecosystems on land and water they own, lease, or manage, to the extent allowed by law. It also tells agencies to encourage states, local governments, and private citizens to prevent exotic species from being introduced into the United States. Agencies must also limit the use of federal funds, programs, or authority to export native species for introduction into ecosystems outside the United States where they do not naturally occur. The order does not apply if the Secretary of Agriculture or the Secretary of the Interior finds the introduction or export would not harm natural ecosystems.

11984.s: This order revokes Executive Order No. 11460. It abolishes the President's Foreign Intelligence Advisory Board.

11985.s: This order changes parts of an earlier executive order about foreign intelligence activities. It replaces the Committee on Foreign Intelligence and the Operations Advisory Group with the NSC Policy Review Committee and the NSC Special Coordination Committee, and it sets who chairs and serves on those committees. It also deletes a statement about Oversight Board members serving on the President's Foreign Intelligence Advisory Board and removes one subsection from the earlier order.

11982.s: This order extends the reporting time for the committee that was selecting a Director of the Federal Bureau of Investigation. It requires the committee to submit to the President and the Attorney General a report listing the five people it considers best qualified and any other information they require by June 11, 1977.

11983.s: This order changes which jobs are listed in Level IV of the Executive Schedule. It replaces one Health, Education, and Welfare position with the Administrator of the Health Care Financing Administration, removes the Special Prosecutor position at the Department of Justice and the Executive Vice President position at the Export-Import Bank, and changes one Agriculture Department title to Director, Office of Congressional and Public Affairs. It also revokes the earlier order that had placed the Export-Import Bank executive vice president in Level IV.

11980.s: This order changes a part of Executive Order 11832 by replacing “45 members to be appointed” with “42 members to be appointed.” It affects the number of members to be appointed to the commission.

11981.s: This order creates the Interagency Committee for the Purchase of United States Savings Bonds. The committee includes a chairman appointed by the President and the heads of Federal agencies, and each agency is responsible for helping make the Payroll Savings Program work in its own agency. It is to help Federal agencies set up and promote plans so uniformed and civilian government personnel can buy Savings Bonds through payroll savings and military bond allotments. It also says each Federal agency shall put into operation a plan recommended by the committee as soon as practicable.

11978.s: This order changes a prior order on trade and other transactions involving Southern Rhodesia. It lets the Secretary of the Treasury exempt shipments of chromium in any form that were already in transit to the United States on March 18, 1977.

11979.s: This order changes the rules for the National Commission on the Observance of International Women's Year, 1975, to increase the number of members on the Commission. It says the President appoints up to 45 members, mostly from private life, and no more than 10 may be state or local government officials. The order also keeps the Commission responsible for organizing and convening a National Women's Conference.

11977.s: This order designates the African Development Fund and the International Fertilizer Development Center as public international organizations. That means they are entitled to certain privileges, exemptions, and immunities under the International Organizations Immunities Act. It also amends a prior executive order to add the African Development Fund and to delegate certain functions to the Secretary of the Treasury.

11976.s: This order changes which federal jobs are placed in levels IV and V of the Executive Schedule. It adds the Director of Agricultural Economics at the Department of Agriculture and the Assistant to the Secretary for Legislative Affairs at the Department of Defense to level IV. It also removes the Defense Representative, Iran, at the Department of Defense and the Deputy Assistant Secretary for Housing at the Department of Housing and Urban Development from level V.

11975.s: This order abolishes the Economic Policy Board and revokes Executive Order 11808. It also allows a new designation of the Chairman of the Council on Wage and Price Stability. The Secretary of the Treasury will continue as Chairman of the Council on International Economic Policy.

11974.s: This order changes the Generalized System of Preferences for certain imported articles from beneficiary developing countries. It amends the Tariff Schedules and updates the lists of articles that can get GSP benefits under the annexes. It also revokes Executive Order 11960 and says the changes apply to articles imported on or after January 1, 1976, and entered for consumption on or after March 1, 1977.

11972.s: This order creates the United States Circuit Judge Nominating Commission, made up of panels for the federal circuit areas. The panels help the President fill vacancies on United States Courts of Appeals by giving public notice, reviewing possible nominees, and sending the President five recommended names. Panel members are appointed by the President, serve without government pay, and must include both sexes, minority groups, and about equal numbers of lawyers and nonlawyers. Members of the commission cannot be considered as nominees while serving, or for one year after they leave.

11973.s: This order creates the President's Commission on Mental Health and lets the President appoint up to twenty members, including a Chairperson and Vice Chairperson. The Commission must study the nation's mental health needs, including service for the mentally ill, emotionally disturbed, and mentally retarded, future stress needs, research, and how programs might be financed. It must report to the President with recommendations and priorities, and it may hold hearings, request information from federal agencies, and use advisory committees.

11971.s: This order creates a committee to help identify people who may be qualified to serve as Director of the Federal Bureau of Investigation. The committee must have a chairman and eight other members appointed by the President, and none of its members may be considered for the job. It must report to the President and the Attorney General with the names of five people it considers best qualified, and it may ask executive and state agencies for information and help.

11970.s: This order creates the Presidential Advisory Board on Ambassadorial Appointments, with members appointed by the President and a chairman chosen from among them. The Board gives confidential recommendations to the President and the Secretary of State about people being considered for ambassador posts and about which posts should be filled by career or noncareer people. Board members cannot be appointed to an ambassadorial post while serving on the Board or for at least one year after, unless the President waives that rule.

11969.s: This order gives the Chairman of the Federal Power Commission the President’s authority under the Emergency Natural Gas Act of 1977, except the power to declare or end a natural gas emergency. The Chairman may pass that authority on to other U.S. officers or executive agencies. Executive agencies must help the Chairman and provide support and information when requested.

11968.s: This order sets rules for agreements on withholding District of Columbia, state, and city income or employment taxes from the pay of Federal employees and members of the Armed Forces. It says these agreements must cover when withholding starts, how the amount is figured, and how returns and payments are handled. It also says agencies may not be required to collect delinquent tax debts, and it revokes earlier executive orders on the same subject.

11966.s: This order designates the International Development Association, the International Centre for Settlement of Investment Disputes, and INTELSAT as public international organizations that may enjoy privileges, exemptions, and immunities under the International Organizations Immunities Act. It says the designation for the International Development Association does not change a specific part of its agreement. The order also revokes Executive Order 11718 and is effective as of November 24, 1976.

11967.s: This order directs the Attorney General to dismiss pending indictments and end pending investigations for violations of the Military Selective Service Act that occurred between August 4, 1964 and March 28, 1973. It does not apply to cases involving serious force or violence, or to cases involving Selective Service System agents, employees, or officers acting in connection with their jobs. It also says people barred from reentering the United States because of such violations may be allowed to reenter under the same terms as other aliens, except for those in the listed exceptions.

11964.s: This order directs the government to carry out the 1972 rules for preventing collisions at sea when they take effect. It requires Navy and Coast Guard officials to certify when certain special-purpose vessels cannot fully meet the rules and to publish those certifications in the Federal Register. It also lets the Navy and Coast Guard set special rules for ships of war, convoy vessels, and fishing vessels in a fleet, and it allows exemptions for some vessels already under construction before July 15, 1977.

11963.s: This order says the Secretary of Agriculture, after consulting with several other officials, must send Congress all reports required by Section 408 of the Agricultural Trade Development and Assistance Act of 1954. It also revokes Section 5 of Executive Order 10900 and renumbers Sections 6, 7, and 8 as Sections 5, 6, and 7.

11965.s: This order establishes a Humanitarian Service Medal with ribbons and related items for members of the Armed Forces, including Reserve Components. It may be given to people who took part in a military act or operation of a humanitarian nature after April 1, 1975. The Secretary of Defense and the Secretary of Transportation for the Coast Guard will decide which acts qualify and set the rules for awarding it. The medal or a device for it may also be awarded after a person has died.

11961.s: This order delegates the President’s functions under the International Investment Survey Act of 1976 to the Director of the Office of Management and Budget. It lets the Director assign some of those functions to other federal officers or agencies. The Secretary of the Treasury handles certain portfolio investment functions, the Secretary of Commerce handles certain direct investment functions, and the Council on International Economic Policy makes periodic reports to Congress.

11960.s: This order changes which articles are eligible under the Generalized System of Preferences. It modifies the Tariff Schedules of the United States and several annexes in a prior executive order. The changes apply to certain articles imported on or after January 1, 1976, and entered for consumption on or after March 1, 1977.

11962.s: This order creates the President's Advisory Board on International Investment. The Board is to advise certain federal officials on matters under the International Investment Survey Act of 1976 and to consider how useful the data is compared with the burden on those who provide it. The President appoints the members and names a chairman and vice chairman. The Board is set to end on December 31, 1978, unless it is extended sooner.

11959.s: This order changes how foreign assistance duties are handled under an earlier executive order. It requires the Secretary of State and the Secretary of Defense to consult with other officials on certain foreign assistance matters, and it excludes some functions from the Secretary of Defense’s delegation. It also gives the Secretary of the Treasury certain foreign assistance functions and says Treasury will continue to administer open special foreign country accounts.

11958.s: This order delegates many powers under the Arms Export Control Act to the Secretaries of State, Defense, Treasury, and Commerce. It also says the Secretary of State will supervise and direct sales and exports under the Act and consult with other agencies as needed. The order allocates funds to the Secretary of Defense for carrying out the Act and revokes Executive Order No. 11501, with some actions under that order left in effect until changed.

11957.s: This order sets who will act as Secretary of Agriculture if both the Secretary and the Deputy Secretary are unavailable because of absence, disability, or a vacancy. It says certain Agriculture Department officers with presidential appointment and Senate confirmation will serve in the order the Secretary sets, or, if there is no order, by rank and oath date. It also revokes Executive Order No. 11793.

11956.s: This order changes who may use certain powers under the Defense Production Act. It gives those functions to the Administrator of General Services and, in some cases, to the Secretary of Defense, the Secretary of the Interior, the Secretary of Agriculture, the Secretary of Commerce, and the Secretary of Transportation. For advisory committees, those powers may be used only after consultation with the Director of the Office of Management and Budget and under that director’s guidelines and procedures.

11955.s: This order allows certain NASA Space Shuttle Astronaut Program candidates to be changed from Schedule B appointments to career or career-conditional appointments if they complete two years of service, get a recommendation, and meet Civil Service Commission standards. If a candidate is not recommended or does not qualify, the candidate must be separated when the current appointment expires unless the appointment is converted another way or the person is placed in another suitable excepted position. The United States Civil Service Commission must issue rules to carry out the order.

11954.s: This order requires executive agencies to review and survey their real property holdings on a regular basis. It directs the Administrator of General Services to set standards, evaluate property use, and identify property that is not used, underused, or not being put to optimum use. It also reconstitutes the Federal Property Council and requires review of reports about federal property and possible alternate uses for it.

11953.s: This order changes emergency preparedness duties for the Energy Research and Development Administration and the Nuclear Regulatory Commission. It says both agencies must prepare plans and procedures for national emergencies, including nuclear attack, and coordinate with other federal agencies as needed. It gives ERDA duties for health and safety, nuclear materials security, production, priorities and allocations, scientific information, state relations, and international liaison. It gives the Nuclear Regulatory Commission duties for regulating licensed nuclear materials and facilities, health and safety, contingency plans, security and safeguards, scientific information, state relations, international liaison, and priorities and allocations.

11952.s: This order changes the Foreign Service Retirement and Disability System to match certain changes made to the Civil Service Retirement and Disability System. It adjusts rules for some death benefits, minimum annuity payments, annuity increases for some former participants and surviving spouses, and recomputation of annuities for retired participants who are not married. It also allows a person receiving an annuity from the Fund to make allotments or assignments from that annuity in ways the Secretary approves.

11951.s: This order changes a reference in Executive Order 11651. It replaces a reference to the old cotton textiles arrangement with a reference to Articles 3 and 8 of the 1973 Arrangement Regarding International Trade in Textiles.

11950.s: This order sets a process for the Director of Central Intelligence to check changes in a price index twice each year. If the index rises, certain annuities from the Central Intelligence Agency Retirement and Disability Fund are increased on March 1 or September 1, depending on the timing of the change. The changes apply to annuity increases after October 1, 1976.

11949.s: This order changes the title of Executive Order 11821 to "Economic Impact Statements." It also extends the date in that order from December 31, 1976 to December 31, 1977.

11948.s: This order continues several federal advisory committees until December 31, 1978. It also says that, for those committees, the head of the named department or agency will perform the President’s duties under the Federal Advisory Committee Act, except for the annual report to Congress. The order revokes three executive orders, revokes one more order on a later effective date, and says another executive order is superseded.

11947.s: This order changes how certain trade agreement reports and materials are sent to the President. It requires the United States International Trade Commission to send determinations, reports, findings, advice, hearing records, briefs, and other information through the Special Representative. It also gives the Special Representative certain presidential functions about publishing article lists, getting advice from the commission and other federal sources, and holding public hearings for trade negotiations. The order also covers work on articles that may be eligible for the Generalized System of Preferences.

11946.s: This order changes the rules for White House Fellows. It says applicants cannot be employed in, or paid for, performing a Federal function when they apply or before they begin service, with exceptions for regular members of the armed forces, special Government employees, and independent contractors or their employees. It also says White House Fellows serve for 12 months and are assigned to the White House staff, the Executive Office of the President, the office of the Vice President, Cabinet offices, or other Executive Branch offices named by the President and the Commission.

11945.s: This order directs the Secretary of Health, Education, and Welfare to develop and coordinate a national program for physical fitness and sports. It calls for public education about exercise, stronger coordination of federal services, and encouragement of state and local governments, schools, businesses, labor groups, and medical and other professional societies to support fitness programs. It also seeks to promote research and community programs for children, youth, adults, and senior citizens.

11944.s: This order changes an earlier executive order to allow the Secretary of the Interior, with approval from the Secretary of the Treasury, to delegate some authority to the Secretary of the Treasury. The authority is to be used as needed to carry out Section 606(a) of the covenant for the Northern Mariana Islands, and the two secretaries must agree on how it is exercised.

11943.s: This order corrects a typographical error in a pay schedule for the Director of Nursing Service. It changes the adjusted maximum scale of pay from "2,611*" to "52,611*" in Executive Order 11941.

11942.s: This order exempts Ashton C. Barrett, a member of the Federal Maritime Commission, from mandatory retirement. It lets him stay in that job until October 31, 1977.

11941.s: This order adjusts rates of basic pay and salaries for several federal pay systems, including the General Schedule, the Foreign Service, and the Department of Medicine and Surgery in the Veterans Administration. It also adjusts pay and allowances for members of the uniformed services, and pay for the Vice President, executive branch salaries, congressional salaries, and judicial salaries. The uniformed services changes take effect on October 1, 1976, and the other changes take effect on the first pay period that begins on or after that date.

11940.s: This order keeps federal export controls in effect even though the Export Administration Act of 1969 had expired. It also keeps existing Commerce Department rules, regulations, licenses, and other actions in force unless they are changed or revoked. The order also allows rules and actions for section 38(e) of the Arms Export Control Act to continue.

11939.s: This order changes the rules for basic allowances for quarters for members of the Armed Forces. It says that when the President allocates up to 25 percent of certain increases in basic pay to this allowance, a member without dependents who was not entitled to it will become entitled to a partial allowance. The partial amount equals the amount of the increase in basic pay that is allocated to the allowance.

11938.s: The order changes how certain cost-of-living allowances and differentials in nonforeign areas are reviewed and adjusted. It tells the Civil Service Commission to review the places, rates, and rules at least once a year. If changes in program or method would greatly lower an established rate, the payment may be reduced gradually.

11937.s: This order changes the Quetico-Superior Committee by increasing the number of members appointed under one section from two to five. It also says those members serve for the remaining life of the committee, with an added term if the committee is extended past January 5, 1977. The Secretary of Agriculture is given the President’s functions under the Federal Advisory Committee Act for this committee, except for the annual report to Congress.

11936.s: This order changes a section of a previous order about the President's Commission on Olympic Sports. It requires a second report to analyze the organizational and developmental problems in each Olympic sport and to discuss each sport's financial and facilities needs and ways to provide needed funds.

11934.s: This order changes the tariff schedules used for the Generalized System of Preferences. It removes Laos from the list of beneficiary developing countries and adds Portugal. It also changes some country names in the list, including Taiwan to Republic of China and Dahomey to Benin, and replaces Gilbert and Ellice Islands with Gilbert Islands and Tuvalu.

11935.s: This order changes civil service rules so only U.S. citizens or nationals may take competitive exams for federal jobs in the competitive service. It also says only U.S. citizens or nationals may get those appointments, though the Commission may allow some aliens in specific cases or for temporary jobs when allowed by law.

11933.s: This order revokes the earlier order that established the Federal Energy Office. It says orders, rules, proceedings, agreements, and other actions made under that earlier order will continue in effect unless amended or revoked by the Federal Energy Administration. It also says authority and responsibility tied to the Federal Energy Administration remain with that agency.

11932.s: This order says information and material obtained through the International Energy Program that needs protection for national defense or foreign relations must be classified. It gives the Secretary of State responsibility for classifying, declassifying, and safeguarding that information when it comes from the Energy Policy and Conservation Act, the International Energy Program voluntary agreement, or similar agreements. It also allows some of that information to be kept off the normal declassification schedule if it was given in confidence or otherwise qualifies for an exemption.

11931.s: This order extends the same privileges and immunities given to diplomatic envoys accredited to the United States to Permanent Observers to the Organization of American States and to their diplomatic staff. Those privileges and immunities apply with the same conditions and obligations, and they are also subject to later agreements between the United States and the Organization of American States.

11930.s: This order creates a Federal Energy Office in the Executive Office of the President and puts it under an Administrator appointed by the President. The office is made the agency to carry out the functions of the Federal Energy Administration under the Energy Policy and Conservation Act, and related authority is given to the Administrator. It also transfers personnel, property, records, contracts, funds, and ongoing orders and proceedings to the new office. The Administrator must give the Environmental Protection Agency a chance to comment before issuing proposed rules, regulations, or policies that affect the environment.

11929.s: This order changes rules for certain enlisted members who do duty as crew members on frequent aerial flights. If they are involuntarily removed from that duty with less than 120 days' notice, they are treated as having met the requirements for incentive pay for up to 120 days after notice. It also updates a prior executive order to add this new section.

11928.s: This order exempts Harold Council from mandatory retirement until July 31, 1977. It affects Harold Council, a member of the Mississippi River Commission.

11927.s: This order changes two parts of the Executive Schedule. It replaces the word "Assistant" with "Counselor" in one level IV position and adds the Deputy Assistant Secretary for Housing at the Department of Housing and Urban Development to level V. It affects those federal positions and the departments tied to them.

11926.s: This order creates a Vice Presidential Service Badge for members of the Army, Navy, Marine Corps, Air Force, and Coast Guard who are assigned to duty in the Office of the Vice President. It says the badge may be awarded to those military personnel, can be worn during and after that assignment, and only one may be awarded to a person. It also allows members assigned to that office to wear the badge starting on their first day of duty, and it keeps earlier awards under a previous order valid for wear.

11925.s: This order amends an earlier executive order about the promotion of Navy and Marine Corps officers. It changes the date in that order from June 30, 1976, to September 30, 1978. It affects the officers covered by Executive Order 11554.

11924.s: This order exempts Arthur S. Flemming from mandatory retirement until June 30, 1977. It affects him in his roles as Commissioner on Aging at the Department of Health, Education, and Welfare and as Chairman of the Commission on Civil Rights.

11922.s: This order changes how funds for the United States Emergency Refugee and Migration Assistance Fund are handled. It says those funds are automatically allocated to the Secretary of State, who may then allocate or transfer them to an agency for use under the law. The funds may not be transferred, obligated, or spent until the President makes the required determinations under the act.

11921.s: This order changes emergency preparedness duties across federal departments and agencies. It updates agency names and shifts the Office of Emergency Preparedness role to the Federal Preparedness Agency in the General Services Administration. It gives or revises emergency planning jobs for water, agriculture, transportation, health, the Environmental Protection Agency, and the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration. It also changes which agencies handle certain emergency resource and planning responsibilities, including postal service activities and civil air and highway systems.

11920.s: This order sets procedures for the President’s review of decisions from the Civil Aeronautics Board. It allows some decisions to be made public after submission, but keeps them from public disclosure for five days for national security review and possible classification. It also directs certain departments and agencies to share their views with the Board and limits private contact with people in the Executive Office of the President before the President decides. The order says it is only for internal guidance and does not give rights to private parties.

11919.s: This order makes the Attorney General the President’s designee for agreeing to certain commissioner appointments in the United States Parole Commission. It applies to commissioners chosen to serve on the National Appeals Board, as vice chairman, or as a regional Commissioner.

11918.s: This order sets up a way to pay claims for bodily injury, death, or property loss from a nuclear incident involving the nuclear reactor of a United States warship. It gives the Secretary of Defense power to approve payments from Defense Department contingency funds and to recommend that Congress provide more money if needed. It also says these duties do not replace the Attorney General’s or other agencies’ roles in litigation, and that foreign claims must be handled with the Secretary of State.

11916.s: This order changes the rules for using the seals of the President and Vice President. It allows their use in encyclopedias, dictionaries, books, journals, pamphlets, periodicals, or magazines when discussing seals, coats of arms, heraldry, or the Presidency or Vice Presidency.

11917.s: This order lets agency heads approve the use of sodium cyanide in Federal programs or on Federal lands, but only under Environmental Protection Agency regulations and restrictions. It also bars that use in areas where endangered or threatened animal species might be affected, in national parks, wildlife refuges, wilderness areas, recreational federal lands, prairie dog towns, national monument areas, and places where the public or family pets are likely to be exposed.

11915.s: This order abolishes the Energy Research and Development Advisory Council. It also rescinds section 2(4) of Executive Order 11827.

11914.s: This order directs federal departments and agencies to carry out section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973 in programs that get federal financial assistance. It tells the Secretary of Health, Education, and Welfare to set standards for who is considered handicapped and what counts as discriminatory practices. Agencies must issue rules to follow those standards, and federal aid can be suspended or ended if a recipient does not comply after a hearing.

11913.s: This order says the U.S. International Trade Commission must give certain factual data it collects from firms to the Secretaries of Commerce and Labor. The data includes sales, production, employment, and financial experience. Commerce and Labor must use that data only for their duties under the Trade Act of 1974.

11912.s: This order gives several federal officials authority to carry out duties tied to energy policy and conservation without further action by the President. It covers energy conservation planning for government buildings, federal procurement standards, contingency plans and annual reports, and some petroleum allocation and export functions. It also assigns certain Defense Production Act functions to the Administrator of General Services and the Secretary of Commerce.

11911.s: This order designates the Secretary of the Interior as the Management Authority for the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora. It also creates an Endangered Species Scientific Authority made up of qualified representatives from several federal agencies, with the Secretary of the Interior providing staff and support. The Secretary of the Interior is directed to develop a system to standardize and simplify permit requirements for the international and interstate shipment of fauna and flora, including parts or products of them. The Secretary of the Interior is also named to represent the United States under the Convention on Nature Protection and Wildlife Preservation in the Western Hemisphere.

11910.s: This order amends a prior executive order that dealt with disaster relief functions. It removes language that assigned certain legal services work under section 412 and deletes one section from that earlier order. It affects the Secretary of Housing and Urban Development and the legal services functions tied to disaster relief.

11909.s: This order exempts Walter C. Sauer from mandatory retirement until March 31, 1977. It affects Sauer in his role as First Vice President and Vice Chairman of the Export-Import Bank of the United States.

11908.s: This order amends a previous order that places certain positions in levels IV and V of the Executive Schedule. It adds the Chief Economist at the Department of Commerce and the Director of the Office of Revenue Sharing at the Department of the Treasury to those positions.

11907.s: This order delegates the President’s powers under the Export Administration Act of 1969 to the Secretary of Commerce, with the power to re-delegate them further. The President keeps the authority under Section 4(h) of the Act. It also re-establishes the Export Administration Review Board and says it is made up of the Secretary of Commerce, the Secretary of State, the Secretary of Defense, and the Chairman of the East-West Foreign Trade Board. The board may invite heads of other government organizations and agencies to take part when their matters are being considered.

11906.s: This order changes the rules for preferential treatment of eligible articles from countries named as beneficiary developing countries. It also adjusts which articles are originally designated as eligible. The changes apply to articles entered for consumption or withdrawn from warehouse for consumption on or after February 29, 1976.

11905.s: This order sets policies for foreign intelligence work to improve intelligence for national security, define roles and responsibilities, and create oversight to make sure intelligence agencies follow the law. It establishes the National Security Council, the Committee on Foreign Intelligence, and the Operations Advisory Group to guide budgets, priorities, special activities, and sensitive collection operations. It also gives the Director of Central Intelligence broad duties to oversee the intelligence community, protect sources and methods, and report to the President, Congress, and oversight bodies. The order applies to intelligence agencies and related officials in the United States government.

11903.s: This order lets the President add more members to the Economic Policy Board from time to time. It also lets the President add more Board members to serve on the Executive Committee.

11904.s: This order creates the Defense Superior Service Medal, with ribbons and other attachments, for members of the Armed Forces. It is for superior meritorious service in certain joint defense jobs and activities, as decided by the Secretary of Defense. The medal is to be awarded under Defense Department rules, with limits on how many one person can receive, and it may be awarded after death.

11901.s: This order amends a federal labor-management relations order to add the Tennessee Valley Authority. It affects the Tennessee Valley Authority by bringing it under that order's rules for labor-management relations in the Federal service.

11902.s: This order sets a process for reviewing export license applications and exemptions for nuclear materials and equipment. The Secretary of State must send each request to other federal agencies so they can give their views on whether the license or exemption should be granted. If the agencies cannot agree, the matter can be sent up for a decision, and the Nuclear Regulatory Commission must be told the executive branch position before it acts.

11900.s: This order allows the House Committee on Government Operations, or a subcommittee, to inspect certain income, estate, and gift tax returns from 1955 to 1975 during the Ninety-fourth Congress. The inspection must follow Treasury rules and the Privacy Act. The committee must give a written statement saying why it needs the inspection, unless the taxpayer has already given written consent.

11899.s: This order directs the United States Civil Service Commission and the Secretary of Labor to issue regulations under the Indian Self-Determination and Education Assistance Act. The regulations are to protect certain civil service employment rights and set up reemployment rights for employees who leave Federal employment to work for an Indian tribal organization. The Commission must consult with the Department of the Interior and the Department of Health, Education, and Welfare before issuing the rules.

11898.s: This order amends a prior executive order to add the Deputy Under Secretary for Congressional and Public Affairs at the Department of Agriculture to level IV of the Executive Schedule. It affects that specific position in the Department of Agriculture.

11897.s: This order changes a prior order on special pay for enlisted members. It says enlisted members attached to ships undergoing repair and overhaul in designated foreign duty areas can get special pay when sea-duty pay has ended, under the same conditions as an enlisted member on temporary additional duty or temporary duty in that area. It also updates a reference in another section to match this change.

11896.s: This order establishes the United States Sinai Support Mission to carry out the United States role in the Early Warning System in Sinai connected to the agreement between Egypt and Israel. The Mission is to help implement the proposal, and it is supervised by the Secretary of State. It sets up a Director, a Deputy Director, and an interagency board, and it calls on executive branch agencies to provide support when needed.
