11895.s: This order gives the United States Civil Service Commission the President’s power to designate certain people appointed by the President for training under Chapter 41 of Title 5. It also gives the Attorney General that power for people appointed as United States Attorneys and United States Marshals. It replaces Executive Order No. 11531.

11894.s: This order adds the Secretary of Defense to the East-West Foreign Trade Board. It also changes the list of ex officio members of that board. The change affects the board’s membership.

11893.s: This order transfers certain policy functions from the General Services Administration to the Director of the Office of Management and Budget. It also allows personnel, property, and records tied to those functions to be moved to the Office of Management and Budget. The order says other policy and oversight functions under the earlier orders stay in place, and it does not affect any function the law gives to the Administrator.

11891.s: This order closes most executive departments, independent establishments, and other government agencies on Friday, December 26, 1975, and excuses their employees from duty. It does not apply to offices or employees that agency heads keep open for reasons of national security, defense, or other public reasons. It also says that day counts under certain pay and leave rules for federal employees.

11892.s: This order adds the Department of Commerce and the Federal Energy Administration to the Federal Regional Council system. It keeps a council in each of the ten federal regions and keeps an Under Secretaries Group to guide the councils and help resolve policy issues. The changes affect the federal departments and agencies named in the order and are meant to improve coordination of services to the States.

11889.s: This order extends the National Commission on the Observance of International Women's Year so it can keep working through June 30, 1976, if funds are available. It also requires the commission to send a final report to the President within 30 days after that date, and then the commission ends.

11888.s: This order implements a Generalized System of Preferences for certain articles imported from beneficiary developing countries. It changes the Tariff Schedules of the United States, removes expired items for the Philippine Republic and the Trust Territory of the Pacific Islands, and adds a new "GSP" column. It also designates certain countries as beneficiary developing countries and certain articles as eligible for duty-free treatment, with some listed articles excluded.

11890.s: This order changes the procedures for handling information about United States citizens employed or being considered for employment by the United Nations Secretariat. It requires the Secretary of State or the Civil Service Commission to conduct investigations, including a limited file search for some short-term applicants and a National Agency Check in other cases. It also updates the rule on knowing membership in groups that unlawfully use force or violence or seek to overthrow the government by unlawful means.

11887.s: This order changes a civil service rule by adding the Department of Commerce to an existing rule that already mentions the Department of the Interior. It affects civil service positions covered by that rule and makes them excepted from the career service.

11886.s: This order revokes Executive Order No. 8684 and abolishes the Culebra Island Naval Defensive Sea Area. It says the Navy had stopped using targets on Culebra Island and ended weapons training near Culebra. It also says the Culebra Island Naval Airspace Reservation had already been revoked.

11885.s: This order changes a prior executive order about positions in the Executive Schedule. It removes the position of Principal Deputy Assistant Secretary of Defense (Comptroller) and puts the Defense Representative, Iran, Department of Defense, in its place at level V.

11884.s: This order sets the official coat of arms, seal, and flag for the Vice President of the United States. It says these designs are to be used only to represent the Vice President. It also revokes Executive Order No. 10016.

11883.s: This order adjusts basic pay and salaries for several federal pay systems, including the General Schedule, the Foreign Service, and the Department of Medicine and Surgery in the Veterans Administration. It also adjusts pay and allowances for members of the uniformed services, including basic pay, subsistence allowances, and quarters allowances. The order further adjusts salaries for the Vice President, executive branch officials, members of Congress, and judges. It sets when the changes take effect and supersedes two earlier executive orders.

11881.s: This order tells the Civil Service Commission, working with the Department of Justice, to issue regulations for carrying out section 459 of the Social Security Act. It applies to executive agencies that make payments based on pay from employment. The agencies must then issue their own rules and directives to follow those regulations, and the regulations must be published in the Federal Register.

11882.s: This order changes the membership rules for several river basin commissions. It adds the Energy Research and Development Administration to the Great Lakes Basin Commission and replaces the Atomic Energy Commission with that agency on the New England, Ohio, Missouri, and Upper Mississippi River Basin Commissions. The Administrator of the Energy Research and Development Administration must appoint a member to each of those commissions to represent the agency.

11879.s: This order gives the Secretary of Commerce the President’s functions under section 1441 of the Public Health Service Act, as amended by the Safe Drinking Water Act. It also lets the Secretary redelegate those functions to other government agencies, officers, and employees. The functions must be carried out under regulations or agreements that match or fit with other similar rules and agreements.

11880.s: This order sets who will act as Secretary of Commerce if both the Secretary and the Under Secretary are unavailable because of absence, disability, or a vacancy. It names certain Commerce Department officers who may serve in that role, in the order the Secretary of Commerce prescribes, or in the order they took office if no order is in effect. It also replaces Executive Order No. 11388.

11878.s:
This order ends the Presidential Clemency Board’s work and says it will stop existing after it sends its final recommendations to the President. It transfers unfinished clemency applications and related files to the Attorney General.

The Attorney General must finish the clemency process and report findings and recommendations to the President on whether clemency should be granted or denied. Executive branch departments and agencies must help with these duties, and the assigned responsibilities must be completed by March 31, 1976.

11877.s: This order changes which positions are listed in levels IV and V of the Executive Schedule. It replaces one Health, Education, and Welfare position with the Administrator of the Alcohol, Drug Abuse and Mental Health Administration, keeps the Treasury adviser position on the list without the earlier end date, and removes one Treasury office position from level V. It also supersedes another executive order.

11876.s: This order creates a three-member board to investigate a dispute between railroad carriers and certain of their employees. The board members must not have a financial or other interest in any railroad employee group or carrier. The board must report its findings to the President within 30 days, and the carriers and employees may not change the disputed working conditions by themselves during that time and for 30 days after the report.

11875.s: This order gives the Secretary of Transportation the job of studying the possible expansion of war risk insurance. The Secretary must do this with the Secretaries of State and Defense and other agencies, then prepare a report with any recommendations for legislation. The report must be sent to the President through the Office of Management and Budget within 70 days.

11874.s: This order gives the Director of the Office of Management and Budget the President’s authority under section 1012 of the Economic Opportunity Act of 1964. It lets the director direct that certain federal support functions may be made available to the Legal Services Corporation for its activities, as long as this does not conflict with other law. Those support functions must be provided under terms agreed to by the Legal Services Corporation and the federal agencies involved.

11872.s: This order amends a previous order about positions in the Executive Schedule. It adds the Executive Vice President of the Export-Import Bank to level IV.

11873.s: This order changes the makeup of the President's Commission on Olympic Sports. It says the Commission will have a Chairman and thirteen other members appointed by the President, and it asks the Speaker of the House and the President Pro Tempore of the Senate to appoint four members from the House and four members from the Senate.

11870.s: This order changes federal rules for animal damage control on federal lands. It tells agencies to manage public lands to protect animal resources and to run mammal and bird damage control programs in ways that support environmental quality and wildlife conservation. It restricts the use of chemical toxicants to kill predatory animals or other mammals and birds, with limited emergency and experimental exceptions. Agencies must issue rules to carry out the order.

11871.s: This order transfers the functions, powers, and duties for the Service Corps of Retired Executives ("SCORE") and the Active Corps of Executives ("ACE") from the ACTION Agency to the Small Business Administration. It also transfers related functions needed to carry out that change. The order says the ACTION Agency may still continue other volunteer programs, and it says volunteer rights and civil service protections are not changed by the transfer.

11869.s: This order exempts Arthur S. Flemming from mandatory retirement until June 30, 1976. It affects his service as Commissioner of the Administration on Aging and Chairman of the Commission on Civil Rights.

11867.s: This order gives the Administrator of General Services the President’s authority to issue regulations on joint funding under several federal laws. It also requires the Administrator to prepare a report for Congress and says the work is subject to the general oversight and policy direction of the Director of the Office of Management and Budget. The order supersedes two earlier executive orders and revises one section of another order.

11868.s: This order creates the President's Commission on Olympic Sports to study U.S. Olympic sports and international amateur athletic competition. The Commission must review the United States Olympic Committee, find what keeps the United States from fielding its best amateur athletes, and study ways to provide financial support for Olympic teams and other amateur athletic teams. It must also report its findings and recommendations to the President and may set up advisory committees.

11866.s: This order designates the World Intellectual Property Organization as a public international organization under the International Organizations Immunities Act. It gives WIPO the privileges, exemptions, and immunities allowed by that law. It also says this designation does not limit any other privileges, exemptions, or immunities WIPO may have under treaty or Congressional action.

11865.s: This order amends a prior executive order to increase the membership of the Executive Committee of the Economic Policy Board. It sets the committee’s members as the Secretary of the Treasury, Secretary of State, Secretary of Commerce, Secretary of Labor, Director of the Office of Management and Budget, Chairman of the Council of Economic Advisers, Executive Director of the Council on International Economic Policy, and the Assistant to the President for Economic Affairs. The Chairman of the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System is invited to attend meetings.

11864.s: This order amends an earlier order about certain positions in the Executive Schedule. It changes the listing for the Adviser to the Secretary (Counselor, Economic Policy Board) at the Department of the Treasury and says that position will end effective August 1, 1975.

11863.s: This order sets rules for agreements between the Treasury Secretary and cities to withhold city income or employment taxes from the pay of federal employees. It defines which agencies, employees, cities, taxes, and pay are covered, and it says the withholding should follow the usual fiscal practices of agencies. It also says agencies do not have to collect delinquent tax debts of employees, and it gives the Treasury Secretary power to make more rules. It revokes a prior executive order.

11862.s: This order changes a prior order on the classification and declassification of national security information. It replaces references to the Atomic Energy Commission with the Energy Research and Development Administration and adds the Nuclear Regulatory Commission in one section.

11860.s: This order establishes the President’s Advisory Committee on Refugees. The committee advises the President and federal agencies on the resettlement of refugees from Southeast Asia, including health, education, cultural adjustments, and the well-being of refugees and their families. It also helps locate private resources and work with government, volunteer, and community groups. Federal departments and agencies are directed to cooperate and provide information, facilities, funds, and assistance as allowed by law.

11861.s: This order places several named offices and positions in level IV and level V of the Executive Schedule. It affects positions in departments and agencies including Health, Education, and Welfare, Defense, Treasury, Labor, Transportation, Commerce, Justice, the Office of Management and Budget, and the General Services Administration. It does not end or change the appointment of anyone already holding one of those positions, and it supersedes Executive Order 11768.

11859.s: This order allows the Senate Committee on Government Operations, or a subcommittee it authorizes, to inspect income, estate, or gift tax returns from 1955 through 1975 during the Ninety-fourth Congress. The inspection must follow Treasury rules and the Privacy Act of 1974. The Commissioner of Internal Revenue may allow access only if the committee gives a written statement saying why it needs the inspection and showing it is within the committee’s jurisdiction, or if the taxpayer gives written consent.

11858.s: This order creates the Committee on Foreign Investment in the United States. The committee monitors foreign investment in the United States, reviews investments that may have major implications for United States national interests, and considers new laws or regulations if needed. The Secretary of Commerce must gather and analyze information on foreign investment, and other departments and agencies must provide requested information and help when allowed by law.

11857.s: This order changes Executive Order No. 11803 to let the President appoint additional members to the Presidential Clemency Board when needed. It affects the board and the President’s power to set its size.

11856.s: This order amends a Civil Service rule. It adds the Small Business Administration to a list that already includes the Environmental Protection Agency. The change affects certain federal positions covered by that rule.

11855.s: This order changes the rules for who serves on the Energy Resources Council. It names several Cabinet members and federal officials as council members, and it lets the President add other members from time to time. It also says the Chairman of the Council is to be designated by the President.

11854.s: This order waives the application of subsections (a) and (b) of section 402 of the Trade Act of 1974 with respect to the Socialist Republic of Romania. It affects the rules in that part of the law as they apply to Romania.

11853.s: This order changes the duties of the Hopi-Navajo Land Settlement Interagency Committee. The committee must develop relevant information and respond to requests from the Mediator to help compile and develop factual information for the negotiation process set up by law. It affects the settlement process involving the Hopi and Navajo Tribes and the lands covered by that law.

11852.s: The order creates a three-member board to investigate a dispute between carriers represented by the National Railway Labor Conference and certain of their employees. The board must report its findings to the President within 30 days. During that time, and for 30 days after the report, the carriers and the employees cannot change the conditions behind the dispute except by agreement.

11850.s: This order renounces the first use of herbicides in war, except for controlling vegetation within U.S. bases and installations or around their immediate defensive perimeters. It also renounces the first use of riot control agents in war, except in certain defensive military situations such as riot control, rescue missions, and protecting convoys. The Secretary of Defense must make sure the Armed Forces do not use these agents in war without advance Presidential approval.

11851.s: The order authorizes the Secretary of the Treasury, with approval from the Secretary of State and the Special Representative for Trade Negotiations, to issue regulations on certain cheeses. Those regulations would block some cheeses from member states of the European Communities if restitution payments were made for export to Puerto Rico, the Virgin Islands, other U.S. possessions and territories, any country other than the United States, or for transshipment through Puerto Rico into the customs territory of the United States.

11849.s: This order creates the Collective Bargaining Committee in Construction, with labor and management members appointed by the President. It is meant to help collective bargaining in the construction industry by handling local and area bargaining, sharing wage and benefit data, and helping resolve disputes. It also asks federal departments and agencies to cooperate with the committee and provide information and assistance.

11848.s: This order changes the reporting deadline for the Commission on CIA Activities Within the United States. It replaces the earlier time limit with June 6, 1975.

11847.s: This order exempts Walter C. Sauer from mandatory retirement. It lets him stay in his position at the Export-Import Bank of the United States until March 31, 1976.

11845.s: This order gives the Director of the Office of Management and Budget the job of sending certain special messages to the Comptroller General and the Office of the Federal Register. It also lets the Director submit cumulative reports to Congress on proposed rescissions, reservations, and deferrals of budget authority. The Director may do these functions without further action by the President.

11846.s: This order sets rules for the trade agreements program and gives the Special Representative for Trade Negotiations the main role in handling it. It also creates the Trade Policy Committee and the East-West Foreign Trade Board, and assigns them duties in trade negotiations, import relief, unfair trade practices, and the generalized system of preferences. The order revokes some earlier executive orders and transfers records from abolished committees to the new bodies.

11843.s: This order changes a prior order about certain positions in levels IV and V of the Executive Schedule. It revises one Treasury Department adviser position so that it will end on June 1, 1975.

11844.s: This order designates certain countries as beneficiary developing countries for the Generalized System of Preferences under the Trade Act of 1974. It says eligible articles from those countries may receive duty-free treatment. It also identifies other countries as under consideration for that designation, and says the list can be changed later.

11842.s: This order changes Executive Order 11803 by extending the deadline to apply for Executive clemency review from March 1, 1975, to March 31, 1975. It affects people seeking review of certain convictions and military service discharges.

11840.s: This order lets the American Revolution Bicentennial Administration carry out its work without following certain listed legal limits. It allows the agency to hire passenger motor vehicles, bypass some federal purchasing rules, and make sole-source contracts with a state or local government agency or a nonprofit organization. It also allows limited spending for official receptions and representation and for transportation and subsistence of volunteers, with legal advice and written approval before each use of the waivers.

11838.s: This order changes rules for labor-management relations in the Federal service. It updates how federal agencies recognize labor organizations, hold secret ballot elections, and handle bargaining over personnel policies, working conditions, grievances, and arbitration. It also changes when agreements are approved and what issues are not part of the duty to meet and confer.

11839.s: This order changes civil service rules for certain regional offices in the Department of the Interior and in several other departments. It puts some of these senior regional positions into Schedule C or Noncareer Executive Assignments. People already serving in covered positions on February 15, 1975, are not affected if they were in the competitive service or Career Executive Assignments as stated.

11837.s: This order changes a date in a previous executive order. It extends the deadline for people to apply for Executive clemency review of certain convictions and military service discharges until March 1, 1975.

11836.s: This order directs the Secretary of Transportation to help the transportation industry plan and test cargo security measures, collect and publish cargo loss data, and issue cargo security advisory standards. It also directs the Attorney General to coordinate law enforcement efforts against cargo theft and support financial help for state and local cargo theft programs. The Secretary of the Treasury is directed to protect cargo in customs custody, investigate certain cargo thefts, and coordinate on security measures at Customs Service facilities, while other federal agencies are urged to help prevent cargo theft in their transportation purchases.

11835.s: This order amends the Manual for Courts-Martial for military justice proceedings. It changes rules on witnesses, requests for trial by a military judge alone, explanations of an accused’s rights, guilty pleas, sentencing instructions, and rehearings. It affects accused service members, military judges, court members, counsel, and convening authorities in court-martial cases.

11834.s: This order sets January 19, 1975, as the effective date of the Energy Reorganization Act of 1974. It also tells the Director of the Office of Management and Budget to carry out the transfers needed under that law and related energy laws. Those transfers can include funds, personnel, positions, assets, liabilities, contracts, property, and records.

11833.s: This order sets rules for agreements between the Treasury Secretary and cities about withholding city income or employment taxes from pay of federal employees. It defines which federal workers and which cities are covered, and says the withholding, returns, and payment of taxes must follow the usual practices of federal agencies. It also says agencies do not have to collect delinquent city tax debts owed by federal employees.

11832.s: This order creates a National Commission on the Observance of International Women's Year, 1975. The Commission is to promote the national observance of International Women's Year and focus attention on women’s rights and responsibilities. It also directs executive branch agencies to name people to help plan and carry out domestic observance activities and to coordinate with the Commission.

11831.s: This order changes a list of federal jobs in level IV of the Executive Schedule. It replaces some position titles in the Department of Health, Education, and Welfare, the Department of Commerce, and the Department of the Treasury. It also deletes one position in the Department of State from that list.

11830.s: This order changes the Interagency Committee on Handicapped Employees to include several top federal officials, or their designees. It also says the Secretary of Health, Education, and Welfare and the Chairman of the Civil Service Commission will serve as co-chairmen, and the President may add other members from time to time.

11828.s: This order creates a Commission on CIA Activities Within the United States. The commission is to review CIA activities in the United States for compliance with federal law, check whether current safeguards are adequate, and make recommendations to the President and the Director of Central Intelligence. It may ask executive departments and agencies for information and help, and it must give the Attorney General any evidence it finds that may relate to federal offenses.

11829.s: This order creates the Hopi-Navajo Land Settlement Interagency Committee. The committee is made up of several cabinet officials and is led by the Secretary of the Interior. It is meant to gather information and respond to requests from the Mediator for negotiations under the Act. The Department of the Interior must provide administrative support, and the committee ends when the Mediator’s duties are completed.

11826.s: This order exempts Willard Deason, a Commissioner of the Interstate Commerce Commission, from mandatory retirement. It lets him stay in that job until December 31, 1975 instead of retiring during January 1975.

11827.s: This order continues certain federal advisory committees until January 5, 1977, unless they are ended sooner. It lists committees from several departments and agencies that will stay in place, including ones on environmental quality, consumer issues, physical fitness, science, exports, mental retardation, occupational safety and health, energy research, and Puerto Rico. Advisory committees created before January 5, 1973 that are not continued by this order will end on January 5, 1975 unless the Federal Advisory Committee Act ends them sooner.

11825.s: This order revokes several earlier executive orders that regulated the acquisition, holding, and other transactions in gold. It applies to those prior orders and their related sections. The revocation does not affect acts already completed, rights already earned, or civil or criminal cases already finished or started, and liabilities, penalties, and forfeitures can still be enforced.

11824.s: This order exempts Whitney Gillilland from mandatory retirement for age until June 30, 1975. It lets him keep serving as a member of the Civil Aeronautics Board during that time.

11823.s: This order abolishes the National Commission for Industrial Peace and revokes two earlier executive orders. It directs the Secretary of the Treasury to close the Commission’s affairs and finish any remaining duties under the Federal Advisory Committee Act. The Secretary must also consult with the Director of the Federal Mediation and Conciliation Service when preparing the required report.

11821.s: This order requires major legislative proposals and executive branch regulations or rules to include a statement certifying that their inflationary impact has been evaluated. It gives the Director of the Office of Management and Budget the job of setting criteria and procedures for identifying and reviewing proposals that may have a significant impact on inflation. Federal departments and agencies must cooperate with the Director and provide information requested under the order.

11820.s: This order authorizes the Administrator of General Services to carry out certain functions for the International Council on Archives meeting in Washington, D.C. in 1976. It says this delegation is for the purposes of the act and for the efficient administration of the meeting during the Nation's bicentennial celebration.

11822.s: The order sets who will act as Secretary of the Treasury if the Secretary or Deputy Secretary is absent, disabled, or there is a vacancy. It says a Department of the Treasury officer appointed by the President with Senate consent will serve in the order the Secretary of the Treasury sets, or by rank if no order is in place. It also revokes Executive Order 11680.

11819.s: This order changes the membership of the Energy Resources Council. It lists the officials who make up the Council, with the Secretary of the Interior serving as chairman. It also says the Chairman of the Federal Power Commission is invited to attend Council meetings, and the President may add other members from time to time.

11818.s: This order revokes Executive Order 11810, but it does not change any violations that happened while that order was in effect. It also continues Executive Order 11533 and related delegations, rules, regulations, orders, and licenses in force until they are changed or ended by proper authority. It affects the administration of export control.

11817.s: This order designates the United States Civil Service Commission as the agency that must concur with agency decisions setting minimum and maximum age limits for original appointments to law enforcement officer and firefighter positions. It affects agencies that make those appointments and people seeking those jobs.

11815.s: This order gives the Chairman of the National Capital Planning Commission the President’s authority and duties for setting the boundaries of the National Capital Service Area. Before doing that, the Chairman must consult with the appropriate representative of the District of Columbia government.

11816.s: This order changes a prior executive order to delegate certain reporting functions under the Foreign Assistance Act to the Secretary of the Treasury. It affects the President’s duties under specific parts of that law.

11813.s: This order lets certain cooperative education students in Federal agencies be converted noncompetitively to career-conditional or career appointments after they finish a bachelor's degree and meet other listed requirements. It covers students in a study-and-work program tied to a Federal agency, and it requires the Civil Service Commission to issue regulations and review each student's work. It also revokes Executive Order No. 11202.

11814.s: This order activates the Energy Resources Council and makes the Secretary of the Interior its chairman. The council includes several federal officials and is to develop a single national energy policy and program. Federal departments and agencies must cooperate with the council and provide help and information when requested. The Committee on Energy is abolished, and the council will end as required by the Energy Reorganization Act of 1974.

11812.s: This order adjusts upward the monthly basic pay for members of the uniformed services within each pay grade. It also raises the basic allowance for subsistence and the basic allowance for quarters for those members. The order limits basic pay so it cannot exceed the rate for level V of the Executive Schedule, and it supersedes several earlier Executive Orders.

11811.s: This order adjusts pay rates for several federal pay systems, including the General Schedule, certain Veterans' Administration medical and nursing positions, and Foreign Service officers and staff. It also says no basic pay or salary may be higher than the rate for level V of the Executive Schedule. The order supersedes several earlier executive orders and takes effect on the first applicable pay period beginning on or after October 1, 1974.

11809.s: This order creates the President's Labor-Management Committee and says the President will choose its members. The committee is to study labor and management policies and advise the President on ways to promote collective bargaining, industrial peace, wage and price policies, higher living standards, and productivity. It also encourages labor-management committees in industries or sectors where they are appropriate, and it directs federal departments and agencies to help the committee.

11810.s: This order continues federal export controls even though the Export Administration Act of 1969 had expired. It keeps the Commerce Department’s export rules, orders, licenses, and other actions in force until they are amended or revoked. It affects people and companies subject to those export regulations.

11808.s: This order creates the President's Economic Policy Board and an Executive Committee to advise the President on national and international economic policy. The board is made up of top cabinet officials and other senior economic advisers. It also gives the board a role in coordinating and carrying out economic policy, and directs departments and agencies to cooperate and provide assistance and information as requested.

11807.s: This order requires Federal agencies to set up and maintain occupational safety and health programs for their workers. Agency heads must designate an official, keep records, inspect workplaces, provide training, and report to the Secretary of Labor each year. The Secretary must issue detailed guidelines, help agencies, evaluate their programs, and send reports to the President. It also continues the Federal Advisory Council on Occupational Safety and Health.

11805.s: This order says tax returns may be delivered to or inspected by the President only after the President makes a written request signed personally. The request must name the taxpayer, the kind of return, and the tax period covered. The President may also name certain White House Office employees to receive or inspect the return, but they may not share it except to the President unless he gives written direction.

11806.s: This order changes an earlier order about the National Commission for the Observance of World Population Year. It sets a new deadline for the Commission to finish its work and report to the President by June 30, 1975, when it will end.

11804.s: This order gives the Director of Selective Service the power to set up, carry out, and run the alternate service program for Vietnam era draft evaders and military deserters. The Director may do this without further approval from the President. Executive branch departments and agencies must help when the Director asks, as allowed by law.

11803.s: This order creates a 9-member Presidential Clemency Board in the Executive Office of the President. The board will review applications for executive clemency from some people convicted of certain Military Selective Service Act violations or certain military offenses, and from some people with punitive or undesirable discharges or confinement sentences for those offenses. It must report its findings and recommendations to the President, and it gives priority to applicants who are currently confined and have no outstanding criminal charges.

11802.s: This order directs that the flag of the United States be flown at half-staff until the day of interment in memory of General Creighton W. Abrams. It applies to federal buildings, grounds, and naval vessels in the United States, its territories and possessions, and to U.S. embassies, consular offices, military facilities, and naval vessels and stations abroad.

11800.s: This order gives certain Cabinet secretaries the power to carry out the President’s authority over aviation career incentive pay, without needing further presidential approval. It applies to regular and reserve officers of the uniformed services, including flight surgeons and other medical officers, for frequent and regular flying duty. The order is effective as of June 1, 1974.

11799.s: This order suspends a rule that had limited the number of Navy and Marine Corps officers below the appropriate promotion zone who could be recommended for promotion as best fitted. The suspension lasts until June 30, 1976. It affects Navy and Marine Corps officers who may be recommended for promotion from below the promotion zone.

11797.s: This order gives the Secretary of Agriculture the President’s authority to handle reporting rules and prepare and submit annual reports to Congress about the location of new Federal facilities in rural areas. Departments and agencies must cooperate with the Secretary of Agriculture in making these reports.

11798.s: This order revokes Executive Order No. 11796, but it does not affect violations that happened while that order was in effect. It also keeps Executive Order No. 11533, along with related delegations, rules, regulations, orders, licenses, and other administrative actions, in full force and effect until they are amended, modified, or terminated by proper authority.

11796.s: This order keeps export controls in place even though the Export Administration Act of 1969 had expired. It says the existing rules and regulations issued by the Secretary of Commerce will stay in effect until changed or revoked. It also keeps export-related regulations tied to earlier orders in force.

11795.s: This order gives the Secretary of Housing and Urban Development authority to carry out most powers under the Disaster Relief Act of 1974 without further presidential action. It keeps certain powers with the President, including declaring emergencies and major disasters, and it gives the Secretary of Defense authority over disaster warning communications and the Secretary of Agriculture authority over food coupons and distribution. The Secretary of Housing and Urban Development must also prepare a plan for legal services and may delegate some duties to other executive branch agency heads with their consent.

11793.s: This order sets who may act as Secretary of Agriculture if the Secretary and Under Secretary are absent, sick, resign, or die. It names Assistant Secretaries of Agriculture and the General Counsel of the Department of Agriculture in the order the Secretary may set, or in order of their taking office if no order is in effect. It also revokes a previous executive order on the same subject.

11794.s: This order revokes Executive Order No. 10958, which related to Civil Defense medical and food stockpiles. It says this revocation does not change civil defense and emergency preparedness planning duties already assigned to the Secretary of Agriculture, the Secretary of Health, Education, and Welfare, the Secretary of Defense, or the Administrator of General Services.

11791.s: This order exempts Kenneth H. Tuggle, a Commissioner of the Interstate Commerce Commission, from mandatory retirement for age. The exemption lasts until December 31, 1975.

11792.s: This order abolishes the Advisory Council on Intergovernmental Personnel Policy effective July 20, 1974. It also revokes Executive Order No. 11607 of July 19, 1971.

11789.s: This order renames the East-West Trade Policy Committee as the President's Committee on East-West Trade Policy and keeps it in place. It lists the committee members and names the Counsellor to the President for Economic Policy as chairman, with the Secretary of the Treasury and the Secretary of Commerce as co-vice chairmen and co-chairmen of the Office of East-West Trade. It also keeps the committee's executive secretary and working group in place, and says major trade initiatives will still be handled under chairmen chosen for each negotiation.

11790.s: This order puts the Federal Energy Administration Act of 1974 into effect on June 27, 1974. It gives the Administrator of the Federal Energy Administration authority under the Emergency Petroleum Allocation Act of 1973, the Economic Stabilization Act of 1970, and parts of the Defense Production Act of 1950 that relate to energy. It also abolishes the Federal Energy Office and transfers its personnel, property, records, and funds to the Administrator.

11788.s: This order ends the Cost of Living Council and gives the Secretary of the Treasury the remaining powers and duties needed to finish the Economic Stabilization Program. It allows the Secretary or a designee to handle pending civil or criminal actions, review pay and price adjustments from before May 1, 1974, and manage records, property, and other administrative matters. It also abolishes several committees and boards, and it creates the President's Committee on Food to review government activities affecting food costs and prices until December 31, 1974.

11787.s: This order revokes Executive Order No. 10987, which had covered agency systems for appeals from adverse actions. It says the appeals system set up by the Civil Service Commission will be the only appeal system for covered employees, unless a statute says otherwise. It also says the order applies to adverse actions that take effect on or after the 90th day after issuance, and earlier appeals filed under the old system must be finished under that system.

11786.s: This order authorizes the House Committee on the Judiciary, or a subcommittee, to inspect President Nixon’s tax returns for 1969 through 1972. It also allows the committee to inspect related records and to receive copies of the returns on request. The inspection must follow Treasury rules for committee inspection of tax returns.

11785.s: This order changes security rules for government employment. It revokes Executive Order 9835, ends the designation of organizations under Executive Order 10450, and abolishes the list of organizations that had been designated. It also updates the membership rule to cover knowing membership with intent to further the aims of groups that use or advocate force or violence to stop others from exercising their rights or to overthrow the government by unlawful means. It revokes Executive Order 11605.

11784.s: This order gives the Administrator of General Services the President’s power to issue regulations on joint funding under the Rehabilitation Act of 1973 and the Domestic Volunteer Service Act of 1973. The Administrator must do this without further approval from the President, but under the general oversight of the Director of the Office of Management and Budget. It also amends a prior executive order to remove a related reference to the Rehabilitation Act.

11782.s: This order establishes the Federal Financing Bank Advisory Council. The council includes several Cabinet officers, the President of the Export-Import Bank of the United States, and the Postmaster General. It will give advice and assistance to the Federal Financing Bank’s board on how the act is administered and serve as a coordinating forum for broader understanding and support for the bank. The Department of the Treasury must provide administrative support, to the extent allowed by law.

11783.s: The order creates a three-member board to investigate a dispute between carriers represented by the National Railway Labor Conference and certain employees represented by the Sheet Metal Workers' International Association. The board must report its findings to the President within thirty days. During that time, and for thirty days after the report is made, the carriers and their employees may not change the conditions out of which the dispute arose except by agreement.

11781.s: This order keeps the Cost of Living Council working through June 30, 1974, so it can finish its duties and keep handling matters tied to wages and prices before May 1, 1974. It also allows certain enforcement actions and reviews to continue for acts or proceedings not yet finished by April 30, 1974. The order does not allow new mandatory economic controls on prices, rents, wages, salaries, dividends, or interest rates. It also continues some related committees and abolishes others.

11780.s: This order amends a prior executive order to add the Principal Deputy Assistant Secretary (International Security Affairs) at the Department of Defense to level V of the Executive Schedule. It affects that specific federal position by placing it in that pay level.

11779.s: This order gives the Secretary of State the President’s authority under section 9 of the United Nations Participation Act. It changes a prior executive order to say the Secretary of State may use that authority.

11778.s: This order changes section 2 of Executive Order 11692. It says the order takes effect on October 1, 1972. It relates to the monthly basic pay rules for members of the Uniformed Services.

11777.s: This order changes Executive Order 11691. It says that order takes effect on the first day of the first applicable pay period beginning on or after October 1, 1972, for the statutory pay systems covered by it.

11776.s: This order keeps the President's Committee on Mental Retardation in operation and expands its membership and duties. The committee is to advise the President and the Secretary of Health, Education, and Welfare on national efforts, Federal programs, and coordination with State, local, and private groups. It must also report each year and may receive staff support from the Department of Health, Education, and Welfare.

11775.s: This order abolishes the Energy Policy Office and supersedes the earlier order that created it. It also updates the Oil Policy Committee so the Administrator of the Federal Energy Office serves as chairman, and it continues that committee. The Administrator of General Services must wind up the office’s affairs, and any unobligated funds left over must be returned to the President’s Emergency Fund.

11774.s: This order changes one Department of Defense job title in Executive Order 11768. It replaces the position of Director of Program Analysis and Evaluation with Director of Telecommunications and Command and Control Systems. It affects that Department of Defense position in the Executive Schedule.

11773.s: This order revokes two earlier executive orders. It also takes away the Department of Agriculture’s authority to inspect income tax returns.

11771.s: This order gives the Liaison Office of the People's Republic of China in Washington, D.C. the same privileges and immunities as diplomatic missions accredited to the United States. It also applies to the office's members who are notified to and accepted by the Secretary of State, with the same conditions and obligations.

11772.s: This order lets the Secretary of State make a certification that it is in the national interest not to move certain money to the Fishermen's Protective Fund or the separate account set up under the law. The Secretary may do this without any ratification or other action by the President, and it affects funds appropriated by Congress for assistance under the Foreign Assistance Act of 1961.

11769.s: This order tells the heads of executive departments and agencies to take action so they can comply with the Federal Advisory Committee Act. It assigns the Administrator of General Services to prepare the annual report to Congress required by the act. It also gives the Director of the Office of Management and Budget authority to carry out certain functions under the act and set management rules for covered advisory committees.

11770.s: This order authorizes the Secretary of the Interior to carry out certain functions for the International Symposium on Geothermal Energy. The symposium is to be held in San Francisco, California, in May 1975. The order says this delegation is for the purposes of the act and for efficient administration of the symposium.

11767.s: This order designates the Organization of African Unity as a public international organization. It gives the OAU the privileges, exemptions, and immunities provided by the International Organizations Immunities Act.

11768.s: This order places certain offices and positions in levels IV and V of the Executive Schedule. It covers jobs in several departments and agencies, including Health, Education, and Welfare; Treasury; Labor; Defense; Commerce; State; Justice; and the General Services Administration. It also says the order does not end or change the appointment of anyone already in one of those positions, and it supersedes Executive Order No. 11708.

11766.s: This order changes the tax rate on certain acquisitions of stock of foreign issuers and debt obligations of foreign obligors to zero percent. It applies to acquisitions made after January 29, 1974, with a special rule for trades made under a registered national securities exchange or the National Association of Securities Dealers, Inc. It affects United States persons who acquire those stocks or debt obligations.

11764.s: This order gives the Attorney General the main role in coordinating enforcement of Title VI in federally assisted programs. It says federal departments and agencies must work with the Attorney General, follow standards and procedures he sets, and report information he asks for. It also gives the Attorney General authority to approve rules, regulations, and orders under Title VI.

11765.s: This order sets rules for selling Navy vessels that have been removed from the Naval Vessel Register and are not covered by other law. It allows those vessels to be sold at public sale to the highest acceptable bidder after at least 30 days of advertising, or by negotiation if the Navy Secretary or designee decides readvertising would serve no useful purpose. Each bid or offer must include a cash deposit of at least 10 percent, or a deposit bond, and no other bond is required.

11762.s: This order gives the Administrator of Veterans' Affairs the power to carry out certain authority over grants-in-aid to the Republic of the Philippines for medical care and treatment of veterans, without further action by the President. It says the Secretary of State will negotiate the agreement and any changes with the Republic of the Philippines. Any rules made under this delegated power must first be approved by the Director of the Office of Management and Budget.

11763.s: This order creates a National Commission for the Observance of World Population Year 1974. The commission is to promote observance of the year in the United States and build a better understanding of population growth and its effects on human life. It may gather and share information, issue reports, and work with groups and government agencies. The commission is to finish its work by the end of 1974 and report to the President.

11761.s: This order sets up coordination of federal education programs across federal agencies. It directs the Secretary of Health, Education, and Welfare and the Assistant Secretary for Education to identify the nation’s education needs and goals, study the effects of federal activities, and make recommendations and advice. Federal agencies must share information, work together to avoid duplication, and help with studies and analyses on education matters.

11760.s: This order designates the European Space Research Organization as a public international organization under the International Organizations Immunities Act. It gives ESRO the privileges, exemptions, and immunities provided by that law. It also supersedes two earlier executive orders.

11759.s: This order sets the pay for the Deputy Assistant Secretary for Domestic and International Business at the rate for level V of the Executive Schedule. It also sets the pay for the Deputy Assistant Secretary for Domestic Commerce at the highest rate for grade 18 of the General Schedule. The order supersedes Executive Order 11567.

11758.s: This order gives the Director of the Office of Management and Budget and the Secretary of Labor authority the President had under the Rehabilitation Act of 1973. The Secretary of Labor may issue rules for the employment of qualified handicapped individuals under Federal procurement contracts and set guidelines for waivers. Federal agencies may exempt some contracts from section 503, and procurement rules must require covered contracts to include compliance provisions.

11757.s: This order exempts Lawrence Quincy Mumford, the Librarian of Congress, from mandatory retirement for age. It keeps him in that job until December 31, 1974.

11756.s: This order exempts Whitney Gillilland, the Vice Chairman of the Civil Aeronautics Board, from mandatory retirement for age. It lets him stay in the job until December 31, 1974.

11755.s: This order replaces an older rule and allows non-Federal prison inmates to work on Federal contracts under set conditions. It applies to executive branch contracts in States and certain U.S. jurisdictions, and it limits when people serving prison sentences may be employed. It does not bar work by people on parole or probation, people who have been pardoned or have served their terms, or some inmates in approved work-release programs.

11754.s: This order changes the tax rates on acquisitions of stock of foreign issuers and debt obligations of foreign obligors. It sets a 3.75 percent tax on stock acquisitions and new rates for debt obligations based on time left until maturity. It applies to U.S. persons making those acquisitions after December 31, 1973, under the stated rules.

11753.s: This order creates the President's Export Council in the Department of Commerce. The Council is a national advisory body that advises the President and other federal groups on export trade and export expansion. It is made up of business and industry წარმომადგენatives appointed by the President, and members serve without pay, though they may receive travel expenses if allowed by law. The order also abolishes the Interagency Committee on Export Expansion and revokes two earlier executive orders.

11752.s: This order directs federal agencies to prevent and control environmental pollution at federal facilities. It requires them to meet applicable air, water, solid waste, noise, radiation, and pesticide standards, and to work with the Environmental Protection Agency and state and local agencies. It also allows exemptions in national security or other extraordinary cases, with special review and reporting rules.

11751.s: This order gives the Secretary of Transportation power to grant exemptions from daylight saving time or to realign time zone limits. A state governor must ask for the change and say it is needed to avoid undue hardship or to conserve fuel. The Secretary must weigh uniform time, commerce, possible energy savings, hardship for large groups, and the national energy conservation program. The Secretary may consult other federal agencies for information and advice.

11749.s: This order gives the Secretary of Housing and Urban Development many disaster relief powers that had been held by the President or the Office of Emergency Preparedness. It also gives the Secretary of Defense power over civil defense communications for disaster warnings, and the Secretary of Agriculture power over food coupons and surplus commodities. It creates the National Council on Federal Disaster Assistance to advise and assist the Secretary, and it supersedes several earlier executive orders.

11750.s: This order closes most executive departments, independent establishments, and other government agencies on Monday, December 24, 1973, and Monday, December 31, 1973. Their employees are excused from duty on those days. Offices in the Department of State, the Department of Defense, and other agencies may stay open if agency heads decide they should remain open for national security, defense, or other public reasons. The order also says those two days count for pay and leave rules under certain laws and similar statutes.

11748.s: This order creates a Federal Energy Office in the Executive Office of the President. It gives the Office’s Administrator authority over energy matters, including production, conservation, use, control, distribution, and allocation of energy, and lets the Administrator make reports to Congress. It also directs executive branch departments and agencies to provide assistance and information, and allows some of the Administrator’s authority to be passed on to other officers or agencies.

11746.s: This order changes a section of a previous executive order about emergency preparedness functions for the Treasury Department. It assigns the Treasury Department responsibilities for administering customs laws, tax laws, laws on alcohol and tobacco, firearms laws, and Title XI on regulation of explosives.

11747.s: This order gives the Director of the Office of Management and Budget the President’s power to review plans and revisions from river basin commissions and send them to Congress with recommendations. It also lets that official approve rules, procedures, arrangements, and provisions for coordinating federal planning assistance programs and related federal agencies. The Chairman of the Water Resources Council is also given the power to approve standards and procedures under the Water Resources Planning Act.

11744.s: This order approves a cost-of-living allowance for employees of the Joint Federal-State Land Use Planning Commission for Alaska. It applies to employees actually serving in Alaska and is retroactive to when the first Commission employee was hired. The order also says the allowance will follow certain conditions tied to the Commission’s pay scale and to the rules for similar federal employees in Alaska.

11743.s: This order keeps the Oil Policy Committee in place and changes how it is set up. It makes the Director of the Energy Policy Office the chairman and lists the other officials who serve on the committee. It also transfers certain personnel, property, records, and funds tied to the committee’s functions. Executive Order 11703 is superseded.

11745.s: This order creates a board of three members to investigate a dispute between the Long Island Rail Road and certain of its employees represented by the Brotherhood of Railroad Signalmen, AFL-CIO. The board must report its findings to the President within thirty days. For thirty days after the report, the rail road and its employees may not change the conditions that led to the dispute, except by agreement.

11741.s: This order directs Federal departments and agencies in the executive branch to use the official American Revolution Bicentennial symbol on publications, envelopes, stationery, and other appropriate documents when allowed by law and considered appropriate. It also says the symbol may be used in one color or in the three colors set in the Commission’s Graphics Manual, and that this use continues through December 31, 1976.

11742.s: This order gives the Secretary of State the power to handle certain presidential functions for international agreements about improving the environment. The Secretary of State must work with the Council on Environmental Quality, the Environmental Protection Agency, and other appropriate federal agencies. These functions can be carried out without further approval by the President.

11739.s: This order adjusts basic pay rates for the General Schedule and for certain positions in the Department of Medicine and Surgery of the Veterans' Administration. It also adjusts per annum salaries for Foreign Service officers and for staff officers and employees. The new rates are limited by the pay cap for level V of the Executive Schedule.

11740.s: This order raises the monthly basic pay rates for members of the uniformed services within each pay grade. It applies to members of the uniformed services and takes effect on October 1, 1973.

11738.s: This order says federal agencies must carry out contracts, grants, and loans in a way that helps enforce the Clean Air Act and the Federal Water Pollution Control Act. It lets the Environmental Protection Agency administrator list facilities tied to certain convictions and remove them when the problem is corrected. Federal agencies generally may not use or support designated facilities, and contracts or assistance must include compliance requirements. The order also allows some exemptions, requires reports to Congress, and does not apply to facilities outside the United States.

11737.s: This order enlarges the Upper Mississippi River Basin Commission to include parts of Minnesota and North Dakota that are drained by the Souris-Red-Rainy River system. It also adds North Dakota to the Commission’s membership and says the Commission should consult nearby states on matters that could affect water and related land resources. The order transfers the funds, property, records, employees, assets, and obligations of the Souris-Red-Rainy River Basins Commission to the Upper Mississippi River Basin Commission.

11736.s: This order changes which federal positions are placed in levels IV and V of the Executive Schedule. It renames some positions and adds others, including the Special Prosecutor and the Associate Attorney General at the Department of Justice, the Commissioner General of the International Exposition on the Environment at the Department of Commerce, and the Associate Administrator for Federal Management Policy at the General Services Administration. It also changes the titles for the National Institutes of Health and certain Treasury and Transportation positions.

11735.s: This order assigns several duties under the Federal Water Pollution Control Act to the Environmental Protection Agency, the Coast Guard, the Federal Maritime Commission, and the Council on Environmental Quality. It lets these agencies act on oil and hazardous substance discharges, set related rules and procedures, inspect vessels and cargo, and handle the National Contingency Plan. It also designates the Coast Guard as the agency to receive discharge notices.

11734.s: This order changes the membership list for the President’s Committee on the National Medal of Science. It removes the words “The President’s Science Adviser” and replaces them with “The Science Adviser.”

11732.s: This order lets the Secretary of Housing and Urban Development do certain presidential duties under the National Housing Act without getting approval from the President first. It covers authorizing the Government National Mortgage Association to buy mortgages for its special assistance functions and deciding that such action is in the public interest.

11733.s: This order amends rules for disability retirement pay, hospitalization, and re-examination for members and former members of the uniformed services. It changes who has the duties, powers, and functions for hospitalization when people choose uniformed services facilities, subject to space, facilities, and medical and dental staff. It also replaces "Coast and Geodetic Survey" with "National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (formerly Coast and Geodetic Survey)" in two parts of the earlier order.

11730.s: This order changes the price freeze on commodities and services, removing the freeze on food except beef and keeping the freeze in other parts of the economy through August 12, 1973. It also directs the Cost of Living Council to publish proposed plans for new controls in other sectors for public comment. The order affects the food industry and other businesses covered by the price freeze.

11731.s: This order keeps Federal Regional Councils in each of the ten federal regions and changes their membership. It broadens the councils' work to include coordinating federal program assistance to state and local governments, along with grant assistance. It also continues the Under Secretaries Group for Regional Operations, changes its membership, and makes the Deputy Director of the Office of Management and Budget its chairman.

11728.s: This order changes a rule for incentive pay for hazardous duty involving aerial flight. It allows hours of aerial flight from the previous five calendar months to count toward the monthly flight requirement if they have not already been used for incentive pay.

11729.s: This order changes a prior order about the National Commission for Industrial Peace. It directs the Department of Labor, the Department of Commerce, and the Cost of Living Council to provide support and technical assistance for the Commission, to the extent allowed by law. It also says the Cost of Living Council must do other work for the Commission as required by the Federal Advisory Committee Act.

11726.s: This order creates an Energy Policy Office in the Executive Office of the President. The Director is the President’s main adviser on energy matters and must identify energy problems, make policy recommendations, work with agencies and outside groups, and help oversee energy policies and plans. The Director must also report to the President for transmission to Congress, and the order abolishes the Special Committee on Energy and the National Energy Office.

11727.s: This order directs the Attorney General to coordinate executive branch work on laws about narcotics and dangerous drugs. It also revokes two earlier orders, abolishes the Office for Drug Abuse Law Enforcement and the Office of National Narcotics Intelligence, and reassigns their functions. Federal departments and agencies must help the Attorney General when asked, to the extent allowed by law.

11725.s: This order transfers several emergency preparedness functions from the Office of Emergency Preparedness to the Secretary of Housing and Urban Development, the Secretary of the Treasury, and the Administrator of General Services. It covers disaster relief, import investigations, and other emergency preparedness duties listed in the order, and keeps existing rules and actions in effect until changed by the proper official. It also directs federal departments and agencies to cooperate and revokes two sections of Executive Order 11051.

11724.s: This order creates a Federal Property Council in the Executive Office of the President. The Council reviews federal real property policies and makes recommendations to the President, and it also looks at reports about unused, underused, or excess property. The Administrator of General Services must survey executive agency property holdings, report properties that may be excess, and work with the Council.

11722.s: This order makes certain income, estate, and gift tax returns for 1964 through 1974 open to inspection by the Committee on Internal Security of the House of Representatives, or a subcommittee it authorizes. The inspection is for investigations allowed under House rules and must follow Treasury rules for congressional review of tax returns.

11723.s: The order sets a 60-day freeze on the prices of most commodities and services, but it does not apply to raw agricultural products. Sellers must prepare and keep a public list of freeze prices, and they must keep supporting records available for review. It does not extend to wages and salaries, interest and dividends, or rents under the limits stated in earlier orders.

11721.s: This order directs federal agencies to use pay rules to keep and motivate good federal workers and to make sure pay is fair and based on the work done. It gives the Office of Management and Budget and the Civil Service Commission roles in the annual pay review process, and it assigns some agencies to set rules for new pay rates under their systems. It also sets rules for special higher pay rates, step-increases, and pay classification under the General Schedule.

11720.s: This order makes certain income, excess-profits, estate, gift, and excise tax returns for 1939 to 1974 open for inspection by the Senate Committee on Commerce or its authorized subcommittee. The inspection is for its investigation of the effects of organized criminal activity on interstate and foreign commerce and must follow Treasury rules on inspecting congressional returns.

11718.s: This order designates INTELSAT as an international organization entitled to certain privileges, exemptions, and immunities under the International Organizations Immunities Act. It also gives INTELSAT's Board of Governors representatives and their alternates the same privileges, exemptions, and immunities that earlier representatives had. The order revokes two earlier executive orders, except for the rule applied to those representatives.

11719.s: This order makes certain income, estate, and gift tax returns for the years 1960 to 1974 open to inspection by the House Committee on Public Works, or a subcommittee it authorizes. The inspection is for that committee’s investigation and must follow the rules set by the Secretary of the Treasury.

11717.s: This order transfers some management, procurement, property, and computer-related functions from the Office of Management and Budget to the General Services Administration and the Department of Commerce. The General Services Administration gets functions tied to certain management and procurement branches, and the Department of Commerce gets functions tied to government-wide automatic data processing standards. The Office of Management and Budget keeps its general oversight role and certain fiscal control functions, and some personnel, property, records, and funds are to be moved as the director decides.

11716.s: This order changes an earlier executive order about incentive pay for hazardous duty. It lets members of a submarine operational command staff use certain extra underway hours from the previous five months to meet the current month’s 48-hour requirement. It affects service members who qualify for this incentive pay.

11715.s: This order changes which positions are placed in levels IV and V of the Executive Schedule. It replaces some listed jobs, adds the Deputy Under Secretary for Legislative Affairs at the Department of Commerce to level IV, and removes one Department of Housing and Urban Development position from level V.

11714.s: This order changes a part of an earlier order on the classification and declassification of national security information and material. It establishes an Interagency Classification Review Committee to help the National Security Council, with members from several federal offices and agencies.

11712.s: This order creates a Special Committee on Energy and a National Energy Office in the Executive Office of the President. The Director of the office is to advise the President on federal energy programs, recommend energy policies and guidelines, and help coordinate federal energy policy. The office is also to review energy programs, make funding recommendations, and serve as a clearinghouse for energy problems from federal departments, agencies, and other public or private entities.

11711.s: This order makes certain income, excess-profits, estate, and gift tax returns from 1950 to 1973 open to inspection by the Senate Committee on Government Operations, or an authorized subcommittee. The inspection is for the committee’s studies of government operations and must follow Treasury rules.

11710.s: This order creates a National Commission for Industrial Peace. The President appoints the chairman and other members, who are to represent labor, management, and the public. The commission is to study ways labor and management can settle disputes, look at how the government can help, and make recommendations to the President. It also gets support from several federal departments, and the President's Advisory Committee on Labor-Management Policy is abolished.

11709.s: This order makes certain income tax returns from people who have farm operations available for inspection by the Department of Agriculture. The inspection is limited to tax returns for years beginning on or after January 1, 1967, and it is for statistical purposes only, under Treasury rules.

11708.s: This executive order places certain offices and positions in level IV of the Executive Schedule and continues certain other offices and positions in level V. It covers positions in the Departments of Health, Education, and Welfare; Treasury; Justice; Defense; Labor; Commerce; Housing and Urban Development; the General Services Administration; and the Executive Office of the President. It also revokes a prior executive order, except for the positions listed in section 2.

11707.s: This order changes the boundaries of the New England River Basins Commission. It adds the parts of Vermont and Massachusetts that were not already within the Commission’s jurisdiction. This affects the Commission and those parts of the two states.

11706.s: This order allows certain tax returns to be inspected by U.S. attorneys and Department of Justice attorneys. It also allows those returns to be used in grand jury proceedings and in litigation, following Treasury rules and regulations.

11704.s: This order extends A. Everette MacIntyre’s exemption from compulsory retirement for age until February 28, 1974. It applies to him as a member of the Federal Trade Commission.

11703.s:
This order continues the Oil Policy Committee and gives its Chairman direction, coordination, and oversight of the oil import control program. The Chairman must consult the committee and follow guidance from the President’s economic affairs adviser, and may approve regulations under the program.

The committee is made up of specified Cabinet and economic officials, and the Chairman may create subcommittees. The order also requires the Chairman to monitor petroleum imports and report any concerns that may call for further presidential action.

11705.s: This order directs that the flag of the United States be flown at half-staff on the day of interment for the Honorable Cleo A. Noel, Junior, and George Curtis Moore. It applies to Federal Government buildings, grounds, and naval vessels in the District of Columbia and throughout the United States and its territories and possessions, and to United States embassies, consular offices, and other facilities abroad, including military facilities and naval vessels and stations.

11702.s: This order moves the Office of Consumer Affairs and its functions from the Executive Office of the President to the Department of Health, Education, and Welfare. The Director of that office stays on as Special Assistant to the President for Consumer Affairs. It also abolishes the Cabinet Committee on Economic Policy and revokes a prior executive order.

11701.s:
The order directs the Secretary of Labor to require executive branch departments and agencies to list suitable job openings with the State Employment Service or the United States Employment Service. It says this does not require hiring the people referred by those offices and does not change Civil Service laws.

It also gives the Secretary of Labor authority under Section 2012 of Title 38 and calls for changes to procurement rules as needed to carry out the program. These rules affect federal agencies and government contractors and subcontractors.

11700.s: The order closes executive departments, independent establishments, and other government agencies on Thursday, January 25, 1973, as a mark of respect for Lyndon Baines Johnson. It also says that day counts under federal rules about employee compensation and leave. Some offices in the Departments of State and Defense, and other agencies, may stay open if their ղեկավարs decide they should remain open for national security, defense, or other public reasons.

11699.s: This order amends a prior executive order on the Federal Executive Salary Schedule. It changes one Treasury Department position listed at level IV, replacing "Special Assistant to the Secretary (Congressional Relations)" with "Assistant to the Secretary for Legislative Affairs." It affects that position in the Department of the Treasury.

11697.s: This order lets the Department of Agriculture inspect income tax returns of people with farm operations, but only for statistical purposes. The returns may be viewed only to get data about those farm operations and only to the extent they are readily available in the Internal Revenue Service. If inspection is needed, it must be done in an IRS office and follow Treasury rules.

11698.s: The order names the Department of Justice as the Central Authority for the Convention on the Taking of Evidence Abroad in Civil or Commercial Matters. It must receive Letters of Request from a judicial authority in another Contracting State and send them to the authority that can carry them out.

11695.s: This order continues the Cost of Living Council and gives its chairman the powers and duties under the Economic Stabilization Act of 1970, except for limits on raw agricultural product prices before the first sale. It also keeps in place committees on health, food, labor-management, and interest and dividends to advise on the stabilization program. The order abolishes the Pay Board, Price Commission, and several related committees, and it sets penalties for willful violations of the order or rules made under it.

11696.s: This order excused many federal employees in the Washington, DC metropolitan area from duty for one-half day on Friday, January 19, 1973. It applied to employees in federal departments, independent establishments, and other agencies whose duty stations were in specified areas of the District of Columbia, Maryland, and Virginia. It did not apply to employees scheduled to work on January 20, 1973, who were already entitled to a holiday then, and some employees could be kept at work for national security or other public reasons.

11693.s: This order closes executive departments, independent establishments, and other government agencies on December 28, 1972, as a mark of respect for Harry S Truman. It says that day counts under federal rules on employee compensation and leave. Some offices in the Department of State, the Department of Defense, and other agencies may stay open if their ղեկավարs decide it is needed for national security, defense, or other public reasons.

11692.s: This order raises the monthly basic pay rates for members of the uniformed services within each pay grade. It takes effect on January 1, 1973.

11694.s: This order creates a three-member board to investigate a dispute between the Port Authority Trans-Hudson Corporation and certain employees represented by the Brotherhood Railway Carmen of the United States and Canada. The board must report its findings to the President, and no change may be made by the company or its employees in the conditions that led to the dispute, except by agreement, for the period stated in the order.

11691.s: This order adjusts basic pay rates for the General Schedule, certain Veterans' Administration medical and nursing positions, and Foreign Service officers and staff. It also says no pay rate may be more than the rate for level V of the Executive Schedule. The Civil Service Commission, the Veterans' Administration, and the Department of State are to set the rules needed to convert pay to the new rates.

11690.s: This order gives the Executive Director of the Domestic Council more duties on intergovernmental relations. He is to help coordinate federal, state, and local problems, report recurring issues to the President, and keep contact with federal offices and state and local officials. Federal departments and agencies must cooperate, and the order revokes a 1969 order and transfers certain records, property, personnel, and funds to the Domestic Council.

11688.s: This order changes how the Indian-leader members of the National Council on Indian Opportunity are appointed. It staggers their terms so only four of the eight terms expire in any year.
