It also covers certain travel, moving, storage, allowance, and reemployment expenses connected to those transfers and to reductions in force or transfers of function.

11289.s: This order creates the National Advisory Commission on Selective Service. The Commission is to review selective service and other national service systems, looking at fairness, military needs, individual careers and education, and other factors. It must make recommendations on classification and selection, military service qualifications, deferments and exemptions, appeals and individual rights, and how the selective service system is run at the national, state, and local levels.

11288.s: This order directs federal departments and agencies to prevent, control, and reduce water pollution from federal government activities in the United States. It requires existing federal facilities to follow pollution control plans and new federal facilities to meet set water pollution control standards. It also covers federal water resource projects, loan and grant practices, and vessel pollution, and it calls for reviews, reports, and technical advice from the Secretary of the Interior.

11286.s: This order designates the Department of Commerce as the department through which the United States will take part in the Inter-American Cultural and Trade Center in Dade County, Florida. It also lets that department use the authority given to the President under the Act of February 19, 1966 for that role.

11285.s: This order changes which foreign countries and areas are treated as "economically less developed countries" for the interest equalization tax. It includes most foreign countries, some overseas territories and possessions, and the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico and all possessions of the United States, while leaving out certain named countries and areas in the Sino-Soviet bloc. It also keeps prior stock or debt acquisitions covered in some cases where there was already a binding commitment before December 7, 1965.

11284.s: This order suspends two parts of Title 10 of the United States Code. Those sections deal with the continuation on the active list of rear admirals in the line of the Navy who are not restricted in the performance of duty.

11283.s: This order designates the International Cotton Institute as a public international organization under the International Organizations Immunities Act. It gives the Institute privileges, exemptions, and immunities listed in its agreement, including protections for its property, archives, communications, and legal process. It also covers certain representatives, officers, employees, and some family members with immigration, registration, service, and tax-related exemptions.

11282.s: This order tells executive branch departments and agencies to prevent, control, and reduce air pollution from Federal Government activities in the United States. It says new federal facilities must be planned and built to meet the order’s pollution objectives, and existing facilities must be reviewed and put on a phased plan for needed improvements. Federal facilities must follow state or local air pollution standards, or the standards set under this order if those are stricter. The order also directs the Secretary of Health, Education, and Welfare to set standards and provide advice and assistance.

11281.s: This order transfers responsibility for certain blocked property and interests from the Attorney General to the Secretary of the Treasury. It applies to property that remained blocked or restricted under Executive Order 8389, and the Treasury Secretary may act directly or through others. Earlier orders, rulings, and licenses on this property stay in effect unless the Treasury Secretary changes them. The order also says no one may challenge actions on the ground that the wrong official had jurisdiction.

11280.s: This order establishes the President's Committee on Mental Retardation. The committee is to advise the President, review how well the nation is dealing with mental retardation, and help coordinate federal agency work in this area. It is also meant to connect federal efforts with state and local governments, foundations, other private groups, and the public.

11278.s: This order creates a President's Council on Recreation and Natural Beauty and a Citizens' Advisory Committee on Recreation and Natural Beauty. The Council reviews federal plans and programs that affect outdoor recreation and natural beauty, makes recommendations to the President, and helps coordinate federal agencies. The advisory committee helps advise the President and the Council on outdoor recreation, city and countryside beautification, and related activities by federal, state, and private groups.

11277.s: This order designates the International Telecommunications Satellite Consortium as an international organization under the International Organizations Immunities Act. It makes the consortium eligible for the privileges, exemptions, and immunities given by that law. The United States participates in the consortium under the Communications Satellite Act of 1962.

11279.s: This order creates the President’s Committee on Health Manpower and a National Advisory Commission on Health Manpower. The Committee is to study health manpower needs and make recommendations for government and private action, including for the civilian population and the armed forces. The Commission is to help the Committee by making its own study and recommendations and sending a final report within one year after its first meeting. The Committee and the Commission will end ninety days after the Commission’s final report is submitted.

11275.s: This order changes a prior order that had delegated some presidential functions to the Director of the Bureau of the Budget. It gives that official authority to prescribe regulations about allowance rates for certain United States employees and to define the areas and job groups covered by those rates.

11276.s: The order creates a three-member board to investigate disputes between the air carriers in List A and certain employees represented by the International Association of Machinists and Aerospace Workers, AFL-CIO. It says the board will report its findings to the President within thirty days, and that for that period and for thirty days after the report, the carriers and their employees may not change the working conditions involved except by agreement.

11274.s: This order sets who will act as Secretary of Housing and Urban Development if the office is vacant or the Secretary is absent or disabled. The Under Secretary would serve first. If neither the Secretary nor the Under Secretary is available, an Assistant Secretary or the General Counsel would act as Secretary in the order set by the Secretary, or by their order of taking office if no order is in place.

11273.s: This order adds the Principal Deputy Assistant Secretary of Defense (Comptroller) in the Department of Defense to level V of the Federal Executive Salary Schedule. It affects that specific federal position.

11272.s: This order changes a prior rule on observing holidays by government agencies. It says the provisions in sections 4, 5, 6, 7, and 9 do not apply to the postal field service. The Postmaster General must make regulations to give postal field service employees equivalent benefits.

11270.s: This order suspends a law that sets the number of officers who can serve in the grade of lieutenant general in the Marine Corps. The suspension lasts until June 30 of the fiscal year after the national emergency named in the order ends.

11271.s: This order directs that the flag of the United States be flown at half-staff as a mark of respect for the memory of Fleet Admiral Chester W. Nimitz. It applies to all Federal Government buildings, grounds, and naval vessels in the District of Columbia and throughout the United States and its Territories and possessions, until interment.

11269.s: This order establishes the National Advisory Council on International Monetary and Financial Policies. It gives the Council certain functions over international financial, exchange, and monetary policy matters, and it directs federal agencies and officers to keep the Council or the Secretary of the Treasury informed about those transactions. It also gives the Secretary of the Treasury certain authority to instruct U.S. representatives to international financial organizations and updates an earlier executive order to use the new council name.

11268.s: This order adds the position of Deputy Director of Defense Research and Engineering (Chemistry and Materials) in the Department of Defense to level V of the Federal Executive Salary Schedule. It affects that federal position and its pay classification.

11267.s: The order designates the Attorney General, and any other Executive Branch officers or employees he chooses, as the United States officials for Article XXIV of the Treaty of Friendship and General Relations with Spain. It says they must carry out the obligations the United States assumed under that article in the way the treaty requires.

11265.s: This order amends the rules for the National Defense Service Medal. It says the medal shall be awarded to members of the Armed Forces of the United States who served during certain periods, including after June 26, 1950 and before July 28, 1954, or during later periods the Secretary of Defense designates. It also says some recipients may wear a bronze star on the medal ribbon for each additional designated period of active duty.

11266.s: This order amends Selective Service rules for registrants in Class III-A. It places in that class any registrant who has a child or children in his home and keeps a bona fide family relationship with them, unless he is a physician, dentist, veterinarian, or in a listed allied specialist category.

11264.s: This order gives the Secretary of State the functions transferred by Reorganization Plan No. 4 of 1965, and allows the Secretary to pass those functions on to State Department officials or bodies. It creates the Board of the Foreign Service and the Board of Examiners for the Foreign Service in the Department of State and sets out how their members are chosen. It also gives both boards their listed functions, makes them subject to the Secretary’s direction and supervision, and assigns the Department of State to provide their administrative services.

11263.s: This order changes the rules for choosing the Chief Executive under the administration of the Ryukyu Islands. It says the Chief Executive must be elected by a majority of the entire legislative body and serves until that body’s term ends. If the legislative body does not choose a successor in a reasonable time, the High Commissioner may appoint one until the body elects a successor.

11262.s: This order changes the Federal Executive Salary Schedule by adding one position to Level IV and two positions to Level V. It affects the Executive Secretary of the President's Commission on Law Enforcement and Administration of Justice, the Director of the Bureau of Outdoor Recreation in the Department of the Interior, and the Assistant to the Secretary of Defense for Legislative Affairs.

11261.s: This order amends a prior executive order on foreign assistance administration. It gives the United States Information Agency the job of handling public information functions abroad for U.S. foreign-assistance, aid, and development programs. It also gives the Agency’s Director certain presidential functions related to informational media guaranties.

11260.s: This order changes an earlier order about coordinating federal education programs. It gives the Assistant Secretary for Education the role of helping coordinate those programs and makes that official the chairman of the Federal Interagency Committee on Education. It also replaces the word "Commissioner" with "Assistant Secretary" in several parts of the earlier order.

11258.s: This order directs federal departments and agencies to help prevent, control, and reduce water pollution caused by federal activities in the United States. It requires existing federal facilities to be reviewed and improved, and new federal facilities to meet water pollution control standards. It also sets rules for waste treatment, water resource projects, and activities supported by federal loans, grants, or contracts. The order affects federal agencies and other groups that work with federal funds or federal projects.

11259.s: This order changes the rules for incentive pay for hazardous duty involving parachute jumping. It lets a commanding officer waive the minimum jump requirements for a member who cannot do the required jumps because of combat operations in a hostile fire area. It affects members of the Armed Forces who are covered by these jump requirements.

11257.s: This order gives the Civil Service Commission the President’s authority to make rules under the Federal Employees Salary Act of 1965. Those rules can exclude some officers or employees from part of that law and can govern severance pay. It affects federal officers and employees covered by the act.

11256.s: This order creates the President's Committee on Food and Fiber and the National Advisory Commission on Food and Fiber. The committee is made up of the Secretaries of Agriculture, State, Commerce, and Labor, and the commission is made up of members appointed by the President. They are directed to study farm and trade policies, the current economic situation in American farming, and related matters, then make recommendations to the President and the committee. Federal departments and agencies may be asked for information and help, and the two bodies end after the commission's final report is submitted.

11255.s: This order designates Vietnam and nearby waters as an overseas combat area for the purposes of certain mailing privileges for the Armed Forces. It applies to the areas described in the order where U.S. armed forces are engaged in military operations involving armed conflict with a hostile foreign force.

11254.s: This order creates the Automotive Agreement Adjustment Assistance Board and puts the Secretary of the Treasury, the Secretary of Commerce, and the Secretary of Labor on it. It gives the Board the President’s functions under Section 302 of the Automotive Products Trade Act of 1965. The Board must gather information and make final decisions about firms or groups of workers under that law, and federal agencies must help it when asked.

11253.s: This order changes a prior order on incentive pay for hazardous duty. It says certain qualified Navy members assigned to a submarine operational command staff may receive incentive pay if they serve the required hours on a submarine during underway operations. It also gives rules for how to count partial months when figuring this pay.

11251.s: This order amends a prior executive order to add the Comptroller of the Department of Health, Education, and Welfare to level V of the Federal Executive Salary Schedule. It affects that federal position and the salary schedule it is placed under.

11252.s: This order transfers all functions of the Director of the Food-for-Peace Program to the Secretary of State. It also creates a Special Assistant to the Secretary of State in the Department of State to help carry out those functions. The change affects the Food-for-Peace Program and the State Department.

11249.s: This order changes Coast Guard rules for vessels, harbors, ports, and waterfront facilities. It defines who the Captain of the Port is, what a waterfront facility is, and what a security zone is. It lets the Captain of the Port control access, inspect and search vessels and facilities, post guards, and remove people or items not authorized.

11250.s: This order amends a previous executive order about the Peace Corps. It gives the Secretary of State the power to make regulations and determinations under a 1965 law. It also says certain Peace Corps functions may be carried out without following the listed laws, subject to the limits in another executive order.

11247.s: This order directs the Attorney General to help federal departments and agencies coordinate how they enforce Title VI of the Civil Rights Act of 1964. It also tells those departments and agencies to work with the Attorney General and give him reports and information he asks for. The order revokes a prior executive order and transfers related records to the Attorney General.

11248.s: This order places certain offices and positions in Level IV and Level V of the Federal Executive Salary Schedule. It also supersedes Executive Order 11244 and Executive Order 11245.

11245.s: This order places the Commissioner on Aging in Level V of the Federal Executive Salary Schedule. It affects that position in the Department of Health, Education, and Welfare.

11244.s: This order places the Special Assistant to the Secretary for Enforcement in the Treasury Department in level IV of the Federal Executive Salary Schedule. It affects that federal office and the pay level tied to it.

11246.s: This order sets a policy of equal opportunity in Federal employment for all qualified persons and bars discrimination because of race, creed, color, or national origin. It requires executive departments and agencies to keep equal employment opportunity programs and to give prompt, fair review of discrimination complaints. It also requires Government contractors and subcontractors to agree not to discriminate, to take affirmative action, and to file compliance reports. The Secretary of Labor and contracting agencies may investigate complaints, issue rules, and use sanctions for noncompliance.

11242.s: This order changes the rules for a type of hazardous duty incentive pay tied to flight operations on an aircraft carrier flight deck. It says the pay applies to certain crew members who are ordered to that duty and meet monthly participation requirements set out in the order. It also says a member cannot get this pay for a month if the member is eligible for other hazardous duty incentive pay under title 37.

11241.s: This order amends the Selective Service regulations for nonvolunteers who are at least 19 years old and under 26. It sets rules for selecting men in that age group by date of birth, with the oldest selected first. It treats men differently based on whether they have a wife and when they married her, if they maintain a bona fide family relationship in their homes.

11240.s: This order creates a new Board of the Foreign Service and a new Board of Examiners for the Foreign Service. Each board keeps the same functions and status as the earlier board of the same name, and the Board of Examiners’ membership is set under the rules named in the order. The order took effect on July 27, 1965, and ends on January 1, 1966, unless an earlier date is set.

11239.s: This order directs several federal agencies to carry out the United States duties under the Convention for Safety of Life at Sea. It requires the Secretary of the Treasury, acting through the Coast Guard, to issue certificates required by the Convention and to make regulations needed to carry it out. It also says the agencies must cooperate with each other, and that the Secretary of the Navy takes over these Coast Guard functions when the Coast Guard operates as a service in the Navy.

11238.s: This order establishes a new National Advisory Council on International Monetary and Financial Problems. The council has the same membership, functions, and status as the earlier council of that name. The order is effective as of July 27, 1965, and the council will end on January 1, 1966, or earlier if set by later action.

11237.s: This order sets rules for how the Secretary of the Interior and the Housing and Home Finance Administrator coordinate land acquisition for recreation and open space programs. It divides responsibilities between urbanized areas and other areas, and it requires each to review and consider the other’s comments on grant plans. It also requires them to develop joint procedures for evaluating applications, sharing information, and making joint decisions in unusual cases.

11236.s: This order creates the President's Commission on Law Enforcement and Administration of Justice. The commission is directed to study the causes of crime and delinquency, the prevention of crime, and the adequacy of law enforcement and the administration of justice at the national, state, and local levels. It may make recommendations to federal, state, and local governments and to private persons and organizations, and it can use advisory committees and other staff to help carry out its work.

11235.s: This order makes certain income, estate, and gift tax returns for 1956 through 1965 open to inspection during the Eighty-ninth Congress. The Committee on Banking and Currency of the House of Representatives, or a subcommittee it authorizes, may inspect them for studies and investigations within its jurisdiction. The inspections must follow Treasury rules for committee review of tax returns.

11243.s: This order creates a three-member board to investigate a dispute between the Atchison, Topeka and Santa Fe Railway Company and certain of its employees represented by the Brotherhood of Railroad Trainmen. The board must report its findings to the President within thirty days, and no changes may be made in the conditions of the dispute except by agreement during that time and for thirty days after the report.

11234.s: This order creates the President's Commission on Crime in the District of Columbia. The Commission is to study the causes of crime and delinquency, law enforcement, the courts, criminal laws, and the correction and rehabilitation of offenders. It is also to make recommendations on police training, police organization and equipment, case handling, and other ways to prevent and control crime. Federal and District of Columbia departments and agencies are directed to cooperate with the Commission and provide information and assistance.

11232.s: This order suspends a law that set a service-in-grade requirement for officers in the line of the Navy who are commanders. It affects those officers by removing that requirement for being considered by a selection board for promotion to the next higher grade.

11233.s: The order directs that the United States flag be flown at half-staff until interment as a mark of respect for Adlai E. Stevenson. This applies to federal buildings, grounds, and naval vessels in the District of Columbia, across the United States and its territories and possessions, and at U.S. facilities abroad.

11231.s: The order creates the Vietnam Service Medal. It says the medal may be awarded to members of the armed forces who serve in Vietnam, nearby waters, or nearby air space after July 3, 1965, under rules set by the military departments and the Secretary of Defense. It also says some members who already qualified for the Armed Forces Expeditionary Medal for service in Vietnam may keep that medal or apply for the Vietnam Service Medal instead, but not both. The Vietnam Service Medal may also be awarded after death.

11230.s: This order gives the Director of the Bureau of the Budget power to carry out many presidential functions without needing the President’s further approval. The delegated powers cover rules and approvals on travel expenses, housing and storage, land transfers, hospital charges, and the transfer of federal property and funds in several programs. It affects federal agencies and employees, and in some cases state governments such as Alaska and Hawaii.

11228.s: This order gives the United States Civil Service Commission and its Chairman authority to handle certain federal personnel matters without further presidential approval. It covers regulations for pay and leave rules, some exceptions from automatic separation from service, and decisions about which government activity benefits from certain employee awards. It also replaces several earlier executive orders and keeps earlier related actions in place unless they are changed or revoked.

11229.s: This order sets up how the United States will take part in the International Coffee Agreement. It gives the Secretary of State, the Secretary of the Treasury, and other named Cabinet officials certain duties under the agreement and the related act. Some functions are kept by the President, and the Secretaries are told to coordinate with each other and may redelegate duties within their departments.

11226.s: This order amends an earlier order on how Government agencies observe holidays. It changes how holidays are counted for pay and leave and sets rules for certain full-time employees when a holiday falls on Sunday, Saturday, or another day of the week. It also says a holiday that is less than a full day gets proportionate credit.

11227.s: This order designates the Interim Communications Satellite Committee as a public international organization under the International Organizations Immunities Act. That gives it certain privileges, exemptions, and immunities, but not all of the ones listed in the act. The order says the committee’s officers and employees do not get the privileges for one section, while representatives and their alternates do. It also says this does not take away any privileges, exemptions, or immunities the organization may have by treaty or congressional action.

11225.s: This order designates the International Coffee Organization as a public international organization under the International Organizations Immunities Act. It gives the organization the privileges, exemptions, and immunities allowed by that law, and does not limit any others it may already have or later get by treaty or congressional action.

11223.s: The order lets foreign assistance functions be carried out without following certain listed laws and rules in some cases. It also allows some contracts with nonprofit institutions, and some other foreign assistance contracts, to be changed without new consideration when the Secretary of State says it is needed to protect U.S. foreign policy interests. The order also sets which foreign countries, territories, and Puerto Rico count as economically less developed for the interest equalization tax, while excluding several named countries and areas.

11224.s: This order designates certain foreign countries and areas as economically less developed countries for purposes of the tax imposed by section 4911 of the Internal Revenue Code. It says the Bahamas, Bermuda, Ireland, Kuwait, and Portugal are no longer included in that status, and it also lists areas that are included, such as the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico and all possessions of the United States. It also keeps certain prior stock or debt acquisitions covered under the earlier status, and it authorizes the Secretary of the Treasury to issue rules to carry it out.

11222.s: This order sets ethics rules for government officers and employees. It limits gifts, favors, outside jobs, financial interests, use of federal property, and use of nonpublic information for private gain. It also requires some officials and special government employees to file financial interest statements and gives agencies and the Civil Service Commission authority to issue and review related regulations.

11221.s: This order amends a previous order about the status of women. It sets up an interdepartmental Committee on the Status of Women made up of several Cabinet and agency officials, and it says the committee must send the President a yearly report after consulting with the Citizens' Advisory Council. It also establishes a 20-member Citizens' Advisory Council on the Status of Women, appointed by the President, with members serving without pay.

11219.s: This order lets certain present or former Foreign Service officers and employees be appointed to the competitive service if they meet the listed qualifications and service requirements. It applies to people appointed under the Foreign Service Act of 1946 or related law, and to some veterans who qualify for preference. People appointed under it may get career conditional or career employee status, and those appointed to nontemporary positions get competitive status automatically.

11220.s: This order transfers part of the Okanogan National Forest in Washington to the Wenatchee National Forest. It applies to land in Chelan County and says the forest boundaries will be adjusted. The transfer is effective July 1, 1965.

11218.s: This order changes an earlier order about the Recreation Advisory Council. It adds the Chairman of the Tennessee Valley Authority to the council, along with several cabinet and agency heads. The chairmanship rotates among the listed officials, and each may appoint a delegate. When the council considers matters affecting other federal agencies, the chairman must invite those agency heads to take part.

11217.s: This order makes certain income, excess-profits, estate, and gift tax returns from 1947 to 1965 open to inspection by the House Committee on Un-American Activities or an authorized subcommittee during the Eighty-ninth Congress. The inspection is for investigations of subversive and un-American activities and propaganda, and it must follow Treasury rules.

11216.s: This order designates Vietnam and the waters next to it as an area where Armed Forces of the United States are and have been engaged in combat, for purposes of section 112 of the Internal Revenue Code of 1954. It also sets January 1, 1964 as the date when combat activities in that area began. This affects members of the Armed Forces in that area for that tax section.

11214.s: This order changes an earlier order about cotton textiles and cotton textile products. It adds the Special Representative for Trade Negotiations and the Office of the Special Representative for Trade Negotiations to the groups named in several sections. The changes affect how the federal government handles those cotton textile matters.

11213.s: This order says information returns made by a commercial bank under the Interest Equalization Tax Act may be inspected by the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System and the Federal Reserve Banks. The inspection must follow rules set by the Secretary of the Treasury. It also supersedes Executive Order 11176.

11212.s: This order changes the boundaries of the Allegheny National Forest in Pennsylvania to add certain described lands. It says lands and interests in land acquired for the forest, or transferred to the Secretary of Agriculture for national forest management, will be treated as part of the forest. Those lands will be subject to the laws, rules, and regulations that apply to the forest.

11211.s: This order says the interest equalization tax will not apply to some U.S. purchases of debt obligations issued or guaranteed by the Government of Japan. The exclusion applies only to certain original or new issues, with notice and certification requirements, and only if the yearly total of excluded acquisitions stays within the stated limit. The Secretary of the Treasury may issue rules to carry out the order.

11210.s: This order creates a Temporary Commission on Pennsylvania Avenue. The commission is to advise the President on the feasibility of the proposed improvement plan, how to carry it out in stages, how it may affect private property owners and businesses, and what legislation may be needed. It is also directed to help coordinate the plan with other national capital planning work and to explain the plan to the public.

11209.s: This order establishes the Federal Development Committee for Appalachia to help coordinate Federal planning for the Appalachian region. It names the Federal Cochairman of the Appalachian Regional Commission as the chairman and adds representatives from several Federal agencies and the Tennessee Valley Authority. The chairman and committee are to review plans, studies, and recommendations for Appalachia and help bring Federal agencies into agreement. The order also abolishes the earlier Federal Development Planning Committee for Appalachia.

11208.s: This order revokes two earlier executive orders that had established and expanded the President’s Advisory Council on the Arts. It affects the council created by those orders, after the National Council on the Arts was established.

11207.s: The order directs the Secretary of Defense to help Alabama law enforcement remove obstructions to the enforcement of United States laws and to suppress domestic violence tied to the march named in the order. It authorizes the use of Armed Forces if needed. It also allows the Secretary of Defense to call Alabama Army National Guard and Air National Guard units into active military service and to delegate authority to the Secretary of the Army or the Secretary of the Air Force.

11206.s: This order says returns for the tax imposed by chapter 41 of the Internal Revenue Code may be open to inspection by certain classes of people and by State and Federal government offices. That access must follow rules and regulations set by the Secretary of the Treasury. It takes effect when it is filed for publication in the Federal Register.

11205.s: This order abolishes the position of Special Assistant to the President for Personnel Management. It also revokes Executive Order No. 10729 of September 16, 1957.

11204.s: This order allows the House Committee on Public Works, or a subcommittee it authorizes, to inspect income, estate, and gift tax returns for the years 1957 to 1965. The inspection is for the committee’s investigation of the policies, procedures, and practices used in administering the Federal-Aid Highway Program. The inspections must follow Treasury rules for congressional review of tax returns.

11203.s: This order lets certain Treasury Department employees in Schedule B jobs that protect the President, his immediate family, or other protected persons be converted to career appointments. They must meet service, recommendation, and examination requirements, and some military service can count toward the service requirement if the worker is rehired in time. If conversion is not recommended or the worker does not qualify, the employee is separated when the current Schedule B appointment expires.

11202.s: This order directs that certain Student Trainee employees in shortage occupations can be converted to career-conditional or career appointments. To qualify, they must complete a preprofessional cooperative work-study program, meet all degree requirements for a bachelor's degree, have at least six months of work experience in the agency, be recommended by the agency, and meet other Commission rules. It also directs the Civil Service Commission to issue regulations to carry out the order.

11201.s: This order makes certain income, excess-profits, estate, and gift tax returns for 1947 to 1966 open to inspection by the House Committee on Government Operations, or a duly authorized subcommittee. The inspection is for the committee’s studies of government operations and efficiency. It must follow Treasury rules for the inspection of congressional returns.

11200.s: This order directs several federal agencies to charge recreation user fees at certain outdoor areas they manage. It covers areas where fees were already collected in 1964 and lets officials add other areas that meet the order’s criteria. The Secretary of the Interior must set fee schedules, posting rules, and coordination measures, and the agencies must review existing contracts that affect whether recreation user fees can be charged.

11199.s: This order ends the defensive sea area off the coast of North Carolina that had existed under a 1932 executive order. It also revokes that earlier executive order.

11198.s: This order makes the interest equalization tax rules apply to some debt obligations of foreign obligors acquired by commercial banks. It covers certain bank loans made in the ordinary course of banking business and sets different rules for some foreign-currency obligations and branch offices outside the United States. It also says some acquisitions by a United States person that is a commercial bank will be taxed under this order.

11197.s: This order establishes the President’s Council on Equal Opportunity. The Council is made up of federal officials and is meant to help coordinate federal work on civil rights and equal opportunity without discrimination based on race, creed, color, or national origin. It can recommend policies and changes to the President, request reports from federal departments and agencies, and work with state, local, and private groups. Each federal department and agency must cooperate with the Council and name an officer to help coordinate related activities.

11196.s: This order lets the Housing and Home Finance Administrator carry out certain housing-related powers without the President’s approval. It covers approving some grants, loans, contracts, easements, and other actions under several housing laws, and it also includes certain Alaska grant and reporting duties. Some actions still require the Secretary of Defense to agree, and the order replaces several earlier executive orders or parts of them.

11195.s: This order adds the Chief of Protocol at the Department of State to level IV of the Federal Executive Salary Schedule. It also adds the Staff Director of the Commission on Civil Rights, the Assistant Director for Program Planning, Analysis, and Research at the Office of Economic Opportunity, and the General Counsel of the Veterans Administration to level V.

11194.s: This order makes certain income, excess-profits, estate, and gift tax returns from 1947 through 1965 open to inspection by the Senate Committee on Government Operations, or a subcommittee it authorizes. The inspection is for the committee’s study of government activities and how to make government more economical and efficient. It must follow the Treasury rules named in the order.

11193.s: This order directs that the U.S. flag be flown at half-staff through the day of interment in memory of Sir Winston Spencer Churchill. It applies to federal buildings, grounds, and naval vessels in the United States and its territories, and to U.S. embassies, legations, consular offices, military facilities, and naval stations abroad.

11192.s: This order makes certain income, estate, and gift tax returns from 1956 through 1965 open to inspection during the Eighty-ninth Congress. The Senate Committee on Rules and Administration, or a subcommittee it authorizes, may inspect them for its study of the financial, business, and other interests or activities of Senate officers, employees, former officers, former employees, members, and former members. The inspection must follow Treasury rules for congressional review of tax returns.

11191.s: This order assigns the Director of Telecommunications Management to help plan and carry out a national program for a commercial communications satellite system. It also tells the Director to review the system, coordinate federal agencies, make recommendations to the President, and serve as the main link between the President and the Communications Satellite Corporation. The Secretary of State is directed to supervise parts of the program, arrange for foreign participation, and handle foreign relations and negotiations tied to the Act.

11190.s: This order gives the Secretary of Defense, and the Secretary of the Treasury for the Coast Guard, the authority to write rules for screening units and members of the Ready Reserve of the Armed Forces. It also revokes Executive Order 10651.

11189.s: This order places certain federal offices and positions in level IV of the Federal Executive Salary Schedule and others in level V. It affects the listed officials and jobs, including several Department of State, Justice, Defense, Labor, Interior, and Veterans Administration positions. The order is effective August 15, 1964.

11188.s: This order amends Selective Service regulations on registration, classification, and appeals. It changes who is exempt from registration, including some foreign government officials, international organization officials, exchange visitors, and foreign students, and it requires some exchange visitors to carry official documents. It also updates rules for permits to leave the United States, military service classifications, deferments, and the time allowed to ask for a local board appearance.

11187.s: This order lets certain Postal Field Service employees with indefinite or temporary appointments have those appointments changed to career appointments if they meet listed service, recommendation, and qualification requirements. It also gives a path for some people who left a competitive postal job to enter the armed forces and were re-employed after discharge under honorable conditions. The order does not apply to postmasters or rural carriers.

11186.s: This order creates the Federal Development Planning Committee for Appalachia. The Committee is meant to work with state representatives on surveys, studies, plans, and recommendations for developing the Appalachian region. It also reviews and comments on draft plans and sends final plans and recommendations to the President and interested federal agencies. Federal agencies are asked to help the Committee, but the order does not give the Committee control over their legal powers.

11185.s: This order sets up a way for federal education programs to be better coordinated across agencies. It directs the Secretary of Health, Education, and Welfare and the Commissioner of Education to identify the Nation’s education needs and goals, study federal effects on schools, and recommend policies. Federal agencies must share information, work together to avoid duplicate activities, and cooperate with studies and analyses. It also creates a Federal Interagency Committee on Education to advise federal officials on these duties.

11184.s: This order amends an earlier executive order on who may carry out certain presidential functions. It covers rules for quarters and facilities, allowance rates for federal employees assigned to duty on the California offshore islands, and matters under the Alaska Omnibus Act. It also covers grants to the State of Alaska, approval of Alaska’s plan, and reports and records tied to those grants.

11183.s: This order creates the President's Commission on White House Fellowships. The Commission sets standards, reviews applications and nominations, and recommends young people for White House Fellowships. Fellows are selected by the President and serve in the White House Office, the Vice President's office, or the offices of the heads of the ten executive departments.

11182.s: The order sets up a Federal Field Committee and a President’s Review Committee to plan federal programs for Alaska’s economic development and use of natural resources. It says the committees should work with the State of Alaska and with federal agencies to make surveys, keep plans current, and prepare recommendations. It also revokes the earlier Alaska planning commission and assigns earthquake-related reconstruction planning duties to the Office of Emergency Planning while the disaster declaration remains in effect.

11181.s: This order creates a Board of Inquiry to look into certain labor disputes in the maritime industry. The disputes involve steamship companies, stevedores, marine carpenters, lighterage operators, and other employers engaged in related pier activities, along with employees represented by the International Longshoremen's Association, AFL-CIO. The board must report to the President and may continue to carry out other duties under the law.

11179.s:
This order creates a National Defense Executive Reserve in the executive branch. It is made up of people from civilian jobs and government who are trained for executive positions in the Federal Government during an emergency.

The Director of the Office of Emergency Planning runs the program, sets recruitment and training standards, and approves members. Members may be assigned to reserve units in departments or agencies, but their service is limited to training and cannot last more than three years.

11180.s: This order creates a board to investigate disputes between certain railroad carriers and some of their employees. The board is to report its findings to the President, and no change may be made in the conditions behind the disputes except by agreement during the stated period. It applies to the carriers listed in the order and to employees represented by the Brotherhood of Locomotive Firemen and Enginemen.

11178.s: This order transfers certain lands in Georgia from the Chattahoochee National Forest to the Oconee National Forest. It also adds lands to the Hoosier National Forest in Indiana, the Ouachita National Forest in Oklahoma, and the Tombigbee National Forest in Mississippi. The order excludes some lands from the Tombigbee National Forest and adds other lands so its boundary matches the Noxubee National Wildlife Refuge.

11177.s: This order designates the Administrator of the Bonneville Power Administration and the Division Engineer of the North Pacific Division, Corps of Engineers, as the United States Entity for the Columbia River Treaty. It gives that entity the treaty functions needed to carry out the agreement, while leaving other department responsibilities unchanged. It also directs the Secretary of the Interior and the Secretary of the Army to appoint members and alternate members to the Permanent Engineering Board for the treaty.

11176.s: This order says certain information returns filed by commercial banks about loans and commitments to foreign obligors must be open for inspection. The Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System and the Federal Reserve Banks may inspect them under Treasury rules for administering the interest equalization tax.

11175.s: This order says the tax will not apply to some stock or debt obligations of Canada and related Canadian governments, agencies, corporations, partnerships, trusts, or individual residents when they are bought as original or new issues and the required notice is filed. It applies to U.S. persons who acquire those securities. The exemption covers acquisitions made from July 19, 1963, until the order is changed.

11174.s: This order reestablishes the Presidential Service Certificate for members of the Army, Navy, Marine Corps, and Air Force who have been assigned to the White House for at least one year after January 20, 1961. It also replaces the White House Service Badge with the Presidential Service Badge for members of the Armed Forces assigned to duty in the White House. The certificate and badge are awarded by the Army, Navy, or Air Force secretaries, and each may be granted posthumously.

11173.s: This order amends a prior executive order on Federal salary administration. It gives the Civil Service Commission authority to prescribe the rules and regulations required under section 504(d) of the Federal Salary Reform Act of 1962.

11172.s: This order sets aside certain public lands and other public property at the Kapalama Military Reservation in Hawaii for the use of the United States. It covers the lands and property described in the order, including land in Kaliawa and Mokauea in Honolulu, Oahu. The property is set aside in fee simple, subject to valid existing rights.

11171.s: This order establishes a Canal Zone Merit System for hiring, reappointment, reinstatement, re-employment, and retention in Canal Zone positions. It gives the Secretary of the Army authority to issue regulations, exclude some employees or positions from the system, and extend certain rights and privileges to employees, including some who are not U.S. citizens. It also creates a five-member Canal Zone Board of Appeals to hear employee appeals and requires the Civil Service Commission to review the system's operations.

11169.s: This order creates a board to investigate labor disputes between certain railroad carriers and their employees. The board must report its findings to the President within thirty days. During that time, the carriers and their employees cannot change the conditions involved in the disputes unless they agree to do so.

11168.s: This order creates a board to investigate disputes between certain railroad carriers and certain employees represented by listed railway labor organizations. The board must report its findings to the President within thirty days. Until then, the carriers and their employees may not make changes in the working conditions tied to the disputes unless they agree to do so.

11170.s: This order creates a board to investigate disputes between the carriers listed in List A and certain employees represented by the labor organizations in List B. The board must report its findings to the President within thirty days. During that time, and for thirty days after the report, the carriers and their employees may not make changes in the conditions that caused the disputes unless they agree to do so.

11166.s: The order sets aside land and other property at the Makua Military Reservation in Hawaii for the use of the United States, subject to valid existing rights. It covers a described area of land and also sets aside access rights to and from the nearest public highway across nearby adjoining lands and properties. The land description includes land at Makua and Kahanahaiki in Waianae, Oahu.

11167.s: This order sets aside certain public lands and other property at the Pohakuloa Training Area in Hawaii for the use of the United States, subject to valid existing rights. The lands include portions of Government Lands of Kaobe and Puuanahulu, the Crown Land of Hummuula, and part of the Mauna Loa Forest and Game Reserve. It covers land in Kaohe, North Kona, and North Hilo on the Island of Hawaii.

11165.s: This order sets aside certain lands and other property at the Fort Shafter Military Reservation in Hawaii for the use of the United States. It covers two parcels of land and says Parcel B remains subject to non-exclusive rights-of-way for access and utility purposes by the State of Hawaii and its assigns.

11164.s: This order changes an earlier executive order about who can carry out certain powers given to the President under the Alaska Omnibus Act. It lets the Director of the Bureau of the Budget handle the President’s authority to decide whether a federal function in Alaska has ended or been taken over by the State of Alaska, and to transfer certain Alaska property to the State without reimbursement. It also says this change does not affect the authority already given to the Secretary of the Interior for other property transfers.

11163.s: This order includes a tract of land in Fannin County, Georgia, in the Chattahoochee National Forest. The land is transferred from the Tennessee Valley Authority to the Department of Agriculture under the agreement named in the order. It covers about 38.5 acres and is subject to the agreement's terms.

11162.s: This order adds the Postmaster General to the President's Committee on Equal Employment Opportunity. It also updates the list of committee members and says each member may choose an alternate to serve in their place. It supersedes a section of a 1963 executive order.

11161.s: This order directs the Secretary of Defense and the Administrator of the Federal Aviation Agency to prepare plans in case the agency is transferred to the Department of Defense in a war. It says the agency would act as an adjunct of the Defense Department, with its Administrator responsible to the Secretary of Defense and subject to his authority. The order also says they should make arrangements so the agency can still perform its functions during a national emergency short of war and so any transfer would be smooth and rapid.

11160.s: This order sets rules for medical care for certain retired Coast and Geodetic Survey ships' officers and crew members, and for the family dependents of active and retired officers and crew members. It lets eligible people get medical care through Public Health Service facilities, including hospitals, outpatient clinics, and outpatient offices. Retired officers and crew members may get medical, surgical, and dental treatment, while dependents may get medical advice, outpatient treatment, and, if space is available, hospitalization. The order also sets charges for dependent hospitalization and limits dental care in some cases.

11158.s: This order designates the Attorney General of the United States to administer and carry out the Agreement between the United States and the Republic of Austria on the return of Austrian property, rights, and interests. It also allows the Attorney General to delegate any of those functions to an officer or employee of the Department of Justice.

11159.s: This order changes Executive Order No. 11143 by replacing “40 members” with “45 members” in one section. It affects the Public Advisory Committee for Trade Negotiations by increasing the number of members listed there.

11157.s: This order sets regulations for incentive pay for hazardous duty and special pay for sea duty for enlisted members. It covers duties such as aerial flight, submarine duty, glider flights, parachute jumping, demolition of explosives, and certain medical and test duties. It also says enlisted members can receive sea-duty pay while on sea duty as defined in the order.

11155.s: This order creates a Commission on Presidential Scholars to choose Presidential Scholars each year. The scholars are to be recent or soon-to-be graduates of public or private secondary schools and are chosen for outstanding scholarship. It also creates a Presidential Scholars Medallion for each selected scholar. The Office of Education is directed to help carry out the order.

11156.s: This order creates a Maritime Advisory Committee with members from the public, labor, management, and certain federal officials. The committee is to consider policy and administration matters affecting the maritime industry, including trade, national defense, manpower, and labor relations programs. It may use federal studies and resources, and federal agencies are to help by providing information and assistance as allowed by law. The committee’s role is advisory only, and it does not control any federal function, agency, or officer.

11154.s: This order exempts J. Edgar Hoover, the Director of the Federal Bureau of Investigation, from compulsory retirement for age. It applies to him for an indefinite period of time under the Civil Service Retirement Act.

11153.s: This order makes certain income, estate, and gift tax returns for 1960 to 1964 open to inspection by the Senate Committee on the Judiciary, or a subcommittee it authorizes. The inspection is for the committee’s study and investigation of how antitrust and monopoly laws apply to professional boxing. It applies during the Eighty-eighth Congress and must follow Treasury rules for inspecting congressional returns.

11152.s: This order creates a President’s Committee on Manpower to help carry out federal duties under the Manpower Development and Training Act of 1962. The committee is made up of several federal officials and can also include other agency heads and staff observers. It is to help assess the nation’s manpower needs and supplies, advise on better methods and programs, and recommend coordination of federal information and reports. The Department of Labor provides administrative support, and the order does not change the legal powers of any federal agency or officer.

11151.s: This order suspends a law that required certain male officers on the active list in the line of the Navy to have had specified sea or foreign service before they could be promoted. It affects those officers in the regular Navy who were subject to that promotion rule.

11150.s: The order sets up a federal commission for Alaska after the March 27, 1964 earthquake. The commission is to make coordinated plans for reconstruction and for economic and resources development in Alaska. It is also to work with state representatives on surveys, studies, and recommendations for short-range and long-range programs, projects, and possible new laws.

11149.s: This order creates the President's Advisory Committee on Supersonic Transport. The committee is to study the supersonic transport program and advise the President, with special attention to its financial aspects. Federal departments and agencies must cooperate with the committee and provide needed information and assistance.

11148.s: This order changes a prior executive order to add the Secretary of the Interior to the Interagency Committee on Export Expansion. It affects the committee’s membership and the Secretary of the Interior.

11146.s: This order changes rules for basic allowances for quarters for members of the uniformed services. It says when certain quarters are occupied without rent, a member may not get the allowance in some cases, but it keeps the allowance in other cases such as temporary duty, leave, or when dependents are not available quarters at the permanent station. It also allows some members serving outside the United States in duties with foreign government officials to be assigned quarters above the usual minimum standards, with limits on single occupancy.

11147.s: The order creates a board of three members to investigate disputes between the listed rail carriers and certain railroad employees. The board must report its findings to the President within thirty days. During that time, and for thirty days after the report, the carriers and their employees may not change the conditions that caused the disputes unless they agree to do so.

11145.s: This order creates a Curator of the White House to help preserve and protect furniture, fixtures, and decorative objects in certain White House areas, and in other areas the President may choose. It also establishes a Committee for the Preservation of the White House to advise the President and the National Park Service on preserving the museum character of the White House’s public rooms. The committee must work with the White House Historical Association, and federal departments and agencies on the committee must provide needed help.

11144.s: This order creates the Temporary Alaska Claims Commission to settle disputes between the United States and the State of Alaska over certain property transfers. The commission has three members appointed by the President with Senate consent, and the General Services Administration will provide support. It will review the listed property, report its settlements to the Secretary of the Interior, and the Secretary will transfer property to Alaska as needed based on those settlements.

11143.s: This order sets up the Public Advisory Committee for Trade Negotiations. The committee is made up of 30 to 40 members from outside the U.S. Government, and they serve without pay. It advises the Special Representative for Trade Negotiations on matters about preparing for and taking part in international trade negotiations.

11142.s: This order lets the Veterans' Administration pay actual travel expenses, including lodging and subsistence, for claimants and beneficiaries traveling for vocational rehabilitation, counseling, examination, treatment, or care. It also allows a mileage payment instead of actual travel costs, plus ferry fares and bridge, road, and tunnel tolls. If an attendant is needed, the attendant's travel expenses may be paid the same way.

11141.s: This order says the Executive Branch policy is that contractors and subcontractors on Federal contracts must not discriminate against people because of age in hiring, promotion, firing, or other terms of employment, except where a bona fide occupational qualification, retirement plan, or statutory requirement applies. It also says they must not put a maximum age limit in job notices for Government contract work unless that limit is based on one of those reasons. Department and agency heads are told to take action to make this policy clear in Federal procurement rules.

11140.s: This order gives the Secretary of Health, Education, and Welfare several presidential powers under the Public Health Service Act. It also lets the Surgeon General accept voluntary resignations of commissioned officers in the Regular Corps or Reserve Corps. The Secretary may redelegate some of these functions to the Surgeon General or other Senate-confirmed Public Health Service officials, and earlier related executive orders are superseded or revoked.

11139.s: This order lets the Secretary of Defense and the Secretary of the Treasury set rules for certain members of the armed forces to accept the United Nations Medal and Service Ribbon. It applies to members of the Army, Navy, Air Force, Marine Corps, and, in some cases, the Coast Guard. A decision that service with the United Nations in a certain area or for a certain purpose justifies acceptance must be made with the Secretary of State’s agreement.

11138.s: This order changes a prior executive order for the transfer of federal personnel to certain public international organizations. It waives two time limits for Frederick Strauss and treats him as on leave from the Federal Government from August 12, 1957, through September 16, 1962, for the rights and benefits covered by the earlier order.

11137.s: This order adds civilian employees paid from nonappropriated funds of certain armed forces instrumentalities to the rules for foreign-area allowances and differentials. It lets the military departments and the Secretary of the Treasury set regulations for these payments without further presidential action, subject to limits in the order. It also lets those officials approve cost-of-living allowance rules for these employees when they are stationed outside the continental United States or in Alaska, but not in the Canal Zone or in a foreign area.

11135.s: This order creates a three-member board to investigate disputes between certain railroad carriers and some of their employees represented by the Brotherhood of Railroad Signalmen. The board must report its findings to the President within thirty days. During that time, and for thirty days after the report, the carriers and their employees may not change the conditions that led to the disputes unless they agree to do so.

11136.s: The order establishes the President's Committee on Consumer Interests and the Consumer Advisory Council. The Committee includes federal officials and private citizens, and the President names the chairmen. The Committee and Council advise federal agencies on consumer issues, and agencies must consider their recommendations and provide information when asked. The order also gives the General Services Administration administrative support for the Committee.

11133.s: This order opens certain income, estate, and gift tax returns from 1959 to 1963 to inspection by the Senate Committee on Rules and Administration or a subcommittee it authorizes. The inspection is for the committee’s study of the financial or business interests or activities of current or former Senate officers or employees. The inspection must follow Treasury rules for Congress.

11134.s: This order changes the rules for the President’s Commission on Registration and Voting Participation. It says the Commission will end no later than March 30, 1964.

11132.s: This order creates the Interagency Committee on Export Expansion to advise the Secretary of Commerce on export expansion policies and programs. The committee includes officials from several federal agencies, and the Secretary of Commerce is responsible for improving coordination among federal agencies on export promotion programs. Federal agencies are to give the committee help, information, data, and reports when requested.

11130.s: This order appoints a commission to investigate and report on the assassination of President John F. Kennedy and the violent death of the man charged with the assassination. The commission is directed to examine evidence from the Federal Bureau of Investigation and any other evidence found by Federal or State authorities. It may set its own procedures, hire assistants, and get help from executive departments and agencies.

11131.s: This order creates a three-member board to investigate disputes between several air carriers and certain of their employees represented by the International Association of Machinists, AFL-CIO. The board must report its findings to the President within thirty days, and the carriers and their employees may not change the conditions at issue except by agreement during that time and for thirty days after the report.

11129.s: This order designates the facilities of NASA’s Launch Operations Center and Station No. 1 of the Atlantic Missile Range in Florida as the John F. Kennedy Space Center. Those facilities are to be known by that name from then on.

11128.s: The order closed executive departments, independent establishments, and other government agencies on Monday, November 25, 1963, as a mark of respect for President John Fitzgerald Kennedy. It also allowed parts of the Department of State, the Department of Defense, and other agencies to stay open if their leaders decided it was needed for national security, defense, or other public reasons.

11126.s: The order creates an interdepartmental Committee on the Status of Women and a Citizens' Advisory Council on the Status of Women. The committee is to review how federal agencies are advancing the status of women, share information, encourage cooperation, and promote research on issues like education, employment, taxes, and civil and political rights. The council is to suggest action, review progress by organizations, and advise the committee on ways to advance the status of women.

11125.s: This order delegates some of the President’s authority under sections 205 and 208(b) of title 18 of the U.S. Code on conflicts of interest. It lets department or agency heads handle certain permission requests for some presidential appointees and government employees, including special Government employees. It does not delegate that authority for department or agency heads, certain White House appointees, or appointees to presidential committees and similar groups.

11127.s: This order creates a board of three members to investigate a dispute between the Florida East Coast Railway Company and certain of its employees represented by eleven railway labor organizations. The board must report its findings to the President within thirty days. During that time, and for thirty days after the report, the company and its employees may not change the conditions that led to the dispute except by agreement.

11124.s: This order changes the membership of the President’s Advisory Council on the Arts. It adds several government officials, up to forty people from private life who are recognized for their role in the arts, and the Librarian of Congress may be invited to join. It also says the order does not end or change the service of anyone who was already a member before it was signed.

11122.s: This order creates the Rural Development Committee to help coordinate federal rural-development work. The committee gives leadership and policy guidance to federal agencies and focuses on cooperation with state, local, private, and other government partners to identify and meet rural needs. It also revokes Executive Order 10847.

11121.s: This order creates a three-member board to investigate a dispute between United Air Lines and certain of its employees represented by the International Association of Machinists, AFL-CIO. The board must report its findings to the President within thirty days. For that period and for thirty days after the report, United Air Lines and its employees may not change the disputed working conditions except by agreement.

11123.s: This order changes an earlier executive order about allowances for certain government personnel on foreign duty. It updates which rules the President’s authority covers for some parts of title 38 of the United States Code. It also says rules set by the Secretary of State may take effect on dates he chooses, but not before the dates listed for Europe and for the territory of the Republic of the Philippines.

11120.s: This order changes rules on incentive pay for hazardous duty, special pay for sea duty and duty at certain places, and basic allowances for quarters. It updates who can receive pay for submarine duty, parachute jumping, work in pressure chambers, and multiple hazardous duties. It also changes pay rules for enlisted members on sea duty or duty outside the contiguous 48 States and the District of Columbia, and lets some commissioned officers without dependents choose basic allowance for quarters instead of assigned quarters.

11119.s: This order amends the Selective Service regulations. It sets the order for selecting nonvolunteers who are 19 years old or older and under 26, with those who do not have a wife in their home selected by date of birth, oldest first, and those who do have a wife in their home selected the same way.

11117.s: This order creates the Interagency Committee on International Athletics. The committee is to collect, exchange, and review information about amateur athletics that might affect the foreign relations or general welfare of the United States. It may ask federal departments, agencies, organizations, and individuals for information, and it must report to the President and the Secretary of State.

11116.s: This order sets charges for hospitalization and dispensary services for United States employees, their dependents, and all others. It gives the President’s authority to set these rates to an executive order function that can be amended or revoked later. It also revokes Executive Order 9411 and says the order takes effect on January 1, 1964.

11118.s: The order directs the Secretary of Defense to take steps to remove obstructions of justice in Alabama and enforce United States laws there, including court orders about enrollment and attendance of students in public schools. It also authorizes the use of Armed Forces if needed. The Secretary of Defense may call Alabama National Guard units into active military service for an indefinite period and may delegate some authority to the Secretary of the Army or the Secretary of the Air Force.

11114.s: This order extends nondiscrimination rules to certain construction contracts financed with federal grants, loans, insurance, or guarantees. It requires agencies to make applicants agree to include those rules in covered construction contracts and to help enforce them. It also gives the President's Committee on Equal Employment Opportunity authority to issue rules, exempt some programs or contracts, and recommend sanctions for noncompliance.

11115.s: This order creates a three-member board to investigate disputes between the Pullman Company, the Chicago, Rock Island & Pacific Railroad Company, the New York Central System, the Soo Line Railroad Company, and certain of their employees represented by the Brotherhood of Sleeping Car Porters. The board must report its findings to the President within thirty days. During that time, and for thirty days after the report is made, the companies and their employees may not change the conditions out of which the dispute arose except by agreement.

11113.s: The order changes the trade agreements office by creating two officers called Deputy Special Representatives for Trade Negotiations, each with the rank of Ambassador. Their main job is to conduct negotiations under title II of the Trade Expansion Act of 1962, and they may also do other duties the Special Representative assigns.

11111.s: This order directs the Secretary of Defense to take steps to remove obstructions of justice in Alabama and to enforce United States laws there, including court orders named in the order. It also authorizes the use of Armed Forces as needed to suppress unlawful assemblies, combinations, conspiracies, and domestic violence that block those laws or justice. The Secretary of Defense may also call Alabama Army National Guard and Air National Guard units into active military service for an indefinite period, and may delegate this authority to the Secretary of the Army or the Secretary of the Air Force.

11112.s: This order establishes the President's Advisory Council on the Arts. The Council includes certain federal officials and up to thirty members from private life who are recognized for their work in the arts. It is to study the arts in the United States, review federal laws and programs that affect the arts, and make reports and recommendations to the President.

11110.s: This order amends a previous executive order about functions affecting the Department of the Treasury. It adds authority to issue silver certificates, set their denominations, and coin standard silver dollars and subsidiary silver currency for their redemption. It also revokes two subparagraphs in the earlier order and says the change does not affect rights, liabilities, or court actions that already existed before the order.

11109.s: This order opens certain income, excess-profits, estate, and gift tax returns from 1947 through 1963 to inspection by the House Committee on Un-American Activities or a duly authorized subcommittee. The inspection is for investigations of subversive and un-American activities and propaganda. It must follow Treasury rules for committee inspection of tax returns.

11108.s: This order gives the Secretary of Agriculture the President’s authority under the International Wheat Agreement Act of 1949. The Secretary may make wheat and wheat flour available, restrict imports or exports of wheat or wheat flour, require reports and records, and examine related books and papers. The Secretary must consult with the Secretary of State, the Special Representative for Trade Negotiations, and other appropriate officers or agencies, and may delegate this authority within the Department of Agriculture.

11106.s: This order amends an earlier order on the trade agreements program. It sets up the Office of the Special Representative for Trade Negotiations in the Executive Office of the President and makes that official directly responsible to the President. It also gives that office duties on trade agreement negotiations, reports to Congress, and related trade matters, and allows certain authority to be passed on to others.

11107.s: This order gives the Secretary of the Interior authority to operate Alaska railroads, branch lines, feeders, and related telegraph and telephone lines. It also lets the Secretary set, change, or modify passenger and property rates, with those rates subject to review by the Interstate Commerce Commission. The Secretary must post the rates for public inspection and file them with the Commission.

11105.s: This order transfers many Atomic Energy Commission functions under the Atomic Energy Community Act of 1955 to the Housing and Home Finance Administrator for the community of Los Alamos, New Mexico. It does not apply to Oak Ridge, Tennessee, or Richland, Washington. The Commission keeps some powers over deciding what property is offered for disposal and other listed duties, and the two agencies must stay in contact on matters under the Act.

11104.s: The order directs that the U.S. flag be flown at half-staff until sunset on Monday, April 15, 1963. This applies to federal buildings, grounds, and naval vessels in the United States and its territories, and to U.S. embassies, legations, consular offices, other facilities abroad, and military facilities and naval stations.

11103.s:
This order lets certain former Peace Corps volunteers be appointed to jobs in the Executive Branch if they are certified as having served satisfactorily and pass any required examination. It applies to the competitive service and to the excepted service in agencies with an established merit system.

It says certificates are generally for people who completed a full Peace Corps term, but some shorter service may qualify if the Director of the Peace Corps approves. Appointments must usually be made within one year after service ends, with some extensions allowed, and any other law or rule that would disqualify a person can still apply.

11102.s: This order says certain tax returns can be inspected by a properly authorized official, body, or commission that administers tax laws in a U.S. possession. The inspection must follow rules set by the Secretary of the Treasury. It applies to returns made under the listed parts of the Internal Revenue Code.

11100.s: This order creates the President's Commission on Registration and Voting Participation. The commission is to study why many citizens do not register and vote in elections for Congress, the President, and Vice President, including registration rules, absentee voting, and other causes of nonvoting. It is also to recommend ways to increase citizen participation in government through voting.

11101.s: This order creates a three-member board to investigate disputes between certain rail carriers and their employees. The board must report its findings to the President within thirty days. During that time, and for thirty days after the report, the carriers and their employees may not change the conditions that led to the disputes except by agreement.

11099.s: This order allows the House Committee on Public Works, or a duly authorized subcommittee, to inspect certain income, estate, and gift tax returns from 1956 through 1963. The inspection is for its investigation into the policies, procedures, and practices used in administering the Federal-Aid Highway Program. The inspections must follow Treasury rules for congressional review of returns.

11097.s: This order changes which agencies have authority to make original classifications of defense information and material. It adds the Export-Import Bank of Washington, the Office of Science and Technology, and the Special Representative for Trade Negotiations to that list. It also removes the Subversive Activities Control Board from the list.

11098.s: This order changes Selective Service rules for mailing classification questionnaires, appeals, and medical screening. It says local boards should mail questionnaires in birth order, may wait to mail one to a registrant on active duty until he is separated, and must reopen a classification if asked by Selective Service officials. It also changes who can be placed in Class III-A, sets rules for medical interviews and examinations, revokes one part of the regulations, and says nonvolunteers age 19 through 25 are to be selected by age, with the oldest first.

11096.s: This order approves a seal as the official seal of the United States Civil Service Commission. It applies to the Civil Service Commission and sets out the seal’s design and wording.

11095.s: This order tells the Tennessee Valley Authority, the Railroad Retirement Board, NASA, the Federal Power Commission, and the National Science Foundation to make emergency plans and preparedness programs for national emergencies, including attack on the United States. It assigns each agency specific readiness duties in areas like electric power, waterways, flood control, health supplies, fertilizers, munitions, rail manpower, benefit payments, research, and support for defense needs.
