It says the land is no longer fully needed for military purposes. The United States keeps the right to enter, leave, and pass over the land for armed-forces maneuver purposes.

10710.s: This order creates a Board of Inquiry to look into a labor dispute between the Goodyear Atomic Corporation and some of its employees at the Portsmouth Plant near Waverly, Ohio. The dispute is said to have caused a strike, and the order says the Board must report to the President. The Board will keep working after the report if needed under the Labor-Management Relations Act, until the President ends it.

10708.s: This executive order changes how parts of the Agricultural Trade Development and Assistance Act of 1954 are administered. It updates which paragraphs of section 4 apply and assigns some duties to the Department of Defense, the Department of State, the Bureau of the Budget, and the United States Information Agency. It also sets rules for how foreign currencies from Title I are to be used for certain loans.

10709.s: The order creates a three-member board to investigate a labor dispute between three dock companies and some of their employees. The board must report its findings to the President, and the companies and their employees may not change the conditions involved in the dispute except by agreement during the covered period.

10707.s: This order approves a seal as the official seal of the United States Coast Guard. It applies to the Coast Guard and establishes the design described in the order as its official emblem.

10706.s: This order makes certain income, excess-profits, declared-value excess-profits, capital-stock, estate, and gift tax returns open to inspection by the Senate Committee on the Judiciary, or a subcommittee it authorizes. The returns covered are for tax years 1945 through 1957. The inspection is for the committee's investigation of the administration, operation, and enforcement of the Internal Security Act of 1950 and other internal security laws.

10704.s: This order changes the membership of the President's Council on Youth Fitness. It makes the Vice President the chairman and includes the Secretaries of Defense, the Interior, Agriculture, Labor, and Health, Education, and Welfare.

10705.s: This order gives the Director of the Office of Defense Mobilization certain presidential authority under the Communications Act of 1934 over radio stations and communications. It applies those powers only during war or when the President proclaims a state of war, depending on the section involved. The Director may issue rules and may redelegate some authority, but the order does not allow control over the content of any station program or communication.

10702.s: The order honors the memory of Rear Admiral Richard E. Byrd. It directs that the United States flag be flown at half-staff on all Federal Government buildings, grounds, and naval vessels in the District of Columbia and throughout the United States and its territories and possessions until interment.

10701.s: This order says certain income, excess-profits, declared-value excess-profits, capital-stock, estate, and gift tax returns for periods up to and including 1957 must be open to inspection by the House Committee on Un-American Activities or a subcommittee it authorizes. The inspection is for investigations allowed by House rules and must follow Treasury rules for congressional review of tax returns.

10703.s: This order allows certain income, excess-profits, declared-value excess-profits, capital-stock, estate, and gift tax returns from 1945 through 1957 to be inspected during the 85th Congress. The Select Committee of the Senate investigating improper activities in labor-management relations, and any authorized subcommittee, may inspect the returns to carry out its work. The inspections must follow Treasury rules for viewing congressional committee access to tax returns.

10699.s: This order allows certain income, excess-profits, declared-value excess-profits, capital-stock, estate, and gift tax returns for 1945 to 1957 to be opened for inspection by the Senate Committee on Government Operations, or a subcommittee it authorizes. The inspection is for the committee’s studies of how government activities operate and how economical and efficient the government is. The inspection must follow rules set by the Secretary of the Treasury.

10700.s: This order creates the Operations Coordinating Board within the National Security Council to help coordinate national security work across certain agencies. It sets out who serves on the Board, how it may use staff, and how it reports to the National Security Council. The order also says the Board does not take away any legal powers from other agencies or their leaders.

10698.s: This order amends a prior order to correct errors in the land descriptions for certain parcels and tracts at Kapahulu, Honolulu, on the Island of Oahu in the Territory of Hawaii. It changes the described courses for Parcel 2, Parcel 3, Tract 1-A, and Tract 1-C. The changes affect the lands that had been restored to the possession, use, and control of the Territory of Hawaii.

10697.s: This order sets fees for official services performed abroad by officers of the Foreign Service of the United States. It says only the listed fees, or fees allowed by Congress, may be charged, and that the fees must be paid in advance in United States coin or its exchange value. It also says no fees may be charged for official services to American vessels and seamen, except that the listed fees apply to "undocumented American vessels."

10696.s: The order creates a three-member board to investigate a dispute between Railway Express Agency, Incorporated, and some of its employees represented by the International Brotherhood of Teamsters, Chauffeurs, Warehousemen and Helpers of America. The board must report its findings to the President within thirty days. During that time, and for thirty days after the report is made, neither the company nor its employees may change the working conditions tied to the dispute except by agreement.

10695.s: This order revokes paragraph 2(b) of Executive Order No. 10096, which dealt with indexing inventions owned or controlled by the United States. It also authorizes the Chairman of the Government Patents Board to transfer records made under that paragraph to the Department of Commerce.

10694.s: This order lets the Secretaries of the Army, Navy, and Air Force issue a citation in the President’s name to military units for outstanding performance in action. It also allows units of armed forces of co-belligerent nations serving with U.S. forces to receive the same kind of citation if they meet the same standards. Units that receive a citation may display an insignia, and eligible service members may wear a ribbon and later citation devices.

10693.s: This order creates a board to investigate disputes between the Akron & Barberton Belt Railroad and other carriers, and certain of their employees represented by the Brotherhood of Railroad Trainmen. The board must report its findings to the President. Until the board reports, and for a time after that report, no change except by agreement may be made in the conditions out of which the disputes arose.

10691.s: This order creates a board of three members to investigate a dispute between the Spokane, Portland and Seattle Railway Company and some of its employees represented by the Brotherhood of Locomotive Engineers. The board must report its findings to the President within thirty days. During that time, and for thirty days after the report is made, neither the company nor its employees may change the conditions involved in the dispute except by agreement.

10690.s: The order suspends compliance with certain legal rules about employment in the Canal Zone. It does not change the rules about how much pay may be received by people in skilled, technical, clerical, administrative, executive, or supervisory jobs there. It applies to employment connected to the United States Government or to companies partly or wholly owned by it.

10688.s: This order restores two parcels of land from the Waianae-Kai Military Reservation to the possession, use, and control of the Territory of Hawaii. The land is restored subject to a condition that the United States keeps the right to enter, leave, and move over it for armed-forces maneuver purposes.

10687.s: This order suspends part of a federal law about how many Navy officers can be recommended for promotion. It applies to the number of officers that may be recommended for promotion to captain in the Civil Engineer Corps. The suspension lasts until June 30, 1957.

10686.s: This order adds the General Counsel of the Post Office Department to the list of officers who may act as Postmaster General. It affects officers in the Post Office Department named in the earlier order.

10689.s: This order creates a Board of Inquiry to look into labor disputes between certain maritime employers and employees represented by the International Longshoremen's Association (Independent). The disputes involve steamship companies, contracting stevedores, contracting marine carpenters, and other employers in related pier activities. The Board must report to the President and then stay in existence to carry out other duties under the law until the President ends it.

10685.s: The order designates the International Cooperation Administration as the federal agency to receive funds for ocean freight costs under Title II of the Act. It says the Commodity Credit Corporation may transfer those funds to that agency. It also keeps with the President the functions to make reports to Congress and to designate the agency for those ocean freight funds.

10684.s: This order includes certain lands in Carter County and Johnson County, Tennessee, in the Cherokee National Forest. The lands are on the shores of Watauga Lake and include some islands in the lake. The inclusion is subject to the terms and conditions of the July 26, 1955 agreement between the Tennessee Valley Authority and the United States Department of Agriculture.

10683.s: This order includes about 100 acres of land in Carter County, Tennessee, as part of the Cherokee National Forest. The land is on the shores of Wilbur Lake and is divided into four parcels. The transfer is subject to TVA's retained rights of way and easements for transmission lines and an electric power distribution line.

10682.s: This order changes an earlier executive order about who can be exempted from automatic separation from service. It says the President’s authority to grant those exemptions applies except for Presidential appointees. The exemptions are for people or employees when the President judges that the public interest requires it.

10680.s: This order designates the International Finance Corporation as a public international organization under the International Organizations Immunities Act. It gives the corporation the privileges, exemptions, and immunities allowed by that law. It also says the designation does not limit any other privileges, exemptions, or immunities the corporation may have by treaty or Congressional action.

10681.s: This order amends a prior executive order on incentive pay for hazardous duty. It adds minimum flight requirements for members of Reserve components of the uniformed services who do both active-duty and inactive-duty training in the same calendar month and may qualify for incentive pay under two sections of the Career Compensation Act of 1949. It says the total flight requirements may be met during that month on inactive-duty training, or on both active-duty and inactive-duty training if the inactive-duty flight requirement has been met.

10679.s: This order sets rules for agreements between the Secretary of Defense and States or Territories about withholding pay from certain civilian Army National Guard and Air National Guard employees for state or territorial retirement systems. It applies to employees paid from federal funds who are eligible for those retirement systems, except those employed by the National Guard Bureau. The order also says the agreements must follow state or territorial law, set out how withholding and payment will work, and may not make the United States subject to extra burdens or penalties.

10678.s: This order puts the Federal Facilities Corporation in charge of the sale or lease contracts for government-owned rubber producing facilities and other duties of the Rubber Producing Facilities Disposal Commission. It also transfers the Commission’s records, property, liabilities, employees, and available funds to the Corporation. The national-security parts of the contracts are to be handled based on the needs of national defense as determined by the Secretary of Defense, and the Secretary of the Treasury directs the matters assigned to the Corporation.

10677.s: This order amends a prior order to authorize enlistments in the Ready Reserve of the Air Force Reserve. It also keeps the earlier authorization for the Army Reserve, Marine Corps Reserve, Naval Reserve, and Coast Guard Reserve. The order says these enlistments may be accepted under regulations the Secretary of Defense prescribes.

10676.s: This order designates the World Meteorological Organization as a public international organization under the International Organizations Immunities Act. It gives the organization the privileges, exemptions, and immunities that come with that status, without limiting any it may already have by treaty or congressional action.

10675.s: This order changes a rule on career-conditional appointments for certain employees entitled to veteran preference who have a compensable service-connected disability of 10 percent or more. It allows their appointments to be converted to career appointments if their agency recommends them and certifies that they have completed a one-year probationary period. If they are not certified under this section, their appointment is converted when they meet the service requirement for a career appointment.

10673.s: This order creates a President's Council on Youth Fitness and a President's Citizens Advisory Committee on the Fitness of American Youth. The Council is directed to promote existing programs and add new ones to improve the fitness of American youth, and to coordinate federal agencies on that issue. The Advisory Committee is to review government and private measures related to making American youth healthier and more fit.

10674.s: This order exempts certain officers and employees in the executive branch from automatic separation from service for a limited time. It applies to presidentially appointed workers who are subject to the Civil Service Retirement Act and reach the retirement age between July 1, 1956, and September 30, 1956.

10672.s: This order sets rules for an agreement between the Secretary of the Treasury and the District of Columbia on withholding District of Columbia income taxes from pay for federal employees. It says federal agencies must follow the tax law for covered employees whose regular place of employment is within the District of Columbia, and it sets procedures for withholding, filing returns, and paying the tax. It does not apply to pay for service in the armed forces or to employees who do not live or are not domiciled in the District of Columbia when the tax is due to be withheld.

10671.s: This order directs the United States flag to be flown at half-staff until interment as a mark of respect for Fleet Admiral Ernest J. King. It applies to all Federal Government buildings, grounds, and naval vessels in the District of Columbia, throughout the United States, and in its Territories and possessions.

10670.s: This order approves an official flag for the United States Army. It describes the flag’s size, color, and design, including the Army seal, the words "UNITED STATES ARMY," and the numerals "1775." It also says some official Army flags may have streamers for each officially recognized campaign, with the campaign name and year embroidered on each streamer.

10669.s: This order changes a previous rule on who would step in to act as Secretary of Defense, Secretary of the Army, Secretary of the Navy, and Secretary of the Air Force. It updates several named offices in the line of succession for the Army, Navy, and Air Force. The changes affect the officials listed in those succession rules.

10668.s: This order amends the rules for the National Research Council of the National Academy of Sciences. It says the Council should promote research in the sciences, help use scientific and technical resources, support cooperation in research, and gather scientific and technical information. It also provides for government representation on the Council and says it does not end the terms of people already named to it.

10667.s: This order changes a previous order on enlistments in the Ready Reserve. It authorizes enlistments in the Ready Reserve of the Army Reserve, Marine Corps Reserve, Naval Reserve, and Coast Guard Reserve. The order applies to people who enlist in those reserve units, under regulations set by the Secretary of Defense.

10664.s: This order returns several parcels of land in the Waianae-Kai Military Reservation on Oahu to the possession, use, and control of the Territory of Hawaii. The order says these lands are no longer needed for military purposes. It applies to five described parcels of land.

10663.s: This order lets the Secretary of State carry out certain functions through any officer or agency of the Department of State. It ends the duty of the Director of the International Cooperation Administration to help make and present U.S. policy on assistance programs for the Intergovernmental Committee for European Migration, the United Nations Refugee Fund, and the United Nations Children's Fund. It also lets the Secretary of State transfer or assign needed offices, personnel, property, and records from the International Cooperation Administration to Department of State agencies.

10662.s: This order changes an earlier order about how the Defense Production Act of 1950 is carried out. It directs the Director of the Office of Defense Mobilization to encourage the exploration, development, and mining of critical and strategic minerals and metals, and to make provision for substitutes for strategic and critical materials. It also removes some functions from that earlier order and revokes another executive order.

10661.s: This order gives certain Cabinet officers the power to choose foreign persons who may be allowed to receive instruction at U.S. service academies and the Merchant Marine Academy. It applies to people from the American Republics other than the United States, Canada, and, for the Naval Academy, Filipinos. It also says the designating officer must consult the Secretary of State before anyone is chosen.

10660.s: This order creates a National Defense Executive Reserve in the executive branch. It is made up of people from civilian jobs and government who are trained for executive jobs in the Federal Government during emergencies. The Director of the Office of Defense Mobilization must run the program, set standards for recruiting and training, and report to the President. Some agencies may set up reserve units, choose members, and non-full-time reservists are limited to training and exempt from certain federal conflict rules.

10659.s: This order amends the Selective Service regulations. It updates the definition of military service and changes who must register, including certain exchange visitors, student nonimmigrants, treaty nationals, and some people connected to NATO forces. It also revises draft classification rules for some members and former members of the armed forces, the Coast and Geodetic Survey, the Public Health Service, National Guard, and Ready Reserve, and it adds rules for some agricultural and sole surviving son deferments.

10657.s: This order transfers many functions under the Atomic Energy Community Act of 1955 from the Atomic Energy Commission to the Housing and Home Finance Administrator. The Commission keeps some duties, including deciding what property is offered for disposal and some related procedures. The order also transfers certain property interests, deeds, and funds linked to property disposal, while keeping prior Commission actions and existing obligations in place.

10658.s: This order changes a prior order that gave the Secretary of Defense authority over certain military draft and active-duty matters. It lets the Secretary set rules for appointing, reappointing, and promoting certain physicians, dentists, and allied specialists, and for ordering some reserve members and other covered persons to active duty, with priority rules to be followed when practical.

10655.s: This order sets up the Air Coordinating Committee to help develop and coordinate aviation policies and activities of federal agencies. It includes representatives from several executive departments, military departments, and federal boards and commissions, with the President naming the Chairman. The Committee is also directed to review aviation problems, recommend policies, consult with other federal and international aviation bodies, and report to the President.

10654.s: This order gives the Director of the Bureau of the Budget the President’s job of sending Congress copies of certain plans for works of improvement and the reasons for them. It applies to the functions listed in the Watershed Protection and Flood Prevention Act.

10656.s: This order creates the President's Board of Consultants on Foreign Intelligence Activities. The board is made up of people from outside the government and is appointed by the President without pay, though they may get travel and daily allowances. It must review the government's foreign intelligence activities and the Central Intelligence Agency, and report its findings to the President. Board members must keep classified information secret except as the President allows.

10653.s: This order designates and authorizes the Honorable A. Cecil Snyder to act as judge of the United States District Court for the District of Puerto Rico during 1956 if the judge’s office is vacant or if the judge dies, is absent, is ill, or has another legal disability. It also lets him sign necessary papers and records as acting judge without extra compensation.

10652.s: This order changes a rule in the Manual for Courts-Martial for enlisted people above the lowest pay grade. If a court-martial sentence approved by the convening authority includes a dishonorable or bad-conduct discharge, confinement, or hard labor without confinement, the person is reduced to the lowest enlisted pay grade. The order also says the reduced pay must match the person's cumulative service, and rights, privileges, and property must be restored if the sentence is later set aside or does not end up including those penalties. It takes effect on January 20, 1956.

10651.s: This order sets rules for screening members of the Ready Reserve. It says some members must be transferred to the Standby Reserve, discharged, or placed in the Retired Reserve based on age, fitness, civilian job needs, military skills, or other listed reasons. It also allows some members to stay in the Ready Reserve if they sign a one-year written agreement. The Secretary of Defense is to make periodic reports to the President about the screening.

10650.s: This order sets rules for choosing certain registrants with critical skills for enlistment in Ready Reserve units. It applies to people in Class I-A who work in critical defense-supporting industries or in research affecting national defense. It also sets a request and appeal process, requires selected registrants to enlist within 30 days, and requires them to report changes in address, job, or employment after training.

10648.s: This order restores several parcels of land in Kapahulu, Honolulu, on the Island of Oahu, to the possession, use, and control of the Territory of Hawaii. The land had been part of the Fort Ruger Military Reservation, and the order says parts of it are needed for National Guard, Air National Guard, and civil-defense purposes. It also keeps certain easements and rights-of-way for the United States.

10649.s: This order changes the rules for counting travel time as active duty when members of the uniformed services are called to active duty. It covers travel from home to the first duty station and from the last duty station back home, and it says travel time is figured using official mileage tables and the rules for public transportation or private conveyance. It also says private conveyance is not specifically authorized when the call to active duty is for less than ninety consecutive days.

10647.s: This order lets the heads of certain departments and agencies hire unpaid people with outstanding experience and ability, and hire experts and consultants, under the Defense Production Act. It says these appointments should be used mainly for advisory or consultative work, and it sets rules to avoid conflicts between government duties and private interests. It also creates filing and reporting requirements for the appointments and revokes two earlier executive orders.

10646.s: The order names the Secretary of Defense to coordinate and help carry out federal responsibilities under the Federal Voting Assistance Act of 1955. It also lets the Secretary of Defense delegate those functions, responsibilities, powers, authority, or discretion to people within the Department of Defense.

10645.s: This order changes an earlier rule that generally barred federal officers and employees from holding certain state, territorial, or municipal offices. It allows a federal officer or employee to serve as a member of the State Board of Agriculture of Michigan, as long as that service does not interfere with the person’s federal duties.

10644.s: The order gives the Attorney General, and any Assistant Attorney General named by the Attorney General, the power to carry out the functions under Title II of the International Claims Settlement Act of 1949. It also names the Attorney General as the officer in whom property will vest under that title, including property from Bulgaria, Hungary, and Romania.

10643.s: This order creates a three-member board to investigate disputes between the Albany Port District Railroad and other carriers and certain of their employees. The disputes involve wage demands and changes in agreements covering health and welfare benefits, and the board must report its findings to the President within thirty days.

10642.s: This order suspends compliance with certain statutory rules about employment in the Canal Zone. It does not change the provisions about how much pay may be received by people in skilled, technical, clerical, administrative, executive, or supervisory positions there. Those pay rules apply to people employed by the United States Government or by a corporation or company partly or wholly owned by the United States Government.

10640.s: The order continues the President's Committee on Employment of the Physically Handicapped and sets up an Executive Committee and an Advisory Council. It tells the committee to help create more job opportunities for physically handicapped people by giving information to employers, doing public education, and working with federal, state, and local officials and groups. It also sets rules for how the committees are staffed, meet, and are paid.

10641.s: This order changes the Civil Service Rules to allow federal agencies to recruit and appoint people for overseas positions in foreign countries and other areas beyond the continental limits of the United States. It lets United States citizens be appointed to these jobs without the usual competitive requirements and creates "overseas limited appointments" that do not give competitive status. It also allows noncitizens to be recruited overseas and appointed to overseas positions without regard to the Civil Service Act. The rule does not apply to positions in Hawaii, Puerto Rico, the Virgin Islands, Alaska, or the Isthmus of Panama.

10639.s: This order changes the Tariff of United States Foreign Service Fees by deleting Items 1 through 5 from the fee list. It also says any earlier executive orders that conflict with this change are amended to match it.

10638.s: This order authorizes the Director of the Office of Defense Mobilization to order the release of strategic and critical materials from government stockpiles if there is an enemy attack on the continental United States, excluding Alaska. The materials may be released in amounts, for uses, and on terms the Director decides are needed for national defense. It affects stockpiles of these materials and their use for military and essential civilian needs.

10637.s: This order gives the Secretary of the Treasury the President’s Coast Guard-related powers in many personnel and disciplinary matters. It covers actions like assigning Coast Guard officers to assist foreign governments, retiring or revoking commissions of officers, and awarding Coast Guard medals and related devices. It also covers certain powers over vessels, wartime clearances, and Coast Guard Reserve appointments and discharges. When the Coast Guard operates as part of the Navy, these references shift to the Secretary of the Navy.

10636.s: This order amends pay rules for certain Federal employees serving outside the United States and for those receiving territorial post differentials and territorial cost-of-living allowances. It says payments start and stop based on arrival and departure, are prorated for part-time service, and are not paid for time when an employee does not receive basic compensation. It also says the related regulations should be uniform when practicable.

10634.s: This order allows loans, loan participations, or loan guarantees when other financial help is not available on reasonable terms. The loans are for rebuilding, fixing, or replacing facilities damaged or destroyed by a major disaster when those facilities are needed for national defense. The Director of the Office of Defense Mobilization must determine that the facilities are required for national defense.

10635.s: This order creates a board of three members to investigate a dispute between the Pennsylvania Railroad and certain of its employees represented by the Transport Workers Union of America, C.I.O., Railroad Division. The board must report its findings to the President within thirty days. During that time, and for thirty days after the report is made, the Pennsylvania Railroad and its employees may not change the conditions that caused the dispute except by agreement.

10633.s: This order reserves the airspace over the Las Vegas Project in Nevada for national defense and other government purposes. No one may fly an aircraft in this area unless authorized by the United States Atomic Energy Commission. Anyone who violates the order is subject to penalties under the Civil Aeronautics Act of 1938. It replaces an earlier order that set up the same airspace reservation.

10632.s: This order suspends part of the Officer Personnel Act rules that apply to the Navy Medical Corps and Dental Corps. The suspension does not cover the rule about how many officers are furnished to the promotion board for temporary promotions, and it lasts until June 30 of the fiscal year after the national emergency ends.

10630.s: This order creates a three-member board to investigate a dispute between the New York Central System, Lines East, and certain of its employees. The board must report its findings to the President within 30 days. During that time, and for 30 days after the report, neither side may change the conditions tied to the dispute except by agreement.

10631.s: This order sets a Code of Conduct for members of the U.S. armed forces. It says service members are expected to follow these standards in combat or captivity, and those at risk of capture must get training and instruction on how to act. The Secretary of Defense, and the Secretary of the Treasury for the Coast Guard in some cases, must take steps to carry out the order and share the code with all members of the armed forces.

10629.s: This order authorizes enlistments in units of the Ready Reserve of the Army Reserve and Marine Corps Reserve. It applies to people enlisting in those reserve units, under rules the Secretary of Defense will prescribe.

10628.s: This order ends the suspension of punishment limits for violations of certain articles of the Uniform Code of Military Justice for offenses committed after it takes effect. It applies to persons under the command of, or within any area controlled by, the Commander-in-Chief, Far East, or that command’s successors. Those offenses are then subject to the Table of Maximum Punishments in the Manual for Courts-Martial, United States, 1951, as amended.

10627.s: This order allows the House Committee on Un-American Activities, or a subcommittee it authorizes, to inspect certain income, business, estate, and gift tax returns for periods up to and including 1955. The inspection is for investigations allowed under House rules and must follow Treasury rules and regulations.

10625.s: This order changes how certain foreign aid functions are handled under the Mutual Security Act of 1954. It gives some of those functions to the Secretary of State and the Secretary of Defense, and says the Secretary of State will determine the value of the program for any country under one section. It also says $300,000,000 will be divided between the Department of State and the Department of Defense as those departments agree.

10626.s: This order creates an interdepartmental committee to promote a voluntary payroll savings plan for buying United States Savings Bonds. The committee is made up of the heads of executive branch departments and agencies, with a chairman appointed by the President. It is meant to help set up the plan, solve problems, share information, and urge officers and employees to take part.

10623.s: This order changes rules on salary differentials and allowances for Foreign Service officers, Reserve officers, and staff officers and employees serving at certain overseas posts. It lets the Secretary of State set salary differentials for posts with very hard living, physical, or health conditions and cancel or make a list of unhealthful posts. It also updates rules on allowances for housing, heat, light, fuel, gas, electricity, cost of living, lodging at temporary quarters, and representation of the United States.

10624.s: This order directs that certain Department of Agriculture personnel assigned abroad follow coordination rules used for overseas work and carry out their duties in line with United States foreign-policy objectives. It also says the Secretary of Agriculture must give instructions on agricultural matters and coordinate these activities with other United States agencies under the Chief of the United States Diplomatic Mission. The order makes State Department rules on allowances and benefits apply to this personnel, and it allows the Secretary of Agriculture to issue needed directions and designate employees to carry out specific actions.

10621.s: This order lets the Secretary of Defense, and certain military department officials he designates, carry out many presidential functions over Navy and Marine Corps matters without further presidential approval. It covers things like Navy vessel classifications, enlistment rules, retirement decisions, temporary appointments, and other personnel and regulatory actions. It also lets the Secretary of Defense and certain defense officials approve changes to Navy Regulations and the dismissal of a midshipman from the United States Naval Academy.

10620.s: This order lets the Senate Committee on the Judiciary, or a subcommittee it authorizes, inspect certain tax returns for periods up to and including 1954. The returns include income, excess-profits, declared-value excess-profits, capital-stock, estate, and gift tax returns. The inspection is for a study of juvenile delinquency in the United States and its causes and contributing factors.

10618.s: This order amends rules for incentive pay for hazardous duty in the uniformed services. It changes the definition of duty involving the demolition of explosives and adds new covered duties for low-pressure chamber inside observers, human acceleration or deceleration experimental subjects, and helium-oxygen deep-sea diving duty. The changes apply to members assigned to those duties.

10619.s: This order says certain individual income tax returns may be inspected by the Department of Health, Education, and Welfare. The inspection is for the department’s work under Title II of the Social Security Act, and it must follow Treasury rules.

10617.s: This order suspends certain mandatory retirement rules for colonels of the Regular Army who hold a temporary grade higher than colonel. It applies only to those the Secretary of the Army chooses to keep on the active list in the public interest, and the suspension lasts until the emergency ends, until June 30, 1957, or until a date the Secretary sets, whichever comes first.

10616.s: This order suspends part of the Officer Personnel Act of 1947 that deals with service-in-grade requirements for Marine Corps brigadier generals. The suspended rules are the ones used to decide whether they can be considered by a selection board for temporary promotion to major general. The suspension lasts until June 30 of the fiscal year after the national emergency proclaimed on December 16, 1950 ends, and the order takes effect on July 1, 1955.

10614.s: This order sets rules for paying general-average contributions for certain baggage, household goods, and effects shipped for military personnel and civilian employees of the United States. It allows departments to pay these amounts or reimburse people who paid them, but only in cases covered by the order and subject to set limits. The order does not apply in some cases, including shipments paid on a commuted basis, shipments chosen by the person, or goods shipped over authorized amounts.

10615.s: This order creates a three-member board to investigate a dispute between certain carriers and certain employees represented by the Brotherhood of Locomotive Firemen and Engine-men. The board must report its findings to the President within thirty days. For thirty days after the board reports, the carriers and employees may not change the conditions that led to the dispute unless they agree.

10613.s: This order changes the Clemency and Parole Board’s powers for cases involving Japanese war criminals. It lets the board investigate and decide requests from the Government of Japan for sentence reduction or parole without further approval from the President. The board may also examine witnesses and take testimony as needed.

10612.s: This order returns a parcel of land in Waianae, Oahu, from military use to the possession, use, and control of the Territory of Hawaii. The land had been reserved for military purposes but was said to no longer be needed for that use. It applies to the same land described in the earlier 1938 order and covers 2.28 acres.

10610.s: This order moves many functions of the Foreign Operations Administration to the Department of State and creates the International Cooperation Administration there. It also transfers some military aid functions to the Department of Defense. The Foreign Operations Administration is abolished except for the parts moved under this order, and existing actions tied to those functions stay in effect unless changed later.

10611.s: This order creates a Civil Defense Coordinating Board within the executive branch. The Board is made up of the Administrator of the Federal Civil Defense Administration, who serves as chairman, and other members representing several federal officials and agencies. It helps plan federal participation in civil defense, makes recommendations to the President, works with the Department of Defense and the Office of Defense Mobilization, and advises the President on progress.

10609.s: This order gives the Secretary of State the power to appoint alternate United States Commissioners to the Caribbean Commission. The Secretary may do this without further approval or action by the President.

10608.s: This order revokes two earlier orders and abolishes the office of United States High Commissioner for Germany. It gives the Chief of the United States Diplomatic Mission supreme authority over civilian responsibilities of the United States in Germany, under the Secretary of State and the President. It also gives the United States Military Commander authority over military matters in Germany, including the command, security, and stationing of United States forces. The order sets rules for handling war criminals confined in Germany and for resolving major differences between the Chief of Mission and the Commander.

10607.s: This order allows the House Committee on Government Operations, or a subcommittee it authorizes, to inspect certain tax returns for periods up to and including 1954. The returns covered are income, excess-profits, declared-value excess-profits, capital-stock, estate, and gift tax returns. The inspection must follow Treasury rules and regulations.

10606.s: This order says certain income, excess-profits, declared-value excess-profits, capital-stock, estate, and gift tax returns for 1945 through 1954 may be inspected by the Senate Committee on Government Operations, or a subcommittee it authorizes. The inspection is for the committee's studies of government activities at all levels to determine the economy and efficiency of the Government. The inspection must follow rules and regulations set by the Secretary of the Treasury.

10604.s: This order gives the Director of the Bureau of the Budget the President’s authority to approve regulations for operating vending stands in Federal buildings by blind persons. It applies to regulations made by the heads of the departments and agencies covered by the law.

10605.s: This order changes the rules for basic subsistence pay for enlisted members of the uniformed services. It says members who are fed in a mess but are away from their station for one or more meals can get a prorated share of the daily allowance for each meal. It also lets the Secretaries of Defense, the Treasury, and Commerce set the meal amounts, and the total for three meals cannot be more than the full daily allowance.

10603.s: This order amends a prior order about certain military lands in Hawaii. It corrects the land description for Tract No. 1 and makes the order apply to a 0.16-acre piece of land that had been excluded before. The parts of the earlier order on possession, use, control, and transfer of title apply to that land in the same way as if it had not been excluded.

10602.s: This order names the Secretary of the Interior as the President’s representative to approve how the government of the Virgin Islands obligates and spends certain money. It affects the government of the Virgin Islands and the Secretary of the Interior.

10601.s: This order gives the Secretary of Agriculture the President’s functions under Title I of the Agricultural Act of 1954, except for the power to declare a national emergency. It also says disposal of commodities outside the United States must follow the Secretary of State’s foreign policy responsibilities. Strategic materials may be acquired only under programs certified by the Director of the Office of Defense Mobilization, and federal agencies must use existing coordination procedures when carrying out Title I.

10600.s: This order amends the rules for awarding the Legion of Merit. It says the decoration may be given to members of the armed forces of the United States and friendly foreign nations who have distinguished themselves by exceptionally meritorious conduct in outstanding services. It also sets out who may recommend the awards and who may approve them for foreign members.

10599.s: This order designates the Honorable A. Cecil Snyder, Chief Justice of the Supreme Court of the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico, to act as judge of the United States District Court for the District of Puerto Rico during 1955 if there is a vacancy or if the judge is dead, absent, ill, or otherwise legally disabled. He may perform the duties of that office and sign needed papers and records. He would do this without extra compensation.

10597.s: This order restores two parcels of land at Kaakaukukui, Oahu, to the possession and use of the Territory of Hawaii and transfers title to the Territory. The transfer is subject to the Territory fully complying with an August 3, 1950 agreement with the General Services Administration. It takes effect only after the work in that agreement is certified as satisfactorily completed.

10598.s: This order amends an earlier executive order about the Operations Coordinating Board. It changes who serves on the Board, including the Under Secretary of State, the Deputy Secretary of Defense, and several other agency directors, and it says one or more representatives of the President may also serve. It also allows alternate members for some agencies and says the Special Assistant to the President for National Security Affairs may attend Board meetings.

10596.s: This order revokes a previous order that required a specific reservation of source materials in disposals, leases, permits, and other uses of certain lands owned by the United States. It applies the policies of the Atomic Energy Act of 1954 to all lands of the United States. It also says the revocation does not change the earlier revocation of Executive Order No. 9701 as provided in the earlier order.

10595.s: This order amends the rules for the Panama Canal and the Canal Zone. It designates the Secretary of the Army to supervise the Canal Zone Government and adds a Lieutenant Governor who is appointed by the Governor with the Secretary’s approval. It also changes rules for hiring and employment in the civil government and says the Secretary of the Army must consult with the Secretaries of the Navy and Air Force in certain cases about military and naval reservations and air-force bases.

10593.s: This order changes an earlier order so the Director of the Office of Defense Mobilization can perform certain presidential functions without further approval from the President. It covers designating periods and projects for insured mortgages, assistance for community facilities or services, and the start of temporary housing or community facilities by the United States. These functions relate to the Defense Housing and Community Facilities and Services Act of 1951 and Title IX of the National Housing Act.

10592.s: This order gives the Secretary of Health, Education, and Welfare the power to make certain findings about school-construction assistance without needing approval from the President. It affects the handling of school facility construction in areas affected by Federal activities.

10591.s: This order waives the Civil Service age requirements so Otto K. Olesen can take the competitive civil-service examination for postmaster in Los Angeles, California. It affects the age rules for entrance to that examination and applies to Otto K. Olesen.

10590.s: This order establishes the President's Committee on Government Employment Policy to advise the President and review federal civilian employment practices. It says federal departments and agencies must follow a non-discriminatory employment policy and must not discriminate because of race, color, religion, or national origin. It also requires each department and agency to name an Employment Policy Officer to handle complaints, review personnel matters, and help enforce the policy. The order replaces Executive Order 9980 and abolishes the Fair Employment Board in the Civil Service Commission.

10588.s: This order sets up the President's Commission on Veterans' Pensions. The commission is directed to study the laws on pensions, compensation, and other nonmedical benefits for veterans and their dependents, and to recommend future policies to the President. Federal departments and agencies must cooperate with the commission and provide information and assistance allowed by law.

10587.s: This order designates the Jewish Restitution Successor Organization as a successor in interest to deceased persons for purposes of section 32(h) of the Trading With the Enemy Act. It also gives the Attorney General the President’s functions under that section, and allows the Attorney General to delegate those functions to officers and agencies of the Department of Justice.

10586.s: This order sets who will act as Secretary of the Treasury if the Secretary and Under Secretary die, resign, are absent, or are sick. It names the Under Secretary for Monetary Affairs first, then Assistant Secretaries in the order set by the Secretary, and then the General Counsel. It also revokes a 1941 order on the same subject.

10585.s: This order designates January 31, 1955, as the date when combatant activities in the stated zone end. It applies to the area described in Executive Order No. 10195 in Korea and the waters adjacent to it.

10584.s: This order sets rules for carrying out the Watershed Protection and Flood Prevention Act. It covers planning, building, running, and maintaining watershed works of improvement, and it applies to related programs in the Agriculture, Interior, and Army departments when they are affected by those projects. It gives the Secretary of Agriculture duties for approving planning help, setting standards, reviewing plans, and holding public hearings, and it requires the other departments to share notices and information about surveys and field investigations.

10582.s: This executive order sets uniform rules for how executive agencies make Buy-American Act decisions when buying materials for public use in the United States. It says when materials count as foreign origin and when domestic materials may be treated as too expensive or against the public interest. It also preserves agency authority to reject bids for national interest reasons, small business needs, areas of substantial unemployment, or essential national-security interests.

10581.s: This order approves a corporate seal for the Saint Lawrence Seaway Development Corporation. It applies to the corporation and describes the seal as part of the order.

10580.s: This order closes certain federal offices in the metropolitan area of the District of Columbia all day on December 24, 1954, and for one-half day on December 31, 1954. It excuses federal employees in that area and in the field service from duty on those times, except for those excluded for special public reasons or whose absence would conflict with existing law. Those times are treated as holidays for compensation and leave rules.

10583.s: This order changes an earlier order about duties involving the Department of the Treasury. It lets the President’s authority to issue orders about registration and a special tax on certain people in the Canal Zone who handle narcotic drugs be carried out under the listed tax code sections. It also lets the Postmaster General approve certain Treasury regulations about printing or importing postage stamps for philatelic purposes, and approve changes or repeals of those regulations, without further presidential action.

10579.s: This order sets rules for creating and running interagency motor-vehicle pools and systems to move government personnel and property more efficiently or economically. The Administrator of General Services is directed to study where these pools should be set up, decide how they should operate, and handle transfers of records, vehicles, personnel, and funds. Executive agencies must provide information and cooperation during studies, and they may appeal or ask for an exemption from a determination. Certain vehicles are exempt, including military, law enforcement, diplomatic, mail, and some specially used vehicles.

10578.s: This order creates a three-member board to investigate a dispute between certain carriers and some of their employees represented by a labor organization. The board must report its findings to the President within thirty days. From the date of the order and for thirty days after the report, the carriers and employees may not change the conditions involved in the dispute except by agreement.

10577.s: This order amends the Civil Service Rules for jobs in the competitive service and the excepted service. It sets rules for competitive examinations, career-conditional and career appointments, probation, and some noncompetitive status in limited cases. It also bars certain political activity and discrimination in executive branch hiring and gives the Civil Service Commission authority to make regulations, investigate, and enforce the rules.

10576.s: This order creates a three-member board to investigate a dispute between several airlines and certain employees represented by the International Association of Machinists. The board is to report its findings to the President within thirty days. During that time, and for thirty days after the board reports, the airlines and their employees may not change the conditions that gave rise to the dispute except by agreement.

10575.s: This order divides foreign-aid functions under the Mutual Security Act of 1954 among the Foreign Operations Administration, the Department of Defense, the Department of State, the Department of Commerce, and the United States Information Agency. It also assigns funds for carrying out the Act and reserves some functions to the President. In each country, the Chief of the United States Diplomatic Mission is the main channel for foreign policy and must coordinate United States agency activities and keep them consistent with United States policy.

10574.s: This order amends parts of Executive Order 10480 on the Defense Mobilization Program. It tells several federal departments and agencies to develop and promote measures to expand production capacity and the supply of materials and facilities needed for national defense in areas the Director of the Office of Defense Mobilization designates. It also says government officers and agencies with mobilization duties must follow programs certified by that Director and make recommendations for certain certificates or other actions under the Defense Production Act and the Internal Revenue Code of 1954. In addition, it says references to the Internal Revenue Code of 1939 in presidential regulations or other executive documents should be read as references to the matching parts of the Internal Revenue Code of 1954 when appropriate.

10573.s: This order amends a previous executive order to let the Housing and Home Finance Administrator exercise a presidential authority under Title II of the act of June 28, 1940. That authority is to determine that housing run or helped by the Public Housing Administration is no longer needed for people engaged in national-defense activities. Such a determination must have the concurrence of the Secretary of Defense.

10572.s: This order lets the Senate Committee on Labor and Public Welfare, or a subcommittee it authorizes, inspect certain tax returns for the years 1947 to 1953. The returns covered include income, excess-profits, declared-value excess-profits, capital stock, estate, and gift tax returns. The inspection is for the committee’s studies of welfare and pension funds and is subject to conditions in Treasury Decision 6064.

10571.s: This order adds certain lands in Graham County, North Carolina, to the Nantahala National Forest and reserves them as part of the forest. The lands are on the southwest shores of Fontana Lake and the south side of Cheoah Lake, and include an island in Fontana Lake. The order says the lands total about 928 acres and are covered by an agreement between the Tennessee Valley Authority and the Department of Agriculture.

10569.s: This order changes a prior order about Frederick C. Mayer, the organist and choirmaster at the United States Military Academy. It replaces his exemption from compulsory retirement for an indefinite time with an exemption until December 31, 1954.

10570.s: This order creates a board of three members to investigate a dispute between The Pullman Company and certain of its employees. The board must report its findings to the President within thirty days, and for that time and thirty days after the report, The Pullman Company and its employees may not change the conditions involved in the dispute except by agreement.

10568.s: This order suspends compliance with certain employment rules for the Canal Zone that were in two 1955 appropriation acts. It does not change the pay limits for people in skilled, technical, clerical, administrative, executive, or supervisory jobs in the Canal Zone who work for the United States Government or a government-owned company.

10567.s: This order designates the Federal Facilities Corporation as an agency included within the definition of “Department” for Title I of the Renegotiation Act of 1951. It makes Title I apply to contracts with the corporation and related subcontracts for amounts received or accrued on or after October 1, 1954. It does not affect any Government renegotiation rights for amounts received or accrued between July 1, 1954 and September 30, 1954.

10566.s: This order changes an earlier order about allowing the House Committee on Government Operations to inspect certain tax returns. It updates the year in that order from 1952 to 1953.

10565.s: This order changes the Manual for Courts-Martial for the military justice system. It adds rules that can allow a dishonorable discharge, forfeiture of pay and allowances, and sometimes confinement at hard labor if an accused has three or more previous convictions in the year before the offense. It also revises the listed offenses and punishments for violations of Articles 86 and 87 of the Uniform Code of Military Justice.

10564.s: This order lets a subcommittee of the House Committee on the Judiciary inspect certain income, excess-profits, declared value excess-profits, capital stock, estate, and gift tax returns for the years 1941 to 1953. The inspection is for studies and investigations within that committee's jurisdiction. The subcommittee must follow rules and regulations set by the Secretary of the Treasury.

10563.s: This order revokes Executive Order No. 10266, which had suspended certain provisions of the Officer Personnel Act of 1947, as amended. It affects the provisions of that law that relate to officers of the Navy and Marine Corps.

10561.s: Federal agencies must set up and keep a separate Official Personnel Folder for each employee covered by the Civil Service Rules and Regulations. These folders are part of the records of the United States Civil Service Commission and must include certain employment records, plus any others the Commission prescribes. Similar records for employees outside the competitive service must also be kept in Official Personnel Folders by executive branch departments and independent establishments. The Commission may issue rules for these folders, delegate some authority to agency heads, and one prior executive order is revoked.

10562.s: This order amends the Selective Service Regulations for some registrants in graduate and professional schools. It changes the school and test requirements that must be met for certain draft classifications. It affects men who have been accepted into graduate schools and into certain professional schools, including medicine, dentistry, veterinary medicine, osteopathy, optometry, pharmacy, chiropractic, and chiropody.

10560.s: This order delegates most of the President’s duties under the Agricultural Trade Development and Assistance Act of 1954 to the Secretary of Agriculture, the Director of the Foreign Operations Administration, the Secretary of State, and other agencies. It also gives the Secretary of the Treasury authority to set rules for foreign currencies received under the Act. Reports to Congress under section 108 stay with the President.

10559.s: This order lets the Director of the Bureau of the Budget use funds for management improvement and assign them to any executive branch agency or office, including the Bureau itself. It also requires the Director to report to the President on the activities funded this way and to direct and control those activities as appropriate under the law.

10558.s: This order changes a prior order about which Post Office Department officers can act as Postmaster General. It adds the Assistant Postmaster General in charge of the Bureau of Personnel to that list.

10556.s: This order authorizes the Civil Service Commission to issue rules for the permanency of promotions and reassignments for permanent employees in the competitive service. It also authorizes the heads of executive departments and agencies to issue rules for permanent employees in positions excepted from the competitive service. The rules must be consistent with law.

10555.s: This order approves an official seal for the President's Committee on Employment of the Physically Handicapped. It applies to that committee and sets the seal's design as the official one for it.

10554.s: This order gives the Secretary of Defense and the Secretary of the Treasury the President’s authority to set rules on when uniforms may be worn. It applies to people who have served honorably in the armed forces of the United States in time of war. It covers the Army, Navy, Air Force, Marine Corps, and Coast Guard uniforms.

10553.s: This order changes how functions under the Abaca Production Act of 1950 are carried out. Most of those functions are to be done through the General Services Administration. The parts about changing the acreage under cultivation to abaca are to be done through the Director of the Office of Defense Mobilization, and some other functions stay with the President.

10557.s: This order approves a new nondiscrimination clause for Government contracts. It says contractors may not discriminate against employees or job applicants because of race, religion, color, or national origin, and they must put the same clause in most subcontracts. Government agencies must add the clause to future contracts, with some exceptions for work outside the United States and for special requirements or emergencies.

10552.s: This order gives the United States Civil Service Commission the President’s authority to make regulations under which certain government employees may be prevented or relieved from working by administrative order. The Commission may do this without the President’s approval or other action.

10551.s: This order says certain income, excess-profits, declared value excess-profits, capital stock, estate, and gift tax returns for 1947 to 1953 may be inspected by the House Committee on Education and Labor, or a subcommittee it authorizes. The inspection is for the committee’s studies of welfare and pension funds and possible legislation to protect and conserve those funds for beneficiaries. The access is subject to the conditions in Treasury Decision 6064.

10549.s: This order delegates to the Secretary of Defense the power to place certain Department of Defense positions temporarily in grades 16, 17, and 18 of the General Schedule. Positions in grades 16 and 17 need prior approval from the Civil Service Commission. Positions in grade 18 need a prior recommendation from the Civil Service Commission and approval from its Chairman.

10550.s: This order amends a prior order on security requirements for Government employment. It requires the Civil Service Commission to report to the National Security Council at least twice a year and to report major deficiencies right away. It also requires department and agency heads to tell the Commission what action they took on certain civilian officers or employees as soon as possible, and no later than ninety days after the final investigative report.

10548.s: This order changes the security rules for government employment. It adds illness, including any mental condition, as a possible reason for concern if competent medical authority thinks it may seriously affect an employee’s judgment or reliability. The change applies to government employees under the security requirements for federal employment.

10547.s: This order makes certain statistical transcript cards from corporation income tax returns open to inspection by the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System. The cards covered are those submitted with, or prepared by, the Internal Revenue Service for tax years ending after June 30, 1951, and before July 1, 1952. The inspection must follow rules set by the Secretary of the Treasury.

10545.s: This order changes the Army ration rules by adding a new section. It lets the Secretary of the Army authorize experimental ration plans and tests under terms and conditions he sets.

10546.s: This order suspends certain service-in-grade requirements for Marine Corps officers who are first lieutenants or captains when they are considered for temporary promotion to the next higher grade. The suspension lasts until June 30, 1957. It also replaces Executive Order 10465.

10544.s: This order lets the Federal Trade Commission inspect corporation income tax returns for 1953 and later years. The inspection must follow rules set by the Secretary of the Treasury. It affects corporations that file these returns and the Federal Trade Commission.

10543.s: This order creates a Board of Inquiry to look into a labor dispute between Union Carbide and Carbon Corporation and some of its employees represented by the Atomic Trades and Labor Council, AFL, and local unions linked to that council. The dispute involves the Oak Ridge National Laboratory and facilities in the Y-12 area in Oak Ridge, Tennessee. The Board must report to the President and then continue to carry out other duties under the Labor-Management Relations Act until the President ends it.

10542.s: The order creates a Board of Inquiry to look into a labor dispute between Union Carbide and Carbon Corporation and some of its employees at Atomic Energy Commission facilities in Oak Ridge, Tennessee, and Paducah, Kentucky. The Board is told to report to the President on the issues in the dispute. It also says the Board will keep working as needed under the Labor-Management Relations Act until the President ends it.

10541.s: This order extends the existence of the Quetico-Superior Committee for four more years, from June 30, 1954, to June 30, 1958. It affects the committee created in 1934 and keeps it in place during that time.

10540.s: This order says the Annual and Sick Leave Act of 1951 does not apply to certain listed officers in the executive branch, the District of Columbia government, and corporations owned or controlled by the United States. It also gives the Chairman of the United States Civil Service Commission the power to make these designations and to add or remove positions from the schedule. The order takes effect at once, with one part starting on the first day of the first pay period for the officers covered.

10539.s:
This order sets up the Federal Facilities Corporation to carry out certain functions that had been handled by the Reconstruction Finance Corporation under the Rubber Act and a 1947 joint resolution. It also changes one earlier executive order to replace references to the Reconstruction Finance Corporation with the Federal Facilities Corporation.

The order says functions under the Abaca Production Act of 1950 will be carried out through the General Services Administration, except for certain powers over acreage changes and other listed sections. It also gives the Director of the Bureau of the Budget duties tied to these changes.

10538.s: This order approves a seal as the official seal of the United States Marine Corps. The seal includes an eagle, a globe, an anchor, and the words "Department of the Navy - United States Marine Corps." It applies to the United States Marine Corps.

10537.s: This order amends two earlier executive orders about a commissioner of the Interstate Commerce Commission. It replaces the words "Bureau of Service of the Commission" with a longer phrase naming the bureau that administers the Commission's car-service functions under the Interstate Commerce Act. The change took effect on June 1, 1954.

10536.s: This order lets heads of departments and agencies carry out certain acts and sign needed papers under section 16 of the Federal Airport Act without getting the President’s approval first. It affects those department and agency heads when they are making conveyances requested by the Administrator of Civil Aeronautics.

10535.s: This order lets the Civil Service Commission give a competitive status to certain government employees or former employees who met the requirements under earlier executive orders but were not recommended because of administrative error. The person must be recommended by the agency where they work, or by an agency seeking to reemploy them or that could have recommended them before. It also says this status does not give a person the right to appeal a reduction in force or other personnel action that happened before the agency is notified.

10534.s: This order puts the Saint Lawrence Seaway Development Corporation under the direction and supervision of the Secretary of Defense. It affects the corporation and the Secretary of Defense.

10533.s: This order designates the Organization of American States as a public international organization under the International Organizations Immunities Act. That gives the organization the privileges, exemptions, and immunities allowed by that law. It also includes the Pan American Union in that designation and replaces the earlier designation of the Pan American Union.

10532.s: This order adds Relapsing Fever (louse-borne) to the list of communicable diseases in Executive Order 9708. That list is used for regulations that allow the apprehension, detention, or conditional release of individuals to help prevent the introduction, transmission, or spread of communicable diseases. It affects people covered by those regulations for listed diseases.

10530.s: This order gives several federal officials and agencies authority to carry out specific presidential functions without further approval from the President. It covers matters like travel and relocation rules for federal employees, civil service regulations, housing and land transfers, submarine cable licenses, and Federal Register duties. It also revokes a prior executive order on submarine cable licenses and keeps earlier actions in place unless they conflict with this order.

10531.s: This order changes a section of an earlier executive order on security requirements for government employment. It expands the listed matters covered in that section from subdivisions (2) through (7) to subdivisions (2) through (8). It affects government employment security reviews and the information covered by that section.

10528.s: This order adds the Marginal Wharf Area at Sand Island, Oahu, to the Sand Island Military Reservation. It places the land under the control of the Department of the Army for military purposes. The land is still subject to possible future use for Reserved Channel purposes.

10529.s: This order lets certain Federal employees volunteer for civil defense training programs and test exercises with States or local governments before an emergency. The Federal department or agency can authorize the participation after considering a recommendation from the Federal Civil Defense Administrator. Employees stay under Federal control, keep their Federal pay and status, and may receive travel allowances and expenses when travel is involved.

10526.s: This order transfers certain lands in Yalobusha County, Mississippi, from the Department of Agriculture to the Department of the Army. The lands are to be used, administered, and disposed of in connection with the Grenada Dam and Reservoir Project, Mississippi. The order covers about 118.44 acres, subject to valid existing rights.

10525.s: This order transfers the Secretary of the Navy’s interest in and control over certain money in a Treasury suspense account to the Secretary of the Interior. The money is to be spent or deposited as provided by the Submerged Lands Act and the Outer Continental Shelf Lands Act.

10524.s: This order lets the Secretary of Health, Education, and Welfare make certain findings the President could make under a school-construction aid law, without the President's approval. For one part, the Secretary must follow the recommendations of the Director of the Office of Defense Mobilization, and for another part, the Secretary must follow the recommendations of the Secretary of Labor. It also says the Secretary of Defense shall give the Secretary of Labor information about the immigration of military personnel, unless doing so would conflict with national security.

10527.s: This order allows the Senate Banking and Currency Committee, or a subcommittee it authorizes, to inspect certain federal tax returns for the years 1942 to 1953. The returns covered include income, excess-profits, declared value excess-profits, capital stock, estate, and gift tax returns. The inspection is for the committee’s investigation of loan projects and related mortgage, construction, and land costs, and it must follow Treasury rules.

10522.s: This order lets the Director of the United States Information Agency carry out certain functions of the Board of the Foreign Service for personnel appointed or assigned to that agency. It does not transfer any Board function that relates to a Foreign Service Officer. It also lets the Director issue regulations, orders, and instructions needed to carry out those functions.

10523.s: This order sets March 31, 1954, as the day to dedicate a memorial to Major General George W. Goethals in the Canal Zone. It allows the Governor of the Canal Zone to arrange suitable ceremonies. It also excuses federal officers and employees on the Isthmus of Panama from duty that day, with some exceptions, and treats the day as a holiday there for pay and leave rules.

10520.s: This order transfers jurisdiction over certain lands in North Dakota from the Department of Agriculture to the Department of the Army. The lands, along with related waters, water rights, improvements, and structures, are to be used for the construction, operation, and maintenance of the Garrison Dam and Reservoir Project. The order says the lands total about 2,863.82 acres.

10521.s: This order directs the National Science Foundation to advise the President on federal science policy and to study the nation’s research needs, resources, and basic research support. It tells federal agencies that do scientific research to review their programs, consult with the Foundation on basic research, share information where allowed, and use equipment and facilities efficiently. It also says the Foundation should study how federal research contracts and grants affect educational institutions and recommend policies that protect the strength and independence of those institutions.

10519.s: This order exempts certain functions under the Mutual Security Act of 1951, as amended, from following several listed laws. It also exempts purchases made outside the continental United States under that act from several other listed laws. The order replaces two earlier executive orders on the same subject.

10518.s: This order makes certain Form 990-A tax returns from tax-exempt organizations open to inspection by a special House committee. The committee may review returns for the years 1950 to 1953 to carry out its investigation of tax-exempt foundations, subject to stated Treasury conditions.

10517.s: This order designates A. Cecil Snyder, the Chief Justice of the Supreme Court of the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico, to act as judge of the United States District Court for the District of Puerto Rico in certain cases during 1954. He may do so if the judge’s office is vacant or if the judge dies, is absent, is ill, or has another legal disability. He may sign necessary papers and records as acting judge, and he would receive no extra compensation.

10516.s: This order transfers certain United States lands to the Secretary of Agriculture. The lands are to be used, managed, and disposed of under Title III of the Bankhead-Jones Farm Tenant Act and related Title IV provisions.

10514.s: This order revokes Executive Order No. 2414 of June 30, 1916. That earlier order had set rules for hospital service connected to the Government railway in Alaska, now the Alaska Railroad.

10515.s: This order amends an earlier executive order about the retirement of colonels in the Regular Army and Regular Air Force. It changes the suspension period to September 30, 1954, or earlier if that comes first. The Secretary of the Army may keep not more than twenty of the officers selected for retention until June 30, 1957, or earlier dates he chooses.

10513.s: This order lets the Assistant Secretaries of Labor and the Solicitor of Labor act as Secretary of Labor if both the Secretary of Labor and the Under Secretary are absent, sick, resign, or die. It sets the order they would serve in, based on a later designation order or, if there is none, their commission dates or oath dates. It also replaces a 1948 order on the same subject.

10512.s: This order revokes a previous order that had exempted certain officers and employees in the executive branch from automatic separation under the Civil Service Retirement Act. It means those officers and employees will no longer have that exemption. The order takes effect at the close of business on March 31, 1954.

10510.s: This order approves a seal as the official seal of the Department of Health, Education, and Welfare. The seal includes an open book, a staff of Aesculapius, an American bald eagle, and the motto "SPES ANCHORA VITTAE." It applies to the Department of Health, Education, and Welfare.

10511.s: This order creates a board of three members to investigate disputes between the Akron, Canton and Youngstown Railroad Company, other listed carriers, and certain of their employees. The board must report its findings to the President within thirty days. From the date of the order and for thirty days after the report is made, no changes can be made in the conditions behind the disputes except by agreement.

10508.s: This order closes certain federal offices in the metropolitan area of the District of Columbia for one-half day on December 24, 1953, and one-half day on December 31, 1953. It excuses federal employees in that area and in the field service from duty on those half days, except for workers excluded for special public reasons or when their absence would go against existing law. The half days are treated as holidays for rules about employee pay and leave.

10509.s: This order creates a board of three members to investigate a dispute between the Railway Express Agency, Inc. and certain of its employees represented by a labor organization. The board must report its findings to the President within thirty days. During that time, and for thirty days after the report, no change in the conditions behind the dispute may be made by the company or its employees except by agreement.
