10507.s: This order changes the rules for reimbursing civilian federal employees who move for permanent duty between places in the continental United States. It sets commuted rates for transporting household goods and personal effects, and it limits reimbursement for temporary storage to the amount actually paid. It also adds special allowances for shipments to or from certain islands and metropolitan areas, and it applies to transportation authorized and started on or after May 8, 1953.

10506.s: This order gives the Secretary of Health, Education, and Welfare the President’s authority to handle several functions under the Public Health Service Act. Those functions include appointing and promoting commissioned officers, setting titles and regulations, approving the voluntary retirement of the Surgeon General, and approving certain sites for institutions and hospitals. It also lets the Surgeon General accept voluntary resignations of commissioned officers of the Regular Corps or Reserve Corps.

10504.s: This order transfers the remaining functions, powers, and duties of the Small Defense Plants Administration to the Small Business Administrator. It covers liquidation work, certain defense production contracts, certificates of competency, and payment of obligations. It also moves related records, property, and unused funds to the Small Business Administration.

10503.s: This order changes a prior order so the Secretary of State can exercise certain presidential powers about allowances and allotments for Government personnel on foreign duty. It covers rules for civilian officers and employees on living-quarters allowances, cost-of-living allowances, and representation allowances. The order is effective as of July 1, 1953.

10505.s: This order amends Selective Service regulations for registrants in medical, dental, and allied specialist categories. It changes how some special registrants are classified, how their records are kept, and how they receive forms and are ordered for induction. It also sets rules for some registrants with prior military service, including when they are placed in Class I-C, Class IV-A, or reclassified in Class V-A.

10502.s: This order suspends compliance with certain statutory provisions about employment in the Canal Zone. It does not change the provisions on how much compensation may be received by people in skilled, technical, clerical, administrative, executive, or supervisory jobs there, including jobs with the United States Government or with companies partly or wholly owned by it.

10501.s: This order sets rules for protecting official information tied to national defense. It limits defense classifications to Top Secret, Secret, and Confidential, and says only certain executive branch officials may classify material. It also requires classified material to be marked, stored securely, and reviewed for possible downgrading or declassification when national defense no longer requires protection.

10499.s: This order lets the Secretary of Defense carry out the President’s duties under section 8 of the Uniformed Services Contingency Option Act of 1953, except where the order says otherwise. It also lets the Secretaries of the Army, Navy, Air Force, Treasury, Commerce, and Health, Education, and Welfare make rules for their own departments, subject to approval by the Secretary of Defense. The Secretary of Defense must prepare a yearly report on operations and financing and send it to the President for Congress. The President keeps the power to choose a member of the Board of Actuaries and set that person’s pay.

10498.s: This order gives the Secretaries of the Army, Navy, and Air Force, and in some cases the Secretary of the Treasury, the President’s authority to remit or suspend part of certain military sentences. It applies to people convicted by military tribunals under their jurisdiction when a death sentence has been commuted to a lesser punishment.

10497.s: This order amends the regulations for commissioned officers and employees of the Public Health Service. It updates several definitions in those rules and applies security requirements to commissioned officers and candidates for commission. It also allows investigations into their appointments and retention, and lets the Secretary suspend or separate officers when needed for national security. One section about transmitting information to certain agencies is revoked.

10496.s: This order restores certain lands on the Island of Oahu from military use to the possession, use, and control of the Territory of Hawaii. The lands include parts of the Pupukea, Kaaawa, Port Ruger, and Fort Ruger Military Reservations.

10495.s: This order sets who will act as Secretary of Defense, Secretary of the Army, Secretary of the Navy, and Secretary of the Air Force if those offices are vacant because of death, disability, or absence. It lists the officers who would take over each job in a set order. The order says these acting roles are temporary and do not remove the person from their current office. It also revokes Executive Order 10332.

10494.s: This order moves remaining functions under Title IV of the Defense Production Act to other officials. Fiscal liquidation of the Economic Stabilization Agency goes to the Secretary of the Treasury, and administrative proceedings go to the Director of the Office of Defense Mobilization. It also gives the Attorney General certain enforcement and investigation functions, including processing enforcement files, concluding some investigations, and certifying disallowances.

10492.s: This executive order approves an official seal for the National Advisory Committee for Aeronautics. The seal shows the Wright brothers' first airplane taking off at Kitty Hawk, with a man running beside it, and it includes the committee's name and "U. S. A."

10493.s: This order gives the Administrator of the Small Business Administration the President’s functions under section 217 of the Small Business Act of 1953. It also gives the Administrator certain functions under section 708 of the Defense Production Act of 1950 for changes to, or other action about, voluntary agreements and programs tied to small-business production pools approved before July 31, 1953. It revokes Executive Order 10370.

10490.s: This order creates a Board of Inquiry to look into certain labor disputes in the maritime industry. The disputes involve steamship companies, contracting stevedores, contracting marine carpenters, and other related pier employers, along with employees represented by the International Longshoremen's Association. The Board must report to the President and may continue to perform other duties under the law until the President ends it.

10491.s: This order changes a prior security rule for government jobs. It adds refusal to testify before a congressional committee, when a person claims the constitutional privilege against self-incrimination, about charges of alleged disloyalty or other misconduct. It affects people seeking or holding government employment under the security rules.

10488.s: This order says that executive departments and agencies of the United States must follow Treasury regulations when they buy, hold, transfer, or sell foreign exchange, including credits and currencies. It gives the Secretary of the Treasury authority to issue those regulations, as long as they do not conflict with certain laws.

10489.s: The order gives the Secretary of the Treasury authority to make and service loans, loan participations, and loan guarantees for private business enterprises, including nonprofit research corporations. These loans may be used for expanding capacity, developing technological processes, and producing essential materials, including strategic and critical metals and minerals, but not for work in foreign countries. The loans must meet conditions set by the Secretary, and each loan must be certified as essential by the Director of the Office of Defense Mobilization.

10486.s: This order creates the Advisory Committee on Government Housing Policies and Programs. The committee will study government housing policies and programs and the Executive Branch organization that carries them out, and will advise the Housing and Home Finance Administrator and the President. The Housing and Home Finance Administrator will serve as chairman, and an executive committee will work on specific studies and recommendations.

10485.s: This order gives the Federal Power Commission the job of handling permit applications for electric energy and natural gas facilities at the borders of the United States. It says the Commission may issue permits only if it finds them consistent with the public interest and gets favorable recommendations from the Secretary of State and the Secretary of Defense. If they cannot agree, the application goes to the President for approval or disapproval. Existing permits stay in effect unless changed or revoked, and Executive Order 8202 is revoked.

10487.s: This order assigns the Department of State to make the investigations and written reports needed for people seeking admission into the United States under the Refugee Relief Act of 1953. It says the Department of the Army and other agencies may help State do this work. It also transfers certain emergency migration funds to the Department of State, lets the Secretary of State allocate some of those funds to other agencies, and directs the Secretary of State and the Secretary of the Treasury to issue regulations under the act.

10484.s: This order lets the Director of the Bureau of the Budget allocate certain funds to any agency or office in the executive branch, including the Bureau of the Budget itself. The Director must report to the President from time to time about the activities carried out with those funds. The Director is also told to direct and control those activities as allowed by law.

10483.s: This order creates an Operations Coordinating Board to help carry out national security policies across government agencies. The board reports to the National Security Council and includes officials from the State Department, Defense Department, Foreign Operations Administration, Central Intelligence, and a presidential representative. It may advise agencies on planning and coordination, make new proposals within national security policies, and report on carrying out the order. The order also abolishes the Psychological Strategy Board and says this new board does not get any function over internal security or take away powers already given by law to other agencies.

10481.s: This order says that if both the Secretary of Agriculture and the Under Secretary of Agriculture are absent, sick, resign, or die, the Assistant Secretaries of Agriculture will perform the duties of Secretary of Agriculture. It applies to the Department of Agriculture and replaces a previous executive order on the same subject.

10480.s: This order gives the Director of the Office of Defense Mobilization broad control over defense mobilization activities in the executive branch, including production, procurement, manpower, stabilization, and transport. It also creates an advisory Defense Mobilization Board and gives the Director authority over priorities, allocations, and programs for defense production. The order authorizes agencies to support expansion of production and supply, loan and guarantee programs, stockpile transfers, and labor planning for defense industry and essential civilian jobs.

10479.s: This order creates the Government Contract Committee to help make sure government contractors and subcontractors follow nondiscrimination rules in their contracts. It makes contracting agencies responsible for getting compliance, sets up complaint handling and reporting, and lets the committee make recommendations and work with government and non-government groups. It also revokes a previous executive order and transfers the old committee’s records and property to the new one.

10478.s: This order gives the Secretary of Defense the President’s authority to make rules for appointing, reappointing, and promoting certain people in the armed forces, including some reserve members and people liable for induction. It also lets the Secretary order certain reserve component members into active federal service, with or without their consent. For Coast Guard Reserve members, the Secretary of the Treasury may use that authority when the Coast Guard is in the Treasury Department.

10477.s: This order lets the Director of the United States Information Agency use certain legal powers that were available to the Secretary of State and the Director of the Foreign Operations Administration for the functions transferred to that agency. It covers personnel rules, foreign service authority, buildings and broadcasting facilities abroad, importation of sound recordings, and other support services for international information work. It also keeps some powers with the Secretary of State, including certain commissioning and compensation authorities.

10475.s: This order changes how powers under the Housing and Rent Act of 1947 are handled. Most of those powers are put under the Director of the Office of Defense Mobilization, and some exceptions for national-defense activities must be handled in consultation with the Housing and Home Finance Administrator. It also abolishes the Office of Rent Stabilization and revokes a prior executive order.

10476.s: This order delegates many foreign aid functions to the Director of the Foreign Operations Administration and makes that office the successor to the Mutual Security Agency. It also gives the United States Information Agency authority over informational media guaranties and requires it to publicize abroad the activities carried on under the Act for International Development. The Chief of the United States Diplomatic Mission in each country is made the channel for foreign policy direction and must coordinate U.S. agency representatives there.

10474.s: This order directs flags on the White House and Federal Government buildings in the District of Columbia and Ohio to be placed at half-staff until interment. It does this as a mark of respect for the Honorable Robert A. Taft, a late Member of the Senate and Majority Leader.

10473.s: This order changes the Foreign Service fee rules and revokes one section of the earlier regulations. It sets or changes fees for some foreign service documents and services, including visa services for aliens, border identification cards, and certified copies for repatriation forms. It also says no fee is charged for some services, including certain certificates, services for American vessels and seamen, and some oath of allegiance actions for native-born American women who lost citizenship by marriage to an alien.

10471.s: This order lets the heads of federal departments and agencies approve leaves of absence for certain people who receive compensation under section 411 of the Foreign Service Act of 1946. They may do this without getting the President’s approval or other action. The order is effective as of July 5, 1953.

10472.s: This order creates the National Agricultural Advisory Commission to advise the Secretary of Agriculture. The commission is made up of farmers and others closely connected with agriculture, and the members are appointed by the President with attention to party balance and geographic representation. It reviews farm policies and the administration of farm programs when the Secretary asks, and the Secretary must arrange at least one meeting each quarter. No Federal funds may be used for the commission until a specific appropriation is available.

10470.s: This order expands the area whose administration is transferred from the Secretary of the Interior to the Secretary of the Navy. It covers all of the Northern Mariana Islands in the Trust Territory of the Pacific Islands except the Island of Rota. It also says the change does not alter the United States' rights or obligations under the Trusteeship Agreement, or the Secretary of State's role in interpreting those rights and obligations.

10469.s: This order amends the Selective Service regulations on Class III-A classification. It allows a registrant to be placed in that class if he has child or children and keeps a bona fide family relationship with them in their home. It also says an unborn child can count only if a licensed physician’s certificate is filed with the local board before the stated deadline and before an induction order is mailed.

10468.s: This order appoints William C. Strand, Director of the Office of Territories in the Department of the Interior, as Administrator of the Puerto Rico Reconstruction Administration. He is to serve without additional compensation, and the earlier executive orders on that office are amended accordingly.

10467.s: This order keeps existing executive orders in place for Defense Production Act functions that are still continued by the 1953 amendments. It also says the Director of the Office of Defense Mobilization has the authority to make certain findings required under section 101(b) of the Act. It affects federal officials carrying out functions under the Defense Production Act.

10466.s: This order keeps certain Army and Air Force appointments in effect for people on active duty on July 1, 1953, if they were found to have been missing, missing in action, interned, captured, beleaguered, or besieged after June 25, 1950, and before the end of the national emergency proclaimed on December 16, 1950. It applies to commissioned officers and warrant officers whose appointments would otherwise end after June 30, 1953. These appointments stay in effect until the person is released from active duty.

10465.s: This order suspends certain parts of the Officer Personnel Act of 1947 that relate to Marine Corps officers who are majors, captains, first lieutenants, and second lieutenants. The suspended parts cover distribution in grades, promotion by selection, temporary promotion, and discharge after a second failure of selection for promotion. It also supersedes a previous executive order.

10464.s: This order delegates to the Director for Mutual Security the President’s functions under the 1953 act on transferring price-support wheat to Pakistan. It also lets the Secretary of State negotiate and make an agreement with Pakistan under that act. The order does not delegate the President’s functions about ending assistance.

10463.s: This order changes the civil service rule on removing people from certain excepted positions. It says the Civil Service Rules and Regulations do not apply to removals from positions in Schedules A and C, or from positions excepted from the competitive service by statute, except where the Veterans' Preference Act requires otherwise. It also says those rules do apply to removals from Schedule B positions held by people with competitive status.

10461.s: This order transfers the functions of the old Office of Defense Mobilization and its director to the Office of Defense Mobilization created by Reorganization Plan No. 3 of 1953. It also changes prior executive order references to fit the new office and director. Records, property, personnel, and funds are moved to the new office, and the old office and director are abolished.

10462.s: This order lets the Housing and Home Finance Administrator carry out certain presidential duties under a 1940 housing law without needing the President’s approval first. It applies to the functions given to the President by that law.

10460.s: This order gives the Director of Defense Mobilization a role in advising the President on telecommunications policy, standards, management, and plans for national emergency security. It also covers assigning radio frequencies to government agencies and developing United States Government frequency requirements. The Director is told to work with other government departments and the Federal Communications Commission, and the order transfers records, property, personnel, and funds from the Telecommunications Advisor to the President to the Office of Defense Mobilization.

10458.s: This order moves certain international development functions from the Secretary of State to the Director for Mutual Security. It also transfers the Technical Cooperation Administration to that director’s control and gives the Mutual Security Agency authority to pay ocean freight charges on shipments of relief supplies and packages. The Secretary of State keeps responsibility for negotiating with other governments, making certain U.S. contributions, and representing the United States in the listed international organizations.

10459.s: This order changes the rules for background checks and loyalty reviews for United States citizens employed by, or being considered for employment by, the United Nations and other international organizations. It requires a full background investigation in many cases, and for some cases involving United Nations staff members employed for more than 90 days, the Federal Bureau of Investigation must do a full field investigation. It also creates an International Organizations Employees Loyalty Board in the Civil Service Commission to review cases, give people notice and a hearing, and send advisory determinations to the Secretary of State for transmission to the Secretary General of the United Nations.

10456.s: This order gives the Secretary of Defense and the Director of Defense Mobilization the President’s powers, duties, and functions under a housing law section about critical defense housing areas. They must act together when using those powers.

10457.s: This order designates the Department of Justice as a defense agency of the United States for the purposes of chapter 17 of title 35 of the United States Code. It applies to patent applications for inventions that might be harmful to national security if they were published or disclosed. In those cases, the chief officer of the Department of Justice may inspect the application.

10454.s: This order restores certain parcels of land from the Schofield Barracks Military Reservation on Oahu to the possession, use, and control of the Territory of Hawaii. The order says these lands were no longer needed for military purposes. It applies to the listed parcels of land in Waianae-Uka, Waianae, and Waikakalaua.

10455.s: This order makes certain tax returns for periods up to and including 1952 open to inspection by the Committee on Government Operations of the House of Representatives, or a duly authorized subcommittee. The returns covered include income, excess-profits, declared value excess-profits, capital stock, estate, and gift tax returns. The inspection is for the committee’s studies of government activities at all levels and is subject to conditions in the related Treasury decision.

10453.s: This order restores certain parcels of land from the Fort Ruger Military Reservation on Oahu to the possession, use, and control of the Territory of Hawaii. The land had been reserved for military purposes, but the order says these parcels are no longer needed for that use. One parcel is restored with a right-of-way for pipeline and roadway purposes.

10452.s: This order gives the Chairman of the United States Civil Service Commission added duties on federal civilian personnel management in the United States and abroad. The Chairman is to help the President with personnel management, policy and standards, and efforts to improve and coordinate personnel management across executive departments and agencies. It also revokes parts of a prior order and abolishes the Liaison Office for Personnel Management, with the White House Office to wind up its affairs.

10450.s: This order sets security requirements for people who work for the federal government. It says federal jobs and retention in jobs must be subject to investigation, and some positions are marked as sensitive and require a full field investigation. It also allows suspension or termination if employment is not clearly consistent with the interests of national security, and it creates a security-investigations index in the Civil Service Commission.

10451.s: This order allows the House Committee on the Judiciary, or a subcommittee it authorizes, to inspect certain tax returns through June 30, 1953. The returns include income, excess-profits, declared value excess-profits, capital stock, estate, and gift tax returns for periods through 1952. The inspection is tied to the committee’s inquiry into the administration of the Department of Justice and the Office of the Attorney General, and it must follow stated Treasury conditions.

10448.s: This order creates the National Defense Service Medal for members of the armed forces who served during a period starting June 27, 1950, and ending on a date set by the Secretary of Defense. It says the medal is to be awarded under rules set by the military secretaries and approved by the Secretary of Defense. No person can get more than one of these medals, and it may be awarded after death.

10449.s: This order creates a three-member board to investigate a dispute between the New York, Chicago & St. Louis Railroad Company and certain of its employees represented by the Brotherhood of Railroad Trainmen. The board must report its findings to the President within thirty days. During that time, and for thirty days after the report, the company and its employees may not change the conditions that led to the dispute except by agreement.

10446.s: This order says the State Department’s escapee program may operate without following three listed laws. It applies to the functions of that program under the Mutual Security Act of 1951, as amended. It also replaces a previous executive order on the same subject.

10447.s: This order lets the Senate Committee on the Judiciary, or a subcommittee it authorizes, inspect certain income and other tax returns for the years 1941 to 1952. It is for reviewing the administration of the Trading with the Enemy Act and must follow the stated Treasury conditions.

10445.s: This order reserves certain lands inside national forest boundaries as parts of the national forests where they are located. It applies to lands the United States acquired by exchange under Title III of the Bankhead-Jones Farm Tenant Act, except in Arizona, California, Colorado, Idaho, Montana, New Mexico, Oregon, Washington, and Wyoming. Future lands acquired the same way will also be added if the Department of Agriculture finds them suitable for national-forest purposes and the United States gets title to them.

10444.s: This order changes the rules for the Good Conduct Medal. It says the medal may be awarded for exemplary behavior, efficiency, and fidelity to enlisted men in the Army and the Air Force who meet the listed active Federal military service requirements. It also says no one may get the medal for less than one year of service, except for people separated because of physical disability incurred in the line of duty.

10443.s: This order suspends the eight-hour limit for laborers and mechanics working for the Atomic Energy Commission on public work essential to the national defense. It applies during the national emergency and allows more than eight hours in a day. Their pay must still be based on an eight-hour day, with overtime paid at least time and one-half for hours over eight.

10441.s: This order keeps certain Army and Air Force officer and warrant officer appointments in effect through July 1, 1953. It applies to people on active duty on March 31, 1953 who are found under the Missing Persons Act to have been missing, missing in action, interned, captured, beleaguered, or besieged during the stated period. It affects appointments that would otherwise end under the listed laws.

10440.s: This order changes Civil Service Rule VI on positions that can be kept out of the competitive civil service. It lets the Civil Service Commission place certain positions in Schedules A, B, or C, including positions where a competitive exam is not practical or that are confidential or policy-determining. It also says people in these excepted positions do not gain competitive status just because of the appointment, and it sets rules for removals, assignments, and revoking exceptions.

10442.s: This order makes certain income, excess-profits, declared value excess-profits, capital stock, estate, and gift tax returns open to inspection by the Senate Committee on Interstate and Foreign Commerce or its authorized subcommittee. It applies to returns for any period up to and including 1952, during the Eighty-third Congress. The inspection is for carrying out Senate Resolution 41 and is subject to the conditions in the related Treasury decision.

10439.s: This order changes the rules for awarding the Armed Forces Reserve Medal. It says the medal may be given to members or former members of the reserve components of the armed forces, including the Coast Guard Reserve and the Marine Corps Reserve, who complete ten years of honorable reserve service within twelve consecutive years. The service cannot include regular component service, and it cannot be service already used for the Naval Reserve Medal or the Marine Corps Reserve Medal.

10438.s: This order transfers the functions of the National Security Resources Board and its chairman, under several earlier executive orders, to the Director of Defense Mobilization. It also moves records and personnel that the chairman and the director jointly determine are mainly tied to those transferred functions to the Office of Defense Mobilization.

10437.s: This order lets Benjamin Ortiz act as judge of the United States District Court for the District of Puerto Rico during 1953 if the judge’s office is vacant or if the judge dies, is absent, is ill, or has another legal disability. He may perform the duties of that office and sign necessary papers and records as acting judge. He is to do this without extra compensation.

10435.s: This order allows the Senate Committee on Government Operations, or a subcommittee, to inspect certain federal tax returns for the years 1945 to 1952 during the Eighty-third Congress. It applies to income, excess-profits, declared value excess-profits, capital stock, estate, and gift tax returns. The inspection is limited to the conditions set in the related Treasury decision.

10436.s: This order takes Kahoolawe Island, except the area already taken for lighthouse purposes, and reserves it for the use of the United States for naval purposes. It places the island under the jurisdiction of the Secretary of the Navy. It also requires soil conservation on the island and lets the Territory of Hawaii enter and inspect it at reasonable intervals, so long as that does not unreasonably interfere with Navy or Coast Guard activities.

10434.s: This order suspends wage, salary, and other compensation controls issued under the Defense Production Act of 1950. It lets pending pay adjustments go into effect without approval from wage and salary control agencies. It also says the order does not affect suits, prosecutions, or enforcement actions for rights, liabilities, or offenses that existed before the order date.

10433.s: This order changes older executive orders so that references to the Defense Production Administrator and the Defense Production Administration now refer to the Director of Defense Mobilization and the Office of Defense Mobilization. It transfers the records, property, personnel, and funds of the Defense Production Administration to the Office of Defense Mobilization. It also revises the Economic Stabilization Agency so the Director of Defense Mobilization serves as its Administrator, and it keeps other related orders and actions in effect unless they conflict with this order.

10431.s: This order creates the National Security Medal and sets out rules for how it is designed and awarded. It may be given to any person, including members of the armed forces, for distinguished achievement or outstanding contribution in intelligence related to national security. The President, or someone designated under approved rules, awards it, and it may also be awarded after death.

10432.s: The order creates the President's Advisory Committee on Government Organization. The committee is to advise the President, the Assistant to the President, and the Director of the Bureau of the Budget on changes to the executive branch that may improve economy and efficiency. Its members are appointed by the President and serve without pay.

10430.s: This order lets Mrs. Beth Campbell Short be appointed to a permanent competitive job in the classified civil service of the United States. It says this can be done without following the competitive rules and regulations that usually apply to civil service appointments.

10428.s: This order gives the Secretary of Defense the President’s authority to allow certain commanders of joint commands or joint task forces to convene general courts-martial. It applies to members of any of the armed forces and says those trials must follow the Uniform Code of Military Justice and the Manual for Courts Martial, United States, 1951.

10429.s: This order revises the rules for the Korean Service Medal. It says the medal is for members of the armed forces of the United States who served in the area of military operations in Korea during the stated period, under regulations set by the Secretaries of the Army, Navy, Air Force, and Treasury and approved by the Secretary of Defense.

10426.s: This order sets aside certain submerged lands of the United States and Alaska continental shelf as a naval petroleum reserve and places them under the Secretary of the Navy. The reservation is for oil and gas only, and it says other lawful uses of the area may continue if they do not conflict with the reservation. It also transfers some duties and payment rules from the Secretary of the Interior to the Secretary of the Navy and revokes an earlier executive order.

10425.s: This order extends certain deadlines for the disposition of housing under the 1940 housing act. It gives more time for requests to convey listed housing projects and for showing the need for low-rent housing. It applies to the governing bodies of municipalities or counties involved in those housing projects.

10427.s: This order puts the Federal Civil Defense Administrator in charge of several disaster-relief duties under the act, including coordinating federal agencies, helping prepare rules, and preparing reports for the President and Congress. It says federal agencies should plan ahead for major disasters, and it encourages state and local disaster plans and organizations. Federal disaster relief is meant to supplement, not replace, help from state, local, or private agencies, and federal aid is tied to reasonable state and local spending.

10424.s: This order gives Norman E. Prince competitive Civil Service status. He was then an employee of the Department of the Navy, and the change is meant to correct an administrative error made by the Veterans Administration while he worked there. It says this will be done without following the competitive Civil Service rules and regulations.

10423.s: This order gives William P. Francisco a competitive civil-service status. It does this without following the usual competitive rules and regulations for civil service.

10422.s: This order sets up a process for investigating United States citizens who work for, or are being considered for work with, the United Nations Secretariat. It requires the Secretary of State to share identifying information with the Civil Service Commission and, in some cases, the FBI, and it allows the person to have a hearing and appeal if derogatory information is found. The order also tells the Secretary of State to send the Secretary General information found in the investigation, or to notify him if no derogatory information is found. These procedures can also be used for United States citizens employed by other public international organizations if an arrangement is made.

10421.s: This order directs federal agencies to develop and carry out programs for the physical security of certain government-owned and privately owned facilities important to defense mobilization, defense production, and the essential civilian economy. It gives the Chairman of the National Security Resources Board power to set policy, standards, and security ratings, assign facilities to agencies, and review agency programs. It also says the order does not make the federal government primarily responsible for the security of privately owned or state-owned facilities, and it does not apply to certain military and Atomic Energy Commission facilities.

10419.s: This order would restore possession, use, and control of a parcel of land in Honolulu to the Territory of Hawaii and transfer the title to the Territory, once required conditions are met. The Territory must set aside another parcel for use by the United States as an addition to the existing immigration station. It must also move or rebuild certain structures, clean and grade the new site, build fences and an entrance way, and pay the costs of the work.

10418.s: This order amends Executive Order 10321 by changing the year from 1950 to 1951. It applies under the listed sections of the Internal Revenue Code and takes effect when filed for publication in the Federal Register.

10417-A.s: This order closes several federal offices in the metropolitan area of the District of Columbia on Friday, December 26, 1952. It also excuses federal employees in that area and in the field service from duty that day, except for those excluded for special public reasons or where absence would conflict with existing law.

10420.s: This order changes several Selective Service rules for classifying, examining, and appealing the classification of registrants. It updates rules for men who have served in the armed forces, conscientious objectors, people assigned to civilian work, and special registrants in medical, dental, and allied specialist categories. It also changes how local boards handle appeal records and forwarding files, and it revokes one section of the regulations.

10417.s: This order creates a Board of Inquiry to look into a labor dispute at the American Locomotive Company plant in Dunkirk, New York. The dispute is between the company and certain employees represented by Local 2286 and Local 4498 of the United Steel Workers of America, CIO. The Board must report to the President by December 10, 1952, and may continue to perform other duties under the Labor Management Relations Act until the President ends it.

10416.s: This order changes two earlier orders that suspended the eight-hour law for certain laborers and mechanics working for the Department of Defense and the Department of the Interior on public work essential to national defense. It says their wages must be figured on an eight-hour basic day, and overtime must be paid at least time and one-half for hours over eight in a day.

10414.s: This order restores a tract of land at Opihipau, North Kohala, on the Island of Hawaii to the possession, use, and control of the Territory of Hawaii. The land was part of the Upolu Point Military Reservation and is described in the order as no longer needed for military or other purposes.

10415.s: This order changes a deadline in a previous executive order about the transfer of personnel to certain public international organizations. It replaces the phrase "within five years from the date of his transfer to such Board" with "on or before December 31, 1953."

10413.s: This order returns Kure (Ocean) Island and the surrounding reef to the possession, use, and control of the Territory of Hawaii. It had previously been under the control and jurisdiction of the Secretary of the Navy for naval purposes. The Secretary of the Navy keeps the right to maintain a radar reflector on the island and to access it.

10412.s: This order lets the Senate Committee on the Judiciary, or a subcommittee it authorizes, inspect certain income and other tax returns for the years 1941 to 1951. The inspection is for an investigation of how the Trading with the Enemy Act was administered, and it must follow the stated Treasury conditions.

10411.s: This order restores possession, use, and control of certain parcels of the Aiea Military Reservation on the Island of Oahu to the jurisdiction of the Territory of Hawaii. It covers all of Lot 1 and part of Lot 2, which the order says are no longer needed for military purposes.

10410.s: This order says the Department of State’s escapee program may be carried out without following three listed laws. It affects the escapee program authorized under the Mutual Security Act and administered by the State Department.

10409.s: This order tells the Secretary of the Navy to award the Purple Heart to people serving with the Navy, Marine Corps, or Coast Guard who are wounded in combat with an enemy or opposing foreign armed force, or because of an act of such a force. It also directs posthumous awards to people in those services who are killed or die after being wounded in those actions, if the wound needed treatment by a medical officer. The Purple Heart must be sent to the nearest kin in eligible posthumous cases, and no more than one Purple Heart may be awarded to one person except as allowed for later awards with a Gold Star or other device.

10408.s: This order transfers the administration of the part of the Trust Territory of the Pacific Islands that includes Tinian and Saipan from the Secretary of the Interior to the Secretary of the Navy. The transfer takes effect on January 1, 1953. The Secretary of the Navy is to manage civil government there and carry out U.S. obligations under the trusteeship agreement and the United Nations Charter, while the President keeps the authority over areas closed for security reasons and the Secretary of State handles relations with United Nations bodies.

10407.s: This order sets rules for agreements between the Treasury Department and a State or Territory to withhold state or territorial income taxes from pay to federal employees. It says federal agencies must follow the state or territorial withholding law for covered employees whose regular place of federal employment is in that State or Territory. The order does not apply to pay for service as a member of the Armed Forces and does not require federal agencies to collect delinquent tax debts from federal employees.

10405.s: This order exempts Theodore Marks, Associate Chief of the Veterans Employment Service in the Department of Labor, from compulsory retirement for age. It applies to him for an indefinite period of time.

10404.s: The order restores possession, use, and control of one tract of land from the Fort Shafter Military Reservation in Honolulu to the Territory of Hawaii and transfers title to it. It also transfers title to three other parcels of land that were described in an earlier executive order. The land involved was previously part of military reservation land on Oahu.

10406.s: The order creates a three-member board to investigate a dispute between United Air Lines, Inc. and certain employees represented by the Flight Engineers' International Association, UAL Chapter. The board must report its findings to the President, and United Air Lines and its employees may not change the conditions that led to the dispute except by agreement during the period set out in the order. The board must also follow section 502 of the Defense Production Act of 1950, as amended.

10403.s: This order reserves certain lands in the Fort Missoula Military Reservation in Montana as an addition to the Fort Missoula District of the Lolo National Forest. The lands are to be managed by the Secretary of Agriculture under rules and plans approved with the Secretary of the Army. They remain available for the Department of the Army to use for national defense, and military rules continue to apply unless the two secretaries agree otherwise.

10402.s: This order directs the Department of State, the Coast Guard, the Weather Bureau, and the Federal Communications Commission to carry out the duties assigned to them under the International Convention for Safety of Life at Sea, 1948. It also says the Coast Guard, or another authorized agency, shall issue required certificates, and that the departments and commission must work together to carry out the Convention. When the Coast Guard operates as part of the Navy, those duties shift to the Department of the Navy (Coast Guard).

10401.s: The order requires the Tariff Commission to keep reviewing products covered by trade-agreement concessions that have been withdrawn, suspended, or modified, and to send periodic reports to the President. It also lets the Commission, or the President, start a formal investigation to see whether those trade changes are still needed to prevent or remedy serious injury, or the threat of it, to the domestic industry. Interested parties must be allowed to attend the hearing, present evidence, and be heard.

10400.s: This order amends an earlier executive order about disability retirement pay, hospitalization, and re-examination for members and former members of the uniformed services. It gives the Secretary concerned authority over hospitalization and re-examination for members on the temporary disability retired list, except where the order gives that authority to the Administrator of Veterans' Affairs. It also sets rules for hospitalization of some members and former members with chronic diseases and amends another executive order to match these changes.

10399.s: This order designates the Surgeon General of the Public Health Service as the United States' "health administration" under the International Sanitary Regulations. It gives that office the duty to carry out the regulations on sanitary and quarantine measures and on reports and notifications of outbreaks of certain diseases. It affects international traffic and the government's work to prevent the spread of disease.

10397.s: This order keeps certain appointments as officers and warrant officers of the Army and Air Force in effect until April 1, 1953. It applies to appointments that would otherwise end after April 27, 1952, and before that date under the laws listed in the order.

10398.s: This order says that for the Canal Zone, the Commander in Chief, Caribbean, has the final say over whether protection matters are part of military security, protection, and defense or part of civil protection. If the Governor of the Canal Zone disagrees, the Governor may appeal to the President, but the decision stays in effect until the President changes it. The order also revokes Executive Order No. 2382.

10396.s: This order approves a design for the official seal of the Small Defense Plants Administration. It applies to the Small Defense Plants Administration and establishes the seal as its official seal.

10395.s: This order extends two deadlines under the housing act for certain temporary housing. It moves the deadline for filing requests to December 31, 1952. It also extends the deadline for meeting all conditions for relinquishments or transfers under those requests to June 30, 1953.

10394.s: This order suspends compliance with certain employment rules in the Canal Zone under two appropriation acts. It applies to those laws from their effective date. It does not change the provisions about how much compensation may be paid to people in skilled, technical, clerical, administrative, executive, or supervisory jobs in the Canal Zone for the United States Government or certain government-owned companies.

10393.s: This order creates a Clemency and Parole Board for War Criminals with three presidentially appointed members from the Departments of State, Defense, and Justice. The board is to investigate cases and advise the President on clemency, sentence reduction, or parole for Japanese war criminals sentenced by U.S. or international tribunals. It may examine witnesses, take testimony, set its own procedure, and act by majority vote.

10391.s: This order amends an earlier order about allowances and allotments for Government personnel on foreign duty. It lets the Secretary of State exercise certain presidential powers over regulations for living-quarters, cost-of-living, and representation allowances for civilian officers and employees of the Government.

10390.s: This executive order amends the rules for the Wage Stabilization Board. It adds up to two alternate members who are to represent business and industry. These alternate members are appointed by the President with the advice and consent of the Senate, and they serve only when a regular member is not participating and the Chairman calls on them.

10389.s: This order returns a tract of land at Ka Lae on the Island of Hawaii to the possession, use, and control of the Territory of Hawaii. The land had been reserved for military purposes of the United States, but the order says it is no longer needed for that use.

10388.s: This order revokes a 1940 executive order that placed Palmyra Island under the control and jurisdiction of the Secretary of the Navy. It also ends the reservation of the island for naval purposes.

10387.s: This order says certain functions under the Mutual Security Act, the Act for International Development, the Institute of Inter-American Affairs Act, and the Mutual Defense Assistance Act are exempt from several listed laws. It also exempts some purchases made outside the continental United States from other listed laws. For functions carried out in Burma and Indonesia under the Act for International Development, it exempts one listed law as well.

10386.s: This order says certain tax returns may be open to inspection when needed to review an accepted offer in compromise about tax liability. It covers income, excess profits, declared value excess profits, capital stock, estate, and gift tax returns, along with related schedules or other papers. The inspection must follow the conditions in the related Treasury decision.

10385.s: This order extends the deadline for removing certain temporary housing. The new deadline is July 1, 1954 instead of December 31, 1952, and it affects temporary housing under the Housing and Home Finance Administration that was built under certain laws.

10384.s: This order restores a parcel of land at Waiakea, Hilo City, to the possession, use, and control of the Territory of Hawaii. The land had been set aside for the United States for use in connection with the Hilo Airport Military Reservation. The order says the land is no longer needed for that purpose.

10383.s: This order restores two parcels of land at Palaau, Molokai, to the possession, use, and control of the Territory of Hawaii. The land had been set aside for use by the United States in connection with the Molokai Airport Military Reservation, but it is no longer needed for that purpose. The two parcels together cover 10.321 acres.

10381.s: This order changes the rules for travel and transportation expenses for civilian officers and employees of the United States when they are transferred to another official station for permanent duty. It says the agency may get transportation services from any available common carrier. It also lets an employee choose a different way to move personal effects, but the employee must pay any extra cost above the government-selected method.

10382.s: This order directs the Secretary of State to make arrangements for the Department of State to take possession of any remaining records and property of the Displaced Persons Commission. It also allows the department to designate officials to certify vouchers paid from Commission funds after August 31, 1952. Any remaining records and property are to be disposed of under applicable laws and regulations when no longer needed.

10380.s: This order says the United States High Commissioner for Germany will act as the representative of the Director for Mutual Security and the Special Representative for Europe in matters with Germany. The High Commissioner is to be helped by a Chief of Special Mission, who is appointed by the Director for Mutual Security and must be acceptable to the High Commissioner. The Chief of Special Mission has the rank of Minister and works under the High Commissioner’s immediate supervision. This order also supersedes a prior executive order on the same subject.

10379.s: This order suspends a provision of the Officer Personnel Act of 1947 that required mandatory retirement for colonels of the Regular Army and the Regular Air Force. The suspension lasts for the emergency proclaimed on December 16, 1950, or until June 30, 1957, whichever is earlier. The appropriate Secretary may choose which colonels are kept on active duty, and the total selected may not exceed sixty percent of those who otherwise would be retired.

10378.s: This order restores certain land at Hilo, Hawaii, to the possession, use, and control of the Territory of Hawaii. The land had been set aside for aeronautical purposes of the United States. The order says the land is no longer needed for that purpose.

10377.s: This order revokes two earlier executive orders and changes the rules for the Wage Stabilization Board. The board would have 18 members appointed by the President with the advice and consent of the Senate, with equal numbers from the general public, labor, and business and industry. The President would choose the chairman and vice chairman from the public members, and the board would be under the supervision and direction of the Economic Stabilization Administrator.

10375.s: This order restores the Round Top Military Reservation and its rights-of-way to the jurisdiction of the Territory of Hawaii. It says the land is no longer needed for military purposes and includes rights-of-way to Tantalus Road and to Sugar Loaf Military Reservation.

10374.s: This order adds certain lands acquired by exchange to the Nicolet and Chequamegon National Forests and says future lands acquired that way will be added too. It also extends the Chequamegon National Forest boundaries to include about 4,160 acres and adds a small tract to the Nicolet National Forest. In addition, it adds some former lighthouse lands to the Chequamegon National Forest and revokes the earlier 1871 order for those lands.

10376.s: This order requires permanent appointments for certain positions in the field service of the Post Office Department, if allowed by law. It converts some employees with indefinite appointments to probational or permanent appointments, including some who were hired from competitive civil-service registers and some who return after service in the armed forces. Employees not converted because there are not enough vacancies are to be placed on competitive registers for later probational appointment.

10372.s: This order creates a three-member board to investigate a dispute between Northwest Airlines and certain of its employees represented by the International Association of Machinists. The board must report its findings to the President within thirty days. During that time, and for thirty days after the board reports, Northwest Airlines and its employees may not change the conditions involved in the dispute except by agreement.

10371.s: This order creates a three-member board to investigate a dispute between Trans World Airlines and certain employees represented by the Flight Engineers' International Association, TWA Chapter. The board must report its findings to the President. It also says no changes may be made, except by agreement, in the conditions out of which the dispute arose, and the board must follow section 502 of the Defense Production Act of 1950.

10370.s: This order delegates some presidential authority under section 708 of the Defense Production Act to the Small Defense Plants Administrator. It covers voluntary agreements and programs, including approval of small-business production pools and related requests and findings. Before making a request or finding, the Administrator must consult with the Attorney General and the Chairman of the Federal Trade Commission, and must get the Attorney General’s approval for requests under section 708(b). The Administrator may also pass this authority on to other government officers or agencies, within the limits of the law.

10369.s: This order designates the Bureau of Reclamation as an agency included within the definition of "Department" for Title I of the Renegotiation Act of 1951. It makes Title I apply to contracts with the Bureau of Reclamation and related subcontracts for amounts received or accrued on or after July 1, 1952, no matter when the contracts were made.

10368.s: This order changes how certain mutual security and economic cooperation functions are handled by the government. It gives many of the President’s functions under the listed laws to the Director for Mutual Security, and some functions to the Secretary of State. It also transfers some personnel, records, property, and funds to the Department of State or the Director for Mutual Security, and it revokes some earlier orders and committees.

10367.s: This order changes a prior executive order about the Commissioned Corps of the Public Health Service being treated as a military service. It replaces the date "June 30, 1952" with "July 3, 1952" in that order. The change affects the Commissioned Corps and the regulations set for it.

10366.s: This order changes Selective Service rules for when a registrant’s work can be considered necessary to the national health, safety, or interest. It says the person must be doing work that cannot be replaced, and removing them would cause a material loss of effectiveness. It also allows apprentice training programs to qualify if they meet required standards and are accepted for deferment purposes.

10364.s: This order exempts John J. Deviny, the Public Printer, from compulsory retirement for age. It applies to him for an indefinite period of time.

10365.s: This order suspends some parts of the Officer Personnel Act of 1947 for Marine Corps officers of the grade of second lieutenant and above. The suspended parts deal with distribution in grades, promotion by selection, temporary promotion, and discharge after a second failure of selection for promotion. It does not suspend promotion rules for any Marine Corps officer whose name was already on a promotion list on the date of the order, and it replaces part of a prior order for Marine Corps officers of captain and below.

10363.s: This order changes Selective Service rules for local board areas, medical expense payments, classification of unborn children, conscientious objector appeals, induction forms, and volunteers. It affects registrants, local boards, appeal boards, and the Department of Justice. It also sets rules for when a volunteer can be classified for military service and lists several exceptions.

10362.s: This order changes a prior order about the Commissioned Corps of the Public Health Service being treated as a military service. It replaces the date "June 15, 1952" with "June 30, 1952" in that earlier order. It affects the Commissioned Corps of the Public Health Service.

10361.s: This order establishes part of the territorial waters of Passage Canal, Alaska, as a defensive sea area for national defense. People and vessels other than public vessels of the United States may not enter the area unless authorized by the Secretary of Defense or a designated officer. The Secretary of Defense is directed to enforce the order and may issue regulations, and violations are subject to the penalties in federal law.

10360.s: This order amends the rules for the Air Coordinating Committee. It says the committee will include one representative from each listed agency, with the President naming the chairman. It also says the Director of the Bureau of the Budget and the Chairman of the National Security Resources Board will each name one non-voting member.

10358.s: This order applies to executive departments, independent agencies, and government-owned or government-controlled corporations. It sets rules for when federal offices are closed and when employees are excused from work if a holiday falls on Sunday or on a scheduled non-workday. It also says certain workdays will be treated as holidays for pay and leave purposes.

10359.s: This order amends earlier rules on defense materials procurement and loans. It gives the Secretary of Agriculture authority over food and certain plant fibers, except abaca, when the procurement or loans are meant to encourage and develop sources of supply in the United States and its territories and possessions. It also says these actions must fit programs certified by the Defense Production Administrator, and it keeps prior actions in effect unless they conflict with this order.

10357.s: This order includes certain lands in Cherokee County, North Carolina, as part of the Nantahala National Forest. It follows an approved agreement between the Tennessee Valley Authority and the United States Department of Agriculture to transfer those lands for national-forest use.

10355.s: This order gives the Secretary of the Interior the President’s authority to withdraw or reserve public lands and other lands owned or controlled by the United States for public purposes. It also allows the Secretary to modify or revoke those withdrawals and reservations, issue rules and procedures, and pass the authority to certain Interior officers. Orders under this authority must be published, and land under another department or agency needs that department’s approval before action is taken.

10356.s: This order changes a previous order about the Commissioned Corps of the Public Health Service being a military service. It replaces the date "June 1, 1952" with "June 15, 1952" in that earlier order.

10354.s: This order changes the pay rules for civil service officers and employees of the Public Health Service who are assigned full-time to a station devoted to the care of leprosy patients for 30 days or more. It gives them extra pay equal to 25 percent of their basic compensation, and it says some officers or employees who were already receiving pay on June 30, 1952, cannot have their total pay reduced while they stay on continuous assignment to that duty before July 1, 1957.

10353.s: This order allows Cressie E. Coffelt to be appointed to a competitive position in the Department of the Interior. It says this appointment may be made without following the competitive rules of the Civil Service Act.

10352.s: This order changes the rules for issuing documents needed to work on a U.S. merchant vessel. A person cannot be employed on such a vessel unless the Commandant is satisfied that the person’s character and habits would not be harmful to the security of the United States. The Commandant may also name categories of merchant vessels where this rule does not apply.

10351.s: This order names the captains of the ports of Cristobal and Balboa in the Canal Zone to issue provisional certificates of registry to certain vessels abroad. It applies to vessels bought by citizens of the United States, including corporations, and it revokes a prior executive order on the same subject.

10350.s: This order approves a design to be the official seal of the Federal Civil Defense Administration. It applies to that agency and sets out the seal’s design and lettering.

10348.s: This order keeps certain earlier orders, regulations, rulings, instructions, and licenses in effect. They apply for the time of the national emergency proclaimed in 1950 and cover blocked property under those orders.

10349.s: This order declares the Commissioned Corps of the Public Health Service to be a military service and a branch of the land and naval forces until June 1, 1952. It makes officers in the corps subject to the Uniform Code of Military Justice, and officers detailed to duty with the armed forces are subject to the laws that apply to that service. It also says offenses and penalties under earlier orders or regulations can still be prosecuted and completed.

10346.s: This order tells each Federal department and agency to make plans for using its people, materials, facilities, and services in a civil-defense emergency. It also requires plans to keep essential functions going at the seat of Government and elsewhere during such an emergency. The Federal Civil Defense Administrator must help identify useful resources and coordinate their use with national, State, and local civil-defense plans.

10347.s: This order tells the Secretary of State to affix the Seal of the United States to certain presidential documents without any special warrant. It applies to proclamations, treaty documents, extradition warrants, letters to foreign government leaders, and exequaturs for certain foreign consular officers. For documents that need the Secretary of State’s counter-signature, the seal may be affixed after that signature is added.

10345.s: This order extends for nine months many military enlistments that would expire after June 30, 1952 and before July 1, 1953. It applies to enlistments in the Army, Navy, Marine Corps, Air Force, and Coast Guard, including the reserve components named in the order. It does not stop voluntary re-enlistments or voluntary extensions allowed by law or service regulations.

10344.s: This order sets rules for registering United States citizens living outside the United States under the Selective Service system. It tells how they must register, how local boards handle their forms, and how their classification and appeals are handled. It also changes Selective Service rules on permits to leave the United States and on who may be placed in Class I-D.

10343.s: This order lets the House Committee on the Judiciary, or a subcommittee it authorizes, inspect certain tax returns for periods up to and including 1951. The committee may do this during the Eighty-second Congress for its inquiry into the administration of the Department of Justice and the office of the Attorney General. The chairman must give a written statement of the specific allegations, complaints, and credible evidence for each taxpayer whose return is sought, and the inspection is subject to Treasury conditions.

10342.s: This order restores the Sugar Loaf Military Reservation and the right-of-way to the jurisdiction of the Territory of Hawaii. It says the land is no longer needed for military purposes and will be returned to the territory's use. The land is on the Island of Oahu in the Territory of Hawaii.

10341.s: This order discontinues four military protected areas: the Rose Island Naval Defensive Sea Area, the Rose Island Naval Airspace Reservation, the Tutuila Island Naval Defensive Sea Area, and the Tutuila Island Naval Airspace Reservation. It affects those sea areas and airspace reservations that had been established earlier by executive order.

10339.s: This order extends several deadlines under the housing act for filing requests, meeting conditions for transfers or relinquishments, notifying tenants to leave, and taking action to evict tenants. It also extends deadlines for requests and agreements involving certain housing projects and for showing the need for low-rent housing. The order applies to housing under the act and to municipalities, counties, public housing agencies, tenants, and the Housing and Home Finance Administrator.

10340.s: The order directs the Secretary of Commerce to take possession of and operate the plants, facilities, and other property of the listed steel companies if needed for national defense. It says federal agencies must help, and the Secretary sets the terms and conditions of employment for the plants under this order. The order also says workers keep the right to bargain collectively and take part in concerted activities, as long as those activities do not interfere with operation.

10338.s: This order sets rules for coordinating United States officials in each country who are carrying out programs under the Mutual Security Act of 1951. It gives the Chief of the United States Diplomatic Mission the lead role in coordinating those activities, avoiding duplication, and reporting on the programs. It also sets a process for settling disagreements and says the Director for Mutual Security may add more procedures. Some prior executive orders are revoked, while others are left unchanged.

10337.s: This order changes the rules for appointing postmasters of the fourth class. It raises the compensation limit for appointments based on a post office inspector’s investigation and report from $1,300 a year to $1,700 a year. It also replaces the earlier regulation with this new limit.

10335.s: This order designates the Provisional Intergovernmental Committee for the Movement of Migrants from Europe as a public international organization. It gives the committee the privileges, exemptions, and immunities under the International Organizations Immunities Act. It applies to the United States' participation in that committee.

10336.s: This order amends the rules for the Medal of Freedom. It says the medal may be awarded to people who have done meritorious acts or service that helped the United States, an allied nation, or the security interests of the United States during a declared war or national emergency. It also says the medal cannot be awarded to U.S. citizens for acts or service done within the continental United States or to members of the armed forces, and it may be awarded posthumously.

10333.s: This order keeps Bernice Pyke, the Collector of Customs for Customs Collection District No. 41 in Cleveland, Ohio, exempt from compulsory retirement for age. The exemption lasts until a successor is appointed and qualified.

10334.s: This order exempts Frederick C. Mayer, the Organist and Choirmaster at the United States Military Academy, from compulsory retirement for age. It affects Mayer and lets him continue in his job for an indefinite period of time.

10332.s: This order sets who will act as Secretary of Defense, Secretary of the Army, Secretary of the Navy, or Secretary of the Air Force if the office holder dies, becomes disabled, or is absent. It lists the succession order for each department, starting with certain deputy or under secretaries and then other named officials. The person who takes over would serve only on a temporary or interim basis and would not lose their own regular office.

10331.s: This order lets the Senate Committee on Interior and Insular Affairs, or a subcommittee it authorizes, inspect certain income tax returns for 1946 to 1950. The inspection is for its studies of relations between the United States and Indians and Indian tribes, and measures about the care, education, management, and lands of Indians. It also covers claims paid out of Indian funds, and the inspection must follow stated Treasury conditions.

10330.s: This order exempts Frances Perkins from compulsory retirement for age for an indefinite period of time. It affects Frances Perkins, a member of the United States Civil Service Commission.

10329.s: This order changes the rules for the Missouri Basin Survey Commission. It says the commission is considered established on February 9, 1952, and must report to the President in writing within one year with its study results and recommendations, including any needed legislation. It also allows the commission to send earlier reports if it wants to.

10328.s: This order sets rules for civilian work that some registrants may do instead of being inducted into the armed forces. It applies to people between 18 and 26 who are classified in Class I-O or claim they qualify, and it tells local boards how to choose and order that work. The work must be in certain government or nonprofit jobs, and private employment is generally not allowed. It also covers what happens if a registrant does not obey an order, and how the work is administered and completed.

10327.s: This order directs a Special Assistant to the Attorney General to investigate improper or illegal conduct tied to federal government business. He may recommend prosecutions, other legal action, or disciplinary action based on what he finds. Executive departments and agencies must cooperate and provide information, personnel, and other help when asked. The order ends on December 31, 1952.

10325.s: This order sets rules for awarding the Medal for Humane Action. The medal may be given to people who served in or with the U.S. armed forces and helped supply necessities of life to the people of Berlin, Germany, during the listed period. It also says no one may receive more than one medal, and if an eligible person dies, the medal may be presented to a representative or next of kin.

10326.s: This order makes certain income, excess-profits, declared value excess-profits, capital stock, estate, and gift tax returns from 1945 through 1950 open to inspection. The Senate Committee on Expenditures in the Executive Departments, or a subcommittee it authorizes, may review them during the second session of the Eighty-second Congress. The inspection must follow the conditions in the Treasury decision on these returns.

10324.s: This order changes the definitions of "solid fuels" and "domestic transportation, storage, and port facilities" in a prior executive order. It says "solid fuels" includes several kinds of coal, coke, and coal chemicals. It also lists the transportation vehicles, services, warehouses, and port facilities covered, except movement of petroleum and gas by pipeline.

10322.s: This order adds certain lands in Arizona and New Mexico to lands covered by a prior order. It transfers jurisdiction over those lands from the Department of Agriculture to the Department of the Interior for administration and exchange under the Taylor Grazing Act. The lands were acquired and administered under Title III of the Bankhead-Jones Farm Tenant Act.

10323.s: This order transfers several small-business functions from the Department of Commerce to the Small Defense Plants Administration. The transferred functions include help with government procurement, advice on small-business production pools, size classifications of manufacturing concerns, economic studies of small-business defense problems, information on government financial assistance, inventorying productive capacity, and managerial aids for small business. It also moves related personnel, records, property, and funds to the new administration.

10320.s: This order further exempts Lawrence M. Lawson from compulsory retirement for age for one year, ending January 31, 1953. It applies to his role as Commissioner of the United States on the International Boundary and Water Commission, United States and Mexico.

10321.s: This order makes certain income, excess-profits, declared value excess-profits, capital stock, estate, and gift tax returns for periods up to 1950 open to inspection by the Senate Committee on Rules and Administration or a duly authorized subcommittee. The inspection is for studies on the election of Members of Congress, corrupt practices, contested elections, credentials and qualifications, and Federal elections generally. It applies during the Eighty-second Congress and is subject to the stated Treasury conditions.

10319.s: This order creates a three-member board to investigate a dispute between Northwest Airlines and certain of its employees represented by the International Association of Machinists. The board must report its findings to the President within thirty days. During that time, and for thirty days after the report, Northwest Airlines and its employees may not change the conditions involved in the dispute except by agreement.

10318.s: This order creates the Missouri Basin Survey Commission and puts it under a chairman and vice chairman chosen from eleven presidentially appointed members. The commission must study the Missouri River Basin’s land and water resources and make recommendations for a program to develop, use, and protect those resources. It must also look at flood prevention and control, consult with state authorities, and report its findings and recommendations to the President within one year.

10317.s: This order creates the President's Commission on the Health Needs of the Nation. The commission is to study the supply of health workers, public health units, medical facilities, health research, and ways to pay for medical care. It is also to report to the President and may hold public hearings. Federal departments and agencies are directed to help the commission, and the commission ends after its final report or after one year, whichever comes first.

10316.s: This order makes certain tax returns for periods up to and including 1950 open to inspection by the Senate Committee on Armed Services or an authorized subcommittee. The committee may inspect income, excess-profits, declared value excess-profits, capital stock, estate, and gift tax returns. The inspection is for studying the policies, programs, activities, operations, facilities, requirements, and practices of the Department of Defense, the Armed Services, and related agencies.

10315.s: This order exempts William E. Lee, a member of the Interstate Commerce Commission, from compulsory retirement for age. The exemption lasts for an indefinite period, but not beyond the end of his present term of office as a commissioner.

10314.s: This order creates a three-member board to investigate a dispute between Pan American World Airways and certain of its employees represented by the Transport Workers Union of America, CIO. The board must report its findings to the President within thirty days. During that time, and for thirty days after the report, Pan American World Airways and its employees cannot change the conditions that led to the dispute unless they agree to do so.

10313.s: This order amends an earlier order about allowances and allotments for Government personnel on foreign duty. It gives the Secretary of State authority to handle regulations for civilian officers and employees on living-quarters, cost-of-living, and representation allowances. It applies to Government civilian workers covered by those rules.

10312.s: This order delegates authority to the Federal Communications Commission to prepare plans for certain radio stations and devices, except those owned and operated by the federal government. It also requires government departments and agencies to prepare plans for their own stations. The plans are meant to minimize radio emissions if there is an attack or an imminent threat, and they may not take over station content or become effective until approved by the Secretary of Defense and the Chairman of the National Security Resources Board.

10311.s: This order suspends compliance with certain statutory provisions about employment in the Canal Zone. It does not change the rules on how much compensation may be received by people in skilled, technical, clerical, administrative, executive, or supervisory jobs there when they work for the United States Government or a company partly or wholly owned by it.

10310.s: This order designates Honorable A. Cecil Snyder to act as judge of the District Court of the United States for Puerto Rico during 1952 if the office is vacant or if the judge is unavailable because of death, absence, illness, or other legal disability. He may perform the duties of that office and sign necessary papers and records as acting judge. He would do this without extra compensation.
