9291.s: The order directs the Treasury Department’s Procurement Division to transfer its stock of block mica to the Metals Reserve Company. The mica is to be sold on terms agreed to by the two groups, and the Metals Reserve Company is directed to use or dispose of it as the Chairman of the War Production Board directs. This affects the block mica held by the Procurement Division and the company that receives it.

9290.s: This order suspends the eight-hour work limit for laborers and mechanics employed by the War Department on public works within the United States that are essential to the war effort. It applies for the duration of the emergency proclamations named in the order. Their pay must still be based on an eight-hour day, with overtime paid at time and one-half for hours over eight in a day.

9289.s: This order sets rules for overtime pay for certain civilian employees of the Government who work more than 40 hours in an administrative workweek. It says executive departments and agencies must set official hours of duty, and extra work must be ordered or approved. Overtime is paid at one and one-half times the regular rate, with limits, and some employees on vessels or in certain posts may be treated differently.

9288.s: This order transfers control and jurisdiction over certain tracts of land in Puerto Rico from the Secretary of the Interior to the Secretary of Agriculture. The land is to be administered for forest purposes under the Bankhead-Jones Farm Tenant Act. It affects the listed tracts in several municipalities, subject to valid existing rights.

9287.s: This order transfers certain functions, duties, and powers from the Council of National Defense to the Secretary of the Interior. The Secretary of the Interior may carry out those duties directly or assign them to officers or employees of the Department of the Interior.

9286.s: This order sets rules for awarding the Medal for Merit. The medal may be given only by the President or by his direction, and it may be awarded to certain civilians from nations involved in the war and other friendly foreign nations for exceptionally meritorious conduct or courageous acts in support of the war effort. It also creates a Medal for Merit Board to receive proposals, review them, and make recommendations to the President. Awards to civilians of foreign nations need the prior approval of the Secretary of State.

9284.s: This order transfers five named commissioned officers from the Coast and Geodetic Survey to the Navy Department. While under Navy Department jurisdiction, they serve under their Coast and Geodetic Survey commissions and are part of the active naval forces of the United States. They are subject to Navy Department orders and rules where applicable, and they are to be returned to the Coast and Geodetic Survey when the national emergency ends.

9285.s: This order creates the United States of America Typhus Commission in the War Department under the Secretary of War. The commission is directed to study typhus fever and control it in and outside the United States when it threatens the military population. It also tells federal agencies to help with equipment, transportation, and personnel, and it creates a medal for meritorious service connected to the commission’s work.

9283.s: This order changes the rules for clothing and cash allowances for members of the Insular Force, the Samoan Native Guard, and the Samoan Native Band. It gives the Insular Force cash clothing allowances, with half rates when they are not required to wear blue clothing. It also sets a $20 cash clothing allowance for members of the Samoan Native Guard and Band on first enlistment or certain reenlistments, and a quarterly cash maintenance allowance of $4 under the stated conditions.

9282.s: This order transfers certain lands in Oklahoma from the Secretary of Agriculture to the Secretary of War for military purposes. It also lets the Secretary of Agriculture keep the jurisdiction needed to finish acquiring some of the lands. A prior order about the same area is superseded, and another order transferring 4.43 acres to the Secretary of the Interior is revoked. The lands are intended to be returned to the Secretary of Agriculture when they are no longer needed for military purposes.

9281.s: This order allows the Special Committee on Un-American Activities in the House of Representatives, or a subcommittee it authorizes, to inspect certain income and excess-profits tax returns. The returns include those filed under several tax laws for 1932 and later years. The inspection must follow rules set by the Secretary of the Treasury and is for carrying out House Resolution 420.

9280.s: This order gives the Secretary of Agriculture control over the Nation's food program. It lets the Secretary plan food supplies, set priorities and allocations, manage civilian rationing, and work on food exports, imports, and transportation needs. It also transfers some War Production Board functions and resources to the Department of Agriculture and allows the Secretary to delegate duties to other agencies.

9279.s: This order moves the Selective Service System to the War Manpower Commission and puts it under the Chairman’s supervision. It gives the Chairman control over how the system is run, including local and appeal boards, and lets the Chairman issue rules and orders to carry out the measure. It also limits new enlistments in the armed forces for certain males and directs hiring and recruitment rules in designated work areas.

9277.s: This order lets the Secretary of the Navy award the Purple Heart to people serving with the Navy, Marine Corps, or Coast Guard who are wounded in action against an enemy of the United States or by an enemy act that needs medical treatment. It also allows the Purple Heart to be awarded posthumously to people in those services who are killed in action or die from wounds received in action. The order limits most people to one Purple Heart, with a Gold Star or other suitable device for later awards.

9278.s: This order appoints Benjamin W. Thoron as Administrator of the Puerto Rico Reconstruction Administration, replacing Guy J. Swope, who resigned. It says he will serve without extra pay and will carry out the powers and duties given to that office under earlier executive orders.

9276.s: This order creates the Petroleum Administration for War and puts a Petroleum Administrator in charge under the President. It gives the Administrator broad duties over petroleum policy, supply, prices, rationing, tankers, pipe lines, and communication with federal and state agencies. It also transfers the former Office of Petroleum Coordinator for National Defense to the new office and leaves some military and other agency powers in place.

9275.s: This order sets rules for people and vessels in defensive sea areas. It bars people from having cameras or film there, except for official duty, national defense work, or when authorized under another law. It requires vessel masters or officers to take and hold prohibited camera equipment, and it requires a posted notice on most vessels. People who violate the rule can be prosecuted under the Criminal Code.

9273.s: This order amends two earlier orders to add more lands in Indiana to the lands transferred from the Secretary of Agriculture to the Secretary of the Navy for national defense purposes. The added lands are in the Martin County and White River Land Utilization Projects. The Secretary of Agriculture keeps whatever jurisdiction is needed to finish acquiring lands that are still in process of acquisition.

9274.s: This order directs the Secretary of War to establish units of the Women's Army Auxiliary Corps as needed to meet the Army’s requirements. It also amends Executive Order No. 9163 to carry out this change. The order applies to women enrolled or appointed in the Corps.

9271.s: This order further exempts George T. Summerlin, a Foreign Service Officer of Class I, from compulsory retirement for age. The exemption lasts for as long as needed, but not beyond the close of business on November 30, 1947.

9272.s: This order extends the trust periods for Indian lands, whether tribal or individual, that would otherwise expire during calendar year 1943. The extension is for 25 more years from the date each trust would have expired. It does not apply to any case where Congress has specifically kept the power to extend the trust period.

9269.s: This order changes how the Treasury Department pays fixed fees on cost-plus-a-fixed-fee contracts for architectural and engineering services on certain projects. The Secretary of the Treasury may set the fee under an appropriate scale, but the fee cannot be more than 4 percent of the estimated cost, not counting payment for those services. It also modifies a later order that extended the earlier contract rules to Treasury and other government agencies.

9270.s: This order corrects the land description in a prior executive order that enlarged Naval Petroleum Reserve No. 1 in California. It changes the listed sections of land covered by that order.

9268.s: This order suspends most of section 12 of the Naval Aviation Cadet Act of 1942 during the present war. It applies to officers who were formerly enlisted as aviation cadets or were moved to that enlisted grade after September 3, 1942.

9267.s: This order suspends the maximum punishment limits for absence without leave under Article of War 61 for offenses committed after the order takes effect. It applies to military courts using the Army Manual for Courts-Martial and stays in effect until further order.

9266.s: This order establishes Buzzards Bay and Vineyard Sound as a defensive sea area for national defense. Vessels may not enter or travel there unless they are under United States Naval or other authorized supervision, and then only with permission and under the stated conditions. It also requires vessels to follow Navy instructions and authorizes enforcement by United States authorities.

9265.s: The order establishes three campaign medals: the American, European-African-Middle Eastern, and Asiatic-Pacific campaign medals. It allows these medals to be awarded to members of the U.S. land and naval forces, including the Women's Reserve of the United States Naval Reserve and members of the Women's Army Auxiliary Corps, who served outside the continental limits of the United States in the listed areas during the stated time period. Alaska is treated as outside the continental limits of the United States for this order.

9264.s: This order extends the rules of Executive Order 9001 to the Department of Commerce for contracts related to the prosecution of the war. It authorizes the Secretary of Commerce, and other officers he designates, to carry out the powers given under that earlier order. The action applies to contracts made or to be made by the Department of Commerce and is subject to the limits in Executive Order 9001.

9262.s: The order gives the Secretary of the Navy the same functions, powers, and duties for the Navy Department that the Secretary of War had under the named defense law. It also says any conflicting executive order, rule, or regulation is superseded to the extent of the conflict. The order took effect right away and stays in force until Title I of the First War Powers Act, 1941 ends.

9263.s: This order revokes the designations of Cordova, Alaska, and Mahukona, Hawaii, as customs ports of entry. It becomes effective on the thirtieth day from the date of the order.

9260.s: This order sets rules for awarding the Legion of Merit. It says the President may award it to members of the U.S. armed forces, the Government of the Commonwealth of the Philippines, and friendly foreign nations who have shown exceptionally meritorious conduct in outstanding service. It also says the Secretary of War and the Secretary of the Navy may propose awards, and awards to friendly foreign nationals need the President’s approval.

9261.s: This order amends the list of basic exchange rates used to pay losses to officers, enlisted men, and employees of the United States in foreign countries when foreign currencies rise against the American dollar. It adds Saudi Arabia to the list with the rial set at 35.74. The change is effective as of April 1, 1942.

9258.s: This order lets the Office of Price Administration inspect corporation statistical transcript cards made by the Bureau of Internal Revenue from certain corporation income and declared value excess-profits tax returns. The inspection must follow rules set by the Secretary of the Treasury for those cards.

9259.s: This order lets the Civil Service Commission act on certain executive branch employees who were serving without classified civil-service status and later became eligible for a probational appointment through an open competitive examination. On recommendation of the employing agency, the Commission may approve the appointment or give the employee classified civil-service status retroactively, even if the employee’s pay was not reduced, except as needed to meet the maximum pay rate for the position.

9257.s: This order expands Naval Petroleum Reserve No. 1 to include certain lands in Kern County, California. It withdraws the public lands in those areas from the public-land laws, including the mining laws, and reserves them as part of the reserve. Any lands in those areas later acquired by the United States will also become part of the reserve.

9256.s: This order ends the Electric Home and Farm Authority as a United States agency and starts proceedings to dissolve it. Its assets, funds, records, contracts, property, and remaining administration are transferred to the Reconstruction Finance Corporation for liquidation and payment of liabilities. All personnel are also transferred to the Reconstruction Finance Corporation without any change in civil service status.

9255.s: This order sets rules for paying rental allowances to officers of the Army, Navy, Marine Corps, Coast Guard, Coast and Geodetic Survey, and Public Health Service, including their adjunct forces. It defines terms like active duty, field duty, sea duty, permanent station, and dependent, and it sets rules for assigning government quarters. Officers are paid a rental allowance only when they are entitled to it and are not assigned adequate quarters at their permanent station.

9254.s: This order directs the Secretary of the Navy to take possession of and operate Triumph Explosives, Inc. plants in Elkton, Maryland. It also allows the Secretary to take over and operate certain plants of affiliated companies in Maryland and Delaware if needed for the war effort. The order says this control will end when the President decides the plants can be run privately in a way consistent with the war effort.

9253.s: This order extends another executive order to the Immigration and Naturalization Service in the Department of Justice. It applies to contracts for the feeding and care of people held by that service. It also lets the Attorney General, and people he designates, carry out the powers given under that earlier order for the Immigration and Naturalization Service.

9252.s: This order approves Civil Service Commission regulations for efficiency-rating boards of review in departments and independent establishments. The boards are set up to review employee efficiency ratings, hear appeals, and decide whether to change or keep a rating. The rules also cover who serves on the boards, how appeals are filed and heard, and how decisions are sent to employees and department heads.

9251.s: This order suspends the eight-hour limit for laborers and mechanics working for the Civil Aeronautics Administration on certain public works tied to the war effort. It applies to construction of landing areas, air navigation facilities, and other public works the Administrator of Civil Aeronautics specifies. It also says workers must be paid overtime at time and one-half for hours over eight in a day.

9250.s: This order creates an Office of Economic Stabilization and an Economic Stabilization Board to help guide national economic policy during the war. It directs federal agencies to work to control civilian purchasing power, prices, rents, wages, salaries, profits, rationing, and subsidies, and to stabilize the cost of living. It also sets rules for wage and salary increases and decreases, and it calls for stabilizing agricultural prices and limiting profits when prices are set.

9248.s: This order changes a rule on overtime wage compensation for federal departments and agencies. It says questions about how the rule applies must go to the Secretary of Labor. It also lets the Secretary decide that some or all of the overtime rules do not apply to certain industries, occupations, or classes of employees in limited cases.

9249.s: This order authorizes the Secretary of Agriculture to use Department officials to acquire, use, and dispose of real property and personal property that is needed for war purposes. It applies to property connected to the Emergency Rubber Project and to the storing and warehousing of agricultural commodities and products by the Department of Agriculture.

9247.s:
This order transfers the United States Employment Service, the National Youth Administration, the Apprenticeship Training Service, and the Training Within Industry Service to the War Manpower Commission. It also transfers related functions, records, property, personnel, and some funds to the Commission.

The Chairman of the War Manpower Commission is given control over certain related duties of the Federal Security Administrator, including some matters handled by the Office of Education. The order also directs the Chairman to make some employment service help available for unemployment compensation administration when it is not inconsistent with the war effort.

9246.s: This order puts the Chairman of the War Production Board in charge of the nation’s rubber program in all of its phases. It creates a Rubber Director inside the War Production Board to run the program and direct other federal agencies as needed. It also assigns certain agencies to help with research, plant construction, and supervision of synthetic rubber production.

9245.s: This order transfers the functions, powers, and duties of the United States High Commissioner to the Philippine Islands to the Secretary of the Interior. It also transfers the office’s personnel, records, property, and funds to that department.

9244.s: This order amends an earlier order that set up the War Shipping Administration. It gives the Administrator more powers over shipping matters, including contracts, payments, insurance, vessel operations, purchase, charter, repair, maintenance, requisition, and property. It also transfers related functions from the United States Maritime Commission, along with some personnel, records, and public property, to the War Shipping Administration. Other government departments must give the Administrator shipping information, except for certain Army and Navy vessels and secret military missions.

9243.s: This order sets rules for transferring civilian executive branch employees between federal departments and agencies, releasing them to private enterprise, and handling reemployment rights after those transfers or releases. It also directs the Director of the Bureau of the Budget to set priority classifications for executive departments and agencies based on their importance to the war program. It revokes two earlier executive orders, but says it does not affect reemployment rights already acquired under them.

9242-A.s: This order changes the rules for the Air Medal. It says the medal and ribbons may be awarded to any person serving in or with the Army, Navy, Marine Corps, or Coast Guard who has distinguished himself by meritorious achievement while taking part in an aerial flight.

9242.s: This order lets the Procurement Division of the Treasury Department use optical glass it bought for binoculars. It directs the division to sell or otherwise dispose of the glass for war production purposes, in amounts requested by the Chairman of the War Production Board.

9240.s: This order sets rules for premium and overtime wage pay for work related to the war. It limits extra pay for work on weekends and holidays, with some exceptions for the sixth or seventh day worked, emergency conditions, and certain listed holidays. Federal departments and agencies must make their contracts follow these rules and change existing contracts to match them.

9238.s: This order exempts Rudolph Forster and Maurice C. Latta, both Executive Clerks in the White House Office, from compulsory retirement for age. It keeps them in service past the retirement age rules that would otherwise apply to them.

9239.s: This order changes the Civil Service Rules by adding a category for special agents in the Bureau of the Census who collect cotton statistics. It also revokes one paragraph in Schedule B of those rules.

9237.s: This order allows the Postal Service to appoint temporary clerks, carriers, and laborers for part-time or intermittent holiday or seasonal work without following the Civil Service Rules. It applies to Postal Service employees needed from November 15, 1942, to January 15, 1943.

9236.s: This order transfers the survey ship Pathfinder from the Coast and Geodetic Survey to the Navy Department after it is built. It also transfers several named officers from the Coast and Geodetic Survey to the War Department, while keeping them serving under their Coast and Geodetic Survey commissions. The order says the ship and officers will return to the Coast and Geodetic Survey when the present national emergency ends, and it returns several other named officers to the Coast and Geodetic Survey.

9241.s: This order extends the rules of Executive Order 9001 to the Office of Strategic Services and the United States Joint Chiefs of Staff for contracts tied to the prosecution of the war. It also lets the Director of the Office of Strategic Services, and people he designates, carry out the powers given to the Secretary of War, the Secretary of the Navy, and the United States Maritime Commission under that earlier order.

9235.s: This order sets rules for how executive branch agencies use supplies and equipment. It directs the Director of the Bureau of the Budget to survey agency supplies, set standards, and order transfers of surplus supplies and equipment from one agency to another when needed. It also assigns the Treasury Department’s Procurement Division to handle warehousing, rehabilitation, and physical distribution for government agencies, with some categories of supplies excluded from the order.

9234.s: This order transfers jurisdiction over certain lands in New York to the Department of the Interior. It reserves those lands as a refuge and breeding ground for native birds and other wildlife, and for research on wildlife and related forest resources. The lands may still be used and managed by New York’s Conservation Department if a lease or cooperative agreement stays in effect.

9233.s: This order extends the rules of Executive Order 9001 to the Board of Economic Warfare for contracts related to the prosecution of the war. It also allows the Board’s chairman, and any officers or employees he names, to carry out the powers given by that earlier order to the Secretary of War, the Secretary of the Navy, and the United States Maritime Commission.

9232.s: This order transfers the functions, records, property, personnel, and administration of the Sample Surveys Section of the Work Projects Administration to the Bureau of the Census in the Department of Commerce. It takes effect on August 24, 1942.

9231.s: This order suspends the eight-hour work limit for laborers and mechanics on certain highway construction and reconditioning projects in Alaska. It applies to work on the Glenn and Richardson Highways and the Alaska-Canada Highway. Their wages must be figured on an eight-hour basic day, with overtime paid at not less than time and one-half for hours over eight in a day.

9230.s: This order amends a prior order on the classified civil service and adds special rules for attorney positions. It creates a Board of Legal Examiners to help set rules for recruiting, examining, appointing, promoting, and transferring attorneys in the classified civil service. It also sets up registers for attorney jobs, limits how names are listed, and covers temporary appointments and current incumbents of those positions.

9228.s: This order adds a new rule for vessels at wharfs or piers in the Canal Zone during war or another period ordered by the Governor. It requires a continuous gangway watch to check who goes on or off the vessel, keep unauthorized persons from boarding, and report any unauthorized boarding or attempted boarding. The rule applies to the master of the vessel or the master’s representative and to people trying to board or leave the vessel.

9229.s: This order directs the Secretary of the Navy to give up possession of the General Cable Corporation plant in Bayonne, New Jersey. It ends the Navy’s control of the plant and allows it to be privately operated in a manner consistent with the war effort.

9227.s: This order amends the rules for navigation of the Panama Canal and nearby waters. It says the pilot assigned to a vessel has control of the vessel’s navigation and movement, and it updates rules for accidents, claims, and damages involving vessels in canal waters. It also covers investigations of accidents, responsibility for injury to canal structures or equipment, and penalties for injuring or obstructing the canal.

9226.s: This order sets clothing allowances for enlisted men in the Navy, Coast Guard, Naval Reserve, and Coast Guard Reserve. It gives cash clothing allowances and quarterly cash maintenance allowances, with different amounts for general enlisted men, chief petty officers, officers' cooks, officers' stewards, and band members. It also covers some retired enlisted men, reserve members on active duty, and members of the Insular Force and the Samoan Native Guard and band.

9224.s: This order transfers certain lands in Alabama from the Secretary of Agriculture to the Secretary of War for military purposes. The lands were being acquired or were in the process of acquisition for a land-conservation and land-utilization project. The Secretary of Agriculture keeps only the jurisdiction needed to finish acquiring the lands that are still in process. The lands are intended to be returned to the Secretary of Agriculture when they are no longer needed for military purposes.

9223.s: This order changes when one provision of transportation regulations becomes effective. The provision applies to the payment of expenses for shipping household goods and personal effects of certain civilian officers and employees of the United States, and it will become effective on October 1, 1942.

9222.s: This order lets department heads pay money instead of providing transportation for dependents of certain officers, warrant officers, and enlisted men when they have a permanent change of station. The payment can cover the cost of commercial transportation for all or part of the travel if transportation in kind is not provided. It also lets those departments set extra rules that do not conflict with the order or the law it follows.

9220.s: The order directs the Secretary of the Navy to take possession of and operate the General Cable Company plant in Bayonne, New Jersey. It allows the plant to produce war materials for the company’s contracts with the United States or as otherwise needed for the war effort. The Secretary of the Navy may hire needed employees and use the company’s existing contractual or other rights. The President will end this control when he decides the plant can be privately operated in a way consistent with the war effort.

9219.s: This order extends the rules of Executive Order 9001 to the Office of Scientific Research and Development for contracts related to the prosecution of the war. It also lets the office’s director, and people he designates, carry out the functions and powers given under that earlier order to the Secretary of War, the Secretary of the Navy, and the Chairman of the United States Maritime Commission. These powers are subject to the same limits and regulations in the earlier order.

9218.s: This order authorizes the Office of Scientific Research and Development in the Office for Emergency Management to acquire, use, and dispose of real property and personal property. It applies to property the office deems necessary for military, naval, or other war purposes.

9221.s: This order extends the rules of Executive Order 9001 to Federal Prison Industries, Inc. for all contracts it makes or will make. It also lets the company’s Board of Directors, and people the board designates, carry out the powers given in that earlier order to the Secretary of War, the Secretary of the Navy, and the Chairman of the United States Maritime Commission.

9217.s: This order authorizes the Reconstruction Finance Corporation to acquire, use, and dispose of real property and personal property it deems needed for military, naval, or other war purposes. It applies to property the corporation decides is necessary for those purposes.

9216.s: The order changes the Manual for Courts-Martial to allow The Adjutant General, or one of his assistants, to certify facts or events that are officially recorded in War Department files. In those cases, the certificate is prima facie evidence of the fact or event. This applies when The Adjutant General or an assistant says it is contrary to public policy to reveal the source of the official knowledge or the text of the official record.

9214.s: This order expands the authority of the Office of Defense Transportation. It adds all domestic transportation within the territories and possessions of the United States to that office’s scope of authority.

9215.s: This order directs the Secretary of War to take full control of certain public airports on specified public lands in Arizona that were leased to the Boards of Supervisors of Maricopa and Pima Counties. It applies during the present war and for six months after it officially ends.

9213.s: This order extends the existence of the Quetico-Superior Committee for four more years, from June 30, 1942, to June 30, 1946. It affects the committee created by Executive Order No. 6783.

9211.s: This executive order lets the Division of Central Administrative Services in the Office for Emergency Management acquire, use, or dispose of leasehold interests in real property and personal property tied to them. It applies to property the division, with approval from the Liaison Officer for Emergency Management, deems necessary for war purposes.

9210.s: This order sets up additional monthly pay for enlisted men of the Navy and Coast Guard who have special qualifications in using the arms they may be required to use. The amount depends on class, from $1 to $5 per month, and it applies when they are stationed so they may need to use those arms, including some temporary duty away from their ship. It also replaces an earlier order on extra pay for Navy enlisted men specially qualified in the use of arms.

9209.s: This order sets rules for extra pay for enlisted men of the Marine Corps who are specially qualified in using ships' guns or other arms. Marine Corps enlisted men on ships get the same additional compensation as Navy enlisted men for special ship-gun qualifications. It also sets monthly extra pay amounts from $1 to $5 and says total extra pay under the order cannot be more than $5 per month.

9212.s: This order lets the Governor of The Panama Canal provide free transportation to the United States for certain employees of The Panama Canal or the Panama Railroad Company when they end their service on the Isthmus of Panama. The port or airport, and the carrier, are to be chosen in the Government’s interest by the Governor or by his authority. If an employee chooses a more expensive route or carrier, the employee must pay the extra cost. The Governor may also set rules to carry out the order, which stays in effect during the present war and for six months after it ends.

9208.s: This order exempts John F. Phillips from compulsory retirement for age for one year. It applies to Phillips, who worked as assistant to the superintendent in the Mechanical Division of The Panama Canal.

9207.s: This order extends the customs port of entry of Salem, Massachusetts, so it includes the territory of the municipality of Peabody, Massachusetts. It applies to Customs Collection District Number 4 in Massachusetts. The order becomes effective on the thirtieth day after July 29, 1942.

9205.s: This order creates the President's War Relief Control Board and gives it control over war relief charities and fund-raising tied to relief, rehabilitation, reconstruction, welfare, refugees, civilians affected by enemy action, and the armed forces and their dependents. It lets the Board register or license groups, regulate fund-raising appeals, set standards for collecting funds and goods, require records and reports, and merge or eliminate agencies for efficiency. The order does not apply to the American National Red Cross or to established religious bodies that are not carrying out those activities.

9206.s: This order sets rules for allowances for quarters and subsistence for enlisted men in the Army, Navy, Marine Corps, Coast Guard, Coast and Geodetic Survey, and Public Health Service when they are not furnished quarters or rations in kind. It also gives allowances for quarters to enlisted men of the first, second, and third grades who have dependents and no public quarters are available for those dependents. Payments may be made up to one month in advance, or up to three months in advance for men going to or from stations beyond the continental limits of the United States or in Alaska.

9203.s: This order authorizes the Treasury Department’s Procurement Division to use stocks of Manila fiber it bought under the act of June 7, 1939. It may sell or otherwise dispose of the fiber to the United States Navy, the United Kingdom, or Canadian manufacturers designated by the Government of the Dominion of Canada. The amounts are to be set from time to time by the Chairman of the War Production Board for national defense.

9204.s: This order sets up the Secretary of the Interior as Fishery Coordinator and creates an Office of Fishery Coordination. The office is directed to work with federal, state, local, and industry groups on the conservation, production, processing, packing, transportation, marketing, and consumption of fish and other fishery products. It also helps coordinate information and make recommendations on supplies, facilities, and other needs for the fishery industry during the war.

9202.s: This order exempts Oscar L. Moritz from compulsory retirement for age for one year. It applies to him as principal storekeeper in the Division of Storehouses and Fuel Oil Handling Plants of The Panama Canal. The exemption ends September 30, 1943.

9201.s: This order exempts Morris B. Hostetter, Chief of Section in the Accounting Department of The Panama Canal, from compulsory retirement for age. It lets him stay in service for one year, ending July 31, 1943.

9200.s: This order changes a Civil Service rule to list certain Foreign Service office jobs in Schedule A. It affects the Chief and Assistant Chief of the Foreign Service Buildings Office and the Chief of the Office of Foreign Service Furnishings.

9199.s: This order exempts Dr. Howard K. Tuttle from compulsory retirement for age for one year. It applies to him as assistant chief of Surgical Clinic in the Health Department of The Panama Canal.

9198.s: This order transfers certain Coast Guard functions to the Administrator of War Shipping Administration. It also transfers related records, property, personnel used mainly for those functions, and some unspent funds for use in carrying out them. Regular Coast Guard officers and men are not transferred, and Coast Guard Reserve members on active duty are not transferred without their consent.

9197.s: This order transfers certain lands in Fall River County, South Dakota, from the Secretary of Agriculture to the Secretary of War for military purposes. The Secretary of Agriculture keeps the authority needed to finish acquiring lands that are still in process of acquisition. The lands are intended to be returned to the Secretary of Agriculture when they are no longer needed for military purposes.

9196.s: This order suspends part of an older executive order for the period of the war and for six months after. It allows federal officers and agencies buying items needed for the war to obtain goods made in federal, state, or territorial prisons, directly or indirectly. It does not allow prison-made goods if they were produced under a contract where prison labor is hired out to or used by a private person, firm, or corporation.

9195.s: This order sets rules for when certain Army, Navy, Marine Corps, Coast Guard, and National Guard personnel must take regular aerial flights. It applies to officers, warrant officers, nurses, enlisted men, and some student and medical flight personnel, and it sets definitions for pilots, observers, and aerial flights. It also says who can issue the orders and how long those orders stay in force.

9193.s: This order amends the rules for the Office of Alien Property Custodian and gives that office authority over certain property and business enterprises tied to designated enemy countries and other foreign countries in some cases. It lets the Custodian direct, manage, control, vest, or arrange for the protection, reorganization, sale, or liquidation of covered property and businesses. It also sets rules for sharing information, transferring Treasury Department records and personnel, and consulting with the Secretary of State before certain actions are taken.

9192.s: This order amends a prior executive order about the Safford National Wildlife Refuge in Arizona. It transfers jurisdiction over acquired lands in Graham County, subject to valid existing rights, to the Department of the Interior. The lands are reserved as a refuge and breeding ground for native birds and other wildlife.

9194.s: This order transfers duties and functions over Navy Department real estate, including interests in it and temporary uses of it, from the Office of the Judge Advocate General of the Navy to the Chief of the Bureau of Yards and Docks. It also transfers the related appropriated funds needed to carry out the order. The Secretary of the Navy must take the steps needed to make this happen.

9191.s: This order changes the Foreign Service Regulations by renumbering several subparagraphs in section VI-1(a). It also adds two new subparagraphs naming the Department of War and the Department of the Navy.

9190.s: This order tells the Secretary of State to run the 1939 law under set rules for sending U.S. officers and employees to foreign governments. Only workers with special scientific, technical, or professional qualifications may be assigned, and only at the request of the foreign government and for the governments named in the order. It also sets rules for travel reimbursement, monthly allowances, possible extra compensation, and the handling of money advanced by foreign governments.

9188.s: This order suspends compliance with certain employment rules in the Canal Zone. It applies during any of the wars the United States is then engaged in.

9189.s: This order suspends compliance with part of section 7 of the Military Appropriation Act, 1943, about certain kinds of employment in the Canal Zone. The suspension lasts during the continuance of any of the wars the United States is then engaged in.

9187.s: This order transfers named commissioned officers from the Coast and Geodetic Survey to the War Department or the Navy Department. While under those departments, they remain under their Coast and Geodetic Survey commissions and are subject to Army or Navy laws, regulations, and orders as applicable. They are to be returned to the Coast and Geodetic Survey when the present national emergency ends.

9185.s: This order sets aside certain lands and waters at the mouth of the Susquehanna River in Maryland for the Department of the Interior. It designates the area as a refuge and breeding ground for migratory birds and other wildlife. The reservation does not interfere with Coast Guard use of part of Shad Battery, or Edmondsons Island, for lighthouse purposes.

9184.s: This order amends the War Manpower Commission to add two new members. One is a representative of the National Housing Agency, and the other is a joint representative of the War Shipping Administration and the Office of Defense Transportation.

9186.s: This order lets the Federal Works Administrator, or another agency officer acting in the Administrator’s place, acquire, use, and dispose of property needed for military, naval, or other war purposes. It covers real property, temporary use of property, and personal property located on or used with it. It also revokes a prior executive order about acquiring and disposing of property.

9182.s: This order creates an Office of War Information and moves several war information offices, powers, duties, records, property, personnel, and funds into it. The new office is placed in the Executive Office of the President and is led by a Director appointed by the President. It is meant to manage war information programs, coordinate federal information activities, and work with other agencies on radio, motion pictures, and information sent abroad.

9183.s: This order changes the name of the Defense Communications Board to the Board of War Communications. It also amends several earlier executive orders and an administrative order to match the new name.

9181.s: This order sets up special federal representatives in Alaska and creates an Alaska War Council with the Governor of Alaska and others. The council is told to work closely with military authorities so federal civil activities in Alaska fit wartime needs. It also says federal departments and agencies in Alaska must follow requests the Secretary of War deems necessary for the war effort.

9180.s: This order authorizes the Secretary of the Interior to make contracts for the disposal of yucca growing on public land. It applies when the products made from that yucca are substitutes for materials that are strategic, critical, or otherwise essential to the war effort.

9179.s: This order authorizes the Commissioner of Public Roads, or an acting officer, to acquire, use, and dispose of real property and personal property. It applies to property that is needed for military, naval, or other war purposes.

9178.s: This order authorizes the Secretary of the Interior to acquire, use, and dispose of real property, temporary use of property, other property interests, and personal property in connection with the department’s helium development and production program. The property must be deemed necessary for military, naval, or other war purposes.

9177.s: This order lets the Secretary of War, the Secretary of the Navy, the Secretary of the Treasury, the Secretary of Agriculture, and the Reconstruction Finance Corporation use the power to make emergency purchases of war material abroad. It also says that this material may be admitted free of duty, and the Commissioner of Customs must issue rules for that process. The order allows these powers to be carried out by designated officers, civilian officials, or certain corporations under their control, and it applies to purchases made before or after the order while it is in effect.

9176.s: This order transfers the functions, powers, and duties for registering agents of foreign principals from the Secretary of State to the Attorney General. It also transfers related property, books, and records to the Attorney General. Existing rules, regulations, and forms stay in effect until the Attorney General changes them, and the Attorney General must send the Secretary of State a copy of each new registration statement for possible comment.

9175.s: This order changes the rule for commercial licenses under the highway and traffic regulations in the Canal Zone. It says commercial licenses are valid for the fiscal year they are issued or renewed, unless they are revoked, suspended for cause, lost, or defaced. It also says commercial motor vehicle operator licenses issued or renewed for 1942 stay in force until the end of the fiscal year ending June 30, 1943, unless revoked, suspended for cause, lost, or defaced.

9174.s: This order exempts Harry P. Hoby from compulsory retirement for age for one year. It applies to Hoby, a foreman in the Mechanical Division of the Department of Operation and Maintenance at The Panama Canal.

9173.s: This order transfers control and jurisdiction over a government dock and approach in Juneau, Alaska, from the Secretary of the Interior to the Secretary of the Navy. The property is to be used by the United States Coast Guard. The transfer is subject to valid existing rights.

9172.s: This order creates a National Railway Labor Panel of nine members for the duration of the war and six months after. The panel can appoint emergency boards to investigate certain railway labor disputes that are not settled under the Railway Labor Act. It also bars strike votes and strike dates in disputes that may interfere with the war effort, and it applies to railway carriers and their employees.

9171.s: This order expands the United States Naval Radio Station, Summit, Canal Zone by adding a described tract of land to the naval reservation. The added land is in the Canal Zone and contains about 29.21 acres, more or less.

9169.s: This order directs the Secretary of the Navy to give back possession of Brewster Aeronautical Corporation plants in Long Island City, Newark, and Johnsville. It says the plants will now be privately operated in a way that is consistent with the war effort. It affects the company and the Navy's control of those plants.

9170.s: The order makes most U.S. navigation and vessel inspection laws apply to the Virgin Islands. It does not apply the coastwise laws, federal tonnage duties, light money, or entrance and clearance fees, and it leaves out part of the vessel inspection laws for certain cargo vessels carrying more than twelve passengers or persons besides the crew.

9168.s: This order sets up the waters of Matagorda Bay, Texas, and nearby approaches and tributaries as a defensive sea area for national defense. Vessels and other craft may not enter or move in the area without specific permission from the Secretary of War or a designated officer. The Army will supervise movement there, and vessels or people who break the rules may be forced to comply and may face prosecution.

9167.s: This order reserves certain federal lands and waters in Stillwater County, Montana, as the Halfbreed Lake National Wildlife Refuge. It is for migratory birds and other wildlife, and private lands inside the area would become part of the refuge if the United States acquires title or control. It makes it unlawful to hunt, trap, capture, disturb, or kill birds or other wild animals in the refuge, and to enter it except under rules set by the Secretary of the Interior.

9166.s: This order sets aside about 800 acres of federal land and water in Wibaux County, Montana, for the Department of the Interior to use as a refuge and breeding ground for migratory birds and other wildlife. It makes it unlawful for anyone to enter the refuge or to pursue, hunt, trap, capture, disturb, or kill any bird or wild animal there, except under rules set by the Secretary of the Interior.

9165.s: The order directs the Office of Civilian Defense to create and run a program to protect essential facilities from sabotage and other destructive acts. It makes the office the center for coordinating plans, setting security standards, and reviewing security measures. It also assigns several federal departments and agencies to carry out security work for specific kinds of facilities, and says owners, operators, and state and local governments still have primary responsibility to protect those facilities.

9164.s: This order changes a prior order to let the Governor of The Panama Canal raise the pay of alien employees of The Panama Canal or the Panama Railroad Company above $960 a year or 40 cents an hour. It also says those employees cannot get more leave privileges than employees paid at or below that rate. The change stays in effect during the war then underway and for six months after it ends.

9163.s: This order establishes a Women's Army Auxiliary Corps for noncombatant service with the Army of the United States. It says the corps is meant to make the knowledge, skill, and special training of women available to national defense. It also directs the Secretary of War to set up units of the corps, with no more than 100 units and no more than 25,000 total enrollees.

9162.s: This order designates the ports of Guayanilla and Jobos in Puerto Rico as customs ports of entry in Customs Collection District No. 49. It affects customs processing at those ports, with the district headquarters at San Juan, Puerto Rico.

9161.s: This order revokes Executive Order No. 8975 of December 13, 1941. That earlier order had let the Attorney General make appointments in the Alien Property Division of the Department of Justice without following the Civil Service Act and Rules.

9160.s: This order amends a prior order by adding more land in Indiana to land transferred from the Secretary of Agriculture to the Secretary of the Navy. The added land is in the Martin County and White River Land Utilization Projects and was acquired or is being acquired by the United States. The Secretary of Agriculture keeps enough jurisdiction over land still being acquired to complete that process.

9159.s: This order amends an earlier executive order so its rules on submitting estimates to the Bureau of the Budget also apply to several additional U.S. agencies and corporations. Those include Federal Intermediate Credit Banks, Production Credit Corporations, Regional Agricultural Credit Corporations, and several defense and reserve corporations. It also changes when one part of the rule applies to those additional agencies.

9158.s: This order establishes the Air Medal with ribbons for people serving in the Army, Navy, Marine Corps, or Coast Guard after September 8, 1939. It may be awarded to a person who shows meritorious achievement while taking part in an aerial flight. No person may receive more than one Air Medal, but additional achievements may be recognized with a bar or other device. The medal and its ribbons are to be designed and awarded under rules set by the named secretaries.

9157.s: This order sets rules for executive departments and independent agencies to request records, reports, and other information from the Department of Commerce for use in connection with the conduct of the war. The request must be in writing and include details about who will use the information, what is wanted, and how it will be used. The Secretary of Commerce may provide the material and may place conditions on its use, and the requesting agency must pay any extra costs. The information may not be used or shared outside the request or the conditions set by the Secretary.

9156.s: This order expands the Office of Defense Transportation’s authority to cover all rubber-borne transportation facilities, including passenger cars, buses, taxicabs, and trucks. It directs the office to develop programs to match the Nation’s transport needs to the available supply of rubber-based transportation services and to conserve their use. It also lets the office limit use in non-essential civilian activities and regulate how these transportation services are used or distributed among essential activities. Federal departments and agencies that work with rubber-borne transportation must follow the policies and measures the Director sets.

9155.s: This order approves Civil Service Commission regulations for efficiency-rating boards of review. It sets up boards in departments and independent establishments to review employee efficiency ratings and appeals, with members chosen by department heads, employees, and the Civil Service Commission. It also sets rules for written appeals, hearings, decisions, and notice of the results.

9153-A.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in Alaska near Unalaska, Hog Island, Unalaska Island, and Umnak Island from use under the public-land laws, including the mining laws. It reserves those lands for the War Department for military purposes, subject to valid existing rights and some earlier land withdrawals. It also revokes a 1941 order that had reserved part of one of the areas for the War Department.

9154.s: This order excludes certain Executive branch Federal employees from the Civil Service Retirement Act unless they qualify for retirement benefits in another way. It covers employees with brief, periodic, part-time, contract, fee-basis, piece-work, unpaid, temporary, or other listed jobs, including certain alien employees outside the continental United States and some post office workers. The Civil Service Commission is authorized to decide how these exclusions apply in specific cases. The order takes effect as of January 24, 1942, but it does not take away retirement rights already earned before then.

9153.s: This order changes the boundaries of the airspace reservation over part of the City of Washington, D.C. It replaces the earlier boundary description with a new one that traces a specific route around the area. The change affects the airspace within the described boundary.

9152.s: The order directs the Secretary of Commerce to make special census or statistical reports needed for the conduct of the war. It also authorizes the Secretary to skip the 1941 census of manufacturing industries and to stop or reduce other regular census work in the Department of Commerce. The Director of the Bureau of the Budget keeps responsibility for coordinating federal statistical activities.

9151.s: This order transfers certain public land in Pinellas County, Florida, from the Public Buildings Administration, Federal Works Agency, to the War Department. The land is reserved for use as a bombing range and for other military purposes.

9150.s: This order authorizes the Federal Public Housing Commissioner, or a Federal Public Housing Authority officer acting in the Commissioner's place, to acquire, use, and dispose of property needed for war purposes. It applies only to property connected with defense housing and temporary shelter.

9149.s: This order changes the rules for representation allowances under a previous executive order. It says those allowances cannot be used for motor vehicles, club or association dues, or printing or engraving expenses. It also says competitive bidding rules apply to spending charged to those allowances, unless it is impossible to get bids and the reason is fully explained in the account.

9147.s: This order revokes Executive Order No. 2987, which had placed certain land and water areas in Gatun Lake, Canal Zone, under the control of the Secretary of the Navy for use as a naval air station. It returns that land to the control and jurisdiction of the Governor of The Panama Canal.

9146.s: This order lets the Secretary of the Interior sign orders that withdraw or reserve public lands of the United States, and orders that revoke or change those orders. Those orders must first be approved by the Director of the Bureau of the Budget and the Attorney General, and filed and published. If an order affects lands run by another federal department or agency, the Secretary of the Interior must get that department or agency head’s agreement first.

9144.s: This order exempts Herbert H. Evans from compulsory retirement for age for one year. It applies to Evans, who was an assistant superintendent in the Mechanical Division of The Panama Canal.

9148.s: This order transfers the Farm Credit Administration’s functions under the Federal Credit Union Act to the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation. It also transfers related records, property, office equipment, personnel, and some funds to the corporation for those functions. Any transferred personnel found to be more than needed may be moved to other government jobs or separated from service.

9145.s: The order reserves a right-of-way for the Alaska Road Commission to use for the construction, operation, and maintenance of the Palmer-Richardson Highway in Alaska. It sets the right-of-way at 200 feet wide and says it runs for about 145 miles. The reservation applies subject to all valid existing rights.

9143.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in California from all forms of appropriation under the public-land laws, including the mining laws. It reserves the lands for the War Department to establish a Holding and Reconsignment Depot and a Quartermaster Depot. The lands are to be returned to the Department of the Interior when they are no longer needed for those purposes.

9142.s: This order transfers certain authority, powers, property, and personnel from the Department of Justice to the Alien Property Custodian. It also says litigation involving the Alien Property Custodian stays under the supervision of the Attorney General. The order says it does not limit the authority of the Federal Bureau of Investigation.

9140.s: This order transfers certain federal lands in Graham County, Arizona, to the Department of the Interior. It reserves the lands as a refuge and breeding ground for native birds and other wildlife. The reservation will be known as the Safford National Wildlife Refuge.

9139.s: This order creates the War Manpower Commission in the Executive Office of the President. It gives the Commission power to set national policies and coordinate the use, recruitment, training, placement, and allocation of manpower for industry, agriculture, government, and the war effort. It also transfers certain labor supply, personnel roster, procurement, and assignment functions to the Commission, and moves some apprenticeship and training functions to the Federal Security Agency.

9141.s: This order directs the Secretary of the Navy to take possession of and operate Brewster Aeronautical Corporation plants in Long Island City, Newark, and Johnsville. The plants are to be used to produce war materials needed for the company’s contracts with the United States or otherwise required for the war effort. The order also lets the Secretary hire needed employees and use the company’s contractual or other rights as needed. The President will end this possession and operation when he decides the plants can be privately operated in a way consistent with the war effort.

9138.s: This order gives the Chairman of the War Production Board and certain department and agency heads authority under Title VI of the Second War Powers Act, 1942, to requisition property for the war effort. It also revokes a required determination in Executive Order 8942.

9137.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in Arkansas from the public-land laws, including the mining laws. The lands are to be used for the construction of the Norfolk Dam and Reservoir on the North Fork of the White River under the War Department. It also replaces an earlier withdrawal order for any of the same lands.

9135.s: This order creates an interdepartmental committee to set up a uniform plan for buying War Savings Bonds through voluntary pay allotments. It directs departments, establishments, and agencies in the executive branch to put the plan into action as soon as they can. The plan is for civilian officers and employees in the executive branch, and the committee may help with problems and recommend improvements.

9134.s: This order sets up the Office of Civilian Defense inside the Office for Emergency Management and puts it under a director appointed by the President. It also creates a Civilian Defense Board and gives the office a role in coordinating federal civilian defense work with state and local governments. The office is told to help plan civil defense measures, support volunteer service, and assist in protecting people and property against war hazards.

9136.s: This order changes earlier orders that had withdrawn certain lands for townsite purposes in Alaska. It reserves a 120-foot-wide right-of-way for the War Department to build, operate, and maintain a road at Fort Richardson. The reservation is subject to valid existing rights, and the Alaska Railroad and its permittees or lessees may use the road.

9133.s: This order transfers the Civilian Conservation Corps’ motor repair shops, along with their supplies, buildings, facilities, and shop and administrative personnel, to the War Department. It also directs the War Department to make some of those shops and equipment available to other government agencies working on projects the War Department deems of military importance and urgency. The War Department is also directed to repair and maintain the Civilian Conservation Corps’ vehicles and other heavy equipment, and may repair other federal equipment, with reimbursement for the cost.

9132.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in Montana from appropriation and use under the public-land laws, including the mining laws. It reserves those lands for the War Department to use for the construction and operation of the Fort Peck Dam and Reservoir project. Some of the affected lands stay under the Secretary of the Interior for wildlife and grazing purposes, as long as that does not interfere with the project.

9131.s: This order exempts Leo A. McIntire from compulsory retirement for age for one year. It lets him stay in his job as Chief, Civil Intelligence, Executive Division, The Panama Canal, until April 30, 1943.

9130.s: This order withdraws about 280 acres of public land in Randolph County, Arkansas, from the public-land laws, including the mining laws. The land is reserved under the Department of the Interior for use by the Arkansas Game and Fish Commission in connection with the Randolph County State Game Refuge. It also replaces an earlier temporary withdrawal for the lands covered by this order.

9129.s: This order lets the United States Maritime Commission acquire, use, and dispose of real property, temporary use of property, other interests in property, and personal property on or used with it. It applies to property the Commission decides is needed for military, naval, or other war purposes.

9128.s: This order gives the Board of Economic Warfare new duties over imported materials and commodities needed for the war production effort and the civilian economy. It also lets the board help set up and finance corporations to get foreign supplies needed for the war, advise on lend-lease agreements, and arrange reciprocal aid from other countries. The board is also given a role in representing the United States with economic warfare agencies of the United Nations and may send technical, engineering, and economic representatives abroad.

9126.s: This order transfers the duties and functions of the Hydrographic Office and the Naval Observatory from the Bureau of Navigation to the Chief of Naval Operations, under the direction of the Secretary of the Navy. It also transfers all personnel, records, and public property in those offices to the Office of Chief of Naval Operations.

9127.s: This order names several government agencies that can inspect plants and audit the books and records of defense contractors and some subcontractors under Title XIII of the Second War Powers Act, 1942. It also lets the Chairman of the War Production Board set rules to coordinate those agencies. Inspections and audits of certain secret or restricted defense work must be handled as secret, confidential, or restricted.

9125.s: This order gives the Chairman of the War Production Board added powers under the Second War Powers Act of 1942. It also lets the Chairman use the Office of Price Administration to carry out priorities and rationing work, and lets the Price Administrator delegate some of that work to others. The order keeps certain earlier directives and orders in force and allows civil proceedings over violations of priorities or rationing rules.

9124.s: This order transfers certain national-forest lands in Idaho and Utah from the Cache National Forest to the Caribou National Forest. It says the order does not give national-forest status to any public lands that did not already have it, and does not remove any public lands from national-forest status.

9122.s: This order changes the rules for paying to move household goods and personal effects for certain civilian federal officers and employees when they are transferred. It says shipments should use the most economical means, but an employee may choose another method by paying the difference, and some items needed right away may be sent by express if approved. It also says shipments should use a Government bill of lading or purchase order when possible, allows shipment from a previous place of residence in some cases, and sets time limits for when shipments must begin.

9123.s: The order directs the Treasury Department’s Procurement Division to use quartz crystals it has acquired. It may sell or otherwise dispose of quartz crystals suitable for piezo-electric use for war production purposes. The buyers or users and the amounts must be requested by the Chairman of the War Production Board.

9121.s: This order transfers certain lands in Williamson County, Illinois, from the Secretary of Agriculture to the Secretary of War for national defense purposes. The lands are part of the Crab Orchard Land Utilization Project. The Secretary of Agriculture keeps whatever jurisdiction is needed to finish acquiring lands still in process of acquisition.

9120.s: This order revokes Executive Order No. 1023, which had reserved certain land near Rampart, Alaska, for an agricultural experiment station. It affects that land reservation and takes effect 90 days after the date of the order.

9119.s: This order adds about 40 acres in Wakulla County, Florida, to the St. Marks National Wildlife Refuge. It withdraws those lands from public-land and mining laws and sets them aside for the Department of the Interior, subject to valid existing rights. The order says this area becomes part of the refuge and replaces an earlier temporary withdrawal for those lands.

9118.s: This order exempts Harry L. Mickey, a messenger in The White House Office, from compulsory retirement for age for one more year. The exemption lasts until April 30, 1943.

9116.s: This order extends parts of Executive Order No. 9001 to contracts made by several federal agencies. It lets those agencies and certain officials use the powers given under that earlier order for contracts tied to the prosecution of the war effort. It also allows the Federal Communications Commission to enter some contracts without prior advertising for bids, under the same regulations.

9115.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in New Mexico from appropriation under the public-land laws, including the mining laws. It reserves those lands for use by the Department of State in connection with the Rio Grande Canalization Project, subject to valid existing rights. The land withdrawn covers 623.90 acres.

9117.s: This order sets rules for overtime pay for certain per-annum field service employees of the National Advisory Committee for Aeronautics. It allows extra pay for work over forty hours in an administrative workweek when their overtime is essential to the national-defense program, and it says overtime should be kept to a minimum and may not be required if it would harm an employee's health or efficiency.

9114.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in Alaska from the public-land laws, including the mining laws, and reserves them for the War Department for military purposes. It covers two tracts of land described in the order, subject to valid existing rights. It also revokes part of a 1925 proclamation that added some of Tract 2 to the Tongass National Forest.

9113.s: This order transfers the vessels Oceanographer and Hydrographer, and several Coast and Geodetic Survey officers, to the Navy Department and the War Department. While under those departments, the officers keep serving under their Coast and Geodetic Survey commissions and become part of the active military or naval forces of the United States. The vessels and officers are to be returned to the Coast and Geodetic Survey when the present national emergency ends.

9111.s: This order changes the Committee on Fair Employment Practice. It says the committee will have a chairman and six other members.

9112.s: This order lets the War Department, the Navy Department, and the Maritime Commission make or guarantee loans, discounts, advances, and related commitments to help finance war production. It also lets them use Federal Reserve Banks and other financing institutions to carry out those contracts and move funds to contractors, subcontractors, and others involved in work needed for the war. The Secretary of the Treasury is directed to name each Federal Reserve Bank as fiscal agent for this work, and the agencies must report the contracts they make.

9110.s: This order enlarges the Fort Gulick Military Reservation in the Canal Zone by adding a new tract of land to the main reservation. The added area contains 8.64 acres. It affects the military reservation’s boundary and land area.

9109.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in New Mexico from all forms of appropriation under the public-land laws, including the mining laws. It reserves those lands for the use of the War Department for military purposes. It also revokes part of a 1934 order as it affects one section, and says the lands will be returned to the Department of the Interior when they are no longer needed.

9108.s: The order directs the Director of the Office of Defense Transportation to take over the Toledo, Peoria and Western Railroad Company and operate it for the war effort. It also allows the Director to return property he does not need and to manage the railroad under terms he thinks are proper while the labor dispute is unresolved. The takeover lasts only until the President decides it is no longer needed.

9107.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in California from the public-land laws, including the mining laws, and reserves them for the War Department for military purposes. The lands are subject to valid existing rights. When the lands are no longer needed for that purpose, they are intended to return to the Department of the Interior.

9106.s: This order lets the Attorney General certify certain alien enemies as loyal to the United States after an investigation. People so certified are excepted from the classification "alien enemy" and may apply for naturalization. It affects alien enemies who are found loyal under this process.

9105.s: This order changes rules for advance payments of allowances for quarters and subsistence for enlisted men in the Army, Navy, Marine Corps, Coast Guard, Coast and Geodetic Survey, and Public Health Service who are not given quarters or rations in kind. It says these payments may be made up to one month in advance. For men going to or from a station beyond the continental United States or in Alaska, the payments may be made up to three months in advance.

9103.s: This order puts the Director of the Bureau of the Budget in charge of watching government publication of statistical data and deciding whether it can be published under wartime policy. It also allows some statistical data that is usually public to be given to authorized Federal agency users under rules set by the Director, but not munitions data marked "secret" by the War or Navy Departments or the War Production Board.

9104.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in Arizona from all forms of land entry, including the mining laws, and reserves them for the War Department as an aerial gunnery range. The lands described include both public and nonpublic lands and total 45,168.09 acres. The order says the lands should be returned to the Department of the Interior when they are no longer needed for that use.

9102.s: This order creates the War Relocation Authority in the Executive Office of the President and puts it under a director who answers to the President. The Authority is directed to carry out the removal of persons from designated areas and to handle their relocation, maintenance, and supervision. It also sets up a work corps for persons removed under this order or Executive Order No. 9066 and requires federal agencies to cooperate with the Director.

9100.s: This order exempts August Thomas, a chief engineer in the Marine Division of The Panama Canal, from compulsory retirement for age. It lets him stay in service for one year, through July 31, 1943.

9101.s: This order temporarily withdraws certain public lands in California from settlement, location, sale, or entry, subject to valid existing rights. The land is described by section and township information and includes about 163.64 acres. It replaces an earlier withdrawal order for the same land.

9099.s: This order removes a described tract of land in Michigan from the Manistee National Forest. It affects Sections 2 and 3, and the east half of Section 4, in Township 20 North, Range 12 West of the Michigan Meridian.

9096.s: This order lets one officer hold both the jobs of Commander in Chief, United States Fleet, and Chief of Naval Operations. It gives that officer command over the Navy’s operating forces and makes the officer the main naval adviser to the President and the Secretary of the Navy. It also sets up staff positions for both roles and says who acts in those jobs if the officer is absent. It also sets the order of succession to act as Secretary of the Navy when those officials are temporarily absent.

9097.s: This order revokes parts of two earlier executive orders that created Power Site Reserve No. 348 and Power Site Reserve No. 563 in Wyoming. It applies only to the specific lands listed in the order under the Sixth Principal Meridian.

9094.s: This order abolishes the Federal Board of Surveys and Maps. It gives the Director of the Bureau of the Budget the Board’s functions and lets the Director ask department and agency heads for information needed to carry out the order.

9093.s: This order certifies the Island of Puerto Rico as a distressed emergency area. That lets the Governor of the Farm Credit Administration make farm loans there without following the usual $400 loan limits, under rules, maturities, and amounts he sets. It affects borrowers in Puerto Rico during the stated period.

9095.s: This order creates the Office of Alien Property Custodian in the Executive Office of the President and puts an Alien Property Custodian in charge. It gives that official powers under the Trading with the Enemy Act and the First War Powers Act, and it says property or interests in property of a foreign country or a national of a foreign country may vest in the Custodian when he directs. It also says existing orders, proclamations, regulations, rulings, licenses, or instructions under those powers stay in effect unless the Custodian changes or revokes them.

9092.s: This order designates the Honorable A. Cecil Snyder to perform the duties of Judge of the District Court of the United States for Puerto Rico. He may sign needed papers and records as Acting Judge without extra compensation during the judge’s absence, illness, or other legal disability during the current calendar year.

9091.s: This order transfers jurisdiction over about 81,049 acres of land in Beltrami, Lake of the Woods, and Roseau Counties, Minnesota, to the Department of the Interior. It reserves the lands as a refuge and breeding ground for native birds and other wildlife, and for research on wildlife and related forest resources. The lands may still be used and managed by the State of Minnesota under a cooperative and license agreement, and the Secretary of Agriculture keeps needed jurisdiction over land still being acquired.

9089.s: This order lets the Defense Communications Board carry out the President’s authority over wire communication facilities during the war. It allows the Board to plan how government and private wire facilities are used, and to designate certain facilities for use, control, supervision, inspection, or closure by the War Department, Navy Department, or another U.S. agency. It also says wire communication businesses should keep operating in the usual course unless the Board orders otherwise, and that just compensation must be set for any use or control of their facilities.

9090.s: This order sets aside the airspace over parts of Ulster and Dutchess Counties, New York, for national defense, other governmental purposes, and public safety. No person may fly a civil aircraft in that airspace without special permission from the Administrator of Civil Aeronautics. Anyone who violates the order can face penalties under the Civil Aeronautics Act of 1938.

9088.s: This order sets rules for how the Office of Civilian Defense and the War Department will handle civilian defense supplies and services. It says funds may be used for facilities, equipment, supplies, research, inspection, shipping, storage, maintenance, and administration to protect people and property from bombing attacks, sabotage, and other war hazards. It also lets the Office accept equipment or supplies from other federal agencies, state and local governments, and private sources, and share them with local civil authorities for loan and use under its rules.

9086.s: The order withdraws certain public lands in Nevada from the public-land laws, including the mining laws. It reserves those lands for use by the War Department as a general bombing range, subject to valid existing rights. It says the lands should be returned to the Department of the Interior when they are no longer needed for that purpose.

9087.s: This order transfers jurisdiction over certain lands in California, as to oil and gas deposits, from the War Department to the Department of the Interior. The Secretary of the Interior is directed to take action needed to protect the United States from loss from drainage or threatened drainage of oil and gas from those lands. The War Department keeps primary jurisdiction over the lands for flood control and navigation, and royalties from oil and gas are to be paid into the Treasury.

9085.s: This order withdraws and reserves a piece of public land in Alaska, subject to valid existing rights. It sets the land aside for the Alaskan Fire Control Service to use as a patrol station site.

9084.s: This order amends an earlier executive order on budgetary administration and financial reporting. It changes one word in section 6(b) from "accounting" to "reporting." It also adds a rule that proposed uniform terminology, classifications, principles, and standards must be referred to the Comptroller General for review before they are established.

9083.s: This order moves many maritime and shipping functions from the Bureau of Marine Inspection and Navigation and the Secretary of Commerce to the Bureau of Customs and the U.S. Coast Guard.
