It also transfers some training duties from the United States Maritime Commission to the Coast Guard, along with related records, property, personnel, and funds. The order changes who handles vessel registration, inspections, licensing, safety rules, marine casualty investigations, and related enforcement duties.

9082.s: This order reorganizes the Army of the United States into ground forces, air forces, and a services of supply command, along with other commands the Secretary of War may find necessary for national security. It transfers the duties and powers of several Army branch chiefs to these new commands, including Infantry, Cavalry, Field Artillery, Coast Artillery Corps, the Air Corps, and General Headquarters Air Force. It also lets the Secretary of War issue instructions on personnel, funds, records, property, and correspondence, while the President keeps direct control over strategy, tactics, and operations.

9081.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in Arizona from all forms of appropriation under the public-land laws, including the mining laws. It reserves the land for use by the War Department for aviation purposes, subject to valid existing rights. The lands are intended to return to the Department of the Interior when they are no longer needed for that purpose.

9080.s: The order creates a joint Mexican-United States Defense Commission for the United States and Mexico. The commission is to study common defense problems, consider defense plans for Mexico and nearby areas of the United States, and propose cooperative measures to both governments. It also sets out United States members, allows the commission to set its own procedure and hire assistants, and says U.S. expenses will be paid from funds allocated to the War Department.

9078.s: This order creates the Army Specialist Corps in the War Department as a corps of uniformed civilian employees. It lets the Secretary of War appoint, assign, promote, regulate, and discharge members, and sets their pay under existing law. The Civil Service Commission recruits for the Corps, and people appointed do not get classified civil-service status. Some government employees may transfer into the Corps and, after leaving, may be restored to their old job or one like it with no loss of seniority, retirement, or other benefits.

9077.s: This order exempts Gustave R. A. Elmgren, a foreman (carpenter) in the Building Division of the Supply Department at The Panama Canal, from compulsory retirement for age. The exemption lasts for one year, ending February 28, 1943.

9076.s: This order lets the Office of Price Administration inspect corporation statistical transcript cards prepared by the Bureau of Internal Revenue from certain corporation income and declared-value excess-profits tax returns. The cards covered are from tax years beginning after June 30, 1935, and ending before July 1, 1941. The inspection must follow rules set by the Secretary of the Treasury.

9075.s: The order directs the Secretary of War to issue citations in the President’s name to certain Army organizations, units, detachments, or installations for outstanding performance in action on or after December 7, 1941. It also allows them to display a streamer, emblem, or guidon band chosen by the Secretary of War. If the same unit is cited two or more times, a device showing those citations must be issued for officers and enlisted men assigned to that unit, and some individuals may wear it on their uniforms.

9074.s: This order makes the Secretary of the Navy mainly responsible for protecting vessels, harbors, ports, and waterfront facilities from sabotage, other subversive acts, accidents, or similar causes. It applies in the United States, Alaska, Hawaii, Puerto Rico, and the Virgin Islands, except for waterfront facilities directly run by the War Department. All federal agencies must follow the Navy Secretary’s regulations and orders and help as they can, and state and local authorities and all persons are urged to assist.

9072.s: This order transfers three vessels from the Coast and Geodetic Survey to the Navy Department. It also transfers named commissioned officers from the Coast and Geodetic Survey to the Navy Department and the War Department. While under those departments, the officers serve under their Coast and Geodetic Survey commissions and are subject to Army or Navy rules as applicable. The vessels and officers are to be returned to the Coast and Geodetic Survey when the present national emergency ends.

9073.s: This order extends the customs port of entry of Detroit, Michigan, in Customs Collection District Number 38. It adds the listed municipalities and townships in Michigan to that port of entry.

9071.s: This order transfers the remaining functions, powers, and duties of the Federal Loan Agency to the Department of Commerce. It covers work related to several named agencies and corporations, and it also transfers the agency’s records, property, personnel, and some funds to Commerce. The Secretary of Commerce will supervise these functions.

9070.s: This order consolidates several housing agencies, functions, and duties into a new National Housing Agency under a National Housing Administrator. It moves work from agencies including the Federal Housing Administration, Federal Home Loan Bank Board, Home Owners' Loan Corporation, Federal Savings and Loan Insurance Corporation, United States Housing Authority, Defense Homes Corporation, and other defense housing functions. It also transfers some property, funds, and personnel, abolishes the Central Housing Committee, and changes jurisdiction over housing on military or naval reservations to the War or Navy Department.

9069.s: This order consolidates several Agriculture Department agencies and their functions, staff, property, and records into new agencies under the Secretary of Agriculture’s direction. It also moves the Agricultural Statistics Division to the Bureau of Agricultural Economics and combines the department’s library and bibliographical services. The order says these changes remain in force during the war and for six months after it ends.

9068.s: This order revokes a 1934 order that had withdrawn certain public lands in Wyoming pending a resurvey. It applies only to the listed townships and becomes effective when the official plats of the resurvey are filed.

9067.s: This order sets up a system to move federal employees to war agencies based on priority classifications tied to the war program. The Civil Service Commission may transfer employees it finds competent for essential war work, but only with the employee’s consent, and transfers to same or lower priority departments also need the consent of the current department or agency. It also gives transferred employees the reemployment benefits provided by a prior order and lets the Civil Service Commission make rules to carry out the order.

9066.s: The order authorizes the Secretary of War and military commanders to set up military areas and exclude any or all persons from them. It also lets them restrict who may enter, stay in, or leave those areas, and provide transportation, food, shelter, and other help to excluded residents. Other federal agencies are directed to assist in carrying out the order.

9065.s: This order changes the rules for highways, vehicles, and vehicular traffic in the Canal Zone. It gives the Governor authority to make, change, and update rules and regulations to carry out the order. In time of war, or when war is believed to be imminent, the Governor may also amend, modify, supplement, or suspend the order for that period if judged necessary in the public interest.

9064.s: This order lets the Governor of the Panama Canal provide free transportation, or reimburse travel costs, for people hired to work on the Isthmus of Panama. It also allows a subsistence allowance of up to six dollars a day while they travel and wait for transportation. The Governor may make rules to carry out the order.

9063.s: The order authorizes the United States Civil Service Commission to adopt special procedures for recruiting, placing, and changing the status of personnel in federal agencies, except for postal field service positions. It applies to positions covered by the Civil Service Act and Rules. People appointed only under these special procedures do not get classified civil service status, but the Commission may keep them for the duration of the war and for six months after.

9062.s: This order exempts Michael Conley, a senior master in the Marine Division at The Panama Canal, from compulsory retirement for age. It lets him stay in service for one more year, ending February 28, 1943.

9060.s: This order adds the listed lands in Oregon to the Fremont National Forest. It says the lands are mainly valuable for timber and will be managed by the Forest Service. The lands are subject to all laws relating to national forests, along with valid existing rights and existing power and reclamation withdrawals.

9059.s: This order excludes certain tracts of land in Alaska from the Chugach and Tongass National Forests and restores them to entry under the public-land laws. The tracts are listed as homesites in the order, and the changes affect land in both forests.

9058.s: This order extends the rules of Executive Order 9001 to the Tennessee Valley Authority for all contracts it makes or will make. It also lets the TVA Board of Directors, and officers or employees it designates, carry out the powers given under that earlier order to the Secretary of War, the Secretary of the Navy, and the Chairman of the United States Maritime Commission.

9061.s: This order places certain lands now within the Fremont National Forest in Oregon under the administration of the Department of the Interior. The lands are described as mainly valuable for grazing and are made subject to public-land laws and regulations for grazing districts under the Taylor Grazing Act. It affects the listed parcels of land in Oregon.

9057.s: This order changes the list of basic exchange rates used to pay certain losses to U.S. officers, enlisted men, and employees in foreign countries when foreign currencies rise against the dollar. It removes the Netherlands (Possessions) listing and replaces it with the Netherlands Indies, Netherlands West Indies, and Surinam, each with a florin rate of 40.19. It also supersedes a prior executive order.

9056.s: This order exempts August G. Ahlfont, the chief engineer of the Dredging Division of the Panama Canal, from compulsory retirement for age. It lets him stay in service for one more year, ending March 31, 1943.

9055.s: This order extends the rules in Executive Order 9001 to the Department of the Interior for all contracts made or to be made by that department. It also lets the Secretary of the Interior, and any officers, employees, and agencies he names, carry out the same powers and duties given under that earlier order.

9054.s: This order sets up a War Shipping Administration in the Executive Office of the President and places it under an Administrator who reports to the President. The Administrator is given control over many United States ocean vessels, can allocate them to the Army, Navy, other federal agencies, and the Governments of the United Nations, and can provide marine insurance and reinsurance for war risks. The order also transfers shipping-related powers, personnel, records, property, and funds from the United States Maritime Commission to the new administration.

9053.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in Utah, subject to valid existing rights, from all forms of use under the public-land laws, including the mining laws. It reserves those lands for the War Department to use as a chemical warfare range. It also says the lands are intended to go back to the Department of the Interior when they are no longer needed for that purpose.

9052.s: This order amends the Civil Service Rules by adding the Solicitor of the Department of the Interior to Schedule A. It affects that Department position by placing it in the listed exempt category.

9051.s: This order changes a previous executive order about administering benefits under an act of Congress approved April 3, 1939. It says the Secretary of War, or someone he designates in the War Department, will handle the administration of certain death gratuity benefits. Those benefits apply to dependents of officers, warrant officers, and enlisted men of the Army of the United States who die in line of duty while in active military service.

9050.s: The order directs the Secretary of the Navy to issue presidential citations to certain Navy and Marine Corps units for outstanding performance in action. It applies to ships, aircraft, detachments, and other higher units that met that standard on or after October 16, 1941. It also allows approved insignia to be displayed by those units, and after two or more citations, the insignia becomes part of the unit uniform and may be worn by certain members and former members.

9049.s: This order puts the organizations, units, and personnel of the Organized Reserves into active military service of the United States, unless they are already in such service. It applies for the duration of the present war and for six months after it ends, unless they are relieved or discharged earlier.

9047.s: This order exempts certain officers and employees in the Executive branch from automatic separation from service. Those appointed by the President are exempted for as long as their appointment or term lasts. Other Executive branch officers and employees who reach the retirement age before April 1, 1942, are exempted until April 30, 1942, though the head of the department or agency may require their retirement sooner.

9048.s: This order suspends the punishment limits in the Army manual for future violations of Articles of War 58, 59, and 86. Those articles cover desertion, helping or advising another to desert, and misbehavior of sentinels. It applies to offenses committed after the order and stays in effect until further order.

9046.s: This order changes a 1941 executive order about foreign merchant vessels. It allows the United States Maritime Commission to document any or all of those vessels under United States law or the law of another country in the Western Hemisphere. It applies to the vessels covered by the earlier order.

9044.s: This order exempts William A. Holt, an Internal Revenue Agent in the Treasury Department, from compulsory retirement for age for one year. It applies only to him and ends on January 31, 1943.

9045.s: This order exempts Richard J. Barrett, a general foreman in the Municipal Engineering Division of The Panama Canal, from compulsory retirement for age. The exemption lasts for one year and ends on January 31, 1943.

9043.s: This executive order exempts Edward F. Ruggles, a highway engineer with the Public Roads Administration, from compulsory retirement for age. It lets him stay in federal service for one more year, ending January 31, 1943.

9041.s: This order sets the grades and ratings for enlisted men of the Army of the United States in active Federal service. It limits how many enlisted men may be in each grade and in each specialists' rating, using maximum percentages. It also says that when enlisted men hold specialists' ratings, the authorized maximum numbers in the first six grades will be reduced by the same cost. The order revokes a prior executive order on these grades and ratings.

9042.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in Oregon from all forms of appropriation under the public land laws, including the mining laws. It reserves the lands for the War Department for aviation purposes, subject to valid existing rights. The order also says the lands should be returned to the Department of the Interior when they are no longer needed for that purpose.

9039.s: This order authorizes the Governor of The Panama Canal to grant sick and rest leave to alien employees of The Panama Canal and the Panama Railroad Company who are not already entitled to leave under certain employment rules. It limits that leave to no more than 15 days in any one year and says unused leave cannot build up beyond 60 days. The order also revokes a 1918 order that had authorized sick leave for these alien employees.

9040.s: This order gives the Chairman of the War Production Board the powers and duties that were held by the Office of Production Management and the Supply Priorities and Allocations Board. It also lets the Chairman carry out other powers through officials or agencies, and says his decisions are final. The Office of Production Management is abolished, and its personnel, records, property, and funds are moved to the War Production Board.

9038.s: This order amends a prior order to allow the appointment of associate members of the National War Labor Board. These associate members may act as mediators in labor disputes when directed by the Board. They also receive compensation and expenses in the same way as regular Board members.

9037.s: This order gives Clarence E. Ingling, Chief of Files in the White House Office, another one-year exemption from compulsory retirement for age. It affects him only and extends the exemption through April 30, 1943.

9036.s: The order reserves a tract of land in the Wenatchee National Forest in Washington for use by the Department of Commerce as a beacon site. It applies to the described 41.60-acre parcel after the Northern Pacific Railway Company released its claim to the land.

9035.s: This order withdraws and reserves 160 acres of public land in Alaska for use by the Alaska Road Commission. The land is to be used as a site for a supply base and repair shop connected to the construction and maintenance of the Palmer-Richardson highway.

9034.s: This order exempts Thomas A. Haigh, a senior engineering draftsman in the General Land Office, from compulsory retirement for age. It lets him stay in service for one year, ending February 28, 1943.

9032.s: This order exempts Lawrence V. Bateman, a chief lithographer in the Geological Survey at the Department of the Interior, from compulsory retirement for age. It lets him stay in service for one more year, ending January 31, 1943.

9031.s: This order exempts Edgar M. Cohee, a chief office clerk in the Treasury Department in Los Angeles, from compulsory retirement for age for one more year. It extends his earlier exemption through April 30, 1943.

9033.s: This order exempts Abraham Straus, an examiner of merchandise in the United States Customs Service, from compulsory retirement for age. The exemption lasts for one year and ends on January 31, 1943.

9030.s: This order exempts Walter C. Mendenhall, the Director of the Geological Survey in the Department of the Interior, from compulsory retirement for age for one more year. It extends that exemption through February 28, 1943.

9029.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in New Mexico from appropriation under the public-land laws, including the mining laws, and reserves them for use by the War Department as a general bombing range. It covers both public and non-public lands, subject to valid existing rights, and says the order takes precedence over two earlier land orders for the affected areas. The local army commandant must consult with representatives of the Department of the Interior about bombtarget sites, and the lands are intended to be returned to the Department of the Interior when they are no longer needed.

9027.s: This executive order amends the Civil Service Rules by adding a third paragraph to Subdivision XL of Schedule A. The new paragraph adds one general counsel.

9028.s: The order revokes an earlier withdrawal for a 10-acre tract of public land in California. It then temporarily withdraws that land from settlement, location, sale, or entry and sets it aside for a lookout station site for Federal and State cooperative forest-protection work. The reservation is subject to valid existing rights and to use for oil and gas development and related purposes.

9025.s: This order allows George Howe to be appointed as Supervising Architect in the Public Buildings Administration, Federal Works Agency. It says the appointment can be made without following the Civil Service Rules.

9026.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in Alaska from all forms of appropriation under the public-land laws, including the mining laws. It reserves the land for use by the War Department as a cantonment site, subject to valid existing rights. It also says this order takes precedence over an earlier order for some of the same lands, but does not revoke it.

9023.s: This order extends the rules of Executive Order 9001 to contracts made or to be made by the Treasury Department, the Department of Agriculture, The Panama Canal, the Federal Works Agency, the Government Printing Office, the National Advisory Committee for Aeronautics, and any other agencies later designated. It also authorizes the named agency heads, and people they designate, to carry out the functions and powers given under that earlier order, subject to its limits and regulations.

9024.s: The order creates a War Production Board in the Executive Office of the President to handle war procurement and production. It gives the chairman control over policies, plans, and methods for federal departments and agencies on war purchasing, contracting, construction, conversion, requisitioning, plant expansion, and financing. Federal departments must follow the chairman’s policies, and the Supply Priorities and Allocations Board is abolished and its personnel, records, and property are transferred to the new board.

9022.s: This order revokes part of a 1935 order that had temporarily withdrawn certain public lands in Alaska from the public-land laws. It applies to the listed tracts in the Seward Meridian and is meant to validate homestead entry No. 08352 for Lannah Z. Scott.

9020.s: This order transfers full control of the airport near Tonopah, Nevada, to the Secretary of War for military purposes. It affects the airport land now leased to the Board of County Commissioners of Nye County, Nevada, and says the transfer lasts until otherwise ordered.

9021.s: This order changes earlier orders that had withdrawn certain public lands in Wyoming so they can be leased for use as a public airport. It applies to 880 acres in the listed land sections in Wyoming. It does not open all of the withdrawn lands, only the described parcels.

9018.s: This order suspends parts of the Act of March 3, 1931 for the War and Navy Departments, the Coast Guard, and their field services during the existing national emergency. It says the hours of employment for civil personnel in those agencies will follow regulations set by the Secretary of War and the Secretary of the Navy. Rules for employees in the District of Columbia must be coordinated and approved by the Director of the Bureau of the Budget.

9017.s: This order creates the National War Labor Board in the Office for Emergency Management. The Board is made up of commissioners representing the public, employees, and employers, and it is meant to help settle labor disputes by peaceful means during the war. It does not apply where other dispute procedures already exist, and it does not override several listed labor laws.

9019.s: This order revokes part of a prior Nevada land reservation and keeps other land reserved for the War Department. It sets aside public land for a general bombing range and an aerial machine-gun range, and it withdraws some land from the public-land laws, including the mining laws. It also says valid existing rights stay in place and that the land should be returned to the Department of the Interior when it is no longer needed.

9016.s: This order exempts Henry L. Schmidt, a senior power plant operative at the Government Printing Office, from compulsory retirement for age for one more year. It extends his earlier exemption until January 31, 1943.

9015.s: This order exempts Charles Gregg, Chief of the Specification Division in the Office of the Municipal Architect of the Government of the District of Columbia, from compulsory retirement for age for one year. It applies only to him and delays his automatic separation from service until June 30, 1943.

9014.s: This order withdraws a specific 160-acre piece of public land in Washington from the public-land laws, including the mining laws. It reserves the land for the War Department to use for aviation purposes, subject to valid existing rights. If the land is no longer needed for that purpose, it must be returned to the Department of the Interior.

9013.s: This order waives the physical requirements for civil service entrance examinations for Walter M. Brucher. It lets him take the competitive civil service examination for Postmaster at Faribault, Minnesota. The order applies to that one examination for which he applied before the closing date.

9012.s: This order tells the Secretary of the Navy to give back possession of the plant of The Federal Shipbuilding & Dry Dock Company. It says the plant had been taken over to produce vessels, facilities, material, and equipment for the United States or as needed. The order says the plant will be privately operated in a way that is consistent with the needs of national defense.

9011.s: This order sets rules for how funds appropriated for the Army of the Philippines are spent and recorded. It applies to disbursing officers of the Army of the United States and the Army of the Philippines, and it covers advances or reimbursements made to the Government of the Commonwealth of the Philippines. It also says some expenditures need the approval or authority of the Commanding General, United States Army Forces in the Far East, and sets how the accounts will be handled.

9009.s: This order further exempts Maurice A. Emerson from compulsory retirement for age for one year. It applies to Emerson, who was Chief of the Division of Paper Custody in the Bureau of the Public Debt at the Treasury Department.

9010.s: This order exempts John W. Mays, a messenger in The White House Office, from compulsory retirement for age for one year. It applies only to him and lasts until January 31, 1943.

9008.s: This order changes a prior order about appointing state employment security personnel to jobs in the Social Security Board. It says certain positions used by the Federal Security Agency for employment office facilities and services are excluded from the Classification Act until the Federal Security Administrator decides they should be classified under it. It also says people appointed to those jobs may, after a six-month probationary period, gain competitive classified civil-service status in the federal service, subject to Civil Service Commission rules.

9007.s: This order transfers several named commissioned officers from the Coast and Geodetic Survey to the service and jurisdiction of the Navy Department. While serving, they are part of the naval forces of the United States and are subject to Navy laws, regulations, and orders. They are to be returned to the Coast and Geodetic Survey when the present national emergency ends.

9005.s: This order lets certain government employees who were paid with funds for administrative expenses tied to Work Projects Administration projects be promoted, transferred, or assigned to other government positions that must be filled under Civil Service Rules. It also allows those employees to gain competitive classified civil-service status under the law named in the order.

9006.s: The order certifies the Territory of Hawaii as a distressed emergency area. This lets the Governor of the Farm Credit Administration make loans there without the usual $400 loan limit. It affects borrowers in Hawaii under the farm loan law.

9004.s: This order changes the Civil Service Rules to list many federal jobs that are excepted from competitive examination. It covers certain positions in the State, Treasury, War, Navy, Justice, Post Office, and Interior Departments, along with some jobs in foreign countries, Alaska, Panama, Puerto Rico, and the Philippines. It also includes some temporary, part-time, intermittent, and confidential jobs.

9003.s: This order exempts Joseph Tombrink, an assistant engineman in the Public Buildings Administration, from compulsory retirement for age. The exemption lasts for one year and ends on December 31, 1942.

9002.s: This order further exempts Frank Burke, an agent in the Secret Service Division of the Treasury Department, from compulsory retirement for age. The exemption lasts for one year and ends on December 31, 1942.

9001-A.s: This order lets the United States Maritime Commission agree to resell the S.S. Normandie to its former owners or their successors. It also allows the ship to be returned after the present emergency has ended and the Commission decides the United States no longer needs it. The order affects the Commission and the former owners of the ship.

9000.s: This order withdraws a parcel of public land in Oregon from the public-land laws, including the mining laws, and reserves it for the War Department for military purposes. It is subject to valid existing rights and to Oregon Grazing District No. 7. After the national emergency ends, the order will stop if the Secretary of the Interior says the land is needed for grazing or other uses by the Department of the Interior.

8999.s: This order withdraws a parcel of public land in Oregon from appropriation under the public-land laws, including the mining laws. It reserves the land for the War Department to use for military purposes, subject to valid existing rights. It also says the order is subject to Oregon Grazing District No. 7 and will end after the national emergency when the Secretary of the Interior says the land is needed for grazing or other uses.

8997.s: This order exempts certain field service employees of the Post Office Department from compulsory retirement for age. It applies to employees who would reach the retirement age in December 1941 because they turn 62 or 65. The exemption lasts for one year, ending December 31, 1942.

8996.s: This order exempts Alvin M. Rankin, a blacksmith-ironworker in the Marine Division of The Panama Canal, from compulsory retirement for age. The exemption lasts for one year, ending December 31, 1942.

9001.s: This order gives the War Department, the Navy Department, and the United States Maritime Commission power to make and change contracts and make advance or progress payments for things and services needed for the war effort. It says these agencies may work to convert manufacturing industries to war production, survey industrial war potential, spread war orders, and conserve strategic materials. It also requires reports to the President, bars discrimination based on race, creed, color, or national origin, and says certain labor laws still apply to contracts made under the order.

8994.s: This order exempts Frank Shoenfield, a division superintendent in the Railway Mail Service, from compulsory retirement for age. It lets him stay in service for one more year, through December 31, 1942.

8995.s: This order further exempts Miss Roberta L. Lindsey, an administrative officer in the Treasury Department’s Bureau of the Public Debt, from compulsory retirement for age. The exemption lasts for one more year, ending December 31, 1942.

8992.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in Washington from all forms of appropriation under the public-land laws, including the mining laws. It reserves those lands for the War Department to use as a practice bombing range, subject to valid existing rights. It also says this order takes precedence over Executive Order No. 6964 for those lands, but does not rescind or revoke that earlier order.

8991.s: This order tells the Secretary of Commerce to control civil weather reports and forecasts so they meet the needs of the Secretary of War and the Secretary of the Navy for the war effort. It also directs the Commerce Department to coordinate civil meteorological services for the Army, Navy, and other defense activities, and not share information that could be considered valuable to the enemy. The Chief of the Weather Bureau is named as the liaison between Commerce, War, and the Navy.

8993.s: This order exempts Victor H. Boyden, an assistant attorney in the Department of Agriculture, from compulsory retirement for age. It lets him stay in service for one more year, ending December 31, 1942.

8988.s: The order says commissioned officers of the Public Health Service who are detailed to duty on Coast Guard vessels and with other Coast Guard units must stay on those details until relieved by proper authority. While serving in those assignments, they are to be part of the naval forces of the United States and subject to the orders of the Secretary of the Navy.

8990.s: This order lets certain state or territorial employment security agency workers be appointed to jobs in the Social Security Board of the Federal Security Agency. To qualify, they must meet listed service, approval, and probation requirements, and they may gain classified civil-service status. It also lets the Federal Security Administrator continue or change their state salary rates until the jobs are classified under the Classification Act of 1923. Vacancies in public employment office facilities and services run by the Social Security Board may also be filled from eligible state merit system lists, with civil-service status possible after probation.

8986.s: This order lets the Governor of the Panama Canal increase pay for not more than 200 employees of The Panama Canal or the Panama Railroad Company who are not citizens of the United States or the Republic of Panama. Those employees would not get greater leave privileges than employees paid at the lower rate. It also amends earlier employment rules and revokes two prior orders on pay increases.

8985.s: This order creates the Office of Censorship and puts a Director of Censorship in charge. The Director may censor communications by mail, cable, radio, or other means between the United States and foreign countries, and it covers the Territories and possessions of the United States, including the Philippine Islands. It also creates a Censorship Policy Board to advise the Director and a Censorship Operating Board to help carry out the work.

8987.s: The order establishes the waters of Honolulu Harbor, Oahu, and its approaches and tributaries as the Honolulu Defensive Sea Area for national defense. Vessels not under United States Naval or other United States authorized supervision may enter only in daylight, with good visibility, and only after specific permission is obtained. It also places loading or unloading of oil fuel or other inflammable or explosive materials under local Naval control, and says people who disregard the rules may be detained, attacked by United States armed forces, or prosecuted.

8989.s: This order creates an Office of Defense Transportation in the Executive Office of the President and puts it under a director appointed by the President. The office is directed to coordinate domestic transportation policies and movements, study transportation needs, and work to avoid congestion and keep traffic moving for the war effort. It also works with federal agencies and private transportation groups, handles certain rate and legislation matters, and is organized into divisions for rail, motor, inland waterway, and coastwise and intercoastal transport.

8983.s: This order appoints a commission to investigate the attack by Japanese armed forces on Hawaii on December 7, 1941. The commission is to find the facts and report on whether any errors or derelictions of duty by United States Army or Navy personnel helped the enemy's success, and who was responsible if so. It is also directed to travel as needed, use assistants, and receive help from other executive offices and agencies.

8982.s: This executive order changes the name of the Economic Defense Board to the Board of Economic Warfare. It also amends four earlier executive orders to match the new name.

8984.s: This order gives the Commander in Chief, United States Fleet, supreme command of the operating forces in the Navy's fleets and coastal frontier commands. It says the commander will report through the Secretary of the Navy to the President and will have a staff to handle intelligence, war plans, operations, communications, training, and personal aide duties. It also says the Chief of Naval Operations will keep the commander informed about what needs can be met, while the Chief of Naval Operations keeps the duty to prepare war plans from the long range point of view.

8981.s: This order sets apart a tract of land in the Canal Zone as a naval reservation called Navy Hospital Area, Coco Solo. It places the area under the control and jurisdiction of the Secretary of the Navy, while keeping it subject to civil jurisdiction of the Canal Zone Government. The naval authorities must pay the costs of the transfer, and Panama Canal personnel and equipment must be allowed access for canal operations such as drainage, sanitation, and surveys.

8980.s: This order changes an earlier rule that had barred federal officers and employees from holding State, Territorial, and municipal offices, with some exceptions. It allows a person who holds a State, Territorial, or municipal office to be appointed to and serve on an Alien Enemy Hearing Board.

8979.s: This order sets aside land and water on the northwest part of the Kenai Peninsula in Alaska as the Kenai National Moose Range. It reserves the area for the Department of the Interior and the Alaska Game Commission as a refuge and breeding ground for moose. Most of the land cannot be settled, sold, or entered under Alaska land laws, with some listed exceptions. Hunting moose and other game, and trapping fur animals, are still allowed under the Alaska Game Law and Interior Department rules.

8978.s: This order establishes naval defensive sea areas in parts of New York Harbor, New London, Delaware Bay and River, Chesapeake Bay-Norfolk, and Charleston Harbor for national defense. It sets boundaries for each area and says vessels need specific permission to enter or travel there in daylight and good visibility. It also lets the Navy control movement inside these areas and regulate loading or unloading fuel and other flammable or explosive materials.

8974.s: The order directs the Secretary of Commerce to control civil aviation in line with war needs, if requested by the Secretary of War. It also authorizes and directs the Secretary of War to take possession and control of any civil aviation system, or part of one, as needed for the successful prosecution of the war.

8975.s: This order lets the Attorney General make appointments to jobs in the Alien Property Division of the Department of Justice without following the Civil Service Act and Rules. It includes the head of that division.

8977.s: This executive order creates the National Patent Planning Commission with five members appointed by the President. The commission will study the American patent system and look at whether changes are needed to better support inventions and their use for the public good. It will also consider how patent laws may be blocking invention and how inventions and discoveries could increase commerce, provide employment, and use expanded defense industrial facilities during normal times.

8976.s: This order lets the Secretary of Commerce waive compliance with the navigation and vessel inspection laws for war purposes. The waiver can be made when requested by the Secretary of the Navy or the Secretary of War, or on the Secretary of Commerce's own initiative or written recommendation of another government agency head. It applies only to the extent needed in the conduct of the war.

8973.s: This order lets certain executive branch employees be transferred if they are qualified for work directly connected with the national-defense program and their current jobs can be filled. The transfer must have the consent of the department head and the employee. It also gives some transferred employees reemployment rights if their service later ends without prejudice, including possible reinstatement or placement on a reemployment list.

8972.s: This order directs the Secretary of War and the Secretary of the Navy to set up and keep military guards and patrols when they think it is necessary or desirable. It also lets them take other appropriate measures to protect national-defense material, premises, and utilities from injury or destruction. The order says this does not change the Federal Bureau of Investigation’s duty to investigate alleged sabotage.

8971.s: This order authorizes the Director of Selective Service to set up and run a program to physically rehabilitate registrants for training and service in the armed forces of the United States. It also lets the Director make rules, issue notices and instructions, and use funds for this purpose. The Director may delegate duties and use available federal facilities when practical.

8969.s: This order further exempts Joshua G. Hefty, a topographic engineer with the International Boundary Commission, from compulsory retirement for age for one more year. It applies only to him and extends his exemption until January 31, 1943.

8970.s: This order establishes naval defensive sea areas for national defense at several harbors and coastal waters in Maine, New Hampshire, Massachusetts, Rhode Island, California, Washington, and the Columbia River entrance. It limits when a vessel may enter or move through those waters unless it is under United States naval or other authorized supervision. A vessel must get specific permission in advance and follow any further instructions from the United States Navy or other United States authority. The Secretary of the Navy is responsible for publishing and enforcing these regulations.

8967.s: This order exempts Arthur W. Exline, a senior power plant operative at the Government Printing Office, from compulsory retirement for age for one more year. The exemption lasts until December 31, 1942.

8968.s: This order exempts Mrs. Ethel A. Barnes, a chief file clerk at the American Embassy in Mexico City, from compulsory retirement for age for one year. It applies only to her and delays her automatic separation from service until the end of that year.

8966.s: This order exempts Bart W. Butler, a Chief in the Criminal Division of the Department of Justice, from compulsory retirement for age. The exemption lasts for one year, ending December 31, 1942.

8965.s: This order extends the trust periods for Indian lands, whether tribal or individual, that would otherwise expire during calendar year 1942. The extension is for 25 more years from the date the trust would have expired, except in cases where Congress has specifically kept the power to extend the trust period for itself.

8963.s: This order changes Executive Order 8389 by adding Thailand to a list in Section 3. It affects Thailand under that order's rules.

8962.s: This order changes the rules for the Canal Zone judiciary. It says there will be a magistrate, a constable, and other needed employees for the magistrates' courts in Balboa and Cristobal, with appointments and pay set by the Governor. It also adds rules for other court employees, saying they must do the duties set by the magistrates and may be required to give bonds by the Governor.

8964.s: This order lets the Defense Communications Board handle powers over radio stations under the Communications Act of 1934. The Board may plan how radio facilities are used, designate stations for use, control, supervision, inspection, or closure by U.S. government agencies, and require priority for communications essential to national defense and security. It also affects radio station owners and employees, government departments and agencies, and carriers subject to the Communications Act of 1934.

8961.s: This order revokes all earlier executive orders, or parts of them, that established airspace reservations within the continental United States, except the District of Columbia. It does not apply to Alaska or the Panama Canal Zone.

8960.s: This order changes Executive Order No. 8546 by replacing one title with another wherever it appears. It affects the Defense Communications Board order and changes the words "Assistant Secretary of the Treasury in Charge of the Coast Guard" to "Assistant Secretary of the Treasury in Charge of Treasury Enforcement Activities".

8958.s: This order exempts Nicholas W. Dorsey, an accountant and auditor at the Smithsonian Institution, from compulsory retirement for age. The exemption lasts for one year and ends on January 31, 1943.

8957.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in Colorado from all forms of appropriation under the public-land laws, including the mining laws. It reserves those lands for the War Department to use as camp sites, subject to valid existing rights. It also says this order takes precedence over Executive Order No. 6910 as it affects these lands, but does not rescind or revoke that order.

8956.s: This order revokes part of a 1926 order that had temporarily withdrawn certain public lands in Montana for classification and in aid of legislation. It applies only to the land described in the order.

8954.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in Nevada from the public-land laws, including the mining laws, and reserves them for the War Department as machine gun ranges. The lands described include both public and nonpublic lands and total about 68,533.75 acres. It is subject to existing rights and to a grazing district order and a power site classification already in place. After the national defense emergency ends, the order can end if the Secretary of the Interior says the lands are needed for grazing or other Interior Department uses.

8953.s: This order establishes the Los Angeles-Long Beach Harbor Naval Defensive Sea Area for national defense. It limits when vessels that are not under United States naval or other authorized supervision may enter or travel in the area, and they must get permission first. It also puts the loading and unloading of oil fuel and other inflammable or explosive materials under local naval control and says vessels must follow Navy instructions while inside the area.

8951.s: This order changes the rules for moving an employee to a higher-paying job paid from emergency funds. Such transfers now need approval from the Civil Service Commission, and requests must be sent directly to that Commission.

8950.s: This order reserves the airspace over a set area of the District of Columbia for national defense, other government purposes, and public safety. No one may fly a civil aircraft in that airspace unless the Administrator of Civil Aeronautics gives special permission. It says people who break the order may face the penalties in the Civil Aeronautics Act of 1938.

8952.s: This order revokes an earlier order that created an Emergency Replacement List for employees without competitive civil service status, except for certain temporary census employees. It allows people appointed from that list to certain classified civil service jobs to gain classified civil service status if they meet the stated service and duty requirements. Appointments in the classified departmental service in the District of Columbia under this order are charged to the regular apportionment of appointments among the States, territories, and the District of Columbia.

8949.s: This order exempts Burt W. Andrews, a principal attorney in the Bureau of Internal Revenue, from compulsory retirement for age for one year. It applies to his retirement from the Treasury Department and sets the exemption to end on November 30, 1942.

8948.s: This order exempts James J. Goutchey, a custodian in the Public Buildings Administration, from compulsory retirement for age. The exemption lasts for one year and ends on November 30, 1942.

8947.s: This order revokes a 1912 order that had withdrawn a parcel of public land in Colorado for use by the Forest Service as the Malachite Administrative Site. It affects that land and the Forest Service use tied to the San Isabel National Forest.

8944.s: This order directs the Federal Works Administrator to take possession of and operate the Grand River Dam project in Oklahoma. It says the project will be used to generate and supply power for explosives or munitions of war, and for other purposes involving the safety and defense of the United States. The Administrator must pay just and fair compensation and later return the project when the President finds continued control is no longer needed.

8945.s: This order exempts John A. Newlin, a principal engineer at the Forest Products Laboratory in the Forest Service, from compulsory retirement for age. The exemption lasts for one year, ending February 28, 1943.

8943.s: This order changes earlier rules on which agencies are in charge of buying and moving certain supplies for refugee relief. It assigns the Secretary of Agriculture, the Secretary of War, and the Secretary of the Treasury different roles for agricultural supplies, medical supplies, and other materials and supplies. The supplies are to be delivered to the American Red Cross or another agency later designated for relief of refugee men, women, and children driven from their homes or made destitute by hostilities or invasion.

8942.s: This order sets rules for the Office of Production Management to handle the requisitioning and disposal of property needed for the defense of the United States. It lets certain departments and agencies, and in some cases U.S. Marshals, requisition property when the legal conditions are met, and it allows compensation to be set for property taken. It also lets the Supply Priorities and Allocations Board set policies and rules for this process.

8941.s: This order amends the Civil Service Rules to add all positions in the War Department on the Isthmus of Panama to Schedule A. It applies during the emergency declared by the President on May 27, 1941.

8940.s: This order changes an earlier executive order about jobs in the classified civil service. It says certain vacant positions may be filled by promotion, transfer, or assignment of qualified employees who meet the stated conditions.

8939.s: This order lets certain Farm Security Administration employees who already had permanent, indefinite, or emergency appointments be promoted, transferred, or assigned to positions that must be filled under Civil Service Rules. It also allows those employees to gain competitive classified civil-service status under the law named in the order. It applies to employees of the Farm Security Administration in the Department of Agriculture.

8938.s: This order gives Army warrant officers the powers usually exercised by commissioned officers when they are assigned certain duties. Those duties include commanding stations, units, or detachments, handling funds and vouchers, issuing travel orders and transportation requests, receiving and administering property, and certifying official papers.

8936.s: This order exempts Dr. Arthur R. Butler, a senior medical officer of the United States Civil Service Commission, from compulsory retirement for age. The exemption lasts for one year, ending March 31, 1943.

8934.s: This order exempts Miss Laura L. Tracy, chief of section in the United States Civil Service Commission, from compulsory retirement for age. It lets her stay in service for one year, ending January 31, 1943.

8935.s: This order exempts William H. Tietgen, Marshal of the United States Customs Court in New York, from compulsory retirement for age. The exemption lasts for six months, ending May 31, 1942.

8933.s: This order exempts Hans Schjeveland, a shipwright in the Mechanical Division of the Panama Canal, from compulsory retirement for age. The exemption lasts for one year, ending November 30, 1942.

8931.s: This order changes a rule for conditions of employment in the Panama Canal service. It says absences of one-half day or more that are regularly authorized must be charged against annual leave. It also says absences due to illness or injury, when supported by a certificate from an authorized physician in The Panama Canal service, must be charged against annual leave. No payment may be made for time lost because of illness due to alcoholism or drug addiction, or for injury caused by an employee's willful intent to bring about injury or death to himself or another.

8932.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in Idaho from appropriation under the public-land laws, including the mining laws. It reserves those lands for the War Department to use as practice bombing ranges, subject to valid existing rights. The order also says it is subject to Idaho Grazing District No. 1 and may end after the national emergency if the lands are needed for grazing or other Interior Department uses.

8929.s: This order directs the Coast Guard to operate as part of the Navy and to follow the orders of the Secretary of the Navy. Coast Guard personnel serving under this order are subject to the laws made for the Navy. It also sets rules for disciplinary action involving Coast Guard officers and enlisted members while they are serving this way.

8930.s: This order establishes a National Indian Institute in the Department of the Interior and affiliates it with the Inter-American Indian Institute. The Institute is directed to help coordinate Indian administration and Indian studies, gather and publish materials, prepare library material and bibliographies, and submit an annual report. It is managed by a Director under the Secretary of the Interior and has a Policy Board with federal and other representatives.

8927.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in Nevada from appropriation under the public-land laws, including the mining laws. It reserves those lands under the Secretary of the Interior for use in producing magnesium metals and magnesium alloys for national defense purposes. The order stays in effect until the President or Congress revokes it.

8928.s: This order authorizes the Secretary of War to take possession of and operate the Bendix, New Jersey, plants of Air Associates, Incorporated. The plants are to produce military airplane parts and equipment for the United States and for national defense. The order also allows the Secretary of War to use needed employees, a civilian advisor on industrial relations, and other steps, including troops if needed. It says possession and operation will end when the President decides they are no longer needed for national defense.

8925.s: This order exempts Dr. Lawrence W. White, a senior medical officer in the Office of Indian Affairs at the Department of the Interior, from compulsory retirement for age. It lets him stay in service for one year, through February 28, 1943.

8926.s: This order creates an Office of Lend-Lease Administration in the Office for Emergency Management of the Executive Office of the President. It puts an Administrator in charge, appointed by the President, and gives that person authority over lend-lease aid for nations the President has found to be vital to the defense of the United States. The State Department will continue to negotiate the master agreements for each nation receiving aid, and Executive Order No. 8751 is revoked.

8924.s: This order withdraws about 80 acres of public land in Hill County, Montana, from the public-land laws, including the mining laws. It also reserves about 2,960 acres of land and water for the Department of the Interior as a refuge and breeding ground for migratory birds and other wildlife. People may not hunt, trap, capture, disturb, kill, or enter the refuge except under rules set by the Secretary of the Interior.

8923.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in New Mexico from all forms of appropriation under the public-land laws, including the mining laws. It reserves those lands for the War Department to use as a National Guard rifle range, subject to valid existing rights.

8921.s: This order withdraws the described public land in California from all forms of appropriation under the public land laws, including the mining laws. It reserves the land for the United States Coast Guard, Treasury Department, to help establish lighted buoys for an emergency landing area for seaplanes. The order is subject to existing rights and to certain earlier land withdrawals, and it says it will end after the national emergency is officially terminated if the Secretary of the Interior gives notice for reclamation or wildlife purposes.

8922.s: This order creates an Office of Facts and Figures within the Office for Emergency Management in the Executive Office of the President. It puts the office under a director appointed by the President and directed by the President. The office is to help share factual information about the nation’s defense effort and the government’s defense policies and activities. It also calls on government departments and agencies to provide information to the director when requested.

8919.s: This order further exempts David D. Caldwell, a Special Assistant to the Attorney General in the Department of Justice, from compulsory retirement because of age. The exemption lasts for one year, ending January 31, 1943. It affects Caldwell and the Department of Justice.

8918.s: This order exempts Wladimir Ayvazoglou, a senior translator at the Geological Survey in the Department of the Interior, from compulsory retirement for age. The exemption lasts for one year, ending October 31, 1942.

8920.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in Okanogan County, Washington, from all forms of appropriation under the public-land laws, including the mining laws. It reserves the lands for use by the Game Commission of the State of Washington in connection with the Sinlahekin Deer Winter Range and Wildlife Refuge. The reservation is subject to valid rights and conditions set by the Secretary of the Interior.

8917.s: This order exempts James E. Amos, a Special Agent in the Federal Bureau of Investigation, from compulsory retirement for age for one more year. It affects only James E. Amos and extends his earlier exemption until January 31, 1943.

8916.s: This order revokes a 1909 order that had reserved land near Copper Center, Alaska, for educational and agricultural experiment station purposes. It withdraws certain public land from appropriation under the public-land laws, including the mining laws, and reserves it for the Alaska Road Commission for aviation purposes.

8914.s: This order changes a prior fingerprinting rule for employees in the executive civil service. It lets the Civil Service Commission decide to exempt any group or groups of temporary employees from the fingerprinting requirement.

8915.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in Washington from appropriation under the public-land laws, including the mining laws. It reserves those lands for the War Department to use as a practice bombing and gunnery range. The order is subject to existing rights and to a prior land withdrawal for reclamation purposes.

8912.s: This order transfers certain lands in New Mexico from the Secretary of the Interior back to the Secretary of Agriculture. The lands are to be used in connection with the land-conservation and land-utilization program of the Soil Conservation Service. It applies to the Jemez Project in Sandoval County, including land within the Ojo del Explritu Santo Land Grant.

8913.s: This order exempts Rutherford H. Baker, a senior instrument maker at the Bureau of Mines in the Department of the Interior, from compulsory retirement for age for one year. It applies only to him and extends his service until November 30, 1942.

8911.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in Oregon from appropriation under the public land laws, including the mining laws. It reserves the land for the Secretary of the Interior to use as an experimental range for scientific research and other studies. The studies are to provide basic information for administering the Taylor Grazing Act, and the order stays in effect until the President or Congress revokes it.

8910.s: This order transfers certain lands in Indiana from the Secretary of Agriculture to the Secretary of the Navy for national defense purposes. The lands are part of the Martin County and White River land utilization projects and include lands already acquired or still being acquired by the United States. The Secretary of Agriculture keeps enough jurisdiction over land still being acquired to finish that process.

8909.s: This order lets the Secretary of the Treasury allow bona-fide samples of coffee to enter the United States for testing purposes. These entries can be allowed without regard to the quota restrictions in the Inter-American Coffee Agreement.

8907.s: This order exempts William C. Alden, a Principal Scientist (Geologist) in the Geological Survey, from compulsory retirement for age for one year. It applies to him and delays his automatic separation from service until September 30, 1942.

8906.s: This order transfers certain national-forest lands in Arkansas from the Ouachita National Forest to the Ozark National Forest. It applies to the lands of the Magazine Mountain Ranger District within the established boundaries of the Ouachita National Forest. It says it does not give national-forest status to any public lands that did not already have that status, or remove that status from any public lands.

8908.s: This order restores certain lands in the United States Chromite Reservation in the Province of Zambales, on the Island of Luzon, to the Government of the Commonwealth of the Philippines. The lands were no longer needed for the purpose they had been reserved for. The restored land is to be administered for the benefit of the inhabitants there.

8905.s: This order further exempts Z. Lewis Dalby, the Chief Counsel of the United States Employees' Compensation Commission, from compulsory retirement for age for one more year. The exemption applies through September 30, 1942.

8903.s: This order exempts Jules A. Rodier, a telegrapher in The White House Office, from compulsory retirement for age. The exemption lasts for one year, ending November 30, 1942. It affects Rodier and the retirement rule that would have applied to him.

8904.s: This order further exempts Maurice C. Latta, an Executive Clerk in The White House Office, from compulsory retirement for age. The exemption lasts for one year, ending October 31, 1942.

8902.s: This order sets rules for coffee from countries that are signatories of the Inter-American Coffee Agreement. A United States consular officer may certify an invoice only if an official document shows the coffee is within the producing country's export quota for the United States customs territory. Starting October 1, 1941, such coffee may not be admitted for consumption in the customs territory of the United States unless each shipment has the required invoice and certificate, with exceptions for shipments valued at less than $100, shipments covered by a bond, or coffee shipped under a through bill of lading before the date of the order.

8901.s: This order exempts Samuel Thomas, an engineer at the Anacostia Junior-Senior High School in the District of Columbia, from compulsory retirement for age for one year. It applies only to him and delays his automatic separation from service until September 30, 1942.

8899.s: This order exempts Edward D. Anderson, Chief Clerk in the Purchasing Department of The Panama Canal, from compulsory retirement for age. It lets him stay in service for one more year, ending September 30, 1942.

8900.s: This order expands the duties of the Economic Defense Board. It gives the board authority over certain export and requisition powers, requires it to estimate materials needed for export and advise other boards, and sets up a clearing service for export proposals. It also transfers personnel, records, funds, and property from the affected agencies to the board.

8898.s: This order allows Soulis Newman to be appointed as a guard in the Public Buildings Administration, part of the Federal Works Agency. The appointment may be made without following the Civil Service Rules.

8897.s: This order exempts Miss Augusta F. Johnston, an administrative assistant with the Public Roads Administration, from compulsory retirement for age. The exemption lasts for one year and ends on September 30, 1942.

8896.s: This order further exempts Nelson S. Thompson from compulsory retirement for age for one year. It applies to his job as Chief of the Mechanical Engineering Section in the Office of the Supervising Architect, Public Buildings Administration, Federal Works Agency.

8895.s: This order directs certain Coast Guard units, vessels, and personnel to operate as part of the Navy during the present unlimited emergency, under the orders of the Secretary of the Navy. It applies to Coast Guard units already transferred or under detail with the Navy, and to additional units, vessels, and personnel later approved for Navy operation. While serving with the Navy, Coast Guard personnel are subject to the laws that govern the Navy. When the emergency ends, they return to the Department of the Treasury and their former Coast Guard status.

8894.s: This order changes Civil Service Rule II for employees whose positions are moved into the classified, or competitive, civil service. It lets some current employees keep the rights of a competitive appointment if they meet service, testing, and other rule requirements. It also allows some returning military or naval employees to gain classified status after reinstatement if they are recommended and meet the stated conditions. Employees who do not meet these requirements may stay in their jobs, but they may not be promoted, transferred, or assigned to another classified position.

8893.s: This order allows S. Royden Burch to be appointed to an appropriate position in the Department of Agriculture without following the Civil Service Rules. It affects Mr. Burch and the Department of Agriculture.

8892.s: This order withdraws public lands in parts of Arizona from appropriation under the public-land laws, including the mining laws. It reserves those areas for the War Department to use as an aerial gunnery range, and the areas described include both public and nonpublic lands. The order also sets aside at least two no-firing days each month for patrol and maintenance work, and some lands may be used only for aerial gunnery and tow-target firing.

8891.s: This order creates a Division of Contract Distribution in the Office of Production Management and sets out its duties. The division is meant to help spread defense contracts among more firms and localities, support the conversion of civilian industries to defense production, and promote subcontracting and local industrial defense groups. It also coordinates financing, engineering help, and liaison with War, Navy, Maritime Commission, and other procurement agencies. The order abolishes the Defense Contract Service and transfers its duties, records, files, and equipment to the new division.

8890.s: This order creates the Office of Defense Health and Welfare Services in the Executive Office of the President. It gives the office the job of coordinating health, welfare, medical, nutrition, recreation, and related services for the defense program, and of helping states and local communities when they ask for help. It also sets up a Health and Medical Committee and allows the Director to appoint advisory committees and use existing government services and facilities.

8887.s: This order exempts certain named plate printers at the Bureau of Engraving and Printing from compulsory retirement for age. The exemption applies only if each employee is physically able to do the job. It ends no more than sixty days after the Civil Service Commission notifies the Bureau that it has set up registers of eligible plate printers to replace them.

8885.s: This order revokes the designation of Peskan, Montana, as a customs port of entry in Customs Collection District No. 33. The change takes effect at the close of business on September 15, 1941.

8886.s: This order directs the Civil Service Commission to give classified civil service status to certain Coast Guard civilian employees who were transferred from the Bureau of Lighthouses. It applies only to people employed aboard Coast Guard vessels who have not been inducted into the military service of the Coast Guard. The employee must pass any non-competitive fitness tests the Commission sets and must not be barred by civil service rules or other law.

8884.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in California from appropriation under the public-land laws, including the mining laws. It reserves those lands for the War Department to use for a reservoir and a water pipe line to Camp San Luis Obispo. It applies subject to valid existing rights.

8883.s: This order withdraws a piece of public land in California from the public-land laws, including the mining laws, and reserves it for the Department of the Navy as an aircraft bombing site. It applies subject to valid existing rights. It also says the order takes precedence over certain earlier land orders for that area, and after the national-defense emergency ends, it will no longer apply if the Secretary of the Interior says the land is needed for reclamation purposes.

8882.s: This order sets rules for within-grade salary advancements for certain Federal Government employees. It defines which positions and service time count, gives priority to periodic salary increases over increases for especially meritorious service, and says salary eligibility must be based on the employee’s current efficiency rating. It also protects pay for employees restored to service after military duty, making sure they get at least their prior rate plus any within-grade increases they would have earned.

8881.s: This order changes a prior order about foreign merchant vessels. It makes that order apply to any or all foreign merchant vessels, and their appurtenances, that are lying idle in waters within the jurisdiction of the United States, including the Philippine Islands and the Canal Zone. The change applies to vessels in that condition at any time after June 6, 1941, through June 30, 1942.

8880.s: This order changes an earlier rule that generally barred Federal officers and employees from holding certain State, Territorial, or municipal offices. It allows a Federal officer or employee to serve as Chancellor of the University of Puerto Rico. That service cannot interfere with the person’s regular Federal duties.

8889.s: This order changes rules for export licenses. It says export licenses cannot be transferred without written authorization from the Secretary of State, and they can be revoked without notice unless they are still valid for one year from the date they were issued. It also requires a license or other document before certain articles or materials can be loaded, mailed, or exported, with a waiver possible if the Secretary of State authorizes it.

8879.s: This order sets the interest rate for postal-savings certificates issued by the Canal Zone Postal Service at one-half of one per cent for each three-month period after issue. It says the interest is paid when the certificates are paid. It also applies these rules to outstanding deposit money orders issued before August 13, 1940, and revokes a prior executive order.

8877.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in Alaska, including some water areas, from the public-land and mining laws and reserves them for the War Department for military purposes. It covers areas near Sitka, Seward, and Kodiak. It also revokes a prior order for these lands and says the order is subject to some earlier lighthouse reservations.

8876.s: This order suspends the Saturday half-holiday rules for certain employees of the War Department and the Coast Guard. It applies to employees working on construction for the military establishment in the United States, and to Coast Guard employees working on the construction, alteration, or repair of vessels or shore facilities. The suspension lasts for the duration of the national emergency declared on September 8, 1939.

8875.s: This order gives the Office of Production Management broad control over priority orders and supply allocation for materials, power, fuel, and other commodities. It creates a Supply Priorities and Allocations Board to set policies, review plans, and coordinate defense, civilian, defense aid, and other demands. It also creates a Division of Civilian Supply, changes the name of the Office of Price Administration and Civilian Supply to the Office of Price Administration, and abolishes the Priorities Board of the Office of Production Management.

8874.s: This order withdraws certain lands in New Mexico from the public land laws, including the mining laws, and reserves them for use by the War Department as a practice bombing range. It applies to public and non-public lands in the listed areas, totaling 14,115.32 acres. The order is subject to valid existing rights and to two earlier orders that affect some of the same land.

8878.s: This order changes rules for post allowances for officers and employees under an earlier executive order. It says a post allowance is available only during the part of the fiscal year when the person stays in the district they are assigned to, unless the Secretary of State decides otherwise. The change also applies to post allowances payable since July 1, 1940.

8873.s: This order exempts Fred E. Edwards, a captain in the United States Customs Patrol, from compulsory retirement for age for one year. It affects only him and lets him stay in service until August 31, 1942.

8872.s: This order withdraws a described area in Alaska from all forms of public-land appropriation, including the mining laws. It reserves the land for the War Department to use as an aerial gunnery and bombing range, subject to valid existing rights. The order excepts fishing villages and an area previously withdrawn by another executive order, and it says the area includes both public and non-public lands.

8870.s: This order restores a parcel of land in the Waimanalo Military Reservation in the Territory of Hawaii to the Territory of Hawaii. The land was said to no longer be needed for military purposes of the United States. The War Department may remove its improvements and installations if that has not already been done.

8869.s: This order sets up a process for the Secretary of Commerce to investigate certain vessels documented under the June 6, 1941 act. If the Secretary finds that a vessel’s physical facilities are not adequate or that using alien masters, officers, or crew is necessary for operation, he must certify that finding to the United States Maritime Commission. The order then allows waiver of laws on masters, officers, crew members, and crew accommodations to the extent and under the terms stated in that certification.

8868.s: This order directs the Secretary of the Navy to take possession of and operate the plant of the Federal Shipbuilding and Drydock Company. It is meant to keep the plant producing vessels, facilities, material, and equipment for the United States and to use any employees needed to carry out that work. The President will end this control when he decides the plant can be privately operated in a way that fits national defense needs.

8871.s: This order authorizes the United States Maritime Commission to issue warrants for certain vessels described in the act. It covers vessels documented under United States laws, vessels owned by United States citizens but not documented, and, on application, foreign-flag vessels not owned by United States citizens. The order says this is to help with the prompt delivery of materials essential to national defense and essential supplies and services.

8867.s: This order transfers a tract of land at La Puntilla in San Juan, Puerto Rico, from the War Department to the Treasury Department. The land is to be used for Coast Guard purposes. The tract includes 1.31 acres.

8866.s: This order further exempts J. Brent Clarke, Superintendent of the Diplomatic Pouch and Mail Section at the Department of State, from compulsory retirement for age. The exemption lasts for one more year, ending September 30, 1942.

8864.s: This order places a tract of public land at Tanana, Alaska, under the control of the Secretary of the Interior. The land had been set aside as a military reservation for the use of the Signal Corps, United States Army, and was found to be useless for military purposes. It is to be handled under the act of July 5, 1884, or as otherwise provided by law.

8865.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in California from the public-land laws, including the mining laws. It reserves those lands for the War Department to use for combat firing ranges and maneuver purposes. The order also says it is subject to some existing rights and earlier land withdrawals that still apply to parts of the area.

8863.s: This order sets how the coffee import quota will be divided for countries that did not sign the Inter-American Coffee Agreement. It assigns shares for the British Empire except Aden and Canada, the Kingdom of the Netherlands and its possessions, Aden, Yemen, and Saudi Arabia, and other non-signatory countries. Coffee from those countries may not be entered for consumption above the set quota shares during the time this order is in effect.

8862.s: This order extends by 18 months the training and service periods of people inducted under the Selective Training and Service Act of 1940, unless they are sooner discharged. It also extends by 18 months the active military service of members of the Regular Army Reserve, the Enlisted Reserve Corps, and the National Guard who are serving under certain orders. The order extends by 18 months the enlistments of people in the Regular Army, the Regular Army Reserve, the Enlisted Reserve Corps, and the National Guard.

8861.s: This order revokes three earlier executive orders that had withdrawn public lands in Alabama, Florida, Mississippi, Michigan, and Wisconsin. The lands released by this order become subject to a later executive order that withdrew public lands in those states and others for classification and other purposes.

8859.s: This order suspends the eight-hour work limit for laborers and mechanics employed by the War Department on certain public works in the Territory of Hawaii. It applies to work on cantonments, air fields, fortifications, and other public works needed for national defense. The suspension lasts for the duration of the emergencies named in the order.

8858.s: This order transfers control and jurisdiction of a tract of land on Crown Mountain, St. Thomas, in the Virgin Islands from the Secretary of the Interior to the Secretary of War. The land is to be used for national defense purposes. The transfer is subject to valid existing rights.

8860.s: This order suspends the Saturday half-holiday law for certain civil employees of the War Department and the Coast Guard, and for their field services, while the national emergency lasts. It applies to employees performing labor or duties in the Territory of Hawaii.
