It also makes the office a channel of communication between defense agencies and the War and Navy Departments, and it revokes a prior executive order.

8630.s: This order further exempts David D. Caldwell, a Special Assistant to the Attorney General in the Department of Justice, from compulsory retirement for age. The exemption lasts for one more year, ending January 31, 1942.

8628.s: This order exempts Walter C. Mendenhall, Director of the Geological Survey in the Department of the Interior, from compulsory retirement for age. It lets him stay in service for one more year, ending February 28, 1942.

8627.s: This order puts certain National Guard units and their members into active military service of the United States. It applies to the listed field artillery, cavalry, engineer, coast artillery, and medical units, along with all active and inactive members of those units. It also moves affected officers and warrant officers into active duty under their Army appointments and commissions, and it relieves them from duty in their state National Guard while they serve.

8625.s: This order exempts Frank Frayser, a special agent in the Intelligence Unit of the Bureau of Internal Revenue, from compulsory retirement for age for one year. It applies only to him and keeps him in service until February 28, 1942.

8626.s: This order exempts Henry L. Schmidt, a senior power plant operative at the Government Printing Office, from compulsory retirement for age. The exemption lasts for one year and ends on January 31, 1942.

8623.s: This order suspends the eight-hour limit for people employed by the U.S. government on work at certain leased Army and Navy bases in British possessions in the Atlantic Ocean. It applies to construction of aviation and other Army and Navy facilities at those bases. It affects government workers on that work, allowing more than eight hours in a day.

8624.s: This order revokes the customs port of entry designation for Ajo, Arizona. It also designates Sonoyta, Arizona, as a customs port of entry.

8620.s: This order changes the Civil Service Rules to add one exempt position for the Rural Electrification Administration. It allows one private secretary or confidential assistant to the Administrator of that agency to be included in Schedule A.

8619.s: This order gives the Director of Selective Service the President’s powers and duties under the Selective Training and Service Act of 1940 for appeals from the decisions of boards of appeal. It also changes the Selective Service Regulations to fit that transfer of authority.

8618.s: This order calls certain National Guard units and members into active military service of the United States. It applies to listed units and to all active and inactive members of those units, and it says they will serve for twelve consecutive months unless relieved sooner. It also changes the status of affected officers and enlisted members as described in the order.

8621.s: This order revokes part of an earlier proclamation that had withdrawn certain lands in Alaska for town-site and railroad-related purposes. It then reserves one tract for the Civil Aeronautics Administration and the Fish and Wildlife Service to build and operate a sea-plane base. It reserves another tract for the Alaska Road Commission to use as an air-navigation site.

8617.s: This order prescribes additional regulations for exporting certain materials, machines, tools, and equipment. It covers items like bromine, ethylene, cobalt, abrasive products, measuring machines, gauges, testing machines, hydraulic pumps, and tools with industrial diamonds. It also applies existing export regulations to these items and to equipment and plans for producing aviation lubricating oil.

8615.s: This order exempts Maurice A. Emerson, Chief of the Division of Paper Custody in the Bureau of the Public Debt, from compulsory retirement for age. It lets him stay in service for one year, ending January 31, 1942.

8616.s: This order places Palmyra Island under the control and jurisdiction of the Secretary of the Navy and reserves it for naval purposes. It says this is subject to any valid existing rights. It also says the civil or criminal jurisdiction of the Territory of Hawaii over people or property on Palmyra Island is not affected, as long as that fits with the island’s naval use.

8614.s: This order allows the first appointments to the Director and Assistant Director jobs in the Bureau of Water Carriers of the Interstate Commerce Commission to be made without following the competitive civil service rules. The people appointed must still show the required qualifications before the Civil Service Commission.

8613.s: This order closes several federal offices in the District of Columbia all day on Tuesday, December 24, 1940. It also excuses federal employees in the District of Columbia and in the field service of executive departments, independent establishments, and other government agencies from duty that day, unless they are excluded for special public reasons or because existing law requires them to work.

8612.s: This order amends an earlier order about priority for naval and Army contracts and orders under section 2(a) of the June 28, 1940 act. It approves the Priorities Board and the Administrator of Priorities and lets them require deliveries of materials for those orders to take priority over deliveries for private account or for export. The order applies to materials, articles, equipment, and supplies needed for national defense.

8610.s: This order exempts Roberta L. Lindsey, an administrative officer in the Treasury Department, from compulsory retirement for age. It lets her stay in service for one year ending December 31, 1941.

8608.s: This order allows Mary Elizabeth Huber to be appointed to a classified under clerk-typist job at the Franklin D. Roosevelt Library in Hyde Park, New York. It says the appointment may be made without following the Civil Service Rules.

8609.s: This order exempts Arthur W. Exline, a senior power plant operative at the Government Printing Office, from compulsory retirement for age. The exemption lasts for one year and ends on December 31, 1941.

8607.s: This order sets additional rules for exporting certain iron and steel materials and products. It defines which items count as iron and steel, including ore, pig iron, ferro alloys, semi-finished products, and finished products such as plates, rails, bars, pipe, wire, and castings. It also changes some earlier export rules for ferro alloys and says other regulations from July 2, 1940 apply to these exports.

8605.s: This order puts certain National Guard units and members into the active military service of the United States. It applies to all federally recognized parts of the 35th Division, the 153d Infantry, and the 110th Observation Squadron, along with the active and inactive members of those units. Those called up are removed from duty in their state National Guard while they serve in the Army and are subject to Army laws and regulations.

8606.s: This order defines what counts as noncombatant military service and noncombatant training under the Selective Training and Service Act of 1940. It says that people whose conscientious objection claim is approved will receive noncombatant training and be assigned to noncombatant service instead of combatant service. The order lists unarmed units, the Medical Department, and certain units or installations as noncombatant service when the person is not required to bear arms or be trained in their use.

8603.s: This order exempts James C. Wynde, a Deputy Collector of Customs in the Treasury Department, from compulsory retirement for age. The exemption lasts for one year, ending November 30, 1941.

8602.s: This order says time served in the armed forces of the United States will not count against the eligibility period for certain people on Civil Service Commission eligible registers. It applies to people whose names were already on those registers when they entered military service, or who became eligible while serving. Those people must notify the Civil Service Commission within 40 days after their military service ends if they want the benefit.

8601.s: This order sets aside federal lands in Marshall County, Minnesota as an addition to the Mud Lake National Wildlife Refuge. The land is to be used by the Department of the Interior, subject to valid existing rights. It covers about 1,585 acres, more or less.

8600.s: This order changes the name of the Minidoka Wildlife Refuge in Idaho to Minidoka National Wildlife Refuge. It also adds about 360 acres of public land in Power County to the refuge and withdraws that land from settlement, location, sale, or entry, subject to valid existing rights. The added land remains subject to use under the reclamation laws.

8599.s: The order transfers certain electric transmission facilities and a substation in Mississippi to the Tennessee Valley Authority. It also transfers needed easements, rights-of-way, and other rights for use, operation, and maintenance of those facilities. Some rights of ingress and egress over land controlled by the War Department are included, so long as they do not interfere with United States operations.

8598.s: This order withdraws about 80 acres of public land in Pima and Yuma Counties, Arizona, from settlement, location, sale, or entry. It reserves those lands for the Department of the Interior to use as administrative sites for the Cabeza Prieta Game Range and the Kofa Game Range. It also replaces an earlier temporary withdrawal for the land covered by this order.

8597.s: This order sets aside the airspace over two areas in Alaska as naval airspace reservations for national defense and other governmental purposes. It covers Sitka Naval Airspace Reservation and Kodiak Naval Airspace Reservation. Aircraft other than public aircraft of the United States may not fly into, within, or through these areas unless the Secretary of the Navy authorizes it. Violations are subject to penalties under the Civil Aeronautics Act of 1938.

8596.s: This order changes an earlier Alaska land order so the Department of Commerce can use certain Nenana townsite lots for aviation-field purposes. It also reserves and sets apart 80 acres of public land next to those lots for the same use. The order stays in effect until the President or Congress revokes it.

8604.s: This order revokes parts of earlier executive orders that created public water reserves. It applies only to certain lands in Arizona, New Mexico, and Wyoming. The revocation covers listed parcels in Public Water Reserves Nos. 24, 34, 65, 20, and 119.

8595.s: This order amends an earlier order on the grades and ratings of enlisted men in the Regular Army for fiscal year 1941. It sets the maximum number allowed in each grade and in each specialist rating, and it includes selective-service trainees assigned to Regular Army units. The number of enlisted men in these grades and ratings may not exceed the limits listed in the order.

8594.s: This order puts certain National Guard units and members into active military service of the United States. It applies to listed units and to all active and inactive members of those units, for a period of twelve consecutive months unless sooner relieved. It also relieves them from duty in their state National Guard while they are in active federal service and places them under Army laws and regulations.

8593.s: This order makes the United States neutrality enforcement rules apply equally to Greece. It is meant to help enforce the country's neutrality and stop unneutral acts within U.S. jurisdiction during the war between Italy and Greece.

8591.s: This order temporarily withdraws certain public lands in Arkansas from settlement, location, sale, or entry. The land is to be used for the construction of the Norfork Dam and Reservoir on the North Fork of the White River, under War Department supervision. It also supersedes an earlier withdrawal order for any of the listed lands that were affected by it.

8590.s: This order sets the number of men to be inducted into the land forces of the United States before July 1, 1941 at 800,000. It directs the Secretary of War to induct up to that many men. It also directs the Director of Selective Service to select men and make enough of them available to fill the Secretary of War’s requests.

8589.s: This order changes Power Site Reserve No. 461 to let the State of Idaho build a highway over certain land in Idaho. The highway use must stop, without liability or expense to the United States or its licensees, if the Secretary of the Interior finds it conflicts with project works authorized by the United States.

8592.s: The order changes the name of the Lake Bowdoin Migratory Waterfowl Refuge in Phillips County, Montana, to Bowdoin National Wildlife Refuge. It also adds about 1,398.16 acres of public land in Phillips County to the refuge and withdraws those lands from settlement, location, sale, or entry, subject to valid existing rights. The added lands remain subject to reclamation laws and to oil and gas development and related purposes.

8587.s: This order changes Civil Service Rules for federal jobs. It bars questions about applicants’ political or religious opinions and bans discrimination based on race, political views, or religion in the executive civil service, except where law allows. It also sets rules for trying to get applicants to withdraw, for classifying certain employees and post office positions, and for appointments, examinations, and probation in the civil service.

8586.s: This order lets receivers and trustees in bankruptcy inspect certain tax returns. It covers income, excess-profits, capital stock, gift tax, and employment tax returns under the Internal Revenue Code and several earlier revenue laws. It also covers returns under Title IX of the Social Security Act and related amended returns.

8585.s: This order changes Civil Service Rules for certain jobs outside the United States. It applies to people employed in a foreign country, the Virgin Islands, Puerto Rico in some cases, island possessions in the Pacific except the Hawaiian Islands, and the Philippine Islands when the Civil Service Commission says the position cannot be treated as part of the competitive classified service. It does not apply to certain employees in Canada or Mexico with the Immigration and Naturalization Service, or to people employed in any foreign country by the Bureau of Customs.

8583.s: This order revokes part of an earlier order that had withdrawn public lands in Wyoming while a resurvey was pending. It applies to the township listed in the order, and it takes effect when the official plat of the resurvey is filed.

8581.s: This order exempts Andrew McClellan from compulsory retirement for age for one year. It applies to his job as Chief of the Stenographic, Typewriting, and Court Reporting Division of the United States Customs Court in New York, New York. The exemption ends on November 30, 1941.

8580.s: This order extends the trust periods for Indian lands that would expire during calendar year 1941. It applies to both tribal and individual Indian lands and adds 25 years from the date the trust would otherwise end. It does not apply to cases where Congress has kept the authority to extend the trust period for itself.

8582.s: This order exempts Hervey G. Mooney, a clerk in the Division of Insurance at the United States Maritime Commission, from compulsory retirement for age. The exemption lasts for one year, ending October 31, 1941.

8579.s: This order withdraws public land in Utah from appropriation under the public land laws, including the mining laws. It reserves the land for the War Department to use as an aerial bombing and gunnery range. The withdrawal covers land subject to valid existing rights and does not rescind or revoke certain earlier withdrawals that apply to the same area.

8578.s: This order withdraws about 3,560,000 acres of public land in Nevada from appropriation under the public-land laws, including the mining laws. It reserves the land for use by the War Department as an aerial bombing and gunnery range, subject to valid existing rights. It also says this withdrawal takes precedence over earlier withdrawals for wildlife and other purposes, but does not rescind or revoke them.

8576.s: This order sets rules for hiring, rating, assigning, promoting, reinstating, and removing unclassified laborers in the executive civil service. It says applicants must be citizens of or owe allegiance to the United States, be physically and mentally qualified, and have good character and habits. It also gives preference in some cases to honorably discharged soldiers, sailors, and marines, and to certain widows and wives. The Civil Service Commission and other officers are given duties to carry out these rules.

8575.s: The order reserves federal lands in Baker and Union Counties, Oregon, as the Thief Valley National Wildlife Refuge. It sets the area aside as a refuge and breeding ground for migratory birds and other wildlife. The reservation is to continue without interfering with reclamation purposes connected to the Baker Reclamation Project.

8574.s: This order sets out Volume Four of the Selective Service Regulations for handling delivery and induction under the Selective Training and Service Act of 1940. It explains how quotas, credits, and debits are determined for the Nation, States, and local boards, and how Governors and the Director of Selective Service report on them. It also covers calls for men, selecting men for induction, preparing papers, and delivering them to induction stations.

8573.s: This order withdraws a described parcel of public land in Alaska from settlement, location, sale, or entry. It reserves the land for town-site purposes and says it will be handled under applicable town-site laws. The land is described as about 100 acres, more or less.

8577.s: This order temporarily withdraws 1.2 acres of public land at Kotzebue, Alaska, from settlement, location, sale, or entry. It reserves the land for the War Department to use as a radio-station site, subject to valid existing rights.

8572.s: This order approves the Priorities Board and the designation of an Administrator of Priorities. It lets them require people with naval and Army contracts and orders to give those deliveries priority over deliveries for private account or for export. The order applies to persons with those contracts and orders and is to be used in the public interest and the interest of national defense.

8570.s: This order sets physical standards for Selective Service examinations under the Selective Training and Service Act of 1940. It tells examining physicians how to examine registrants, classify them for general or limited military service, and report certain diseases to civil authorities. It also requires a syphilis test for every registrant and says no anesthetic may be used without the registrant’s written consent.

8571.s: This order transfers control and jurisdiction over certain lands in Muskogee County, Oklahoma, from the Secretary of Agriculture to the Secretary of the Interior. The Secretary of the Interior is authorized to administer the lands through the Commissioner of Indian Affairs for the benefit of Indians he may designate. The lands include about 4.43 acres and also include the improvements on them.

8569.s: This order gives the Director of Selective Service the power to appoint needed members of local boards, local board physicians, government appeal agents, and appeal board members. It applies to the local and appeal boards covered by the Selective Service Regulations.

8567.s: This order sets up how parts of the 1940 law will be carried out for national defense. The Secretary of War and the Secretary of the Navy, working through the Army and Navy Munitions Board, will decide whether to requisition and take over military or naval equipment, munitions, and related parts, machinery, tools, materials, and supplies. They will also handle the sale or other disposition of items taken over under the law. The remaining parts of the law will be administered by the Administrator of Export Control under regulations set by the President.

8566.s: This order amends the Foreign Service Regulations to set duties for Foreign Service officers, except consular agents, in connection with the admission of aliens into the Philippine Islands. Those duties are to be prescribed by the Secretary of State under the Philippine immigration law named in the order. It also revokes Executive Order No. 7224-A.

8565.s: This order amends a prior executive order to extend its provisions to property in which Rumania or any national of Rumania has had any interest, direct or indirect, on or since October 9, 1940. It also changes the date used in the definitions of “Rumania” and “national” of Rumania to October 9, 1940.

8564.s: This order amends a previous order about filling certain jobs tied to the national-defense program. It lets the Civil Service Commission authorize appointments without the usual competitive civil service rules when there is a public exigency or an urgent need to fill a position. People appointed this way do not get classified competitive civil service status.

8563.s: This order amends Civil Service Rules to add temporary clerks, carriers, and laborers for part-time or intermittent work in the Postal Service. The work is for holiday or seasonal business from November 15, 1940, to January 15, 1941.

8562.s: This order further exempts James L. Hughes, the District Director of Immigration and Naturalization in Gloucester City, New Jersey, from compulsory retirement for age for one year. It applies only to him and extends his earlier exemption through November 30, 1941.

8561.s: This order sets finance and personnel rules for the Selective Service system under the Selective Training and Service Act of 1940. It says Congress money may be used only for approved selective service expenses, and contracts cannot commit the government to pay more than appropriations allow. It also gives the Director of Selective Service and state governors certain powers over hiring, spending, supplies, vouchers, and expense reporting.

8559.s: This order gives Lieutenant Colonel Lewis B. Hershey authority to do certain duties under the Selective Training and Service Act of 1940 until a Director of Selective Service is appointed. It lets him handle administration of the Selective Service law and appoint members of local boards, local board physicians, government appeal agents, and appeal boards.

8558.s: This order transfers certain United States lands in Oconee County, South Carolina, to the Secretary of Agriculture. The lands are to be used, administered, and disposed of under Title III and related provisions of the Bankhead-Jones Farm Tenant Act. The lands include the Saluda Garden Homes Project and other parcels described in the order.

8557.s: This order sets rules for paying expenses when certain civilian officers and employees of the United States die while traveling on official business or while assigned outside the United States. It covers preparing and transporting the remains, and in some cases transporting dependents, household effects, and other personal property to a place in the United States. The order also says when the department head must notify relatives and when payment is not allowed if another U.S. law already covers the expenses.

8556.s: This order transfers the use, possession, and control of certain lands in Lawrence County, Alabama, including the Elk River Shoals Canal, locks, buildings, and other improvements, to the Tennessee Valley Authority. The lands had been under the control of the War Department. The order says the War Department no longer needs the property and that the Tennessee Valley Authority needs it for its purposes.

8555.s: This order keeps Samuel A. Cottrell, an auditor in the Bureau of Internal Revenue, from being forced to retire because of age for nine more months. It affects only him and extends an earlier exemption.

8554.s: This order exempts William T. Andrews from compulsory retirement for age for one more year, ending September 30, 1941. It applies to Andrews, who served as a valuation expert in the Department of Justice and had already been exempted for a previous one-year period.

8553.s: This order designates Lieutenant Colonel Lewis B. Hershey to perform all duties connected with administering the Selective Service law. It applies while a Director of Selective Service has not yet been appointed under the Act.

8560.s: This order sets regulations for how Selective Service boards must handle registration cards, assign serial and order numbers, and make the master list used in the national lottery. It also covers classification of registrants, physical examinations, deferments, conscientious objectors, and appeals. The rules apply to local boards, the Governor, and registrants under the Selective Training and Service Act of 1940.

8552.s: This order extends George W. Stose’s exemption from compulsory retirement for age for one more year, ending October 31, 1941. It applies to him as a principal scientist (geologist) with the Geological Survey in the Department of the Interior.

8551.s: This order puts certain National Guard units and members into active military service of the United States. It says they will serve for twelve consecutive months unless they are sooner relieved. People ordered into active service are relieved from duty in their State National Guard while they remain in federal service, and certain officers and warrant officers are moved to active duty under their appointments or commissions.

8549.s: This order names the Secretary of the Treasury to accept a parcel of land and the buildings on it from the people of Puerto Rico for the United States. The land is to be used for the purposes of the United States Coast Guard. It also directs the Secretary to do the steps needed to complete the transfer.

8548.s: The order transfers jurisdiction over the lands in Moore, Richmond, and Scotland Counties, North Carolina, to the Department of the Interior. It reserves the area as a refuge and breeding ground for native birds and other wildlife, and for research on wildlife and related forest resources. The lands may still be used and managed by North Carolina if a cooperative and license agreement remains in effect, and the Secretary of Agriculture keeps needed jurisdiction over lands still being acquired.

8547.s: This order amends the Foreign Service Regulations and adds new rules for Foreign Service officers. It requires reports on catastrophes abroad and rescues at sea, and it says officers should help distressed American citizens abroad when they can. It also limits officers from making personal loans, taking private property for safekeeping except in certain cases, and taking an active part in Red Cross membership or fund drives.

8550.s: This order modifies a prior order that withdrew certain public lands in Box Elder County, Utah. It lets the Secretary of the Interior complete land exchanges in certain applications under Public Resolution No. 84. The changes are for the purposes of the law authorizing the Bear River Migratory Bird Refuge.

8545.s: This order sets out regulations for carrying out the Selective Training and Service Act of 1940. It describes how selective service will register, classify, select, and induct males subject to registration into the land and naval forces. It also lays out the duties of the Director of Selective Service, state officials, local boards, boards of appeal, and other helpers in the system.

8546.s: This order creates the Defense Communications Board. The Board is to plan for the use and control of radio, wire, and cable communications for national defense during a national emergency or war. It covers the needs of the armed forces, other government agencies, industry, and other civilian activities, and it may appoint committees and work with other agencies and the communication industry.

8544.s: This order transfers a described area of national-forest land in Montana from the Lolo National Forest to the Helena National Forest. It says the change does not give national-forest status to public lands that do not already have it, and it does not remove public lands from national-forest status.

8542.s: This order allows Harold Ambrose to be appointed to a classified position in the Post Office Department without following the Civil Service Rules. It applies to his appointment in the Post Office Department after he had been serving in an excepted position there since June 12, 1933.

8543.s: This order further exempts Samuel J. Gompers, Chief Clerk in the Department of Labor, from compulsory retirement for age for one year. It applies only to him and extends his earlier exemptions.

8541.s: This order says the Assistant Secretary of Commerce must carry out the Secretary of Commerce's duties if the Secretary and Under Secretary are absent, sick, resign, or die. It also says the Solicitor of Commerce must do those duties if the Secretary, Under Secretary, and Assistant Secretary are all unavailable. The order replaces an earlier order on the same subject.

8540.s: This order revokes part of a previous order for a tract of public land on Woody Island in Alaska. It then withdraws that land from settlement, location, sale, or entry and reserves it for use by the Department of Commerce as an air-navigation site. The reservation stays in place until the President or Congress revokes it.

8538.s: This order exempts Z. Lewis Dalby, Chief Counsel of the United States Employees' Compensation Commission, from compulsory retirement for age for one year. It applies to him and lets him stay in service until September 30, 1941.

8539.s: This order exempts Herbert A. Howell, an Assistant Register of Copyrights at the Library of Congress, from compulsory retirement for age. It lets him stay in the job for one more year, ending September 30, 1941.

8537.s: This order lets the named people be appointed as experts in the Antitrust Division of the Department of Justice without following the Civil Service Rules. It also says they will not get competitive classified civil service status from these appointments.

8536.s: This order expands the defensive sea area around San Clemente Island, California, to one nautical mile from low-water mark. It says the area is for national defense and will be known as the San Clemente Island Naval Defensive Sea Area. Vessels or other craft may not enter unless authorized by the Secretary of the Navy, and violators are subject to penalties provided by law.

8534.s: This order amends the Civil Service Rules to list many federal jobs that are excepted from competitive examination. It covers positions in several departments, including private secretaries, chauffeurs, certain field workers, teachers, interpreters, and other specified roles. It also sets special rules for some temporary, part-time, or local jobs in the United States and overseas.

8535.s: This order changes Chapter XXII of the Foreign Service Regulations. It says that, in section XXII-1, the words "except consular agents" are added, and "Secretary of Labor" is replaced with "Attorney General."

8532.s: The order changes an earlier order so the Civil Service Commission must make a replacement list of Federal employees who do not have competitive civil service status, were involuntarily separated, had good records, and had at least six months of Government service before separation. That list is for temporary appointments to national-defense positions, and those appointments may not last beyond the national-defense program.

8531.s: This order changes an earlier order about certain public lands covered by the Bankhead-Jones Farm Tenant Act. It says those lands cannot be sold, exchanged, or granted without approval from the Secretary of the Interior, and a transfer of title is not complete unless a patent is issued by the General Land Office. It does not apply to lands included in a national forest or certain wildlife, waterfowl, migratory bird, or research refuges. It also does not limit the United States' rights in mineral resources on those lands.

8530.s: This order brings certain National Guard units and members into active military service of the United States. It covers listed divisions, coast artillery units, and observation squadrons, along with all active and inactive members of those units. While they are in active service, they are relieved from duty in their state National Guard and are subject to Army laws and regulations.

8529.s: This order revokes Executive Order No. 4901 of June 4, 1928, which had withdrawn public land in New Mexico for classification and in aid of legislation. It becomes effective on the sixtieth day after the date it was signed.

8528.s: This order extends the customs port of entry of Kansas City, Missouri, to include the municipalities of Kansas City, Kansas, and North Kansas City, Missouri. It affects customs entry boundaries in Customs Collection District Number 45 (St. Louis).

8527.s: This order transfers a certain tract of land on Sand Island, Oahu, in the Territory of Hawaii from the War Department to the Treasury Department. The land is to be used for Coast Guard purposes. The tract is described as 4.08 acres, more or less.

8525.s: This order further exempts Harry T. Edwards, a senior technologist in the Bureau of Plant Industry at the Department of Agriculture, from compulsory retirement for age. The exemption lasts for one year and ends on October 31, 1941.

8533.s: This order names the Secretary of the Treasury as the officer who may sell, exchange, or otherwise dispose of certain bonds, notes, or other securities covered by the Transportation Act of 1920, as amended. It also lets the Secretary arrange to extend the maturity of those securities. The Secretary may do this on terms and conditions he considers advisable and in the public interest.

8524.s: This order exempts J. Brent Clarke, Chief of the Diplomatic Pouch and Mail Section at the Department of State, from compulsory retirement for age. The exemption lasts for one year and ends on September 30, 1941.

8523.s: This order directs that enlisted Coast Guard members who are specially qualified to use certain arms and are stationed where they may be required to use them can receive extra pay. The extra pay ranges from $1 to $5 a month, depending on class. It also supersedes a 1922 executive order on the same subject.

8522.s: This order allows Anna F. Smith to be appointed as a relief telephone operator in the custodial service of the Post Office Department in Boston, Massachusetts. Her appointment may be made without following the civil service rules.

8520.s: This order exempts George F. MeDade, a foreman shipwright and dockmaster at The Panama Canal, from compulsory retirement for age. It lets him stay in service for one year, ending September 30, 1941.

8519.s: This order reserves certain townsite lots in Wyoming for the use of the Forest Service, part of the Department of Agriculture. The lots are set aside for administrative purposes, subject to valid existing rights. It applies to lots in the Esterbrook Townsite.

8517.s: This order changes the name of the Delta Migratory Waterfowl Refuge in Plaquemines Parish, Louisiana, to Delta National Wildlife Refuge. It also adds lands owned or controlled by the United States in that parish to the refuge. Private lands in the area would become part of the refuge if the United States acquires title or control of them.

8518.s: This order changes a 1915 order that had reserved certain public land in Washington as a refuge, preserve, and breeding ground for native birds. It lets the Navy Department have primary control of the listed land for naval purposes. The change affects the Dungeness Spit Reservation land described in the order.

8516.s: This order suspends part of an 1873 rule that had barred federal officers and employees from holding state, territorial, and municipal offices. It applies only where the United States Civil Service Commission, by regulation, authorizes appointments to positions directly concerned with national defense.

8515.s: This order sets aside Barro Colorado Island in the Canal Zone for scientific observation and investigation. Its natural features, including existing plants and animals, are to be left in their natural state except in a declared national emergency. The area is to be used by qualified students under rules set by the Canal Zone Biological Area Board.

8514.s: This order authorizes the Civil Service Commission to allow transfers during probation to appropriate positions directly concerned with the national defense program. It affects probationary civil service workers and the positions tied to that program.

8512.s: This order sets rules for how government agencies report financial information and how the Treasury Department keeps accounting records. It requires agencies to give the Secretary of the Treasury financial data, and it requires the Secretary to prepare reports for the Director of the Bureau of the Budget. It also makes agency spending subject to approved apportionments, with limited exceptions to prevent loss of life or government property.

8513.s: This order allows Neal Smith, William T. Bie, Charles Leo Milroy, Willinm S. DeGroff, and Cornelius Lynch to be appointed to classified jobs in the Public Buildings Administration, Federal Works Agency. It says these appointments can be made without following the Civil Service Rules.

8511.s: This order transfers control of certain land on the island of St. Croix in the Virgin Islands from the Department of the Interior to the War Department. The land is part of a tract known as "Bethlehem Estates" and is to be used for national-defense purposes. It covers about 213.72 acres, more or less.

8510.s: This order transfers jurisdiction over certain lands in Chesterfield and Darlington Counties, South Carolina, to the Department of the Interior. The area is set aside as a refuge and breeding ground for native birds and other wildlife, and for research on wildlife and related forest resources. The lands may still be used and managed by South Carolina’s Commission of Forestry under an agreement, and the Secretary of Agriculture keeps the authority needed to finish acquiring lands still in process.

8508.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in Florida from appropriation under the public-land laws, including the mining and leasing laws. The lands are set aside for the War Department to use as an antiaircraft firing range. It also supersedes two earlier withdrawal orders for any of those lands.

8509.s: The order transfers jurisdiction over certain lands in Boone County, Missouri, to the Department of the Interior. It reserves the area as a refuge and breeding ground for native birds and other wildlife, and for related research. The lands may still be used and managed by the Curators of the University of Missouri if a cooperative and license agreement remains in effect.

8507.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in California from appropriation under the public-land laws, including the mining laws. It sets aside those lands for the War Department to use as an anti-aircraft firing range, subject to valid existing rights. It also replaces earlier withdrawals for any of the same lands that are affected.

8506.s: This order removes listed tracts of land in Alaska from the Chugach and Tongass National Forests. It restores those homesites to entry under the applicable public-land laws. The change applies to the specific homesites named in the order.

8504.s: This order exempts James E. Amos, a special agent with the Federal Bureau of Investigation in the Department of Justice, from compulsory retirement for age. It keeps him in service for one year, ending January 31, 1942.

8505.s: This order removes a tract of public land in Alaska from the Chugach National Forest. It also withdraws the part of that tract that is not already reserved from settlement, sale, entry, or other disposition. That land is reserved for townsite purposes tied to the construction and operation of railroad lines.

8502.s: This order sets the grades and ratings for enlisted men of the Regular Army during fiscal year 1941. It also sets the maximum number allowed in each grade and in each specialist rating.

8501.s: This order transfers the Fort Howard Military Reservation in Maryland from the War Department to the Veterans Administration. The War Department will keep using the reservation until new facilities at the Arlington Cantonment in Virginia are ready for military use.

8500.s: This order changes Power Site Reserve No. 661 enough to let Lane County, Oregon, build a highway over a described area in Lane County. The highway use must stop, without liability or expense to the United States or its licensees, if the Secretary of the Interior finds it conflicts with project works authorized by the United States.

8499.s: This order modifies a 1914 executive order that created Power Site Reserve No. 454 on the Kootenai River in Idaho. It allows the Secretary of the Interior to approve an application by the Great Northern Railway Company for an amended definite location of part of its railway. The railway segment is described as built on a right-of-way granted in 1902 in Idaho.

8498.s: This order transfers a tract of land on Ediz Hook in Port Angeles Harbor, Washington, from the Navy Department to the Treasury Department for Coast Guard purposes. It covers the remaining part of a former naval reservation. If the land stops being used for Coast Guard purposes, control and jurisdiction will go back to the Navy Department.

8497.s: This order exempts Maurice C. Latta, an Executive Clerk in The White House Office, from compulsory retirement for age for one more year. It extends a previous exemption and runs through October 31, 1941.

8503.s: This order exempts Zebedee LaPelle, an administrative officer in the Office of Information at the Department of Agriculture, from compulsory retirement for age. It lets him stay in service for one more year, ending September 30, 1941.

8496.s: This order changes an earlier order that created Reservoir Site Reserve No. 16 in Oregon. It allows the Federal Power Commission to issue permits, licenses, and amendments for power projects on certain unsurveyed land near Odell Lake. The power projects must stop being used, without liability or expense to the United States or its licensees, if the Secretary of the Interior finds they conflict with project works authorized by the United States.

8495.s: This order designates the Secretary of Agriculture and the Secretary of the Treasury to buy and deliver materials and supplies for refugee men, women, and children who have been driven from their homes or made destitute by hostilities or invasion. It also designates The American Red Cross to receive, transport, and distribute those materials and supplies. The Secretary of Agriculture and The American Red Cross are to decide on agricultural supplies together, and the Secretary of the Treasury and The American Red Cross are to decide on the other materials and supplies.

8493.s: This order adds new restrictions on certain securities tied to foreign countries named in the order. It prohibits some buying, selling, transferring, and other dealings in those securities unless the Secretary of the Treasury authorizes them. It also lets the Secretary investigate, regulate, or prohibit bringing those securities into the United States and require people to give sworn information and records about covered transactions or property.

8494.s: This order authorizes the Civil Service Commission to give competitive classified civil service status to five employees in the Disbursing Office of the Division of Disbursement of the Treasury at Honolulu, Territory of Hawaii. The employees must meet several requirements, including prior service in the positions, satisfactory service, United States citizenship, and passing the tests set by the Commission. Anyone who does not meet the requirements must be separated from service unless the Secretary of the Treasury certifies that the employee should be retained without competitive classified status.

8492.s: This order temporarily withdraws a small tract of public land in California from settlement, location, sale, or entry. It reserves the land for use as a fire lookout station for Federal and State cooperative forest-protection work. The State of California may use the land, but that use must not interfere with the nearby U.S. Coast and Geodetic Survey triangulation station.

8491.s: This order exempts William F. Yates, a maritime personnel assistant at the United States Maritime Commission, from compulsory retirement for age for one year. It applies to his service and delays his automatic separation from the service for that period.

8490.s: This order lets certain officials in the District of Columbia, Alaska, Hawaii, the Philippine Islands, and Puerto Rico inspect certain tax returns. It covers income, excess-profits, capital stock, estate, and gift tax returns, as well as employment tax returns under the Internal Revenue Code. It also covers some returns filed under earlier revenue laws and returns under Title IX of the Social Security Act, but only under Treasury rules.

8489.s: This order further exempts William M. Smith, a Special Assistant to the Chief of the Bureau of Yards and Docks in the Navy Department, from compulsory retirement for age. The exemption lasts for one more year, ending October 31, 1941.

8488.s: This order allows Walter Kuhn to be appointed as a guard in the Public Buildings Administration, Federal Works Agency. It says the appointment may be made without following the Civil Service Rules.

8486.s: This order changes a previous withdrawal of public land in Arizona that had been for use by the War Department as an enlargement of a target range used by the Arizona National Guard. It lets the Secretary of the Interior withdraw the described land for use by the Civil Aeronautics Authority to establish and maintain air-navigation facilities. The land described is 160 acres.

8487.s: This order designates Ronald Ransom as Vice Chairman of the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System. He is to serve in that role for four years from August 6, 1940, unless his service on the Board ends sooner.

8483.s: This order exempts Louis Loebl, a special agent in the Federal Bureau of Investigation, from compulsory retirement for age. It lets him stay in service for one more year, ending September 30, 1941.

8482.s: This order allows Norman H. Stevens to be appointed as a rural letter carrier in the Postal Service at East Falls Church, Virginia. It says the appointment may be made without following the Civil Service Rules.

8481.s: This order exempts Ernest G. Dodge, a principal civil service examiner at the United States Civil Service Commission, from compulsory retirement for age. The exemption lasts for one year and ends on July 31, 1941.

8484.s: This order amends a prior executive order to extend its provisions to property in which Latvia, Estonia, or Lithuania, or any national of those ქვეყნies, has had any direct or indirect interest since July 10, 1940. It also changes the date used in the definitions of those countries and their nationals to July 10, 1940.

8479.s: This order transfers about one acre of land in Juneau County, Wisconsin, from the Secretary of Agriculture to the Secretary of the Interior. It adds the land to and reserves it as part of the Necedah National Wildlife Refuge, subject to valid rights.

8478.s: This order allows four named people to be appointed to jobs in the Welfare Unit of the Public Buildings Administration without following the competitive Civil Service Rules. The jobs are Senior Welfare Worker, Assistant Welfare Worker, Under Clerk-Typist, and Chauffeur. It applies to those appointments in the Federal Works Agency.

8477.s: This order exempts Samuel Cohn, an internal revenue agent in the Treasury Department, from compulsory retirement for age for one year. It applies only to him and lets him stay in service until July 31, 1941.

8476.s: This order waives the time limits in Civil Service Rule IX so Mrs. Martha Overstreet can be reinstated to a clerical job in the post office at Douglas, Georgia. It says she was formerly employed there and is the widow of Post Office Inspector Thomas M. Overstreet.

8475.s: This order revokes part of Executive Order No. 924 that had established the Klamath Lake Reservation. It applies to one described parcel of land in Klamath County, Oregon.

8480.s: This order excludes a described tract of land in Alaska from the Chugach National Forest. It also withdraws that land from settlement, location, sale, entry, or other disposal. The land is reserved for townsite purposes in connection with the construction and operation of railroad lines.

8474.s: This order allows Newton B. Drury to be appointed as Director of the National Park Service in the Department of the Interior. It says the appointment may be made without following the competitive requirements of the Civil Service Act and Rules.

8473.s: This order transfers jurisdiction over certain lands and the improvements on them in North Dakota from the Secretary of Agriculture to the Secretary of the Interior. The Secretary of the Interior is authorized to administer the lands through the Commissioner of Indian Affairs for the benefit of Indians he may designate. The lands were acquired in connection with the Standing Rock Project.

8471.s: This order transfers jurisdiction over certain lands in New Mexico from the Secretary of Agriculture to the Secretary of the Interior. The lands include areas tied to several listed projects and are near existing Indian reservations. The Secretary of the Interior may administer the lands through the Commissioner of Indian Affairs for the benefit of Indians he designates.

8470.s: This order accepts title to about 35 acres of land on Government Island in Alameda, California, from the City of Alameda. It places the land under the control of the Federal Works Agency for public use by several federal agencies, including the Public Roads Administration, the Forest Service, the Coast Guard, and the United States Maritime Commission.

8469.s: This order allows John F. Hardy to be appointed as Regional Director in the Social Security Board without following the competitive rules of the Civil Service Act and Rules. He must still show the Civil Service Commission that he has the qualifications for the job.

8472.s: This order changes an earlier order that moved jurisdiction over certain lands in New Mexico from the Secretary of Agriculture to the Secretary of the Interior. It adds some listed lands in McKinley and Valencia Counties to that earlier order. It also removes some listed lands in McKinley County from the order, so it no longer applies to those lands.

8468.s: This order temporarily withdraws all public lands in Louisiana, whether surveyed or unsurveyed, from settlement, location, sale, or entry. It reserves those lands for classification and to aid legislation, and it stays in effect until the President or Congress revokes it.

8463.s: This order allows Charles Leo Milroy and James E. Spratt to be appointed to classified guard positions in the Public Buildings Administration, Federal Works Agency. It says they may be appointed without following the Civil Service Rules.

8462.s: This order allows Wilford S. Alexander to be appointed as District Supervisor in the Alcohol Tax Unit of the Bureau of Internal Revenue without following the Civil Service Rules. It affects that appointment and the office of District Supervisor.

8465.s: This order sets rules for certifications by the Secretary of War or the Secretary of the Navy about special additional equipment and facilities used to build naval vessels and Army or Navy aircraft. It requires the contractor or subcontractor to file a request that lists the equipment, its cost, and the share of cost to be charged to the contract. It also says no certification may be made unless steps are taken to protect the government's interest and give the government priority use of the equipment for national defense purposes.

8461.s: This order changes how eligibility for certain retirement pay benefits is decided under the earlier order. It gives the Secretary of War, or someone he designates in the War Department, the job of deciding all questions of eligibility, including questions of law and fact, under the standards set by law or regulations for Regular Army personnel.

8460.s: This order modifies a 1913 order that created Power Site Reserve No. 339 in Colorado. It allows the Secretary of the Interior to approve Jerome Craig’s application for a right-of-way to enlarge the Casto Reservoir in the listed tracts. It affects land in the reserve where that right-of-way would be used.

8461-A.s: This order lets the Archivist of the United States make the first appointments of one clerk-stenographer and one junior clerk-stenographer at the Franklin D. Roosevelt Library. Those appointments can be made without following the Civil Service Act and Rules.

8459.s: This order revokes part of a prior withdrawal for certain public lands in New Mexico. It then temporarily withdraws those lands from settlement, location, sale, or entry and reserves them for use by the Farm Security Administration of the Department of Agriculture. The lands are to be used to resettle native farm families who live in or near El Pueblo in San Miguel County, and the United States keeps its rights to the mineral resources.

8458.s: The order directs the Civil Service Commission to create a replacement list of certain former federal employees who were separated involuntarily, had good records, and had at least six months of government service before leaving. That list is to be used for temporary appointments to national-defense positions for terms no longer than the national-defense program. The commission must decide which jobs count as national-defense positions and set rules for joining and using the list. People appointed from the list do not get competitive civil-service status from that appointment.

8456.s: This order lets certain employees of the General Accounting Office stay in service for another year, through June 30, 1941. It does not change the status of the positions held by employees who are allowed to get a competitive classified civil-service status under a separate executive order.

8455.s: This order adds more Federal agencies to the list of construction agencies. It covers agencies that plan or carry out construction paid for in whole or in part by the Federal Government, and agencies that help construction through grants, loans, or other financial aid. It requires certain agencies to make six-year construction plans and send reports to the Bureau of the Budget and the National Resources Planning Board. It also lets those officials issue rules, decide which agencies fit each class, and temporarily exempt an agency or project if needed.

8454.s: This order lets the Administrator of Veterans' Affairs approve travel payments for claimants and beneficiaries who travel, with prior authorization, to or from a Veterans' Administration facility or other place for examination, treatment, or care. It allows payment of actual necessary travel expenses, including lodging and subsistence, or a mileage allowance set by the order. It also lets an attendant receive travel expenses on a similar basis when one is needed.

8453.s: This order exempts Burnett Booker, a head messenger in the Department of State, from compulsory retirement for age. It lets him stay in his job for one more year, ending July 31, 1941.

8452.s: This order exempts Albert Clyde-Burton from compulsory retirement for age for one year. It applies to him as Chief of the Recreation Division of National Capital Parks in the National Park Service.

8450.s: This order withdraws certain public lands in California from entry under the public-land laws, including the mining laws, while keeping valid existing rights in place. It sets aside those lands for use by the War Department as a bombing and gunnery range. It also replaces earlier executive orders on the same subject and stays in force until the President or Congress revokes it.

8451.s: This order allows Russell Sturgis to be appointed as an assistant territorial representative in the Wage and Hour Division of the Department of Labor. The appointment may be made without following the Civil Service Rules. It also says the appointment will not give him competitive classified civil-service status.

8448.s: This order exempts Maitland S. Wright, Chief of the Supply Unit in the Department of State, from compulsory retirement for age. The exemption lasts for one year, ending July 31, 1941.

8449.s: This order amends the Civil Service Rules to allow some field service jobs in the Bureau of Fisheries for scientific fishery investigations to be filled by students at colleges and universities of recognized standing. It applies only when those colleges or universities make substantial contributions to the investigations and the student is a bona fide student who gets academic credit toward a degree for the work.

8457.s: This order lets certain employees of the General Accounting Office keep working and gain competitive classified civil-service status if they meet the stated requirements. It applies to employees who were appointed before July 1, 1935, are not paid from emergency funds, have had continuous satisfactory service since July 1, 1935, pass the required tests, are citizens of the United States, and are not otherwise disqualified. It also says the affected positions are classified civil-service positions and future vacancies must be filled under competitive civil-service requirements.

8447.s: The order lets the Civil Service Commission give competitive classified civil-service status to certain employees of the Department of Labor. It applies to some workers in wage determination, the Conciliation Service, and the Office of the Secretary of Labor, if they meet set service, citizenship, and fitness requirements. Employees who do not meet those requirements may be separated from service unless the Secretary of Labor certifies that they should be retained without that status.

8445.s: This order changes the rules for appeals from decisions of the Auditor General of the Philippines to the President of the United States. It says the appeal period runs from the date a copy of the decision is received by the party filing the appeal, and it changes the offices named in sections 4 and 5.

8444.s: This order reserves certain lands in Mississippi as the Noxubee National Wildlife Refuge. It sets the area aside for the Department of the Interior as a refuge and breeding ground for migratory birds and other wildlife, while the Secretary of Agriculture may continue some activities on certain lands, including grazing, forestry, recreational facilities, and fish-taking, by mutual agreement with the Secretary of the Interior. It also says private lands in the area will become part of the refuge if the United States acquires title or control, and it bars hunting, trapping, capturing, disturbing, or killing birds or wild animals in the refuge except under rules set by the Secretary of the Interior.

8443.s: This order directs the Secretary of the Treasury to assemble a Coast Guard Personnel Board each year, as allowed by the cited law. It also replaces Executive Order No. 7922, which had given the same direction.

8442.s: This order revokes part of a 1933 order for two tracts of public land in Alaska. It also reserves about 531.40 acres on Kodiak Island for town-site purposes and says the land will be disposed of under applicable town-site laws. The reservation stays in force until the President or Congress revokes it.

8446.s: This order amends Executive Order No. 8389 and extends its provisions to property in which France or any French national has had any direct or indirect interest since June 17, 1940. It also changes the definitions of “France” and a French national to use June 17, 1940, instead of the earlier dates.

8440.s: This order changes rules for allowances for quarters and subsistence for enlisted men who are not furnished quarters or rations in kind. It gives enlisted men of the Army on duty in Bogota, Colombia, and enlisted men of the Navy and Marine Corps in certain Naval Attaché offices in Bogota and Guatemala City a per diem allowance of $3.00 for subsistence and $1.00 for quarters. It affects only those enlisted men serving in those places.

8441.s: This order changes the Civil Service Rules for a set period from July 1, 1940, through June 30, 1941. It covers all positions in the Federal Bureau of Investigation except fingerprint classifiers.

8439.s: This order changes Chapter IX of the Foreign Service Regulations of the United States. It replaces one agency heading with "Federal Security Agency," moves "Treasury" to a later section, and deletes the words "by the Secretary of the Treasury" from section IX-8.

8437.s: This order revokes part of Executive Order of November 22, 1924, that created Power Site Reserve No. 759. It removes the reserve from the listed lands in New Mexico described by township, range, and section.

8438.s: This order extends the Civil Service Retirement Act to employees of the Office of the Legal Adviser in the Department of State. It applies to employees whose jobs are not intermittent or of uncertain duration.

8435.s: This order changes a 1916 power site reserve in Idaho so the State of Idaho can build a highway across certain lots in the reserve. The highway must be stopped if the Secretary of the Interior finds it conflicts with project works authorized by the United States. The order says this must be done without liability or expense to the United States or its licensees.

8436.s: This order allows Baird Snyder III to be appointed Deputy Administrator in the Wage and Hour Division at the Department of Labor without following the Civil Service Rules. It also says that the appointment will not give him competitive classified civil-service status.

8434.s: This order transfers control and jurisdiction of a tract of land in Texas from the Secretary of State to the Federal Works Agency for use by the Bureau of Customs. The transfer must allow proper U.S. agencies to build, operate, and maintain ditches or canals for the Rio Grande Federal Irrigation Project across the land. If the land stops being used by the Federal Works Agency and the Bureau of Customs, control and jurisdiction return to the Department of State.

8433.s: This order says the United States is neutral in the war between Italy and France and the United Kingdom. It applies the existing neutrality rules equally to Italy to help enforce the laws and treaties that bar unneutral acts within U.S. jurisdiction.

8431.s: This order revokes Executive Order No. 6845, which had withdrawn public lands in Colorado pending a resurvey. It takes effect when the official plats of the resurvey of the lands involved are filed.

8430.s: This order sets document rules for aliens entering the United States. Nonimmigrants and immigrants must generally show passports and the right visas, though some listed exceptions can use other certificates or have the requirements waived in limited cases. It also lets certain officials issue these documents for aliens coming from the Canal Zone, American Samoa, and Guam, and it replaces an earlier executive order on the same subject.

8429.s: This order sets rules for when bona fide alien seamen may enter the United States temporarily without passports or visas. It also requires masters of most ships sailing to a U.S. port to submit a visaed list of alien crew members, and it bars seamen not on a required visaed crew list from landing without permission. Alien seamen who are not exempt must show an identifying travel document with their nationality, identity, and fingerprints before shore leave.

8432.s: This order revokes Executive Order No. 5208 of October 12, 1929, which had withdrawn public lands in Nevada while a resurvey was pending. It applies to the rest of the lands covered by that earlier order and takes effect when the official plat of the resurvey is filed.

8428.s: This order revokes part of Executive Order No. 6228 as it applies to the transfer of the Custer Battlefield National Cemetery in Montana. It becomes effective on July 1, 1940.

8427.s: This order sets up a regularly scheduled mail and messenger service in the Post Office Department for government agencies in the District of Columbia and part of Virginia near the Arlington Memorial Bridge. It puts the service under the Postmaster General and covers mail, papers, documents, packages, and other articles sent to and from buildings used by government agencies. It also sets rules for vehicle markings, schedules, pickup points, size and weight limits for items, and the use of special envelopes, tags, and labels.

8426.s: This order waives the maximum age limit for civil service exams so Mrs. Florence S. Eilenberger can compete for the postmaster examination at East Stroudsburg, Pennsylvania. It affects her application for that position.

8425.s: This order changes the rules for reinstating certain federal workers. It sets different time limits for applying for reinstatement based on how long the person previously served, with no time limit for service of 5 years or more. It also allows the time limit to be waived for reinstatements to positions in federal agencies concerned with preparedness and the national-defense program.

8424.s: This order changes a Civil Service rule about which jobs are outside the competitive classified service. It covers certain people employed in foreign countries, the Virgin Islands, Puerto Rico when public need warrants, certain Pacific island possessions, and U.S. citizens employed in the Philippine Islands. It does not apply to some people employed in Canada or Mexico by the Immigration and Naturalization Service, or to some people employed in foreign countries by the Bureau of Customs.

8422.s: This order exempts James E. Harper, Chief of the Division of Appointments in the Treasury Department, from compulsory retirement for age for one more year. It affects Harper only and lets him keep serving until June 30, 1941.

8421.s: This order exempts Joseph F. Reardon, a master joiner and shipwright at the Navy Yard in New York, New York, from compulsory retirement for age. The exemption lasts for one year ending May 31, 1941.

8420.s: This order further exempts Frank B. Bourn from compulsory retirement for age for one year. He is the Chief of the Supplies and Accounts Division in the Office of the Secretary of War at the War Department. The exemption runs until June 30, 1941.

8419.s: This order revokes part of a 1910 executive order that had created Coal Land Withdrawal, Utah No. 1. It applies to the listed lands in Utah described by township, range, and section.

8423.s: This order changes Civil Service Rule VII on how a nominating or appointing officer makes selections for the first vacancy. It says the officer must choose from not more than the highest three certified persons, or from the register, based on merit and fitness. It also allows the Civil Service Commission to object to one or more certified persons for reasons listed in Rule V, section 3, and, for some federal agencies, for other approved reasons.

8416.s: This order allows William T. Geurts to be appointed as Senior Mediator on the Maritime Labor Board without regard to his standing on the civil service eligibles register. It applies to that appointment and says the action was taken after a recommendation from the Chairman of the Maritime Labor Board.

8417.s: This order amends the rules for the Panama Canal Zone to list classes of people who are forbidden to enter, stay in, or pass through the zone. It also lets the Governor of The Panama Canal deport such people when found in the Canal Zone. The order covers people with certain mental or contagious conditions, people convicted of certain crimes, beggars and paupers, anarchists, people who try to incite insurrection, and people who take part in certain strikes or other conduct that could interfere with Canal Zone operations.

8415.s: This order allows Lyman A. Fillmen to be appointed to a classified instrument maker position in the Smithsonian Institution without meeting the Civil Service Rules. It affects Mr. Fillmen and the Smithsonian Institution.

8414.s: This order further exempts William C. Shambaugh from compulsory retirement because of age for one more year, ending August 31, 1941. It affects Shambaugh, who was a blacksmith instructor in the Medical Department at Large of the War Department.

8413.s: This order exempts Hubert K. Bishop, Chief of the Division of Construction in the Public Roads Administration, from compulsory retirement for age. It lets him stay in federal service for one more year.

8412.s: This order exempts Charles M. Eichelberger, Chief Accountant and Auditor for the Compensation Board in the Navy Department, from compulsory retirement for age. The exemption lasts for one year and ends on June 30, 1941.

8411.s: This order temporarily withdraws a tract of public land in Alaska from settlement, location, sale, or entry. It reserves the land for the use of the Alaska Road Commission. The order stays in force until the President or Congress revokes it.

8409.s: This order exempts Jacob C. Lesher, a principal clerk in the Department of Labor, from compulsory retirement for age. The exemption lasts for one year, ending May 31, 1941.

8408.s: This order exempts Huntt P. Larcombe, a principal clerk in the Office of the Surgeon General, from compulsory retirement for age. The exemption lasts for six months and ends on November 30, 1940.

8410.s: This order exempts Harry C. Oberholser, a senior biologist in the Department of the Interior, from compulsory retirement for age. It lets him stay in service for one year, ending June 30, 1941.

8406.s: This order says the United States must not allow unneutral acts within its jurisdiction while it is neutral in a war. It applies the rules from Executive Order No. 8233 equally to Belgium, Luxemburg, and the Netherlands. It is meant to strengthen enforcement of the United States' neutrality laws and proclamation.

8405.s: This order amends earlier foreign exchange rules to prohibit certain credit transfers, payments, foreign exchange transactions, and exports or dealings in gold, silver, currency, and property interests involving Norway, Denmark, the Netherlands, Belgium, or Luxembourg, unless authorized by the Secretary of the Treasury. It also requires sworn reports and additional information about property and dealings involving those countries or their nationals. The order gives definitions for those countries, their nationals, and banking institutions, and updates Treasury regulations to carry out these rules.

8404.s: This order lets the Civil Service Commission reopen certain competitive exams so people can be considered for jobs in the Social Security Board. The reopened exam must be recommended by the Social Security Board and the Federal Security Agency, and the person must meet several conditions, including prior work in a state agency that administers grants of federal funds under the Social Security Act. People who gain a civil service status under this order may be appointed only to appropriate positions in the Social Security Board and the Federal Security Agency.

8407.s: This order revokes part of a prior order for the Louisiana lands described here. It withdraws those public lands from settlement, location, sale, or entry and reserves them for flood-control purposes for the Bayou Bodcau Dam and Reservoir project. The land is to be handled under the direction of the Secretary of War and the supervision of the Chief of Engineers, and the reservation stays in force until the President or Congress revokes it.

8403.s: This order establishes a naval defensive sea area in part of the waters off Los Angeles and Long Beach for national defense. It bars vessels or other craft from anchoring there unless the Secretary of the Navy authorizes it, with exceptions for public vessels of the United States and California, and for merchant vessels and small craft during a thick fog or emergency. People who violate the order are subject to legal penalties.

8402.s: This order exempts Nelson S. Thompson from compulsory retirement for age for one year. It applies to him in his job as Chief of the Mechanical Engineering Section in the Office of the Supervising Architect, Public Buildings Administration, Federal Works Agency.

8401.s: This order exempts Percy Nicholls, a heat transmission engineer at the Bureau of Mines in the Department of the Interior, from compulsory retirement for age. It keeps him in service for one year, ending June 30, 1941.

8399.s: This order changes an earlier rule that barred most federal officers and employees from holding state, territorial, or municipal offices. It lets officers and employees of the Social Security Board and Federal Security Agency hold certain outside offices if the work is tied to Social Security Board work and does not interfere with their federal duties. It also lets certain state, territorial, and municipal officers or employees take jobs with the Social Security Board when the Board and the Administrator decide it is needed, and civil-service rules still apply where required.

8398.s: This order says the United States is neutral in the war between Germany and Norway. It makes the earlier neutrality regulations apply equally to Norway. It is meant to help enforce the rules against unneutral acts within the United States.

8400.s: This order amends the Foreign Service Regulations on visas for aliens. It requires Foreign Service officers to know and help enforce immigration laws, report suspected violations, and handle documents for admissible Chinese under the rules in place. It also allows diplomatic visas to be granted abroad under rules set by the Secretary of State and cancels some older regulations and executive orders.

8397.s: This order revokes an earlier withdrawal for certain public lands in Idaho. The lands are temporarily withdrawn from settlement, location, sale, or entry, subject to valid existing rights. The withdrawal is for classification and to help pending legislation about protecting watersheds or sources of water supply for cities or towns.

8396.s: This order amends the Foreign Service regulations and sets rules for Foreign Service officers, vice consuls, consular agents, and other employees. It describes how they are appointed, what oath and paperwork they must take, when they must give bonds, and how they may be assigned to posts, special duties, or training school. It also sets limits on their speeches, political activity, correspondence, business interests, family employment, and acceptance of gifts or presents.

8395.s: This order allows Floyd E. Julian to be appointed as a rural letter carrier in the Postal Service at Loudon, Tennessee. It says the appointment may be made without following the Civil Service Rules.

8394.s: This order revokes an 1866 executive order that had reserved certain public land in Oregon for lighthouse purposes. It applies to the described land in Willamette Meridian, Township 5 North, Range 11 West, section 1, lot 2, containing 45.64 acres.

8392.s: This order further exempts Zeke Johnson, a custodian at Natural Bridges National Monument, from compulsory retirement for age. The exemption lasts for one more year, ending April 30, 1941.

8391.s: This order exempts Clifton E. Johnson, a senior mechanic with the United States Coast Guard in the Treasury Department, from compulsory retirement for age. The exemption lasts for one year and ends on May 31, 1941.

8390.s: This order changes an older rule that barred most federal officers and employees from holding certain state, territorial, or municipal offices. It allows federal employees to work as teachers or instructors in any state, territorial, or municipal school or university. They may do so only if the outside position does not interfere with their federal duties during regular work hours.

8393.s: This order restores two parcels of land in Makua Valley, Oahu, from the Makua Military Reservation to the use of the Territory of Hawaii. The lands had been set aside for military purposes, but the order says they are no longer required for those purposes. It also keeps the War Department’s right to remove material from the howitzer emplacements if that has not already been done.

8389.s: This order amends a previous order on foreign exchange and credit transfers. It prohibits certain bank transfers, payments, foreign exchange transactions, and exports or withdrawals of gold, silver, coin, bullion, or currency when the property involves Norway, Denmark, or their nationals, unless authorized by the Treasury Secretary. It also requires sworn reports and can require extra records for property and dealings involving Norway or Denmark or their nationals.

8388.s: This order restores 5.994 acres near Port Allen Airport on Kauai to the use of the Territory of Hawaii for aeronautical purposes. It also sets aside 17.82 acres near Puolo Point, adjoining Port Allen Airport, for military purposes of the United States. It affects land used by the Territory of Hawaii and by the War Department for military purposes.

8387.s: This order revokes part of a 1913 executive order that created Public Water Reserve No. 12. The revocation applies only to the land in Wyoming described in the order.

8386.s: This order exempts John W. Kindle, a master mechanic at the Navy Yard in Washington, D.C., from compulsory retirement for age for one year. It applies to him only and lasts until May 31, 1941.

8385.s: This order sets rules for sick leave for civilian officers and employees of the United States, the District of Columbia, and certain corporations covered by the law. It says sick leave with pay may be granted for sickness, injury, pregnancy and confinement, or certain contagious disease situations. It also sets how sick leave is earned, carried over, advanced, charged, and when some employees are excepted from the rules.

8383.s: This order authorizes the Civil Service Commission to give competitive classified civil-service status to certain employees of the Office of Indian Affairs. It applies to employees in Washington, D.C., and in the field who were properly appointed before February 1, 1939, under specific Civil Service Rules.

8382.s: This order amends an earlier rule for vessels passing through the Panama Canal during a war in which the United States is neutral. It bars people on board from having cameras or making photographs, sketches, maps, or other images of the canal locks or nearby areas without permission from the Governor of The Panama Canal. It also requires the master of each vessel to collect and hold cameras during transit and to help prevent forbidden photography. Violations are punishable under the Canal Zone Code.

8381.s: This order defines certain military and naval installations, equipment, and official records as vital and needing protection from wide sharing of information.
